detail: The Reserve Bank of India's governor said global financial market sentiment remains fragile and that there are limited signs of supply-side pressures becoming embedded. The bank raised its FY27 core inflation projection to 4.4% from 4.3%.

headline: Hedge fund industry group warns BoE that its proposed gilt repo reforms could backfire and reduce liquidity under stress
detail: Reuters reports that a hedge fund industry group has told the Bank of England its proposed reforms to the repo market, where short-term loans are secured against gilts, could cut liquidity during periods of market stress.

headline: German August industrial production rises 2% m/m, above the 0.5% forecast; annual growth of 2.3% also beats
detail: German industrial production rose 2% on the month against a 0.5% forecast, after a 1.1% fall previously. On the year, output was up 2.3%, against a 0.7% forecast and a previous reading of -1.63%.

headline: Brent crude tops $101 a barrel after more attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: City AM reports that Brent edged above $101 a barrel on Wednesday morning after attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz intensified in recent days. It adds that Middle East tensions are offsetting a rise in supply.

headline: IMF's Georgieva calls for a prudently hawkish stance and says rate rises are still right for the Fed, ECB and BoJ
detail: The IMF Managing Director said energy and food shocks, the AI construction boom, tariffs, defence spending and high debt could add to inflation, and that global public debt is set to exceed 100% of GDP, with advanced economies carrying the heaviest burdens. She said new IMF forecasts show weaker growth in Ukraine, the Gulf states and some energy-importing economies.

headline: UK house prices flat in September at 0.0% m/m, Lloyds data show, against a 0.1% rise expected
detail: Lloyds' September house price index was unchanged on the month, below the 0.1% rise forecast in a poll.

headline: Swedish September CPI rises to 1.1% y/y, just short of the 1.2% forecast; CPIF in line at 1.5%
detail: Swedish headline CPI rose 0.9% m/m against a 1.0% forecast, and CPIF rose 1.5% y/y as expected, up from 0.7%. CPIF excluding energy held at 0.5% y/y, below the 0.7% forecast.

headline: Germany to join a further release of energy reserves under the volume the IEA set in March
detail: Germany's Economy Ministry says the country will take part in a further release of the energy reserve volume the IEA agreed in March. It says approval of the release is under way.

headline: EUR/GBP falls 0.3% to 0.84528, its lowest level since June 2025
detail: The euro fell 0.3% against sterling to 0.84528, reaching its lowest level since June 2025, according to a market commentary account.

headline: EU imposes temporary limits on imports of Chinese hybrid cars
detail: Market newswire headlines report that the EU is setting temporary caps on imports of hybrid cars from China. European carmaker shares are reported higher on the news.

headline: German 7-year Bund auction yields 3.36%, up from 2.68% last time; bid-to-cover rises to 1.4 from 1.2
detail: Germany's sale of the new 7-year Bund came in at an average yield of 3.36%, against 2.68% at the previous auction. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.4, up from 1.2.

headline: French 10-year government bond yield rises 15bp to 4.8974%
detail: A market news feed reported the French 10-year yield up 15bp on the day at 4.8974% on Wednesday morning.

headline: Sterling falls 0.55% to $1.3205 as euro drops 0.73% to $1.1178
detail: A market commentary account reported sterling down 0.55% at $1.3205 and the euro down 0.73% at $1.1178 against the dollar.

headline: Global bond sell-off resumes, with UK gilts, French and Italian bonds under pressure in volatile trading, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the global bond sell-off has resumed, with the US 30-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2002. UK, French and Italian government bonds are also reported under pressure in volatile trading; no gilt yield levels were given.

headline: Houthi rebels fire a new missile barrage at Riyadh and Aden, FT reports
detail: The FT reports a new Houthi missile assault on the Saudi capital and on Aden. It follows a government offensive announced days earlier to retake the Bab al-Mandab waterway.

headline: UK 30-year gilt yield climbs to 6.034%, its highest since 1998, up more than 12bp on the day
detail: The UK 30-year gilt yield rose to 6.034%, its highest level since 1998 and more than 12bp higher on the day, a market wire reported.

headline: Polish central bank keeps its main interest rate at 3.75%, as expected
detail: Poland's central bank left its main rate unchanged at 3.75%, which matched the forecast.

headline: IEA members back speeding up the oil stock releases agreed in March, with about 100m barrels still to come
detail: An IEA statement says member governments support completing the oil stock releases pledged in March as soon as possible, which would bring about 100 million barrels to market, and also back giving priority to releasing diesel stocks. Members still hold around 1.1bn barrels in reserve, including more than 200m barrels of diesel, and will review the situation at next week's governing board meeting.

headline: German 2-year yield falls 6bp to 3.02% while French and Italian 2-year yields rise 6bp to 3.61% and 3.48%
detail: Germany's 2-year government bond yield is down 6bp at 3.02%, against the move in other eurozone sovereign debt. France's 2-year yield is up 6bp at 3.61% and Italy's is up 6bp at 3.48%.

headline: NY Fed survey shows US 1-year inflation expectations up to 3.9%, above the 3.64% forecast and the previous 3.58%
detail: The New York Fed's consumer survey puts 1-year-ahead inflation expectations at 3.9%. That compares with a forecast of 3.64% and a previous reading of 3.58%.

headline: France weighs shifting issuance towards shorter-term debt amid bond market turmoil, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that France is considering issuing more short-dated debt in response to the turmoil in bond markets.

headline: EU envoys sign off on about 1,650 new sanctions listings against Russia
detail: EU ambassadors have approved roughly 1,650 new listings under the Russia sanctions regime, according to EU diplomats. No market reaction was reported.

headline: French Finance Ministry says there is no change to its bond issuance strategy, after WSJ report of a shift to shorter debt
detail: The French Finance Ministry said its bond issuance strategy is unchanged and follows investor demand. This comes after a WSJ report that France was considering moving issuance towards shorter-term debt amid the bond market sell-off.

headline: France to release 10m barrels of diesel from its strategic reserves, France Info reports
detail: French broadcaster France Info reports that France will release 10m barrels of diesel from its reserves. The report comes after IEA members backed speeding up the oil stock releases agreed in March.

headline: US $39bn 10-year note auction stops through by 1.7bp at 5.3%; bid-to-cover rises to 2.77
detail: The US Treasury's $39bn 10-year note sale drew a high yield of 5.3%, compared with 4.834% at the previous auction and a when-issued yield of 5.317% before the sale. Bid-to-cover rose to 2.77 from 2.71. Indirect bidders took 80.34%, directs 17.12% and primary dealers 2.54%.

headline: French PM Lecornu asks lawmakers to hold the 2027 budget deficit to 5% of GDP
detail: French Prime Minister Lecornu called on parliament to keep the 2027 deficit within 5% of GDP. The call comes during French budget talks.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield reaches its highest since 2002 as global bond sell-off spreads, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that the global bond sell-off on Wednesday took US 30-year borrowing costs to their highest since 2002, while UK 30-year gilt yields hit a 28-year high. The move comes three weeks before Chancellor Healey's first Budget.

headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent calls high bond yields a global phenomenon and says rates will fall once the Iran conflict ends
detail: The US Treasury Secretary said high bond yields are a global phenomenon and that bond yields and mortgage rates will come down once the Iran conflict ends, when he also expects the energy market to be well supplied. He also said core inflation is nearing the Fed's target.

headline: Fed minutes show all 19 officials backed the September rate rise and most saw another 2026 hike as likely appropriate
detail: Minutes of the September FOMC meeting show almost all participants saw inflation risks tilted to the upside and job market risks as broadly balanced, and many cited risk-management grounds for the hike. Several saw the current rate as not restrictive or only mildly so; many said financial conditions still support growth despite the recent rise in long-term Treasury yields.

headline: New York Fed reportedly intervenes in the currency market on behalf of the US Treasury
detail: A market news account reports that the New York Fed intervened in the foreign exchange market for the US Treasury. The report gives no details of the currency or amounts involved.

headline: Diesel prices jump after the IEA says no fuel will be released beyond the stock release agreed in March
detail: The FT reports that IEA members say the 100mn barrels promised by the G7 will come out of the 400mn barrel release agreed in March, not from additional stocks. Diesel prices are reported to have jumped in response; no figure for the move was given.

headline: US Gulf of Mexico oil output of 511,619 b/d shut in, about 25% of the region's production
detail: Figures attributed to the MMA show 511,619 barrels a day of US Gulf oil production shut in, equal to 25.08% of output. No market reaction was reported.

headline: FT estimates the Iran war has cut UK public finances by nearly £12bn, roughly halving Chancellor Healey's fiscal headroom
detail: FT estimates find that higher inflation and borrowing costs have probably cut the Chancellor's headroom by about half. The FT says this leaves him relying on tax rises and spending cuts at the Budget to help with living costs.

headline: Iran says it and Oman have agreed coordinates for safe transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said Iran and Oman, as coastal states, agreed the geographical coordinates of safe transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz and how to present the agreement internationally. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK RICS house price balance falls to -32% in September, weaker than the -30% expected and down from -28%
detail: The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors reports that downward pressure on house prices increased in September for the first time in four months. It said the prospect of higher interest rates weighed on the housing market.

headline: KPMG/REC survey shows UK permanent staff placements rising at their fastest pace in four years in September
detail: The KPMG/REC survey of recruitment firms, published on Thursday, shows more signs of the UK labour market recovering from its long slowdown in September.

headline: US oil futures rise more than 2% to $90.07 a barrel on storm and shipping supply risks
detail: US crude futures gained more than 2% to $90.07 a barrel in early trading on worries about the storm and shipping supply. The US National Hurricane Center had earlier said Isaias had strengthened into a hurricane.

headline: BoJ regional report finds firms passing on higher costs and some raising prices more often
detail: In its regional economic report, the Bank of Japan said firms in many regions are passing on higher costs from the Middle East conflict, the weak yen and labour, and many are keeping wage offers high. It also said strong global AI-related demand is lifting output.

headline: German trade surplus narrows to 19.5bn, above 19bn forecast; exports fall 0.8% m/m against a forecast 0.9% rise
detail: Germany's seasonally adjusted trade balance came in at 19.5bn, compared with a forecast of 19bn and 21.3bn previously. Exports fell 0.8% m/m, the same as the previous month. Imports rose 0.9%, short of the 2.8% forecast, after a 5.7% fall previously.

headline: ECB's Sleijpen describes the energy shock as fairly persistent
detail: ECB Governing Council member Olaf Sleijpen said the energy price shock is proving persistent. No further detail or market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB's Moulin says euro area inflation is entirely energy-driven and sees no second-round effects
detail: ECB official Moulin said the ECB faces an inflationary shock, euro area inflation is 100% energy and second-round effects are not visible. He also said the geopolitical shock is feeding through into a financial shock.

headline: ECB's Wunsch says the case for raising the minimum reserve requirement is unclear and unconvincing
detail: ECB Governing Council member Pierre Wunsch questioned the reasoning behind raising banks' minimum reserve requirement. No market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB's Dolenc sees upside inflation risks from oil, gas, food and strong growth; steadier core offers some reassurance
detail: ECB Governing Council member Dolenc said inflation risks are tilted to the upside because of oil, gas, food and strong growth. He added that more stable core inflation gives some comfort that wider price pressures remain contained.

headline: SNB Vice Chairman Martin attributes the recent rise in Swiss inflation to oil products
detail: Swiss National Bank Vice Chairman Martin said the recent increase in Swiss inflation is due to oil products. He also said the Swiss franc has weakened recently but has stayed stable in real terms since 2020.

headline: Fed's Waller says more rate rises are needed, though they need not come at back-to-back meetings
detail: Fed Governor Waller said inflation is too high, pointing to the AI buildout and the continuing energy shock as persistent pressures, and that he expects further rises if data come in as expected. He also said inflation has been above target for nearly 5-1/2 years, putting expectations at risk, and called the September labour market solid and stable even though job creation slowed.

headline: BoE's Pill calls current price pressures concerning and says they must be tackled
detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said current price pressures are a concern and need to be addressed, according to a market newswire headline.

headline: BoE's Greene sees a material risk that some second-round inflation effects may develop
detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene warned of a material risk of second-round effects emerging, according to a market news feed on 8 October.

headline: ECB's Lane expects food prices to face upward pressure next year and says central banks should be believed on inflation returning to target
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said the ECB expects upward pressure on food prices over the next year. He also said central banks should be believed when they say inflation will return to target.

headline: Germany raises its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 1.3% from 0.5% and its 2027 forecast to 1.1% from 0.9%
detail: The German Economy Ministry more than doubled its 2026 growth forecast, citing a rally in manufacturing. It forecasts 2028 GDP growth of 0.6%.

headline: UK 10-year gilt yield rises to 5.515%, its highest since July 2007, up more than 6bp on the day
detail: The 10-year gilt yield reached 5.515%, its highest level since July 2007, after rising more than 6bp on the day.

headline: European Commission says Italy can use the national escape clause from EU fiscal rules for energy
detail: European Commission spokespeople said Italy may invoke the national escape clause in the EU fiscal rules to cover energy-related spending.

headline: Brent crude extends its rise to 5% on the day and trades above $105 a barrel
detail: Brent's gain widened to 5%, taking it above $105 a barrel. The blotter earlier reported it topping $101 after more attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: UK 20-year gilt yield reaches 6% for the first time since March 1998, up 7bp on the day
detail: A market news account reported that the UK 20-year gilt yield hit 6%, its first time at that level since March 1998, up 7bp on the day. The move came as the global bond sell-off continued.

headline: BoE's Greene says she is worried by the UK pay outlook, with employers on track for pay rises of about 3.5% next year
detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said on Thursday that pay rises of around 3.5% next year would be larger than is helpful for bringing inflation back to the 2% target, Reuters reports.

headline: ECB's Stournaras sees no significant second-round inflation effects and says inflation expectations remain anchored near 2%
detail: ECB Governing Council member Stournaras said he does not see important second-round effects. He also said inflation expectations are well anchored at around 2%.

headline: BoE survey shows UK lenders cut mortgage availability for the first time in three years
detail: A Bank of England survey released on Thursday shows that in the three months to the end of August, UK lenders reduced the supply of mortgages and other secured lending to households. It is the first such reduction in three years.

headline: UK announces sanctions on Russian oil companies and tankers
detail: The UK has imposed new sanctions on Russian oil companies and tankers. The report gave no further details.

headline: French 10-year yield rises above last week's high as other high-debt European bond yields climb with it
detail: An economist reports that France's 10-year government bond yield has moved past the previous high it set a week ago, with yields across other high-debt European countries also rising. No new yield level was given.

headline: ECB accounts say a 2.50% deposit rate is still within staff estimates of neutral and warn against guidance on the rate path
detail: The ECB's account of its latest policy meeting says officials thought it particularly important not to give guidance on future rates, wanted the policy response to stay proportionate and stressed continued vigilance. The account also says risks did not all point the same way and that monetary policy transmission has been smooth.

headline: French Finance Minister Lescure says the bond market is not dysfunctional
detail: France's finance minister said bond markets are not dysfunctioning, as French and other high-debt European government bond yields climb in a global sell-off.

headline: BoE's Bailey calls for more resilient core markets and says greater absorption of government debt has brought more fragility
detail: In a speech, the Bank of England Governor said central clearing, minimum haircuts and better risk management deserve consideration, and that monetary policy must stay firmly committed to bringing inflation back to target. He also said repeated shocks and higher government debt make it harder for governments to cushion a downturn, and warned of a shock if expectations for AI are sharply revised.

headline: BoE's Bailey says market moves are some way from normal but finds no illiquidity or stressed conditions
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said market movements are well away from normal. He added that the Bank is not seeing illiquidity or stressed conditions, as the global bond sell-off continues to hit gilts.

headline: BoE's Bailey sees subdued evidence so far of energy costs feeding wider inflation, but says risks grow the longer prices stay high
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said there was currently little evidence of higher energy costs passing through into broader inflation, but that risks remain. He added that inflation risks increase the longer high energy prices persist.

headline: BoE's Bailey says markets show an elevated risk premium and the Bank must test for a significant shock to inflation expectations
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey also said markets remain resilient and that he is fully committed to bringing inflation back to target.

headline: BoE's Bailey says fiscal policy must be credible and fiscal commitments matter more than ever after negative shocks
detail: The Bank of England Governor said fiscal policy must be credible and aimed at stability, and that fiscal commitments are needed most when negative shocks hit. He also said the Bank cannot be at all relaxed about large and concentrated market positions or the risk of wider disruption.

headline: WTO raises 2026 global goods trade forecast to 3.9% from 1.9% but cuts its services trade outlook
detail: The World Trade Organization now forecasts global goods trade growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 4.1% in 2027, up from a 1.9% estimate for 2026 in March, and global economic growth of 2.6% in 2026. It lowered its 2026 services trade forecast, citing disruption to transport and travel from the Middle East conflict.

headline: Riksbank Governor Thedéen says there are grounds for an interest rate increase
detail: Riksbank Governor Erik Thedéen said there are grounds for raising interest rates, according to a newswire headline. No further detail was given.

headline: EU reminded its primary dealers of their market-making obligations on Monday as bond volatility peaked, IFR reports
detail: IFR reports that the European Union contacted its primary dealers on Monday after extreme volatility led banks to cut their quoting to the minimum required, to limit potential losses.

headline: NatWest Markets quits European and US primary dealer roles but stays on as a gilt-edged market maker
detail: IFR reports that NatWest Markets is giving up its primary dealerships for six European sovereigns, the EU and the US following a review of its markets business. It will keep its UK role as a Gilt-Edged Market Maker.

headline: UK and EU agree to link their carbon emissions trading systems, Politico reports
detail: Politico reports that the UK and the EU have reached an agreement to link their emissions trading systems.

headline: US publishes its diesel executive order in the Federal Register
detail: The US administration has published the diesel executive order in the Federal Register. No further details of what the order contains were given.

headline: Forecasts put the UK energy price cap 16% higher for Q1 2027, Resolution Foundation says
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the latest forecasts show the Q1 2027 energy price cap 16% higher, approaching the peak levels capped in 2022 and 2023.

headline: Trump says the US will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections and reports productive talks with Tehran
detail: The US President said the US would not strike Iran ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November and described discussions with Iran as productive. The posts reported no market reaction.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says the ECB has tools to counter unwarranted market dynamics and is paying attention to markets
detail: ECB President Lagarde made the remarks to Euro Finance Chief. She also said she sees no sign that price rises are broadening.

headline: US $22bn 30-year bond auction tails by 0.1bp at 5.618%; bid-to-cover falls to 2.54
detail: The US Treasury's $22bn 30-year auction had a high yield of 5.618%, against 5.617% in when-issued trading and 5.308% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover was 2.54, down from 2.61, with indirect bidders taking 72.32%, directs 20.89% and primary dealers 6.79%.

headline: US sanctions 17 vessels for carrying Iranian crude, oil products and petrochemicals
detail: The US Treasury Department announced new Iran-related sanctions covering dozens of people, entities and vessels. A Treasury official said Iran has stopped loading and offloading crude vessels because of the US blockade and sanctions, and estimated that 20 million barrels of Iranian crude remain on vessels outside the blockade.

headline: US Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins rise to 1.3m b/d, or 63% of production, MMA data show
detail: Figures attributed to MMA put shut-in US Gulf oil output at 1.3m b/d, or 63% of the region's production. An earlier figure put shut-ins at 511,619 b/d, about 25% of output.

headline: Fed's Musalem says further policy firming will be needed to return inflation to target, sees rates rising in next 6 to 9 months
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said inflation is elevated, driven by persistent demand pressures and supply shocks, and that limiting second-round effects is key. He said his contacts are mostly worried about inflation rather than the job market, and that he goes into every meeting with an open mind.

headline: Oil prices surge as Houthis strike Riyadh for a second day and Iran steps up attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Semafor reports that Yemen's Houthis carried out missile strikes on the Saudi capital for a second day, while Iran increased the pace of its attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices were reported as surging; no figure was given.

headline: WTI crude futures settle 3.64% higher at $91.49 a barrel
detail: NYMEX November WTI crude futures settled up $3.21, or 3.64%, at $91.49 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.8829 a gallon.

headline: Brent crude futures settle 4.07% higher at $104.28 a barrel
detail: Brent crude futures closed the session up $4.08 at $104.28 a barrel, a gain of 4.07% on the day.

headline: European Commission rejects Italian and Greek requests for more fiscal rules flexibility to cover energy-driven inflation
detail: Reuters reports that the European Commission on Thursday turned down requests from Italy and Greece for extra fiscal leeway for euro zone governments over energy-driven inflation and support measures. The Commission said the rules could not be changed all the time.

headline: Heavy explosions reported in the southern Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian media blaming tankers hitting mines
detail: Iran's Fars news agency cites military sources as reporting heavy explosions in the southern Strait of Hormuz, which it says were caused by tankers striking mines. The inputs report no market reaction yet.

headline: German Bund futures rise 0.45% and French OAT futures 0.78% in Asian trading
detail: Euro area government bond futures gain in early Friday trading. Reuters reports that France's debt market has stabilised after its recent sell-off and that US yields have fallen.

headline: Japanese government bond yields fall, with 10-year down 5.5bp to 3.025%
detail: In Asian trading the 10-year JGB yield fell 5.5bp to 3.025%. The 5-year yield fell 4bp to 2.345% and the 30-year fell 6bp to 4.060%.

headline: UK retail footfall falls 2.9% in September, a steeper drop than August's 1.7% decline, BRC data show
detail: The British Retail Consortium's figures show total UK retail footfall fell 2.9% in September, compared with a 1.7% fall the previous month, City AM reports.

headline: China and EU reach understanding on hybrid vehicle trade and agree to manage trade disputes, China's commerce ministry says
detail: China's commerce ministry said the hybrid vehicle deal follows intensive negotiations and complies with WTO rules, and that talks will continue on price undertakings in the EU's anti-subsidy probe into Chinese electric vehicles. It also said China will keep looking at lowering tariffs on some goods under WTO rules, will keep speeding up rare earth and permanent magnet export licences to the EU, and that the two sides will hold their next regular meeting in March 2027.

headline: Yemeni government forces reportedly take control of Bab al-Mandeb, with Saudi envoy saying the strait is cleared of Houthis
detail: Saudi Arabia's ambassador to Yemen is reported as saying Houthi forces have been cleared from the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Separate reports say Yemeni government forces have taken control of Bab al-Mandeb and Mayun. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Bank of Spain lifts its 2026 inflation forecast to 3.9% and its 2027 forecast to 3.7% from 2.7%
detail: The Bank of Spain raised its 2026 growth forecast to 2.6% from 2.3% and its 2027 forecast to 2.2% from 1.7%. It expects a budget deficit of 2.6% in 2026 and public debt of 98.5% of GDP at the end of 2026, and named geopolitics, oil prices and rising bond yields as risks to the outlook.

headline: IMF says global government debt could reach 100% of GDP by 2028, a level not seen since World War II
detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said advanced economies are the largest contributors to the rise. She said it is unrealistic to count on stronger growth to reduce debt burdens.

headline: Germany to release up to 15m barrels of oil and petroleum products from reserves under the G7 stock release deal
detail: Germany's economy minister says diesel and heating oil will be released first, followed by crude oil. The minister also says Germany will fully implement the G7 agreement on releasing energy stocks.

headline: Canada sheds 68.3k jobs in September against a forecast 10k gain; unemployment rate rises to 6.5%
detail: Canadian employment fell by 68.3k in September after a 41.7k fall the previous month, and the jobless rate rose to 6.5% from 6.4%, in line with forecast. The participation rate slipped to 64.8%, while average hourly earnings growth picked up to 2.3% year on year, matching the forecast, from 2.0%.

headline: University of Michigan preliminary current conditions index falls to 44.7, short of the 50.1 forecast
detail: The preliminary University of Michigan current conditions reading for the US came in at 44.7. The forecast was 50.1 and the previous reading was 50.9.

headline: White House sets up committee to investigate allegations of false statements by Fed Governor Lisa Cook
detail: In a statement, the White House said President Trump has set up a committee of inquiry to look into allegations that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook made false statements.

headline: US Michigan sentiment drops to 46.3 in preliminary October reading, below 47.6 forecast; 1-year inflation expectations at 4.7%
detail: The University of Michigan's preliminary October sentiment index came in at 46.3, against a forecast of 47.6 and 48.1 previously, while the expectations index rose to 47.3 against a 45.7 forecast. One-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6% (forecast 4.8%), and five-year expectations rose to 3.5% from 3.4%, matching the forecast.

headline: Saudi Aramco to supply full contracted oil volumes to European customers in November
detail: A market commentary account reports that Saudi Aramco will deliver full oil volumes to its European customers for November. No further figures were given.

headline: US Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins climb to 1.5m b/d, or 72% of production, MMA data show
detail: MMA data show 1.5m b/d of US Gulf of Mexico oil output is now shut in, which is 72% of production. The previous reading was 1.3m b/d, or 63%.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says 2.5% is the top of neutral and the ECB is in a fairly comfortable position on rates
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said 2.5% marks the upper limit of the ECB's neutral range and that the European economy is relatively resilient to shocks.

headline: Trump says Russia will supply diesel to world markets after Putin call; US Treasury issues temporary licence to allow it
detail: After a call with President Putin, Trump said Russia will supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel immediately, another 500,000 tons in November and 1,000,000 tons after that, followed by 3,000,000 tons within a short period, depending on the condition of its refineries. The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control said it is issuing a temporary general licence, effective immediately, to allow Russian diesel to be supplied to the global market.

headline: S&P affirms UK sovereign rating at AA/A-1+ with a stable outlook
detail: S&P Global Ratings affirmed the UK's 'AA/A-1+' ratings with a stable outlook and raised its 2026 UK real GDP growth estimate to 1.3%, citing a stronger-than-expected first half. The agency said oil, gas and other input prices linked to the Middle East conflict, such as fertiliser, are affecting inflation and interest rates.

headline: Russia lifts diesel export restrictions with immediate effect and offers extra supply to the US and other partners, Novak says
detail: Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Moscow welcomes US steps to stabilise global energy markets and is ready to supply additional diesel to the US and all partners as early as October. He said exports should rise further in November and December as refineries return from maintenance, and that the domestic market will remain fully supplied.

headline: Saudi-led coalition launches wide-ranging operation against Houthi forces in Yemen, says 136 military targets destroyed
detail: The Saudi-led coalition says it is conducting a broad operation against Houthi capabilities in Yemen and has destroyed 136 military targets in areas the group controls. The inputs do not report any market reaction.

headline: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco facilities and Dammam airport in Saudi eastern province; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed
detail: Yemen's Houthis said on Sunday evening that they struck Aramco facilities and Dammam airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern province. Saudi civil aviation said Dammam airport was targeted and damage is being assessed, and the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a drone in the eastern province; there was no immediate Saudi confirmation of any hit on Aramco sites.

headline: IFS says Chancellor Healey may need about £36bn in tax rises or welfare cuts to cover the inflation hit and the defence pledge
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says higher inflation could force the Chancellor to top up department budgets by as much as £35bn by the end of the decade. Reuters reports the think tank put the tax rises or welfare cuts needed in his first Budget to offset the inflation hit to public services and meet a defence spending pledge at £36bn.

headline: Brent and WTI futures fall more than $2 a barrel in early Asian trading on prospect of more Russian oil supply
detail: A market newswire reported that Brent and WTI crude futures fell by more than $2 a barrel in early Monday trading, citing pressure from potential increases in Russian supply.

headline: Trump says there is an energy ceasefire in the Russia-Ukraine conflict; crude prices fall, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that US President Trump has said an energy ceasefire is in place in the Ukraine conflict, and that crude oil prices fell on the news. No price levels were given and no confirmation from Moscow or Kyiv was reported.

headline: IFS Green Budget says Chancellor's fiscal headroom may be bigger than expected but flags spending pressures before the Budget
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies has published its 2026 Green Budget, produced with Barclays. It finds that Chancellor John Healey's fiscal headroom could be larger than many expect, and it names spending pressures as a key challenge for the Budget.

headline: EU foreign ministers adopt almost 1,600 new sanctions listings on Russia's military-industrial complex
detail: The EU's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, says EU foreign ministers have just approved nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings aimed at Russia's military-industrial complex.

headline: French debt worries drive busiest euro-dollar options trading since mid-March, IFR reports
detail: IFR reports $213bn notional of euro-dollar FX options traded in the week to October 2, the busiest period since mid-March. Risk reversals show downside euro protection at its highest premium since mid-2024.

headline: Kremlin says it is ready to halt strikes for Ukraine's election day, Tass reports
detail: Russian state news agency Tass reports the Kremlin as saying it is prepared to pause strikes on Ukraine for the day of the Ukrainian election. The inputs do not report any market reaction.

headline: Kremlin's Peskov says Ukraine wants a 60-day ceasefire to regroup and keep fighting rather than to hold elections
detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Ukraine is seeking a 60-day ceasefire so it can recover and carry on the war, not so it can hold elections, according to reports. The Kremlin has separately said it is ready to suspend strikes on Ukraine's election day.

headline: Kremlin rejects Zelensky's proposed 60-day ceasefire and says it wants a broader peace agreement instead
detail: The Kremlin turned down the 60-day truce proposed by Ukraine's president and said it wants a wider peace agreement. Putin's offer to halt Russian attacks on the day of Ukraine's presidential election still stands.

headline: UK PM's spokesman says the Brexit deal left the UK worse off and the country can do much better
detail: The Prime Minister's spokesman made the remarks on the UK's relationship with the EU on 12 October. He also said Russia had tried and failed to influence the Brexit vote.

headline: Iran offers to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis after attacks on the kingdom, NYT reports
detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi made the offer to his Saudi counterpart Faisal bin Farhan in a phone call on Sunday night, according to a statement from his office. The statement said the region's overlapping conflicts had no military solution.

headline: Iran to reply through mediators to the US proposal on Hormuz as talks remain stalled
detail: Iran has assessed Washington's Hormuz proposal and plans to send its response through mediators, according to a market news report. Negotiations remain stuck over Tehran's terms and US expectations on the nuclear issue.

headline: Germany's Merz rules out the US-Russia diesel deal for Germany and says sanctions on Russia must be tightened
detail: German Chancellor Merz said the diesel arrangement between the US and Russia is not an option for Germany and called for tighter sanctions.

headline: Germany's Merz says electricity tax will be cut to the EU minimum for everyone, funded from room in the budget
detail: German Chancellor Merz said his CDU party wants electricity tax lowered for all users to the minimum level allowed under EU rules. He said the cut would be paid for from room in the German budget.

headline: OPEC lowers its 2026 oil demand growth forecast to 400,000 b/d and expects pent-up demand in 2027
detail: OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al Ghais said on Monday that the group has cut its forecast for oil demand growth this year to 400,000 barrels per day, from 1.4m b/d at the start of the year, Reuters reports. He said the cut reflects how the year has developed and that OPEC expects pent-up demand in 2027.

headline: Global bond sell-off eases, with yields lower across markets except France, economist Robin Brooks says
detail: Economist Robin Brooks says the global bond sell-off has calmed today, with yields falling everywhere except in France. No figures were given.

headline: European Commission to set out possible trade defence measures on China in December, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports the European Commission plans to present potential trade defence steps in December to reduce its trade deficit with China and its reliance on China for critical supplies. The report follows the EU-China deal on car imports.

headline: ECB's Stournaras says the ECB may keep raising rates gradually
detail: ECB Governing Council member Yannis Stournaras said on Monday that the ECB may stay on a path of gradual rate increases.

headline: Poland's Wrochna expects an IEA agreement on releasing fuel stocks on Thursday
detail: Polish official Wojciech Wrochna said he expects the International Energy Agency to reach a deal on Thursday to release fuel stocks.

headline: BoE's Mann says conditions are in place for possible wage-price drift
detail: Bank of England MPC member Catherine Mann said conditions are in place for possible drift in wages and prices, according to a market news account. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready for an energy truce but doubts whether Putin is
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Kyiv is prepared to agree an energy truce with Russia, while expressing uncertainty about whether President Putin is willing. The remarks follow Trump's statement that there is an energy ceasefire in the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

headline: EU's Kallas welcomes Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire and urges US to impose sanctions on Russia
detail: The EU foreign policy chief welcomed the announced energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine. She called for a wider end to the fighting and urged the US to impose sanctions on Russia.

headline: Zelensky says Russia carried out no attacks on energy targets overnight
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky reported no Russian attacks on energy infrastructure overnight, after the announcement of an energy ceasefire. He also repeated that Ukraine is ready for an energy truce.

headline: Saudi Arabia reports a new barrage of incoming missile and drone fire; Riyadh airport stays closed for now
detail: Saudi Arabia said on Monday it was facing fresh incoming fire, Reuters reports. The attacks follow Saturday's deadly missile strike on a Riyadh airport departure terminal, which Yemen's Houthis claimed.

headline: Europe faces at least another year of high gas prices as storage falls to record lows, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that European households and industry face high gas prices for at least another year because storage reserves are at record lows and will need restocking. It says this holds even if the Iran war is resolved and the winter is mild.

headline: Iran's IRGC says it hit a third supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz in two days, setting it on fire
detail: The IRGC Navy said the tanker was struck this morning and caught fire after it disabled its navigation system and ignored warnings while trying to leave the strait, Fars News reports. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: China's Wang Yi says Beijing will cooperate with Russia to protect key shipping lanes
detail: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said China will work with Russia to safeguard key shipping lanes. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Zelensky says it is increasingly clear Russia will not accept the US proposal for an energy ceasefire
detail: Ukraine's president said Russia appears unwilling to accept the US-proposed energy ceasefire.

headline: Fitch says France's 2027 budget plan points to a weaker fiscal starting point
detail: Fitch Ratings said France's rating is held back by high and rising debt, political and social conditions that make fiscal consolidation difficult, and low potential growth.

headline: Zelensky says Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities on Monday
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Russia hit six energy facilities in Ukraine on Monday. He also said Russia appears unwilling to accept the US proposal for an energy ceasefire.

headline: Trump defends his Russia energy decision and says the EU has paid Russia $250bn for energy
detail: In a social media post, the US President said his decision on Russian energy was the right one for Americans and claimed the European Union had paid Russia 250 billion dollars for energy. This follows his earlier announcement that Russia would supply diesel to world markets.

headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says trade talks with the US are making progress
detail: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on 12 October that trade negotiations with the United States are advancing. She gave no further details.

headline: Riksbank's Bunge says Sweden's economy is showing a long-awaited upturn
detail: Riksbank policymaker Bunge said the Swedish economy is showing a long-awaited upturn. No figures or market reaction were reported.

headline: UK PM Burnham says Iran's IRGC very likely directed RAF Fairford incident and pledges further sanctions on Iran
detail: Speaking in the Commons, Prime Minister Burnham said the RAF Fairford incident was highly likely coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the IRGC, and that the UK will bring further sanctions against Iran and the IRGC. He also said the UK will meet its NATO commitments in full and that he welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.

headline: UK PM Burnham says EU deals will add the equivalent of £10bn a year to UK GDP by 2040 as he seeks closer EU ties
detail: In the House of Commons, the Prime Minister said the UK-EU summit offers a chance to make progress on growth and to raise UK concerns about 'Made in Europe', and that he will work to secure an EU-UK deal. He said public opinion backs a pragmatic approach to post-Brexit options; some MPs booed as he argued for closer ties.

headline: EU's Kallas proposes 100 new sanctions listings on Russian interference networks and says pressure on Moscow should not ease
detail: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the EU is proposing 100 new sanctions listings aimed at Russia's foreign information manipulation and interference infrastructure. She also said now is not the time to ease pressure on Moscow, and that a ceasefire cannot work if only one side honours it.

headline: Iran's foreign ministry rejects US claims that energy shipments are moving freely through the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Baqaei disputed US claims that energy cargoes are passing freely through the Strait of Hormuz, Press TV reported.

headline: UK summons Iran's ambassador, Foreign Secretary Miliband says
detail: UK Foreign Secretary David Miliband says the government has summoned Iran's ambassador. This follows the Prime Minister's earlier statement linking Iran's IRGC to the RAF Fairford incident.

headline: EU's Kallas says 60 countries have signed a declaration backing freedom of navigation
detail: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says 60 countries have issued a declaration calling for freedom of navigation to be preserved. On Russia, she also said pressure on Moscow rather than concessions is the quickest way to end the war.

headline: More than 25 countries, including the US, back UK's attribution of Iranian involvement in RAF Fairford incident
detail: The UK Foreign Office has issued a joint statement signed by more than 25 countries, including the US, recognising Britain's finding that Iran was involved in the incident at RAF Fairford. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK PM Burnham says the UK is ready to consider further Saudi requests for support
detail: UK Prime Minister Burnham said the government would consider further requests for support from Saudi Arabia, which has come under missile and drone attacks. He also said he would not let the two-state solution die while he is in office.

headline: UK PM Burnham says Britain will take the toughest line on Russia sanctions in response to Trump's diesel deal
detail: Asked about the US-Russia diesel arrangement, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK will always pursue the strongest sanctions approach on Russia and hopes other countries will follow its lead.

headline: Fitch's base case is a durable deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in the first quarter of 2027
detail: The rating agency Fitch said its central scenario assumes some form of lasting agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is reached in 1Q27.

headline: Iranian parliamentary security committee reviews a Strait of Hormuz bill, which will go to the full parliament soon
detail: Tasnim News reports an Iranian member of parliament as saying the National Security Committee has reviewed the Strait of Hormuz bill. The MP said it will soon be sent to parliament for debate.

headline: Turkey's Erdogan condemns Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia and says Turkey stands with the kingdom
detail: Turkish President Erdogan condemned the Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, which included the airport, in the strongest terms and said Turkey stands by Riyadh. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US, Australia, Canada and other allies call any Iranian bid to threaten or coerce people on their territory unacceptable
detail: A joint statement from the US, Australia, Canada and other governments says any Iranian attempt to threaten, intimidate or harm people on their territories, including through proxies, is unacceptable.

headline: Mortgage-related hedging adds selling pressure to US Treasuries as long-term yields climb, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that the sharp rise in long-term US Treasury yields has set off mortgage-related hedging, which adds to selling in an already strained bond market. The report says the effect is probably smaller than in earlier sell-offs.

headline: Iran's ambassador to the UK denies any Iranian role in suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford
detail: Iran's ambassador rejected UK claims of Iranian involvement in the RAF Fairford incident, according to Iranian state news agency IRNA. The denial follows the UK summoning the ambassador and the government's pledge of further sanctions on Iran.

headline: Iran's ambassador to the UK says Tehran is willing to cooperate with Britain on investigating the RAF Fairford incident
detail: Iran's ambassador to the UK offered cooperation with the British investigation, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported. The offer follows the UK summoning the ambassador after it said Iran was involved in the suspected plot.

headline: US Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins ease to 604,503 b/d, or 30% of output, from 1.5m b/d; 25% of gas output remains shut
detail: The latest MMA data show 604,503 b/d of US Gulf of Mexico oil production shut in, equal to 30% of output, down from the 1.5m b/d reported earlier. Gas shut-ins stand at 531 mln cf/d, or 25% of gas production.

headline: Fed's Hammack says US interest rates need to go higher
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said interest rates need to be higher, according to a Barron's report. No figures or timing were given.

headline: Fed's Hammack says inflation is still too high and the economy needs more tightness, with an inflationary mindset the biggest risk
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack added that she is keeping an open mind on the right timing. These remarks follow her earlier comment that US interest rates need to go higher.

headline: UK PM Burnham tells MPs a summit with EU leaders will be held on 20 November and calls his approach to the EU pragmatic
detail: Prime Minister Andy Burnham gave the summit date in the Commons on Monday. City AM reports that two weeks earlier he had suggested he could look at a full return to the EU.

headline: Germany's stability council expects the debt-to-GDP ratio to rise to 78.25% in 2030
detail: The council, which coordinates Germany's federal and state finances, published the projection on Monday, Reuters reports.

headline: Fed's Hammack puts trend inflation in the mid-to-high 2% range and favours smaller but quicker rate moves
detail: In prepared remarks, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said policy needs to be restrictive to bring inflation back to 2%, that financial conditions are neutral and that it will take some time to reach the target. She said demand pressures, including from AI, are broad and not self-correcting, and that business contacts describe conditions as generally strong to booming.

headline: OPEC+ ministers meet on the sidelines of a conference in Riyadh, according to a statement
detail: A statement says OPEC+ ministers met on the sidelines of the Riyadh conference. The post gave no details of any decisions.

headline: OPEC+ ministers say disrupted energy flows have driven shipping and insurance costs to unprecedented levels
detail: In a statement after their meeting in Riyadh, OPEC+ ministers stressed the need to protect international maritime passages so that energy keeps flowing. They said the current disruption to energy flows has pushed shipping and insurance costs to unprecedented levels.

headline: Fed's Hammack calls Treasury yields modest by historical standards and says the neutral rate is likely higher
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said current Treasury rates are modest by historic standards and the neutral rate is probably higher, though hard to pin down. She added that a return to 3% home mortgage rates would probably mean something had gone wrong in the economy.

headline: Iran's Major General Razaei calls US response to Tehran's conditions for ending the war inadequate
detail: Iranian Major General Razaei said the US response to Iran's conditions for ending the war falls short. He also said Iran will not go back to the way it conducted diplomacy in the past.

headline: Fed's Hammack says she sees early warning signs of a possible problem with inflation expectations
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said the economy needs to be cooled at the margins. She added that higher interest rates would not deter hyperscalers but could affect firms in other industries.

headline: Fed's Hammack says the question now is how quickly to tighten policy, but she does not want to put jobs at risk
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said further restraint is needed and the issue for the Fed is the pace of tightening. She added that she does not want rates to hit the economy radically or threaten the employment side of the Fed's mandate.

headline: Fed's Hammack calls for more restraint and warns market conditions could shift if policy is not acted on
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said further monetary restraint is needed and that her FOMC projection for the neutral rate is one of the higher ones. She also said low-income workers have moved from trading down to choosing which bills to pay.

headline: OPEC+ ministers stress protection of international sea passages to keep energy flowing
detail: OPEC+ ministers who met on the sidelines of the Riyadh conference said in a statement that protecting international maritime passages matters for keeping energy supplies moving.

headline: Fed's Hammack says business contacts report strong conditions, but low-income workers are struggling to pay bills
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said her business contacts describe activity as generally strong to booming. She said low-income workers first spoke of trading down and are now deciding which bills to pay.

headline: Bank of France keeps its estimate for French third-quarter growth at 0.1%
detail: The Bank of France estimates French GDP growth of 0.1% in the third quarter, the same as its previous estimate.

headline: ECB's Moulin says the French economy is withstanding the energy shock as the Bank of France's industry uncertainty gauge hits highest…
detail: Bank of France Governor and ECB Governing Council member Moulin said the French economy is holding up in the face of the energy shock. He said the central bank's gauge of industry uncertainty is at its highest level since April.

headline: Saudi energy minister says the kingdom is looking to lift pipeline crude export capacity to as much as 10m b/d
detail: Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said on Monday that Saudi Arabia plans to repurpose a domestic gas pipeline and invest in its existing East-West network to raise pipeline crude export capacity to up to 10 million barrels a day, Reuters reports.

headline: Russia's Novak confirms government-level talks with the US on diesel supply and says Russia can send more diesel to global markets
detail: Russian Deputy PM Novak said extra Russian diesel would partly rebalance supply and demand, and that diesel exports could reach 3-3.5 million tons by the end of the year. He also said Russia has supplied $21.3bn of energy to the EU so far this year.

headline: WTI crude futures settle 2.06% higher at $93.74 a barrel
detail: NYMEX November WTI crude futures settled up $1.89 at $93.74 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.7232 a gallon and gasoline at $3.2917 a gallon.

headline: Russia's Novak says Russia has supplied $21.3bn of energy to the EU this year and OPEC+ discussed rising transport costs
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak put Russian energy supplies to the EU this year at $21.3bn. He said OPEC+ had discussed transportation costs, which he said have risen significantly.

headline: Russia's Novak says Russian companies are in talks with buyers over diesel sales
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on 12 October that Russian companies are discussing diesel sales with buyers. He had earlier confirmed government-level talks with the US on diesel supply.

headline: EU considers a bloc-wide windfall profit tax on oil and gas companies as energy prices climb
detail: On Monday the EU's tax commissioner told Reuters the bloc is looking at a windfall profit tax on oil and gas firms across the EU. Governments are looking for money to help households with high energy bills.

headline: Russia's foreign minister rejects a proposed 60-day Ukraine ceasefire and says Moscow wants a long-term peace deal
detail: Russia's foreign minister turned down a proposed 60-day ceasefire that would have let Ukraine hold elections. He said Moscow wants a long-term peace agreement, not a temporary truce.

headline: US envoy Kushner says the diesel deal with Russia is meant to soften Moscow's stance
detail: US envoy Jared Kushner described the US-Russia diesel supply arrangement as an attempt to soften Russia. The deal has already drawn UK pledges of tougher Russia sanctions, and Trump has defended it.

headline: Trump says Zelensky and Putin need to meet and bring the war to an end
detail: US President Trump called for the Ukrainian and Russian leaders to meet to end the war. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump criticises the Houthis' conduct after their attack on Saudi Arabia
detail: US President Trump said the Houthis are behaving very badly. He gave no details of any US response, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says Russia and Ukraine have both committed ceasefire violations and that he told both sides to agree a ceasefire
detail: The US President said both Russia and Ukraine had committed violations and that he had told both to agree to a ceasefire. He added that he thinks both sides want a deal but do not know how to reach one.

headline: Trump says Putin is keener on a deal than Zelensky and the US must get Ukraine's leader to agree one
detail: US President Trump said Putin wants to reach a deal more than Zelensky does, and that Zelensky has to concentrate on making one. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Oil prices rise as the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire agreed by Trump with Putin shows signs of fraying, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that oil prices are climbing as the energy ceasefire comes under strain. Trump announced the ceasefire after a deal with Putin. The report gives no price figures.

headline: Fed's Hammack says inflation pressures are spreading beyond AI and she is open to adjusting the pace of rate rises
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said further tightening is needed and policy will have to curb demand through capital spending or consumption, but that she is open to adjusting the pace of increases. She added that inflation pressures are spreading beyond AI firms and that business contacts describe a thriving economy rather than one about to slow.

headline: BRC: UK September like-for-like retail sales rise 1.0% y/y, above the 0.7% forecast; total sales up 1.3%
detail: The British Retail Consortium reports that total UK retail sales rose 1.3% year on year in September, up from 0.7% in August. Like-for-like sales grew 1.0%, against a 0.7% forecast and 0.5% previously.

headline: RBA minutes show unanimous backing for a 25bp hike after members weighed a hold
detail: Minutes from the Reserve Bank of Australia show members unanimously supported a 25bp rate increase after considering holding, with falling home values among the factors discussed. Members said inflation pressures had materialised or gained momentum since August, that acting promptly was important to keep expectations anchored, that Middle East tensions had pushed oil well above forecast assumptions, and that the neutral rate may have risen.

headline: Barclays: UK consumer spending grows 2.0% y/y in September, slightly below August's 2.1%
detail: Barclays reports that UK consumer card spending rose 2.0% year on year in September, compared with 2.1% in August.

headline: Japan's September corporate goods prices rise 6.8% y/y, below the 7.6% poll; down 0.3% on the month
detail: Bank of Japan data show the domestic corporate goods price index rose 6.8% year on year in September, below the 7.6% poll and down from 7.6%, and fell 0.3% month on month against an expected 0.5% rise. Outstanding bank loans grew 5.3% year on year, from 5.4%.

headline: Trump says he believes both Putin and Zelensky support an energy ceasefire
detail: The US president said he thinks both the Russian and Ukrainian leaders support an energy ceasefire, and repeated that the two need to meet and end the war.

headline: IMF projects UK inflation as second-highest in G7 over next two years; says UK stands out for starting fiscal consolidation
detail: In its latest World Economic Outlook, the IMF projects that UK inflation will be the second-highest of any G7 economy over the next two years, City AM reports. IMF chief economist Tenreyro said the UK stands out in the G7 because it has begun fiscal consolidation.

headline: IMF raises 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% from 3.0% and warns top economies face their biggest deficits since Covid
detail: The IMF's World Economic Outlook says AI investment is offsetting energy-price shocks. It keeps its 2027 global forecast at 3.4% and sees advanced-economy growth at 2.1% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027. The Fund calls for urgent action to rebuild public finances, and chief economist Tenreyro urges highly indebted countries to start fiscal consolidation.

headline: South Korea's President Lee says interest rates may have to rise
detail: South Korea's president said the country may need to raise interest rates. The KOSPI index was reported down 6% in heavy selling on the same morning.

headline: BoE's Greene says the MPC must act before second-round inflation effects set in and calls UK policy still relatively accommodative
detail: MPC member Megan Greene said the risk of acting too late on inflation outweighs the risk of raising rates too early, and that the latest IMF outlook for the UK was not a surprise.

headline: IMF chief economist Tenreyro says the UK should keep to its deficit reduction plans
detail: IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro made the remarks as the Fund published its updated World Economic Outlook at its annual meetings in Bangkok.

headline: IMF warns against market complacency, naming an AI-led selloff and rising government bond yields as risks
detail: The IMF named a reversal in AI-related investment, rising government bond yields and cyberattacks as threats to financial markets, and its officials said an AI correction could hit the real economy by eroding wealth.

headline: BoJ survey shows Japanese households expect prices to rise 11.8% on average over the next year, with a 10% median
detail: The figures come from the Bank of Japan's household survey on expected price changes over the year ahead.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says core inflation is gradually nearing 2% and the BoJ is watching the bond market closely
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said inflation needs to stay anchored around the 2% target and that long-term bond yields are normally set by markets and reflect several factors.

headline: Dutch CPI rises 3.4% y/y in September, in line with forecast and up from 3.3%; 0.1% m/m
detail: Dutch consumer prices rose 3.4% on the year, matching the 3.4% forecast, after 3.3% previously. On the month, prices rose 0.1%, down from 0.3% before.

headline: Dollar slips in Asian trade as oil prices ease and bond yields stabilise
detail: Reuters reports that the dollar fell in Asian trading on Tuesday, after a holiday in some US markets, as bond yields and oil prices eased and global stocks slid. The report gives no figures.

headline: IMF expects the BoJ to lift rates gradually towards neutral despite a projected slowdown in Japanese growth
detail: The International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday that the Bank of Japan is likely to raise interest rates step by step towards a neutral setting, even though it expects Japan's growth to slow, Reuters reports.

headline: Banking regulators step up scrutiny of AI risks amid financial stability concerns, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters cites six people familiar with the matter as saying banking watchdogs are increasing efforts to contain AI-related risks. Some of the sources pointed to possible cyberattacks on banks or rogue AI agents as threats to global financial stability.

headline: German final CPI confirmed at 3.3% y/y and 0.6% m/m, both in line with forecasts
detail: Germany's final consumer price index reading shows inflation at 3.3% year on year, matching both the forecast and the previous figure of 3.3%. The monthly rise is 0.6%, also in line with the forecast and the previous reading.

headline: German September harmonised CPI is 3.3% y/y and 0.6% m/m, both matching forecasts and the previous readings
detail: Germany's EU-harmonised consumer price index for September rose 3.3% on the year and 0.6% on the month. Both figures matched the 3.3% and 0.6% estimates and were unchanged from the previous readings.

headline: US government bond funds take in almost $14bn since start of October after record $59.3bn Q3 inflows, FT says
detail: FT calculations using EPFR data show almost $14bn of inflows into US government bond funds so far in October. This follows record net inflows of $59.3bn in the third quarter.

headline: EU's von der Leyen condemns escalation in the Black Sea as a new front in Russia's war in Ukraine, calling it unacceptable
detail: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the Black Sea as another front of escalation in Russia's war in Ukraine and called it unacceptable. No market reaction was reported.

headline: IMF 2026 forecasts put UK growth joint-2nd fastest in G7 on annual average, but 6th of 7 per capita
detail: Based on the IMF's 2026 forecasts, the UK ranks joint-2nd in the G7 for annual average GDP growth, 3rd on a Q4/Q4 basis and 6th of 7 for per capita growth. A separate headline reports that UK growth has been upgraded but that energy prices and interest rates will weigh in 2027.

headline: Fed's Waller says AI could help widen GDP per capita
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said artificial intelligence could add to growth in GDP per capita. The report gave no remarks on the rate outlook.

headline: Fed's Waller links the level of real yields to the effect of real growth
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said real yields are being driven by real economic growth. No market reaction was reported in the inputs.

headline: Fed's Waller says US government bonds no longer carry a safety premium
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said the safety premium on US government bonds has disappeared. No market reaction was reported in the post.

headline: Fed's Waller says higher yields are partly doing the Fed's job and that Trump threatens Fed independence but is not succeeding
detail: In further remarks, Federal Reserve Governor Waller said rising bond yields were doing some of the Fed's tightening work. He also said President Trump poses a threat to Fed independence but has not succeeded so far, and that he trusts Congress and the courts to protect it.

headline: Resolution Foundation publishes its UK Budget preview report, titled 'Hitting the buffers'
detail: The Resolution Foundation released its Budget preview and is holding a launch event this morning. Its summary points to higher inflation from the Middle East conflict and to a retreat from sovereign debt that has raised borrowing costs.

headline: BoJ reportedly unlikely to raise rates again at its October meeting
detail: A market newswire post reports that the Bank of Japan is unlikely to raise interest rates again in October. No source or further detail was given.

headline: IMF's UK growth upgrade of 0.5ppts is the joint largest in the G7, alongside Germany, Resolution Foundation notes
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the UK economy has grown faster than forecast this year, and that the IMF's upgrade to UK growth this morning was 0.5 percentage points. It says only Germany received an upgrade as large among G7 economies.

headline: Chancellor will not lift capital gains tax to match income tax rates, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK Chancellor has ruled out raising capital gains tax to the same level as income tax ahead of the Budget.

headline: Zelensky says Ukraine has not struck Russian energy facilities for two days
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Ukraine has carried out no strikes on Russian energy targets for two days, amid the running US-brokered energy ceasefire story. He also said allies had not given warning of Russia's latest missile strike.

headline: German 5-year Bobl auction sells at 3.22% yield, down from 3.28%, with bid-to-cover of 1.1 against 1.2 previously
detail: The German 5-year Bobl auction gave an average yield of 3.22%, compared with 3.28% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.1, down from 1.2.

headline: Kremlin says contacts continue on Trump's energy ceasefire and sees no link between the US diesel deal and its Ukraine peace stance
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said Moscow still has nothing to say about what Trump called an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, but contacts on it are ongoing. He called European criticism of the US-Russia diesel deal cynical because EU states actively buy Russian oil, and said Russia will keep selling energy on global markets.

headline: ECB opposes Finland's proposal to give bank supervisors a growth objective
detail: The European Central Bank has criticised a Finnish proposal that would require banking supervisors to target economic growth, according to a market news headline.

headline: Kremlin says EU sanctions could obstruct the US-Russia fuel deal and it has no knowledge of Trump plan to halt intelligence for Kyiv
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said EU sanctions and other EU measures could hinder implementation of the fuel agreement between Russia and the US. He also said the Kremlin was not aware of plans by Trump to stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine.

headline: BoK's Shin says the won has strengthened markedly on tighter policy and sees room for further gains
detail: Bank of Korea Governor Shin said the won has risen substantially because of tighter policy and that there is more scope for it to appreciate. He also said the BoK will review how its K-dot plot system has worked, with the review due next year or later.

headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says intelligence-sharing cooperation with the US is continuing
detail: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha said Ukraine is still cooperating with the US on intelligence sharing. Earlier, the Kremlin said it had no knowledge of a Trump plan to halt intelligence for Kyiv.

headline: US NFIB small business optimism index falls to 97.9, below the 98.2 forecast and down from 98.7
detail: The NFIB small business optimism index for the US came in at 97.9. That was below the forecast of 98.2 and the previous reading of 98.7.

headline: BofA October fund manager survey names a disorderly rise in bond yields as the biggest tail risk to markets
detail: In BofA's October Fund Manager Survey, investors rank a disorderly rise in bond yields as the top tail risk, ahead of an AI bubble. They say a 5.9% 10-year Treasury yield would lead them to shift allocation from stocks to bonds, and a net 1% expect high long-term rates. A net 4% now expect the global economy to weaken over the next 12 months.

headline: Brent and WTI crude futures drop 2%
detail: A market commentator reports that Brent and WTI crude futures are both down 2% in Tuesday morning trade in Europe. No price levels were given.

headline: Resolution Foundation says the Chancellor's fiscal headroom has halved to £12bn ahead of the Budget
detail: The Resolution Foundation published new analysis estimating that headroom has halved to £12 billion. It says the Chancellor must weigh support for struggling families against rebuilding confidence in the public finances at the Budget.

headline: Germany's Merz calls for an immediate end to Iranian and Houthi naval blockades after a call with Saudi crown prince
detail: The German government said Chancellor Merz spoke by phone with the Saudi crown prince about Houthi attacks, including on Riyadh airport, the Middle East situation and the effect on energy prices. The statement also said Iran must enter serious negotiations and stop destabilising the region.

headline: NIESR analysis says UK long-term gilt yields are likely to stay elevated near 5% even if the Iran war ends soon
detail: The National Institute of Economic and Social Research has published a Market Anatomy report on this year's rise in gilt yields. It says higher borrowing costs are likely to persist, leaving the UK public finances more exposed.

headline: UK energy secretary Miliband approves drilling off the Falklands, Telegraph reports
detail: The Telegraph reports that the energy secretary has given approval for drilling in waters off the Falkland Islands.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says AI is an inflation problem, Semafor reports
detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee described AI as a source of inflation pressure, according to Semafor.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says inflation must show progress before the Fed can return to its earlier rate-cutting path
detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee told Semafor that the Fed needs to see some progress before it can resume the rate-cutting path it had been on. In the same interview he said the AI boom is beginning to push prices up.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee voices concern that tariffs and oil prices could lead to stagflation
detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said he is concerned that tariffs and oil could produce stagflation, according to a newswire headline. This adds to his earlier remarks on Tuesday about inflation and the Fed's rate path.

headline: Retrofit industry warns over reported plan to cut heat pump subsidies to fund defence in the autumn Budget
detail: Inside Housing reports that retrofit industry leaders have warned of serious harm to households after reports that the government could reduce heat pump subsidies in the autumn Budget to pay for defence spending.

headline: Russia's Putin and UAE president discuss the US diesel deal by phone
detail: Putin held a phone call with the President of the UAE in which they covered the diesel deal with the US, bilateral cooperation and peace in the Middle East.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK growth beat forecasts in the first half of 2026 but the Middle East conflict has worsened the near-term…
detail: The Resolution Foundation made the point in material from its Budget preview. It said UK growth in the first half of 2026 came in ahead of forecasts, and that the Middle East conflict has weakened the short-term outlook.

headline: Saudi-led coalition says it will soon tell civilians to evacuate a site in Sanaa, Yemen, ahead of a special operation
detail: A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition said civilians at a site in the Yemeni capital Sanaa would shortly be warned to evacuate ahead of a planned special operation. The warning follows the Houthis' attack on Saudi Arabia. No market reaction was reported.

headline: OPEC lifts 2027 oil demand growth forecast to 2.55m bpd and cuts its 2026 forecast to 180,000 bpd
detail: In its monthly report, OPEC raised its 2027 forecast for global oil demand growth to 2.55 million bpd from 2.36 million bpd. It cut the 2026 forecast to 180,000 bpd from 380,000 bpd.

headline: Saudi Arabia tells OPEC its crude output rose to 8.372m bpd in September, recovering from a three-decade low
detail: Saudi Arabia reported to OPEC that it produced 8.372 million bpd of crude in September, up from 6.238 million bpd in August. OPEC said OPEC+ crude output, including former member UAE, averaged 39.07 million bpd in September, up about 900,000 bpd from August.

headline: Iran's oil ministry says it has finished major repairs to war damage at the South Pars gas field, according to reports from Iran
detail: Reports from Iran attribute the statement to the head of the oil ministry. They say the major repairs to war damage at the South Pars gas field are complete.

headline: Argentina asks an international tribunal for provisional measures to stop the UK exploiting hydrocarbons off the Falklands
detail: In a statement, Argentina's government said it had asked an international tribunal for provisional measures to stop the UK exploiting hydrocarbons on a continental shelf around the Falklands. The move follows reports that the UK energy secretary has approved drilling off the islands.

headline: BoK's Shin says policy will stay restrictive until the bank is confident inflation will return to its 2% target
detail: Bank of Korea Governor Hyun Song Shin welcomed further gains in the won, saying they would support household purchasing power. He said policy will remain restrictive until the bank is confident inflation is heading back to 2%.

headline: Hassett says the market trusts the new Fed chair and a slowdown in inflation could give the Fed a reason to hold
detail: Kevin Hassett said markets have confidence in the incoming Fed chair. He also said the Fed may treat slowing inflation as grounds for holding rates.

headline: Houthis warn Saudi Arabia that any attack on Sanaa will bring a harsh response against Riyadh
detail: A spokesperson for Yemen's Houthis said any Saudi strike on the capital, Sanaa, would be met with retaliation against the Saudi capital, Riyadh. The warning follows the Saudi-led coalition's statement that it will soon tell civilians to evacuate a site in Sanaa.

headline: US ADP weekly data shows private employers added an average of 24,750 jobs a week in the four weeks to 26 September
detail: ADP's weekly employment measure showed an average gain of 24,750 US private-sector jobs a week in the four weeks to 26 September, up from 23,750 in the previous reading.

headline: Saudi-led coalition names Yemeni Oil Company site in Sanaa as the location civilians must evacuate
detail: A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition's Joint Forces Command asked civilians to leave the Yemeni Oil Company site at Al-Sabaha Central Station in Sanaa, citing their safety. This follows the coalition's earlier statement that it would soon issue an evacuation call ahead of a special operation.

headline: Turkey's Erdogan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in a call with the Saudi crown prince and pledges support
detail: The Turkish presidency says President Erdogan told the Saudi crown prince by phone that Turkey condemns the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the strongest terms. He also said Turkey will keep standing by Saudi Arabia.

headline: Houthis declare Saudi Aramco facilities legitimate targets and tell nearby workers and residents to evacuate
