detail: Yemen's Houthi armed forces told employees and civilians near any Saudi Aramco oil facility to leave the area, saying the sites are legitimate targets for their forces. Separately, the US issued a notice advising its citizens to reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia.

headline: Retailers urge Chancellor Healey to cut high street taxes at Downing Street meeting; no Budget measures confirmed
detail: City AM reports that bosses from Tesco, Sainsbury's and Marks & Spencer pressed the Chancellor on business rates and youth unemployment at a meeting on Tuesday. The Chancellor did not confirm any Budget measures.

headline: Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will also reduce fiscal headroom at the upcoming Budget
detail: The Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will also eat into the Chancellor's fiscal headroom at the forthcoming Budget. The point comes from its Budget preview, which put the headroom at £12bn, half its previous level.

headline: Zelensky says intelligence support from partners has stopped during overnight attacks on Ukraine
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said intelligence support from partners has stopped while night-time attacks continue. Earlier, Ukraine's foreign minister had said intelligence sharing with the US was continuing, and the Kremlin said it knew nothing of a reported Trump plan to halt intelligence for Kyiv.

headline: Fitch says the jump in bond yields adds to the strain on developed market public finances
detail: Fitch Ratings said the surge in government bond yields makes the challenges facing developed market public finances harder. No figures were given in the report.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK 10-year gilt yields are the highest among rich countries
detail: In its Budget preview, the Resolution Foundation said this year's global rise in borrowing costs has also hit the UK. It said UK 10-year government bond yields are now the highest of any rich country.

headline: Explosions reported in Sanaa after Saudi-led coalition warning; Houthis say the targeted oil company station holds no fuel
detail: There are reports of explosions in Sanaa, Yemen. They follow the Saudi-led coalition's order for civilians to evacuate a Yemeni Oil Company site. The Houthis cited an oil company source as saying its As Sabah station is empty of petroleum products and has no military value.

headline: Warplanes reportedly strike oil company facilities west of Sanaa; Houthis say they are fighting Saudi forces attacking the capital
detail: Reports say warplanes bombed oil company facilities west of Sanaa, following the Saudi-led coalition's evacuation warning. The Houthis say their forces are confronting Saudi attacks on the Yemeni capital.

headline: US existing home sales come in at 3.99m, above the 3.95m forecast
detail: US existing home sales were 3.99m, against a forecast of 3.95m. The previous reading of 3.98m was revised to 3.93m.

headline: UK defence secretary Streeting says the MoD must end its culture of overspending and live within its means
detail: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the Ministry of Defence cannot have a culture of overspending and has a responsibility to stay within its budget. No specific spending measures were announced.

headline: Saudi cabinet, chaired by the crown prince, says the Houthis will face consequences for repeated attacks on the kingdom
detail: Saudi state news agency reports the cabinet statement after the Houthis' attacks on Saudi Arabia. No market reaction is reported.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK household energy bills are set to rise again in January
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the increase will come in the first quarter, when 46% of domestic gas use takes place.

headline: India's foreign minister says Indian and US officials are resolving issues in trade deal talks and progress is positive
detail: India's external affairs minister said Indian and US officials are working through outstanding issues in their trade deal negotiations, which he described as moving in the right direction.

headline: Pimco's Ivascyn says US Treasury yields have not yet peaked and sees the Fed holding this month, with 1 to 2 more hikes this cycle
detail: Pimco's chief investment officer Dan Ivascyn also said long-dated Treasuries can absorb further Fed tightening. He said spillover risks are greatest in rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and commercial real estate.

headline: Trump says the US has not stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine
detail: The US president said the US is still sharing intelligence with Ukraine and wants the war to end. Earlier, Ukraine's president had said intelligence support from partners stopped during overnight attacks.

headline: Trump says diesel from the Russia deal will go to the world market rather than to the US
detail: The US president made the remarks about the US-Russia diesel deal. Separately, Republican senators are reported to be urging him to withdraw from the Russian oil deal.

headline: US 6-month bills sell at 4.2% and 3-month bills at 4.085%, both higher than the previous auctions
detail: The US sold $82bn of 6-month bills at a high yield of 4.2%, against 4.165% previously, with bid-to-cover of 2.76 against 2.79. It also sold $95bn of 3-month bills at 4.085%, against 4.05%, with bid-to-cover of 2.68 against 2.51.

headline: Trump says he spoke to the Saudi crown prince, may ask Turkey to join a Yemen response and will decide on Iran soon
detail: Speaking to reporters, the US president criticised the Houthis' conduct but would not say whether he had made a decision on them, and said a decision on Iran would come very soon. He also said the US is working with Russia and Ukraine to end the war and will say later whether Russia broke the ceasefire.

headline: Trump says Yemen's Houthis are behaving very badly as fallout from the US-Iran war spreads across the region
detail: Reuters reported that US President Trump made the comments about the Houthi militants who control much of Yemen on Tuesday. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Fitch says fiscal paths of Western European sovereigns are still diverging
detail: Fitch Ratings published a commentary saying that the fiscal trajectories of Western European sovereigns are continuing to diverge. The post did not give any country-level figures.

headline: Netanyahu discussed possibly resuming the war on Iran with Trump last week, Israeli TV reports
detail: Israel's N12 News reports that Netanyahu and Trump spoke last week about possibly resuming the war against Iran. It also reports that senior US officials were impressed by Netanyahu's apparent interest in resuming attacks before the elections.

headline: US EPA proposes making larger refiners blend more biofuels over the next two years
detail: Reuters reports that the US Environmental Protection Agency on Tuesday proposed fully reallocating refinery biofuel exemptions, which would require larger refiners to blend more biofuels over the next two years.

headline: US VP Vance says the Defense Production Act is being used to expand a Texas refinery
detail: US Vice President Vance said the administration is using the Defense Production Act to expand refining capacity in Texas. No further details were given in the report.

headline: Fed's Barkin says the 2% inflation target can be reached
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said in remarks on Tuesday that the 2% inflation goal can be hit.

headline: Houthi political council head says Bab al-Mandeb shipping is safe and calls an end to Saudi attacks the easiest solution
detail: Fars News reports that Mahdi al-Mashat, chairman of Yemen's Houthi-run Supreme Political Council, said shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait is safe and the Houthis are meeting their international obligations. In separate reported remarks, he said the easiest way to resolve the crisis is for Saudi Arabia to end its attacks on Yemen and its siege.

headline: IRGC Navy commander threatens to sink US ships that approach the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian reports say
detail: Iranian reports quote Rear Admiral Azmaei, commander of the IRGC Navy, as saying Iran is waiting for American ships to approach the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz so that it can sink them. He also challenged the US to come closer if it believes the strait is open.

headline: OPEC+ oil output rises sharply in September, led by Saudi Arabia, despite Hormuz disruption
detail: OPEC reported on Tuesday a sharp gain in OPEC+ production in September, driven by higher Saudi output, even though the Iran war continues to disrupt shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. No aggregate figure was given in the report.

headline: Zelensky says Ukraine has sent the US proposals for further talks and is ready to meet in the coming days
detail: Ukraine's president said his team has sent the US side proposals for possible next meetings and further talks.

headline: IRGC says missiles fired from Iranian islands towards ships it calls offending vessels in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say missiles were fired from Iranian islands towards ships in the Strait of Hormuz that they described as offending. This follows an earlier IRGC Navy threat to sink US ships approaching the strait. The post did not report any market reaction.

headline: Iran summons UK ambassador over claims linking Tehran to a suspected plot against RAF Fairford
detail: Iran's foreign ministry says it summoned the UK ambassador over accusations that Tehran was linked to a suspected plot against the Fairford air base in Britain.

headline: Netanyahu's office denies he is urging Trump to attack Iran before the elections
detail: Israel's N12 News reports that the Israeli prime minister's office has denied claims that Netanyahu is pressing Trump to strike Iran before the elections. The same outlet quotes a US official as saying Washington is continuing to increase pressure on Iran.

headline: Fed's Barkin says the effect of AI investment can be seen in US inflation
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the impact of AI investment is visible in US inflation, according to remarks reported on Tuesday.

headline: Iran's acting oil minister says South Pars gas capacity is coming back faster
detail: Iran's acting oil minister said capacity at the South Pars gas field is returning at a faster pace, Mehr News reports. This follows earlier Iranian reports that major repairs to war damage at the field had been finished.

headline: Saudi-led coalition confirms it struck an oil facility in Sanaa it says the Houthis used to support their attacks
detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it attacked the site because the Houthis used it to support drones and missiles that threaten Saudi Arabia and Red Sea ports and shipping. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran threatens to reconsider its relations with the UK and asks for evidence linking it to the Fairford incident
detail: Iran's Fars news agency reports that Tehran has threatened to seriously reconsider its ties with the UK. Iran has also asked the UK for evidence of any Iranian links to the suspected plot against RAF Fairford.

headline: Saudi civil defence warns of possible danger in the Eastern Province
detail: Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority has issued an alert about possible danger in the kingdom's Eastern Province. The alert follows Houthi statements that Saudi Aramco facilities are legitimate targets. It gave no further details.

headline: Fed's Barkin says inflation is clearly proving persistent and that taking action makes sense
detail: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said US inflation is clearly enduring and that it makes sense to act. This follows his earlier remarks on AI investment and on reaching the 2% target.

headline: Fed's Williams says one more rate hike this year is appropriate but sees no need for a hike in 2027 at this stage
detail: New York Fed President Williams said the September hike was rooted in risk management, that the economy is not overheating, and that disinflationary forces are still at work. He said the labour market is not adding to inflation, he sees no broad price pressure beyond AI and energy, and AI is the inflation driver he is watching most closely.

headline: Fed's Barkin says economic shocks are clearly still coming
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin made the remark at an event at Howard University, which has now ended. He also said again that acting on inflation makes sense.

headline: Saudi statement says the danger in the Eastern Province has passed
detail: A Saudi statement says the danger in the kingdom's Eastern Province is over. It follows an earlier civil defence warning of possible danger in the region and Houthi threats against Saudi Aramco facilities. No market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB's Lane says a rise in long-term interest rates amounts to a material tightening relevant to policy setting
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said higher long-term rates represent a material tightening of conditions, which the ECB takes into account when setting its policy stance.

headline: ECB's Lane says AI's potential to replace some workers could weaken their bargaining power and moderate wage growth
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said the possibility of AI displacing some workers may reduce their bargaining power, which could moderate wage growth. The remarks follow his earlier comments on long-term interest rates.

headline: Loud explosions reported in Dhahran near Saudi Aramco headquarters, according to six sources
detail: Six sources report hearing loud explosions in Dhahran, close to Saudi Aramco's headquarters. The cause has not been confirmed, and no market reaction has been reported so far.

headline: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missiles fired at Dhahran and Dammam; Saudi Arabia warns of aerial threat to Riyadh
detail: The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Dhahran and Dammam in the Eastern Province, and that interception debris fell on a residential area in Dhahran. Saudi Arabia separately warned of a possible hostile aerial threat to Riyadh.

headline: Saudi civil defence says the threat to Riyadh has passed after the earlier aerial threat warning
detail: Saudi civil defence says the danger over Riyadh has lifted. This follows its earlier warning of an aerial threat to the capital during Houthi missile attacks on the kingdom.

headline: Iranian crude exports remain at zero in October under the US blockade, Vortexa data shows
detail: Energy intelligence platform Vortexa says Iran's crude exports have stayed at zero in October after falling sharply in the second week of September, Reuters reports.

headline: PM Burnham and the Chancellor hold roundtables with business leaders, giving reassurance on tax ahead of the Budget
detail: The prime minister and the chancellor hosted roundtable meetings with senior business figures ahead of the Budget, with Burnham presenting himself as pro-business on tax, the FT reports. No specific measures were reported.

headline: UKMTO reports a container ship and a tanker hit by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz in two separate incidents
detail: UKMTO said a verified source reported a container ship hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, then received a further report of a tanker being struck there minutes later. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted three missiles and two drones over Riyadh and the southern region
detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three missiles and two drones in the Riyadh region and the south of the kingdom. This follows the Houthi warning that any attack on Sanaa would bring a response against Riyadh.

headline: Trump accuses Iran-backed Houthis of deliberately trying to push up oil prices before the US midterms
detail: The Financial Times reports Trump's accusation alongside its report of Saudi-led coalition strikes on Houthi targets in Sanaa.

headline: IMF cuts its 2026 Gulf growth forecasts and now sees Middle East and North Africa as the only region to shrink this year
detail: Semafor reports that the IMF has lowered its 2026 growth forecasts across the Gulf states.

headline: Fed's Collins says elevated inflation risk is the Fed's main focus and expects inflation to stay above 2% on high energy prices
detail: Boston Fed President Collins said the risk of high inflation is the Fed's main focus at present and that she expects inflation to remain above 2% because of high energy prices. She said the path of policy in the new year will depend on the data.

headline: BoE's Bailey says second-round inflation effects in the UK have been subdued so far but get harder the longer the shock lasts
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said second-round effects have so far been subdued in the UK. He added that the longer an inflation hit persists, the harder it becomes to deal with.

headline: Fed's Collins expects the Fed to raise rates a bit further by year-end and says she backed the September hike
detail: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said tighter policy will help return inflation to 2% and that the path of policy in the new year will depend on the data. She described the US job market as broadly balanced, said the economy has been resilient to shocks and said the data-centre build-out is adding pressure to inflation readings.

headline: RBNZ is to start buying back April 2027 New Zealand government bonds
detail: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand will begin repurchases of the April 2027 government bond.

headline: US Treasury fines Bank of America $1.2bn over money laundering and sanctions failures, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the US Treasury fined Bank of America for money laundering and sanctions violations after concluding it did not properly report more than $5bn of suspicious transactions. One report puts the fine at $1.2bn.

headline: BoE's Bailey backs Warsh's view that forward guidance went too far and notes the UK's budget profile shows a falling deficit
detail: In further remarks on Tuesday evening, Bank of England Governor Bailey also said leveraged finance is now far more widespread. He repeated that the energy shock gets harder to handle the longer it lasts.

headline: US Treasury's OFAC agrees $11.66m settlement with Bank of America over 475 apparent sanctions violations
detail: The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control said on its website that Bank of America is settling potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations. The violations relate to sanctions programmes covering Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia and narcotics.

headline: Fed's Collins says she is watching how broad inflation pressures are in the data and takes a holistic view of the economy
detail: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said she is looking at the economy as a whole when considering the future path of rate policy, and is monitoring the breadth of inflation pressures in incoming data.

headline: Fed's Collins says economic uncertainty is elevated
detail: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said in further remarks that the level of economic uncertainty is elevated.

headline: Saudi Aramco headquarters in Dhahran is reported hit during Tuesday's Houthi attacks
detail: A market news account reports that Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters was hit during Tuesday's Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The reports came after earlier accounts of explosions near the site. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Fed's Collins says officials know that higher rates can cause difficulties
detail: Boston Fed President Collins said policymakers are aware that higher interest rates can create challenges. She made the remark in further comments on Tuesday.

headline: Saudi Aramco headquarters is evacuated after missile attacks from Yemen, Iranian media report
detail: Iranian media report that Saudi Aramco's headquarters was evacuated after missile attacks launched from Yemen. This follows earlier reports on Tuesday that the Dhahran headquarters had been hit.

headline: US CENTCOM says US forces helped Gulf partners move more than 19 million barrels of crude through the strait yesterday
detail: US Central Command says US forces helped Gulf partners ship more than 19 million barrels of crude oil through the strait on Monday.

headline: Fed's Collins says the Fed is not rethinking its 2% inflation target and its models take account of government debt levels
detail: Boston Fed President Collins says the Fed is not reconsidering its 2% inflation target. She also says the Fed's economic models take account of government debt levels.

headline: Israeli TV reports no intelligence change justifying an Israeli-US move against Iran in the coming weeks
detail: Israel's N12 News reports that Israel, the US and Gulf states are coordinating and preparing for a range of scenarios, but that no intelligence change justifies a joint Israeli-US move in the coming weeks. The channel also reports that Iran has carried out several ballistic missile tests in recent days, which the Israeli army describes as a slow and only partial restoration of its missile capability.

headline: US retail diesel averages $6.28 a gallon on Tuesday, little changed after Trump's Russia diesel announcement
detail: US retail diesel prices averaged $6.28 per gallon on Tuesday, slightly above Friday's level and below September's record of $6.53 per gallon. The figure shows the announcement has had limited immediate effect on prices.

headline: Saudi energy ministry says the attack on an Aramco building in Dhahran caused a limited fire and no casualties
detail: Saudi state news agency, citing an energy ministry official, says Tuesday's attack on the Aramco building in Dhahran caused a limited fire and no casualties.

headline: UK plans fresh Russia sanctions and more support for Ukraine to push Moscow into joining Trump's energy ceasefire
detail: The UK is reported to be seeking to pressure Russia into joining the energy ceasefire proposed by Trump, with new sanctions on Russia and increased support for Ukraine planned.

headline: Houthi official threatens new attacks on Saudi oil and other key installations tonight
detail: In a post on X, a Houthi official said Saudi oil and vital installations would be targeted tonight, following Tuesday's attacks on Dhahran.

headline: Fed Governor Cook's lawyer challenges Trump's latest attempt to remove her and questions the White House probe
detail: Reuters reports that a letter from Fed Governor Lisa Cook's lawyer, seen on Tuesday, disputes the objectivity of a White House investigation into mortgage fraud allegations against her. The letter responds to President Trump's latest attempt to remove her from the Fed.

headline: BoE's Bailey says UK companies are concentrating hard on holding down costs as Iran war lifts energy prices
detail: BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said British firms are focusing closely on containing costs during the energy price surge caused by the Iran war, Reuters reported.

headline: China's September CPI rises 0.9% y/y, below the 1.0% poll, while PPI climbs 5.0% y/y, above forecasts
detail: China's CPI rose 0.2% m/m against a 0.3% forecast, with core CPI unchanged at 1.0% y/y. PPI rose 5.0% y/y against forecasts of 4.4% to 4.5% and a previous 3.8%, and rose 1.2% m/m.

headline: Deloitte survey finds large UK firms expect inflation and interest rates to rise over the next year
detail: The Deloitte survey, published on Wednesday, found big British companies are focusing more on cutting costs. It comes two weeks before Chancellor John Healey's first Budget.

headline: Chancellor Healey plans to make online marketplaces collect tax owed by sellers on their platforms, Times reports
detail: The Times reported that the government plans to make platforms such as Amazon, eBay and Temu responsible for collecting tax owed by retailers selling through them, as part of a tax crackdown.

headline: Iran is using new tactics to step up attacks on Hormuz shipping before the US midterms, senior Iranian officials say
detail: Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Iran aims to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections by targeting ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: China's September exports rise 29.6% y/y and imports 24.6% y/y in yuan terms, with goods trade topping CNY5tn for the first time
detail: Chinese customs data show September goods trade of CNY5.16 trillion, up 27.5% y/y. Exports were CNY3.03 trillion and imports CNY2.13 trillion; January to September exports rose 16.4% and imports 22.3%. The customs vice minister said geopolitical conflicts and other global uncertainties cloud the full-year outlook.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says energy explains most but not all of the rise in inflation and second-round effects have not emerged so far
detail: ECB President Lagarde said the ECB cannot wait for signals to become obvious and is monitoring the wage increases expected through collective bargaining in Europe.

headline: IMF urges advanced economies to cut deficits and debt urgently, citing higher bond yields and rising debt-service costs
detail: The IMF warned that delaying fiscal consolidation would make it harder and called on countries to strengthen their public finances before markets force them to. An IMF official also said a combination of corporate, inheritance and capital gains taxes could be preferable to a wealth tax.

headline: Singapore's central bank leaves monetary policy unchanged, against analysts' expectations
detail: The Monetary Authority of Singapore kept its settings on hold on Wednesday and expects growth and inflation to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.

headline: IMF does not recommend that the UK speed up its fiscal consolidation
detail: The IMF said it is not recommending that the UK accelerate its fiscal consolidation efforts. Earlier, the IMF had urged advanced economies to cut deficits and debt urgently.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says the ECB must act before risks fully emerge and is watching wage bargaining for early signals
detail: ECB President Lagarde said policymakers are monitoring collective bargaining for early signs of wage growth, that France's debt problems must be addressed mainly through French fiscal policy, and that 1.1% eurozone growth in 2026 is not bad. She also said she has no plans to run for the French presidency.

headline: China's September exports rise 36.3% y/y in dollar terms, beating the 25.5% poll; trade surplus is $133.53bn
detail: Chinese customs data show a September trade surplus of $133.53bn against a poll estimate of $118.1bn, including a $34.01bn surplus with the US. The customs vice minister said the export outlook for the fourth quarter is unchanged.

headline: China's September crude imports slip to 37.10m tonnes from 37.93m tonnes in August
detail: Chinese customs data show January to September crude imports of 357.97m tonnes, down from 422.61m tonnes a year earlier. September natural gas imports rose to 10.86m tonnes from 10.33m tonnes in August.

headline: Chancellor Healey is set to pay for Budget giveaways without extra borrowing, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Healey plans to fund the giveaways in the upcoming Budget without adding to government borrowing.

headline: IMF's Georgieva says UK debt-curbing steps have improved growth prospects and many countries may need a cautiously hawkish policy stance
detail: At a press conference in Bangkok, the IMF Managing Director said advanced economies have done worst at rebuilding buffers since the pandemic and that debt-service costs are rising as interest rates go up. She also pointed to rising yields across the euro area, said countries can still borrow in markets but at higher cost, and called for further fiscal adjustment in the US.

headline: ECB's Wunsch says the ECB is likely to raise interest rates again
detail: ECB Governing Council member Wunsch said a further ECB rate rise is likely.

headline: ECB's Moulin says Middle East conflict and energy are the main drivers of inflation and expectations remain well anchored
detail: The Bank of France governor said higher yields may weigh on demand and call for a more moderate policy response to the inflation shock. He also said France must urgently show it is committed to fiscal consolidation and pass its 2027 budget.

headline: IMF's Georgieva says the US cannot rely on growth to reduce its debt and needs further fiscal adjustment
detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday that US growth alone will not shrink mounting public debt, and that other fiscal measures are needed to put it on a more sustainable path, Reuters reports.

headline: ECB's Moulin says the ECB focuses on inflation and stays out of individual countries' fiscal matters
detail: Asked about the French budget, ECB official Moulin said the central bank concentrates on inflation and does not get involved in the fiscal affairs of specific member states.

headline: Japanese banks and insurers return to domestic bonds as JGB yields surge, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that Japanese banks and insurers are buying domestic government bonds again as yields climb. Investors are watching for signs that Japanese institutions are starting to bring capital home from overseas.

headline: German wholesale prices rise 8.7% y/y in September, up from 6.8% in August
detail: German wholesale prices rose 1.9% m/m in September, compared with 0.9% the previous month. The annual rate climbed to 8.7% from 6.8%.

headline: Swedish CPI holds at 1.1% y/y in September, in line with forecasts; CPIF steady at 1.5%
detail: Swedish CPI and CPIF both rose 0.9% m/m, matching estimates. CPIF excluding energy was 0.5% y/y, and household consumption growth slowed to 3.5% y/y from 4.0%.

headline: Zelenskiy says Russia's latest attack shows Moscow does not take the US president's statements seriously
detail: Ukraine's president made the comment after a Russian attack, as the US pushes Moscow to join an energy ceasefire.

headline: BoE's Pill says markets may be overpricing the chance of four rate hikes in the next 12 months
detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said market pricing of four rate increases over the coming 12 months may be overdone. No market reaction was reported in the input.

headline: India's September wholesale price inflation climbs to 11.39% y/y, above the 10.60% forecast
detail: India's wholesale price index rose 11.39% y/y in September, up from 9.92% in August and above the 10.60% estimate. The output PPI also rose 11.39% y/y, up from 9.81% previously.

headline: Oil prices rise on Wednesday after two vessels are hit in Hormuz and Iran says it is using new tactics against shipping
detail: Reuters reports that oil prices climbed on Wednesday after two ships were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian officials said they were using new tactics to target vessels. No size for the price move was given.

headline: Eurozone bond yields fall ahead of US CPI data and bond auctions
detail: Eurozone government bond yields were reported lower on Wednesday morning, ahead of the US CPI release and upcoming auctions. No figures were given for the size of the move.

headline: Oman says Hormuz discussions cannot be completed without US-Iran talks
detail: Oman said that whether discussions on the Strait of Hormuz can be completed depends on talks between the US and Iran.

headline: Italy's Meloni says a deal with the EU on limiting the effect of gas costs on electricity prices is close
detail: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Italy sees an agreement with the EU nearing on measures to reduce how much gas costs feed through to electricity prices. No details of the measures or timing were given.

headline: Italy's Meloni calls the US-Russia diesel deal very risky and says the EU needs a seat in Russia-Ukraine talks
detail: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the US-Russia diesel deal works against efforts to bring Putin to the negotiating table with Ukraine. She also said the EU needs a representative in negotiations on the war.

headline: Germany plans to press the EU to cap additional imports from China
detail: A market newswire reports that Germany will push the EU to put caps on additional Chinese imports. No market reaction was reported.

headline: IEA now sees 2026 world oil demand down 2.6m bpd and supply down 5.8m bpd, both slightly steeper than it forecast before
detail: In its monthly report, the IEA put 2026 supply at 1.73m bpd below demand (previously 1.74m bpd) and sees 2027 supply 3.94m bpd above demand (previously 3.73m bpd), citing disruption from the Iran war and very high prices. It said tight middle distillate supply will last well into 2027 and that the latest wave of attacks puts September's recovery in Middle East oil exports at risk.

headline: German economy ministry says the economy's momentum probably slowed temporarily in the third quarter
detail: Germany's economy ministry gave the assessment in its monthly report, published on Wednesday.

headline: ECB's Elderson says banks and supervisors must look beyond data-driven models to deal with non-linear climate and nature risks
detail: The ECB Executive Board member called for scenario analysis and stronger risk management frameworks. He said uncertainty also comes from demographics, AI and quantum computing.

headline: German economy ministry sees little short-term support from domestic demand and a subdued industrial outlook
detail: Germany's economy ministry says weaker purchasing power from higher energy prices, uncertainty and financing costs mean the domestic economy is unlikely to add much momentum in the short term. It also says the outlook for industrial activity remains subdued.

headline: Yemen's Houthi forces say they will announce a military operation deep inside Saudi territory
detail: Houthi armed forces say they will announce a 'qualitative' military operation deep inside Saudi Arabia at 11:40 AM. The statement follows Tuesday's Houthi attacks, which included a reported hit on Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters.

headline: IFS launches its Green Budget 2026 ahead of the Budget
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies began its live launch of the Green Budget 2026 on Wednesday morning, with presentations from IFS authors and Barclays. The report is funded by the Nuffield Foundation.

headline: European Commission proposes delaying EU methane rules on imported oil and gas by one year
detail: The European Commission has proposed postponing by one year the EU methane emissions rules that apply to imported oil and gas.

headline: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco in Dhahran, a Riyadh Aramco refinery and King Khalid Airport, and say attacks will continue
detail: A Houthi military spokesperson said the group targeted Aramco facilities in Dhahran, an Aramco refinery in Riyadh and King Khalid Airport. The group said its operations against airports and oil facilities will continue in the coming days.

headline: China buys 8-10 US soybean cargoes, its first such deals since the Trump-Xi summit, Reuters reports
detail: Chinese state buyers bought 8-10 Panamax cargoes of US soybeans this week, three trade sources told Reuters. These are the first such purchases since the September summit in Washington between Presidents Trump and Xi.

headline: Trump is considering revisiting US intelligence sharing with Ukraine, Semafor reports
detail: Semafor reports that the White House is actively discussing intelligence sharing with Ukraine. It says CIA Director Ratcliffe is opposed to halting it.

headline: UK 4-year gilt auction yields 4.945% with bid-to-cover of 3.415
detail: The 4-year gilt auction had an average yield of 4.945%, up from 4.786% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover was 3.415, compared with 3.237 last time.

headline: IEA says tight diesel supplies could last well into 2027
detail: In its monthly oil market report, the International Energy Agency said diesel shortages could last well into next year. It said large stock drawdowns at a time of year when stocks usually build, together with limited production, come just before peak winter demand.

headline: German 30-year Bund auction yields 3.8% with bid-to-cover of 1.4, down from 1.6 last time
detail: Germany's 30-year Bund auction has an average yield of 3.8%, the same as at the previous sale. Its bid-to-cover ratio is 1.4, compared with 1.6 last time.

headline: Israel's Netanyahu says he opposes a pre-emptive attack on Iran for now, ahead of the elections, reports say
detail: Reports say the Israeli prime minister told IDF Radio that a pre-emptive strike on Iran before the elections would not suit Israel at present. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Fed's Bowman sees no urgency for further rate action and says the Fed can wait and assess conditions
detail: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said there was no immediate need for more moves on rates. She said the Fed could wait and assess conditions before acting again.

headline: Kremlin says the terms of Trump's proposed energy ceasefire have not been set out and work is continuing
detail: The Kremlin said the provisions of the energy ceasefire proposed by the US president remain unclear and that work on it is in progress. It also accused European countries of acting to prolong the war in Ukraine while US negotiators pursue a peace settlement.

headline: Russia restarts diesel exports from Primorsk after the US temporarily eases sanctions under the Trump deal
detail: Russia has resumed diesel shipments from its Baltic port of Primorsk, with a 40,000-ton tanker heading to Morocco. Moscow expects its exports to reach 3-3.5 million tons a month by the end of the year.

headline: Fed's Bowman says the Fed is planning a full reorganisation to fix the risk-averse culture seen in the SVB collapse
detail: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said work is under way on a complete reorganisation to address the culture problems that surfaced during the Silicon Valley Bank failure.

headline: Saudi shares fall after the attack on an Aramco building while other Gulf markets trade mixed
detail: Reuters reports Saudi stocks fell in early trade on Wednesday after the attack on a Saudi Aramco site added to concerns over the escalating conflict between the kingdom and Yemen's Houthis. Other major Gulf markets were mixed.

headline: Russia's Novak says Russia and the US are discussing diesel contracts and a US diesel supply deal is in sight
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak made the remarks, according to TASS and Interfax. Russia remains under sanctions.

headline: Russia's Novak expects oil output to recover and says OPEC+ capacity assessment report is due late 2026
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak also said the fuel oil market is improving and some Russian refineries have finished maintenance, TASS and Interfax report.

headline: Russia's Novak says US diesel contract will include a mechanism to keep supplies flowing despite Western sanctions
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia and the US are negotiating to finalise a diesel contract. He said the contract will include a mechanism to secure supplies despite Western sanctions.

headline: European Commission warns of a very difficult winter, with high energy prices and an affordability crisis
detail: A European Commission spokesperson says the EU faces high energy prices, an affordability crisis and a very volatile, unpredictable outlook this winter.

headline: Aramco's Dhahran headquarters reported extensively damaged in Tuesday's attack, though sources say operations continue normally
detail: According to sources, fire spread across several floors of the Dhahran headquarters. Aramco has told staff to work from home and has moved some operations to its offices abroad, and sources say operations are continuing normally.

headline: Fed's Williams sees no need for further rate hikes in 2027 while markets still price three
detail: Reuters reports that New York Fed President John Williams does not see a need for more rate hikes in 2027. Markets are still pricing three Fed hikes.

headline: Putin's envoy Dmitriev says Russia will keep up economic cooperation with the US beyond diesel
detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Russia's economic cooperation with the United States would continue and would not be limited to diesel. The remark follows reports that Russia and the US are discussing diesel supply contracts.

headline: Houthis claim to have driven Saudi forces out of Bab al-Mandab and Dhubab airport
detail: A Houthi spokesperson says Saudi forces have been expelled from the Bab al-Mandab area and Dhubab airport, with vehicles burned or captured and personnel taken prisoner. The spokesperson says footage will be released at 4 PM on 14 October.

headline: PM Burnham pledges to bring down the UK welfare bill
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said on 14 October that the government will reduce welfare spending. He gave no figures or timetable.

headline: Russia's Novak says US diesel deal lets Russia raise output and refining, with supplies going to world markets and the US
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said the Russia-US diesel deal gives Russia room to increase its production and refining volumes. He said supplies will go both to global markets and directly to the United States.

headline: PM Burnham says at PMQs that his priority on the Trump-Russia diesel deal is to build bridges, ahead of meeting Zelenskiy
detail: At Prime Minister's Questions, Prime Minister Burnham was asked about the US-Russia diesel deal and said his job is to bring people back together. He also said Ukraine's President Zelenskiy would not leave their meeting empty-handed.

headline: German foreign minister calls for a ceasefire for civilian shipping in the Black Sea and expects US support for Ukraine to continue
detail: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany does not see a substantial cut in US support for Ukraine and that the US is right to push for Russia-Ukraine talks. He also called for a ceasefire covering civilian shipping in the Black Sea.

headline: Russia's Novak says first diesel export shipments are under way and exports could reach 3.5m tonnes a month by year-end
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak said the first diesel export cargoes are under way and that Russian and US companies are already negotiating contracts for diesel supplies to the US, Tass reported. Tass also reported that Russia could raise diesel exports to 3.5m tonnes a month by the end of the year.

headline: EU's Dombrovskis says trade with China must be rebalanced in other sectors after the hybrid car deal
detail: European Economic Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said on Wednesday that the deal to halve Chinese hybrid car imports into Europe must be followed by rebalancing in other sectors and better EU access to the Chinese market, Reuters reports.

headline: ECB's Simkus says recent data point to a possible need for more tightening, with no clear second-round effects so far
detail: ECB Governing Council member Simkus said recent data suggest further tightening may be required, and that second-round effects are not yet evident. He added that French yields are rising because of economic developments, that he sees no role for the ECB in France at present, and that discussing minimum reserve requirements is not wrong.

headline: Oman, Russia and China are mediating ceasefire talks with the Houthis, an official tells AP
detail: AP reports an official as saying Oman, Russia and China are mediating ceasefire talks with Yemen's Houthis, who have been attacking Saudi targets including Aramco sites.

headline: Container ship and dry bulk ship reported sinking near Strait of Hormuz after being hit by projectiles
detail: Maritime security sources say a container ship has sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after a projectile hit it, and a dry bulk ship is reported to be sinking after being hit in a separate incident. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Germany's Merz says the European Commission will get a new trade tool so it can respond quickly to developments
detail: German Chancellor Merz said the European Commission will have a new trade instrument for responding quickly to developments. The remarks come amid German moves to press the EU on capping additional imports from China.

headline: US September CPI rises to 3.7% y/y, above the 3.6% forecast; core CPI 2.6% y/y; traders add to Fed hike bets
detail: US headline CPI rose 0.6% m/m in September, in line with forecasts, and 3.7% y/y against 3.4% previously; core CPI rose 0.3% m/m against a 0.2% forecast and 2.6% y/y against a 2.5% forecast. The FT reported that fuel prices rebounded because of the war in Iran; US short-term rate futures fell and traders added to bets on a Fed rate hike in October.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield climbs 10bp to 4.89% and dollar index hits its highest since November after hotter US CPI
detail: The moves followed September US CPI. Core rose 0.3% m/m against 0.2% expected. Kalshi pricing put the chance of an October Fed hike at 33%, up from 21%, and the Bloomberg dollar spot index rose to its highest since November.

headline: US supercore CPI rises to 3.13% y/y in September from 3.02% the month before
detail: The supercore figure comes from the same US September CPI release, which put headline inflation at 3.7% y/y. The FT reports that higher fuel costs linked to the Iran war pushed prices up.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield extends rise to 12.72bp at 4.92%, its highest since 29 September
detail: The US 2-year Treasury yield was last up 12.72bp at 4.92%, its highest level since 29 September, after the September US CPI data.

headline: US supercore CPI rises 0.42% m/m in September, slower than 0.51% the month before
detail: US supercore CPI rose 0.42% month on month in September, compared with 0.51% in the previous month, according to the September US CPI release.

headline: US gasoline prices jump 9.1% m/m in September, making up more than half of the monthly CPI increase
detail: BLS data show headline CPI at 3.7% y/y in September, up from 3.4%, and core CPI at 2.6%, up from 2.4%. Gasoline rose 9.1% on the month and made up more than half of the monthly rise in CPI.

headline: US Federal Maritime Commission proposes a fee on all Spanish vessels
detail: The US Federal Maritime Commission has proposed charging a fee on every Spanish vessel, according to a market news report. The report gave no figures or timing.

headline: Dollar index hits 18-month high at 102.75 and euro falls to lowest since mid-May 2025 at $1.112
detail: Market reports put the US dollar index up 0.57% at 102.75, a new 18-month high. The euro was last down 0.7% at $1.112, its weakest against the dollar since mid-May 2025.

headline: Traders fully price two Fed hikes by end of January after hot US CPI; October hike odds put at about 50-55%
detail: After the September US CPI data, market pricing shows two Fed rate hikes fully priced by the end of January. Prediction market Kalshi puts the chance of a 25bp hike in October at 55%, up from 21% earlier, and an economist says rates markets price about 50% odds of a hike this month.

headline: UK energy minister says a decision on the Jackdaw gas field is imminent
detail: Britain's energy minister says the government is close to deciding on the North Sea Jackdaw gas field. No timing or outcome was given.

headline: White House adviser Hassett calls the headline US inflation figure disappointing and names the energy shock as the main story
detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said the US economy's strength is visible and is showing up a little in the inflation data. He described spending as almost healthy and said the energy shock is the headline story of the day.

headline: White House adviser Hassett calls this month's US core inflation a blip and says the Fed needs more data before deciding on rates
detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett made the comments after the September US CPI release. He described the core reading as a blip and said more data were needed before the Fed takes a rate decision.

headline: Iran's IRNA reports an explosion in Riyadh after a missile attack, with reports of damage to oil facilities
detail: Iranian state news agency IRNA reported a blast in the Saudi capital after a missile attack and said there were reports of damage to oil facilities. The report gives no details of which facilities were hit or how much damage was done.

headline: Bank of America shares fall 8.3%, their biggest drop since April 2025
detail: A market news feed reports that Bank of America shares are down 8.3%, the steepest fall since April 2025. The post gives no reason for the drop.

headline: Citigroup now expects a 25bp Fed rate hike in December 2026; it had previously forecast no change this year
detail: Citigroup has changed its Federal Reserve call and now expects a 25bp rate increase in December 2026. Its previous forecast was for no change this year.

headline: Traders bet the Fed may need two hikes or a 50bp move by December, CNBC reports
detail: CNBC reports that traders are betting the Federal Reserve may have to raise rates twice, or by 50bp in one step, by its December meeting. The report follows the hotter-than-expected US September CPI data.

headline: Trump plays down talk of halting intelligence sharing with Ukraine and says the US still shares it
detail: Trump told reporters the US is still sharing intelligence with Ukraine, but Semafor reports that cutting it off is being actively discussed inside the White House.

headline: Fed's Williams says one more rate hike may be appropriate but sees no reason at present to expect more beyond that
detail: New York Fed President John Williams said his view has not changed that one more hike may be appropriate, and that he currently has no reason to think further increases would be needed.

headline: Resolution Foundation estimates UK fiscal headroom has halved to about £12bn in 2029-30 before Budget measures
detail: The Resolution Foundation estimates that, before any policy measures, headroom against the fiscal rules will be around £12 billion in 2029-30. It says John Healey would need £18 billion of headroom to keep a buffer equivalent to the one Rachel Reeves had.

headline: Russia's Novak says two Russian oil refineries were attacked today
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said two Russian oil refineries came under attack on Wednesday, Interfax reported. No details of damage or effect on output were given.

headline: IEA meets on Thursday, with the pace of Europe's planned diesel stock release in focus, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that the International Energy Agency meets on Thursday and that the market's attention is on how quickly Europe will release its large diesel stocks.

headline: Adviser to Ukraine's Zelenskiy rejects as false Russian reports of strikes on refineries today
detail: An adviser to Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Russian reports of attacks on refineries today were fake. Earlier, Russia's Novak had said two Russian oil refineries were attacked today.

headline: Resolution Foundation says funding defence pledges within existing plans would mean £9bn real-terms day-to-day spending cuts
detail: The Resolution Foundation notes that the government has not yet set out how it will pay for its defence commitments. It estimates that funding them within current plans would require £9bn of real-terms day-to-day spending cuts for unprotected departments between 2028-29 and 2029-30, which it says is more than a typical austerity year.

headline: Saudi Arabia does not intend to back down in its conflict with the Houthis, CNN reports
detail: CNN reports that Saudi Arabia has no intention of backing down against Yemen's Houthi forces, after Houthi attacks on Aramco facilities in Dhahran and Riyadh. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Russian deputy foreign minister says Russia has had no proposal yet to mediate between Saudi Arabia and Yemen
detail: Iran's IRNA news agency reported the remark from Russia's deputy foreign minister. It comes after an official told AP that Oman, Russia and China were mediating ceasefire talks with the Houthis.

headline: Zelenskiy says he feels betrayed by Trump's diesel deal with Russia but calls the situation complicated
detail: Ukraine's president told a Piers Morgan interview that it hurts when the US president takes a side different from Ukraine's. He added that anyone acting as a mediator needs to stay neutral.

headline: Draft EU summit conclusions seek sanctions on Russian ex-combatants and express regret over the US-Russia diesel deal
detail: The Kyiv Independent reports that draft conclusions for the EU summit call for sanctions on former Russian combatants and register regret at the diesel deal between the US and Russia.

headline: Trump says Taiwan has committed to a $70-80bn offtake deal for Alaska LNG
detail: US President Trump said Commerce Secretary Lutnick has obtained an offtake commitment from Taiwan worth between 70 and 80 billion dollars for the Alaska LNG project.

headline: Trump says Taiwan will also put $4.4bn of equity into the Alaska LNG project
detail: US President Trump said on Truth Social that Taiwan has agreed to a $4.4bn equity investment in the Alaska LNG project. This is in addition to the $70-80bn offtake commitment he announced earlier.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield falls to session low, down 3.2bp at 5.531%, while 2-year yield is up 2.98bp at 4.823%
detail: The US 30-year Treasury yield touched a session low, last 3.2bp lower at 5.531%. The 2-year yield was last 2.98bp higher at 4.823%.

headline: Fed's Barkin says he does not see job losses from AI happening at scale
detail: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said job losses caused by artificial intelligence are not yet happening at scale.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker says Iran wants neither endless war nor drawn-out talks and will fight until its demands are met
detail: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf made the remarks in an address to the nation, Fars news agency reported. He said Iran will keep fighting until the enemy is forced to accept its demands.

headline: Fed's Barkin says AI accounts for most investment in the US economy but that growth cannot be relied on to continue indefinitely
detail: Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said investment activity in the US economy comes largely from AI, and added that AI investment cannot be counted on to keep growing for ever. These remarks follow his earlier comments on AI and jobs.

headline: Fed Beige Book: three districts call price growth robust and most report little or no net change in employment
detail: The Federal Reserve's Beige Book says two of the twelve districts reported moderate growth in activity, with most seeing little or no net change in employment and expectations generally for slight growth. Three districts described overall price growth as robust and eight as moderate, and three of those eight said input price pressures were intensifying.

headline: Fed's Barkin says US CPI came in above what he had hoped and declines to prejudge the October FOMC outcome
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the September CPI report was higher than he would have liked and that he would not project the result of the October FOMC meeting. He said Thursday's producer price data would help shape his inflation outlook.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker says a deal with the US cannot stop Iran from being attacked again
detail: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said an agreement with the US would not prevent a further attack on Iran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's Tasnim says Yemeni forces have targeted Saudi Aramco oil distribution facilities in northern Jeddah
detail: Iran's Tasnim News Agency reports that Yemeni armed forces targeted Saudi Aramco oil distribution facilities in northern Jeddah. The batch does not report any damage assessment or market reaction.

headline: New York Fed desk plans about $14.6bn of reinvestment purchases between 15 October and 13 November
detail: The New York Fed says its trading desk plans to carry out approximately $14.6bn in reinvestment purchases between 15 October and 13 November.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee calls US CPI data discouraging and flags services inflation as a concern
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee called the latest US CPI figures discouraging and said services inflation in the report was a worry, according to Yahoo.

headline: Fed extends pause on reserve management purchases to mid-November
detail: The Federal Reserve has extended its pause on reserve management purchases until mid-November, a market commentator reports.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the Fed must head off a build-up of overheating and that inflation has not proved transitory
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said there is no ambiguity for the Fed when the economy is solid and inflation is high, and that prices and costs are the weakest part of the economy. He added that contacts are not voicing recession worries, that he hopes energy effects will soon fade from the inflation data, and that he does not favour signalling Fed moves before meetings.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says further bad inflation months would be unacceptable and policy would have to respond if current levels persist
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said tariff effects on prices are proving more lasting than expected, that he does not want to tie the Fed's hands on policy and that the Fed will return inflation to 2%. He also called consumer spending, GDP and investment strong and said AI-driven tech investment could add to the risk of overheating.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says tariff effects on prices are lasting longer than expected and he will not precommit to future policy moves
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said energy, tariffs and services are keeping price pressures high, and that policy should stay data-dependent while the Fed returns inflation to 2%. He also said a slowdown in AI investment need not cause a recession and that he is watching the financial stability implications of AI investment.

headline: US maritime regulator proposes $200,000 fee on Spanish-flagged ships and limits on Spanish olive oil imports in port dispute
detail: Reuters reports the US Federal Maritime Commission proposed on Wednesday a $200,000 fee on Spanish-flagged ships calling at US ports. The proposal would also restrict imports from Spain, including olive oil, its biggest export to the US.

headline: China's September exports rise 36% y/y
detail: Semafor reports that Chinese exports grew 36% year on year in September. It says this comes as trading partners press Beijing to address trade imbalances and alleged overproduction.

headline: Fed's Daly says more rate hikes are likely but sees no urgency, with timing still under consideration
detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said core inflation remains stubborn while gas prices are lifting headline CPI, and that risks of inflation staying above target remain high. She said markets have calmed after their initial strong reaction to the CPI data.

headline: US weighs easing some sanctions on shadow fleet vessels to cut global freight rates and lift Middle East oil flows
detail: A US official told Reuters that Washington is discussing lifting some sanctions on shadow fleet tankers. The stated aims are to lower global freight rates and increase oil flows in the Middle East.

headline: US considers unfreezing some Russian assets to revive Ukraine peace talks; European officials reject the plan
detail: The FT reports that the US is considering releasing some frozen Russian assets to restart Ukraine peace talks. In a later report, the FT says European officials have rejected the plan.

headline: Conservative leader Badenoch warns against a possible bank tax increase in the UK Budget
detail: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch is expected to warn the government against raising taxes on banks in the Budget during a visit to Edinburgh on Thursday, according to City AM and the FT. The FT reports that investors are warning of a possible hit to UK competitiveness.

headline: Israel's Netanyahu says Iran's regime must be overthrown but does not see it happening before Israeli elections
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said Iran is at its weakest point ever and that Israel needs to finish the job. He also said he does not think regime change in Iran is realistic before Israel's elections.

headline: Australian employment falls 39.3k in September against a forecast 20k rise; jobless rate rises to 4.7%
detail: Australian employment fell 39.3k in September against a forecast 20k gain, after a 39.5k rise the month before. The unemployment rate rose to 4.7% from 4.6%, above the 4.6% forecast, and the participation rate fell to 66.8% against a forecast of 67.0%.

headline: 10-year JGB yield falls 5.5bp to 2.94%, its lowest since 10 September
detail: Japan's 10-year government bond yield fell 5.5bp to 2.94% in Asian trading, its lowest since 10 September. The 30-year JGB yield fell 4.5bp to 3.995%.

headline: UK's Healey says the 28 October Budget will keep the deficit reduction strategy, in line with IMF advice
detail: Healey, described in the report as UK finance minister, said the government will stick with its deficit reduction strategy in the 28 October Budget, as the IMF has advised. He also called for a tougher UK ban on shipping services linked to Russia and urged other countries to keep up sanctions on Russia.

headline: BoJ's Koeda says the Bank should not be too cautious about raising rates, citing big upside price risks and loose financial conditions
detail: BoJ board member Koeda said Japan's neutral rate is well above 1%, near the bottom of its estimated range, and that underlying inflation has been about 2% over the past year. She named yen weakness, AI demand and the Middle East as upside risks to prices, and said balance sheet normalisation should carry on calmly.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield falls to 5.1183%, a three-week low, as equities drop; December 2027 fed funds futures gain 9bp
detail: The US 10-year yield fell to its lowest in three weeks as a global tech sell-off spread through Asian markets. December 2027 fed funds futures rose 9bp, which was reported as easing expectations for the peak in rates.

headline: Bund futures rise 0.65% and French OAT futures gain 0.76% in early trading
detail: German and French government bond futures rose in Asian hours as global equities fell.

headline: ECB's Santos Pereira links rising yields mainly to fiscal factors and says central banks must act if inflation broadens
detail: ECB policymaker Santos Pereira said inflation is not spreading so far, but that natural gas prices would become a problem if this winter is like the last one.

headline: US Treasury yields fall, with 2-year down 8bp at 4.7235%; dollar slips from 18-month high as October Fed hike bets are pared
detail: US 2-year yields are 8bp lower at 4.7235% and 30-year yields 6bp lower at 5.4595%, and the euro is up 0.63% at $1.1228. Reuters reports that cautious remarks from Fed officials and the fall in yields have led traders to scale back bets on an October rate hike, despite the hotter-than-expected US CPI.

headline: KOSPI trading halted for 20 minutes after an 8% drop as the Nikkei falls 5%; European stock futures lower
detail: Trading on the South Korean stock market is suspended for 20 minutes after an 8% fall, and the Nikkei is down 5%. Euro Stoxx 50 futures are down 1.0%, DAX futures 0.8% and FTSE futures 0.2%.

headline: ECB's Santos Pereira says growth is beating expectations and could keep surprising on the upside in coming months
detail: ECB policymaker Santos Pereira says growth has come in above expectations and that he would not be surprised if this continues over the coming months.

headline: BoE chief economist Pill cautions against signalling a run of rate hikes if the Bank raises rates now
detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said that if rates were raised now, the MPC should not signal a series of further hikes. The remarks were reported early on 15 October.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries
detail: In an FT interview, Ukraine's president said the restriction on attacking Russian refineries had been lifted. He also criticised the withdrawal of US intelligence sharing and the weakening of Starlink service as dangerous.

headline: US military strike plans include possible use of 'mother of all bombs' on Iranian energy and nuclear sites, CNN reports
detail: CNN, citing US officials, reported that the plans could use the GBU-43/B bomb against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if President Trump orders renewed combat operations.

headline: IMF sees Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan region contracting 1.3% in 2026 after 3.3% growth in 2025
detail: The IMF named a prolonged war and further energy and shipping disruption as the biggest risks, noting lower inventories and tighter spare capacity. It called for tighter monetary policy, prudent fiscal measures and a focus on price stability, and an official said oil prices would stay higher.

headline: French CPI holds at 3.0% y/y in September and falls 0.3% m/m, both in line with forecasts
detail: French consumer prices rose 3.0% year on year, unchanged from the previous month and in line with the forecast. Prices fell 0.3% month on month, matching expectations, after a 0.3% rise the previous month.

headline: Italy's draft budgetary plan aims to raise 0.44% of GDP from the financial sector over 2027-2029
detail: Italy's Draft Budgetary Plan sets out a levy on the financial sector worth 0.44% of GDP across the 2027-2029 period.

headline: BoJ's Koeda says the Bank's basic view is that the neutral rate has to be thought of as a range
detail: Bank of Japan board member Koeda said the Bank's basic stance is to consider the neutral interest rate as a range. She made the remark in the same appearance where she said the BoJ should not be too cautious about raising rates.

headline: BoJ's Koeda says the Bank has no set pace for rate hikes and should adjust rates in a timely way
detail: BoJ board member Koeda said the Bank has not settled on a particular pace for raising rates. She described monetary conditions as accommodative and called for appropriate policy adjustments in light of upside risks to prices.

headline: Germany's Merz is expected to reject the €2tn EU budget proposal at the summit, Welt reports
detail: Welt reports that German Chancellor Merz is likely to oppose the proposed €2tn EU budget at the EU summit.

headline: BoJ's Koeda signals a neutral rate well above 1% and sees underlying inflation settling near 2%
detail: Bank of Japan board member Koeda indicated that the neutral interest rate is considerably above 1% and said underlying inflation is stabilising at around 2%. She also said there needs to be discussion of whether the price target has been achieved.

headline: South Korea's KOSPI extends its slide to 9% in a sharp sell-off
detail: South Korea's KOSPI index was reported down 9% in a sharp sell-off, following an earlier 20-minute trading halt after an 8% drop.

headline: BoJ's Koeda says cost pass-through is tracking the July forecast and data showing resilience supported the September hike
detail: Bank of Japan board member Koeda said the pace at which costs are passed on to prices is in line with the Bank's main scenario from July. She said the September rate hike reflected additional data showing the economy's resilience, and pledged appropriate policy adjustments to keep underlying inflation at the 2% target.

headline: UK GDP grows 0.7% on a three-month basis, ahead of the 0.5% forecast and up from 0.4% previously
detail: The UK three-month-on-three-month GDP estimate came in at 0.7%, against a forecast of 0.5% and a previous reading of 0.4%.

headline: BoJ's Koeda calls for a broad review of financial conditions, including neutral rates and funding demand
detail: Bank of Japan board member Koeda said the assessment of financial conditions should be broad and should take in neutral rates and demand for funding.

headline: UK GDP rises 0.1% m/m in August against a forecast 0.1% fall; annual growth reaches 2.1% against 1.7% expected
detail: Monthly GDP for August rose 0.1% after 0.4% previously, and annual growth was 2.1% against 1.6% previously. Services were flat m/m (forecast -0.1%), construction fell 0.2% (forecast 0%), industrial production rose 0.8% m/m and 1.6% y/y, and manufacturing rose 1.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y.

headline: UK goods trade deficit narrows to £18.0bn, smaller than the £21.9bn forecast
detail: The UK goods trade balance came in at -18.007bn against a forecast of -21.9bn and -20.96bn previously. The non-EU goods deficit narrowed to 5.287bn from 9.663bn.

headline: UK industrial output rises 0.8% m/m in August against a forecast 0.1% fall; manufacturing up 1.2% against flat expected
detail: August figures show industrial production up 1.6% y/y (forecast 0.7%) and manufacturing up 3.0% y/y (forecast 2.3%). Services output was flat m/m (forecast -0.1%) and rose 0.9% on a three-month basis (forecast 0.7%), while construction output fell 1.8% y/y (forecast -2.1%).

headline: South Korea's financial regulator holds an emergency meeting on the stock market sell-off and orders steps to keep markets stable
detail: The regulator told financial firms to avoid excessive lending and to tighten investor safeguards and risk controls. It also said it would take firm action against behaviour that disrupts markets.

headline: Concern over French public debt drives French stocks to their biggest underperformance since 2010, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that investors want large discounts on French equities compared with regional peers because of strained public finances and the coming presidential election.

headline: Swiss producer and import prices fall 0.2% y/y in September, up from -0.7%; monthly rise of 0.3%
detail: Swiss producer and import prices fell 0.2% year on year in September, after a 0.7% fall the previous month. Month on month, prices rose 0.3%, compared with 0.7% previously.

headline: French final HICP holds at 3.4% y/y in September as expected; monthly fall of 0.3% is smaller than the 0.4% forecast
detail: France's final EU-harmonised inflation for September was 3.4% y/y, the same as the previous reading and the forecast. The monthly figure was -0.3%, against a forecast of -0.4% and a previous 0.4%.

headline: BoE's Greene calls the risk of second-round inflation effects pretty significant
detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said the risk of second-round effects on inflation is pretty significant. No market reaction was reported.

headline: BoE's Greene says leaning on market pricing is not a workable long-term approach
detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said that relying on market pricing does not work over the long term. The remark follows her earlier comment that the risk of second-round inflation effects is significant.

headline: BoE's Greene voices concern over the short-term inflationary effect of AI
detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Greene said she is worried about the near-term inflationary impact of artificial intelligence, according to a market news headline.

headline: Sweden's PM Kristersson says Sweden will reject the EU multiannual budget proposal and is in no rush to reach a deal
detail: Swedish Prime Minister Kristersson said the proposal for the EU's multiannual financial framework is not acceptable and not even a starting point, and that he is unsure a deal can be reached before the end of the year. He also said the US-Russia diesel deal goes in the wrong direction.

headline: UK ministers to launch statutory best value inspection of Tees Valley Combined Authority, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Rayner will order a statutory best value inspection of the mayoral authority led by Ben Houchen. The report says the move follows concerns in Whitehall about the body's governance and debt levels.

headline: German 10-year Bund yield falls 8.5bp to 3.3819%, its lowest since 9 September
detail: The 10-year German government bond yield was last down 8.5bp at 3.3819% in early European trading, its lowest level since 9 September.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says inflationary forces remain stronger in the near term
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said inflationary pressures are still stronger in the immediate future.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says the ECB does not need to move quickly on rates
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said there is no immediate need to rush on rates, while repeating that inflationary forces remain stronger in the near term.

headline: South Korea and Japan to extend their currency swap agreement
detail: South Korea and Japan will extend their bilateral currency swap agreement, according to a market news report. The report comes during a sharp sell-off in South Korean equities.

headline: Greek PM Mitsotakis rejects Irish EU budget proposal and opposes cuts to farm spending
detail: Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis said Greece is not satisfied with the Irish proposal on the EU multiannual financial framework and will not accept cuts to agricultural spending. He also asked the EU to look at more flexibility to support energy aid for consumers and businesses.

headline: BoE's Breeden says the UK economy has absorbed the energy shock better than she expected
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said she was surprised at how the UK economy had coped with the energy shock. She added that companies say they are focusing on cutting costs rather than passing the energy price shock on to customers.

headline: BoE's Breeden says the Bank is examining whether the energy shock has passed or is only delayed, and hopes a cooler labour market avoids…
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said businesses report absorbing the shock and cutting costs, and that the Bank is assessing whether the energy shock is over or merely delayed. She said she hopes an easing labour market will prevent wage-price pressure like that seen in 2022.

headline: Spain's PM Sanchez rejects the current EU budget proposal as inadequate
detail: Speaking in Brussels, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Spain does not agree with the current EU budget proposal and called it insufficient.

headline: Germany's Merz says no EU member can afford the current budget plan and does not expect a long-term budget deal this weekend
detail: German Chancellor Merz said no EU country could manage the current long-term EU budget proposal and that he expects difficult talks. He said he does not expect agreement this weekend but hopes for a deal before the end of the year.

headline: BoE's Breeden says UK activity is not collapsing and the labour market is holding up
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said she sees resilience and cost management among UK firms, with activity not dropping sharply and the labour market holding up.

headline: Russia's Novak says first diesel deliveries to the US could come in 2-3 weeks at the earliest
detail: According to Russian reports, Deputy Prime Minister Novak says this depends on a contract being signed and shipping being arranged.

headline: Russia considers banning LPG exports and will keep importing gasoline until at least the end of the year
detail: Interfax reports that Russia is weighing an LPG export ban because of market conditions, and that gasoline imports will continue until at least year-end.

headline: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi says the Japanese economy can no longer be called deflationary
detail: Japan's Economy Minister Kiuchi said on Thursday that the economy can no longer be described as deflationary.

headline: Russia's Novak says contracts must be signed before diesel exports to the US begin
detail: Russian Deputy PM Novak said contracts will be signed before diesel exports start, Interfax reported. He also repeated that Russia plans to keep importing gasoline until the end of the year.

headline: Chancellor Reeves's Budget will give the UK breathing space and include steps to strengthen economic resilience, says Healey
detail: UK minister Healey said the Budget will give Britain some breathing space and will include measures to reinforce the resilience of the UK economy. He also said there are already signs that AI is improving productivity.

headline: Chancellor Healey blames global uncertainty for rising UK yields and says the UK must give investors confidence
detail: Chancellor Healey said the rise in UK yields has been driven by global uncertainties, that the UK must give investors confidence and that spending must be paid for within the available budget. He declined to speculate on taxes ahead of the Budget.

headline: Eurozone industrial production falls 0.5% m/m in August against a flat forecast; annual rate drops to -1.1%
detail: Eurozone industrial output fell 0.5% on the month, against a forecast of 0% and -0.1% previously. On the year, output fell 1.1%, against a forecast of -0.1% and 0.0% previously.

headline: France sells 5-year OATs at 4.16%, up from 3.92% at the previous sale; bid-to-cover rises to 2.297
detail: The French 5-year OAT auction priced at an average yield of 4.16%, compared with 3.92% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.297, up from 2.22.

headline: Gulf stock markets fall in early trade after the Houthis threaten further attacks on Saudi Arabia
detail: Reuters reports that major Gulf markets fell early on Thursday after the Houthis threatened more attacks on Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia's benchmark index is on course for a sixth weekly loss.

headline: Houthis deny striking Saudi territory today and reject Saudi claims of an attack aimed at Medina
detail: Yemen's Houthi armed forces said they had carried out no operations against Saudi Arabia on Thursday and called Saudi claims of an attack aimed at the city of Medina false. The statement follows Houthi threats of further attacks on Saudi Arabia earlier in the day.

headline: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi says the Takaichi government is not pursuing reflationary policy
detail: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi said reflationary policy is not needed at present and is not the policy of the Takaichi administration.

headline: India's trade minister says the first phase of the India-US trade deal is finalised
detail: India's trade minister said the first phase of a trade deal with the US has been finalised. India's trade secretary said talks were moving in the right direction and that India wants preferential access to the US market.

headline: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi leaves monetary policy to the BoJ and says sharp short-term FX swings should be avoided
detail: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi said decisions on monetary policy are a matter for the Bank of Japan, and he declined to comment on specific currency levels. He said exchange rates are set by markets and that wild short-term moves should be avoided.

headline: India's trade secretary says India wants to close and sign the US trade deal as soon as possible and seeks more tariff stability
