detail: India's trade secretary said India is seeking preferential market access and greater tariff stability in the deal with the US. The secretary added that the sticking points identified by the end of June negotiations have since narrowed.

headline: Economists poll: 54 of 63 expect the BoE to raise Bank Rate to 4.00% on 5 November
detail: In the previous poll, 54 of 65 economists expected a hold. The same poll raised UK inflation forecasts to an average of 3.6% in Q4 2026, 3.8% in Q1 2027 and 3.0% in 2027, from 3.3%, 3.2% and 2.5% in September, and put GDP growth at 1.3% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027, against 1.1% and 1.2% previously.

headline: China indicates rare earth supplies to Europe will continue, CNBC reports
detail: CNBC reports that China has signalled rare earth exports to Europe will keep flowing. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield extends its decline to 5.08%, down 11bp on the day
detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell further to 5.08%, an 11bp drop on the day, extending the earlier move to a three-week low.

headline: Ukraine strikes a Russian refinery overnight, citing Russian attacks that breached the Trump energy truce
detail: A Ukrainian official said Ukraine hit a Russian oil refinery overnight. The official said it was a response to Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks that breached the energy truce brokered by Trump.

headline: Spain to release 4.4 million barrels from its strategic reserves in October
detail: An official at Spain's energy ministry says 4.4 million barrels will be drawn from the country's strategic reserves during October.

headline: Kremlin says Russian diesel is reaching global markets and will help but cannot fully stabilise them
detail: The Kremlin said Russian diesel has begun arriving on global markets. It said the supply will have a positive effect on markets but will not be enough to fully stabilise them.

headline: Kremlin says Ukraine's refinery strikes run counter to US peace efforts and calls the latest attack nothing new
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov was responding to Zelenskiy's statement that Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries. He said US efforts to settle the war are failing because Kyiv, and Zelenskiy personally, are unwilling to seek a peaceful solution.

headline: Chancellor Healey says the UK will meet its fiscal rules and any energy support must be targeted and temporary
detail: In remarks on 15 October, the Chancellor also acknowledged that energy costs are punishing. She said the UK is still considering all options on Russian assets.

headline: BoE's Breeden says banks need deep 'bare metal' cyber-recovery options in the face of AI-enabled attacks
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said on Thursday that the Bank is working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options. She said lenders can no longer assume their defences cannot be breached, Reuters reports.

headline: France's Moulin says the French deficit can be brought down to 3% within three years, CNBC reports
detail: Moulin made the remarks in an interview with CNBC. They come amid reported concern over French public debt.

headline: German 10-year Bund yield falls further, down 10bp to 3.37%, its lowest since 8 September
detail: The German 10-year yield dropped 10bp on the day to 3.37%, its lowest level since 8 September, according to a market wire report.

headline: ECB's Moulin says he is confident about financial stability in France, CNBC reports
detail: Speaking to CNBC, Moulin said he was confident about France's financial stability. In the same interview he said the French deficit could be cut to 3% within three years.

headline: Iran has struck Gulf infrastructure dozens of times in precision attacks, and Gulf states often hide the damage, Reuters reports
detail: A Reuters report says repeated Iranian precision strikes on Gulf infrastructure have weakened the US war effort. It adds that Gulf governments have often hidden how much damage was done.

headline: Oil tanker freight costs surge, with a US-to-Japan supertanker voyage costing $81m against $9.1m last year, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that the cost of shipping crude oil has risen sharply. It says a supertanker carrying about 2 million barrels from the US to Japan in late November will cost $81 million, compared with an average of $9.1 million for the same voyage last year.

headline: SNB's Tschudin says inflationary pressures are slightly higher than in June
detail: Swiss National Bank official Tschudin said inflation pressures have risen slightly compared with June.

headline: PBOC Governor Pan says exchange rates cannot fix global imbalances
detail: Pan Gongsheng, governor of the People's Bank of China, said exchange rate adjustments cannot correct global imbalances.

headline: Russia is suspected of striking two tankers in NATO waters, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Russia is suspected of attacks on two tankers in waters belonging to NATO members. The report gives no market reaction.

headline: Global stock sell-off deepens as chipmakers fall and sovereign bonds rally in a risk-off move, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that European and Asian equities are falling as investors question how long the AI boom can last, with chipmakers leading the decline. Sovereign bonds are gaining as investors move out of riskier assets.

headline: Saudi Aramco offers more spot crude cargoes to Europe for late October to mid-November delivery, trade sources say
detail: Three trade sources say Saudi Aramco is offering additional spot crude oil cargoes into the European market for delivery between late October and mid-November.

headline: UN rural development agency head says Hormuz shipping disruption is starting to hurt harvests and could raise food prices
detail: The head of a United Nations rural development agency said on Thursday that disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is already showing up in agricultural harvests and threatens lower farm yields and higher food prices, Reuters reports.

headline: Trump says he may back a suspension of the federal diesel tax
detail: US President Trump said he could support suspending the federal tax on diesel. He did not give a timetable or any figures.

headline: Poll finds UK government should aim for £15-16bn of fiscal headroom in the October Budget
detail: A poll reported on 15 October puts the fiscal headroom the government should target in the October Budget at £15-16bn. The report does not name who was polled.

headline: Senior Iranian military official Sayyari says the Strait of Hormuz is closed, reports say
detail: Reports say Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, a senior Iranian military commander, has stated that the Strait of Hormuz is closed. No market reaction has been reported yet.

headline: Poll finds UK fiscal headroom has probably been eroded to £10-12bn
detail: A poll finds the UK government's current fiscal headroom has probably fallen to £10-12bn. An earlier poll found the government should aim for £15-16bn of headroom in the October Budget.

headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says Russia is openly rejecting Trump's peace proposals
detail: Ukraine's foreign minister said Russia rejects peace and is openly rejecting President Trump's proposals, and argued that easing pressure on Moscow has made it more defiant.

headline: China's finance minister Lan says China will implement a more active fiscal policy
detail: China's finance minister Lan said fiscal policy will become more active and that the economy continues on a stable, positive trend. He said protectionism and geopolitical risks are hurting growth.

headline: US tells IEA members it is unhappy with the emergency oil release and proposes adding 100m barrels, reports say
detail: A market news account reports that the US has told IEA member countries it is dissatisfied with the current emergency oil stock release. It reports that the US has suggested adding a further 100 million barrels to the release.

headline: US retail sales rise 0.8% m/m in September against a 0.3% forecast; core sales up 0.9% against 0.5% expected
detail: US headline retail sales rose 0.8% on the month, down from 1.2% previously. Core retail sales rose 0.9%, against a 0.5% forecast and 1.4% previously.

headline: US jobless claims rise to 199K, below the 200K forecast; NY Fed manufacturing index jumps to 25.5
detail: US initial jobless claims rose by 1K to 199K in the week to 10 October, and the prior week was revised to 198K. Continuing claims came in at 1.71M, while the NY Fed manufacturing index rose to 25.5, against a forecast of 12 and 7.60 previously.

headline: US producer prices rise 6.3% y/y in September against a 5.4% forecast; monthly rise of 1.3% is double the expected 0.6%
detail: US headline PPI rose 1.3% m/m in September, up from 0.4% the previous month. Core PPI rose 0.7% m/m against a 0.3% forecast, and 5% y/y against an expected 4.4% (previous 4.6%).

headline: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index falls to 20.9 in October, below the 28 forecast and down from 37.8
detail: The October Philadelphia Fed business index came in at 20.9, against a forecast of 28.0 and 37.8 previously. US continuing jobless claims were 1710K, against an expected 1709K and 1716K previously.

headline: Zelenskyy pledges to resume Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries after what he describes as a US withdrawal of intelligence support
detail: Semafor reports that Ukraine's president has pledged to resume attacks on Russian refineries. Washington has pressed Kyiv to curb strikes on energy facilities and has linked them to rising fuel prices.

headline: Japan's finance minister Katayama tells G20 that market moves need urgent monitoring as the G20 reaffirms its FX commitments
detail: Japan's finance minister Katayama said the G20 had reaffirmed its earlier commitments on foreign exchange. She also told the G20 that market moves need to be monitored with high urgency.

headline: US Treasury rejects IMF warning on US debt and criticises the Fund's forecasting, CNBC reports
detail: CNBC reports that the US Treasury has dismissed an IMF warning on US debt and called the Fund's forecasting messy. No further figures were given.

headline: UK 30-year gilt yield falls 13bp to 5.781%, heading for its largest one-day drop since April
detail: The long-dated gilt yield fell 13bp to 5.781% during a global bond rally, with the move on course to be the biggest daily fall since April.

headline: US core PPI rises 0.7% m/m and 5.0% y/y in September as headline posts its biggest increase since 2022
detail: BLS data show producer prices excluding food and energy rose 0.7% on the month and 5.0% on the year, alongside headline gains of 1.3% m/m and 6.3% y/y, the largest jump since 2022.

headline: France begins putting in place operational parts of an agreement to help protect Saudi oil facilities
detail: A spokesperson for the French foreign ministry said France has started implementing operational elements of the agreement to help protect Saudi Arabian oil installations.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield decline widens to more than 28bp since yesterday
detail: A market commentary account reports that the US 10-year Treasury yield has fallen by more than 28bp since yesterday. This is a larger fall than the 11bp drop reported earlier in the session.

headline: WEF could name ECB President Lagarde as its next chair as early as 2 November, sources say
detail: Sources say the World Economic Forum could appoint ECB President Christine Lagarde as its chair as soon as 2 November. A second report also put the possible timing at November.

headline: Saudi-led coalition says Houthis tried to hit dozens of Saudi airports, oil sites and ports; reports destroying over 120 Yemeni arms depots
detail: The Saudi-led coalition said Yemen's Houthis had attempted attacks on dozens of airports, oil facilities and ports in Saudi Arabia and had acquired advanced weaponry. It also said it had destroyed more than 120 arms depots and many launchers in Yemen's mountains.

headline: Saudi-led coalition says 1,104 missiles and 1,135 drones have been fired at Saudi Arabia since operations began
detail: The Saudi-led coalition gave the cumulative totals of missiles and drones launched at the Kingdom since the start of its operations. No market reaction was reported.

headline: IEA agrees to complete release of the outstanding 100m barrels of emergency oil stocks
detail: The International Energy Agency has agreed to release the remaining 100m barrels of oil in full. The decision follows reports that the US had proposed adding 100m barrels to the emergency release.

headline: Iran instructs Hezbollah to raise readiness and prepare for possible conflict, reports say
detail: Iran has told Hezbollah to increase its readiness and get ready for a potential conflict, according to reports carried by a market news account. No market reaction was reported.

headline: IEA aims to release 20m barrels of diesel as soon as possible and says its March stock release will exceed 400m barrels
detail: The IEA Governing Board said about 330m barrels have been released so far. It agreed to speed up the remaining releases, and some members have released more than they pledged in March. The Board also urged members with production and refining capacity to increase supply of crude and refined products, especially diesel, and said it is willing to take further action.

headline: IEA confirms 330m barrels already released and urges producing members to raise crude and diesel supply
detail: The IEA Governing Board says 330m barrels of emergency stocks have been released and it will act on 100m more soon. It also calls on members with production and refining capacity to increase supply, especially of diesel, and says it is ready to take further steps.

headline: French finance minister Lescure says the G7 has raised €260m for Ukraine
detail: French finance minister Lescure gave the figure in Bangkok.

headline: French finance minister Lescure says the G7 has pledged $2.5bn for fertilisers
detail: French finance minister Lescure said G7 members have committed $2.5 billion to fertiliser supply. This follows his earlier statement on G7 funding for Ukraine.

headline: US business inventories rise 0.4% m/m, matching forecast and slowing from 0.8% previously
detail: US business inventories rose 0.4% month on month. That was in line with the 0.4% forecast and down from the previous 0.8% rise.

headline: US 5-year and 7-year Treasury yields fall 15bp on the day
detail: US Treasury 5-year and 7-year yields were reported down 15bp on the day, as the Treasury market rally widened further.

headline: France and Germany would let the UK into EU car policy if it aligns with EU tariffs on China, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that France and Germany are willing to admit the UK to EU car policy on condition that it aligns with the EU on tariffs on China.

headline: UK manufacturing output hits a real-terms record high in August, above its March 2024 peak
detail: Today's UK GDP release shows manufacturing output reached a real-terms record in August, surpassing the previous peak set in March 2024.

headline: EU starts assessing more sectors for possible trade quotas on China
detail: The EU has started assessing further sectors that could become subject to trade quotas on Chinese imports, according to a market newswire headline.

headline: NIESR GDP Tracker puts UK growth at around 0.2% in the final quarter after a strong third quarter
detail: NIESR's latest GDP Tracker says the UK economy kept growing in August, with production rather than services leading. It puts growth in the fourth quarter at around 0.2%.

headline: Yemen turns down a Saudi request for talks in Oman, reports say
detail: Iran's Tasnim news agency, citing AFP, reports that Yemen has rejected a Saudi Arabian request to hold talks in Oman. The report comes as fighting between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia intensifies.

headline: Houthis claim missile strike on Aden presidential complex, calling Saudi forces anywhere a legitimate target
detail: Reports say a missile attack on the presidential complex in Aden killed two security guards. The Houthis said they were targeting a Saudi military operations base and would strike Saudi military deployments wherever they are.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK household energy bills are due to rise again in January
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the January increase in energy bills comes at the coldest point of the year, with 46% of household gas use falling in the first quarter. It gave no figure for the size of the rise.

headline: ECB officials are reported to be growing impatient for Lagarde to set out her plans
detail: A newswire headline reports impatience among ECB officials for President Lagarde to clarify her plans. Earlier reports said the WEF could name her as its next chair as early as 2 November.

headline: US crude futures rise more than $2 to their highest since 21 September as Brent turns higher on the day
detail: Market reports say US crude futures gained more than $2 to reach their highest level since 21 September. Brent futures moved back into positive territory for the day.

headline: UN Security Council condemns escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in a presidential statement
detail: In a presidential statement, Security Council members condemned the continuing and escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the strongest terms, according to reports. Separately, Yemen's cabinet said the strike on the Maashiq Palace was part of a wider Houthi escalation that included attacks on vital facilities in Saudi Arabia.

headline: Putin says recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries have caused no significant damage
detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Ukraine's recent strikes on Russian oil refineries had not caused significant damage. Ukraine had pledged to resume strikes on Russian refineries.

headline: Putin says Russia will respond to Ukraine's strikes on its oil refineries
detail: Russian President Putin said Russia would respond to Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries. In the same remarks, reported by Interfax, he said the recent strikes had caused no significant damage.

headline: Chancellor Healey is preparing to raise taxes on banks in the Budget, Guardian reports
detail: The Guardian reports that Chancellor Rachel Healey is set to increase taxes on banks in the upcoming Budget. No figures were given.

headline: Japan finance ministry official says G7 and G20 raised no financial stability concerns over the AI-led sell-off
detail: A Japanese Ministry of Finance official said G7 and G20 policymakers saw no risk of financial system instability from the AI-led sell-off, though they agreed on the need for vigilance. The official also said the ministry watches markets closely but will not comment on individual stock, currency or bond moves.

headline: UK trade minister signals the UK is ready to align with EU tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, Politico reports
detail: Politico reports that the UK trade minister has said the UK is prepared to align with the EU's tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles. This follows an FT report that France and Germany would let the UK into EU car policy if it aligns with those tariffs.

headline: German regulator says gas storage is well below previous years but sees no risk to supply security
detail: Germany's network regulator said on Thursday that gas storage levels are significantly below those at the same point in previous years and that it is taking this very seriously. It said low recent injections reflect trading strategies and do not put supply security at risk, Reuters reports.

headline: US Treasury announces new Iran-related sanctions
detail: The US Treasury Department has published a fresh round of Iran-related sanctions on its website. No details of who is targeted were given in the initial report.

headline: US issues new sanctions and licences covering Iran, Cuba and Russia
detail: OFAC published new sanctions and licences relating to Iran, Cuba and Russia. The US Treasury website also showed an Iran-related general licence allowing transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance to be wound down.

headline: France and Germany agree a deal on the future of the car industry, diplomats say
detail: Diplomats say France and Germany have reached a deal on the future of the car industry. No further terms were reported.

headline: Switzerland authorises drawdowns from mandatory jet fuel reserves as Zurich Airport faces a supply shortfall
detail: On Thursday the Swiss government approved withdrawals from mandatory jet fuel stocks to deal with a looming fuel shortage at Zurich Airport, Reuters reports.

headline: Netanyahu warns Iran against attacking Israel and says Israel could act on its own, Israeli reports say
detail: According to Israeli media reports, Prime Minister Netanyahu said an Iranian attack on Israel would be a grave mistake and that Israel has the option of acting independently. The reports carried no market reaction.

headline: Chancellor Healey hints at a higher bank levy in the Budget, saying decisions are coming, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Healey referred to upcoming 'decisions' as the financial sector prepares for an increase in a key levy in the Budget. This follows an earlier Guardian report that she is preparing to raise taxes on banks.

headline: French parliamentary committee rejects the revenue section of the social security budget, Le Monde reports
detail: Deputies on the French National Assembly's social security committee voted down the revenue part of the social security budget bill, according to Le Monde.

headline: EU plans a trade instrument that could shut China out of the single market, report says
detail: A market news account reports that the EU is planning a trade tool that could be used to block China from the single market. No further details or market reaction were given.

headline: US Treasury buys back the maximum $6bn of coupons maturing in 2037-2046 against $40.836bn of offers
detail: The US Treasury's debt buyback operation covered coupons maturing between 2037 and 2046. It received $40.836bn of offers and accepted the $6bn maximum across 3 of the 42 eligible issues.

headline: US crude settles 3.03% higher at $97.97 a barrel, up $2.88 on the day
detail: NYMEX WTI November crude futures settled at $97.97 a barrel, up $2.88 or 3.03%. November diesel futures settled at $4.8456 a gallon and gasoline at $3.1802 a gallon.

headline: White House is drawing up plans to use the 'mother of all bombs' against Iran, CBS News reports
detail: CBS News, citing sources, reports that the White House is preparing plans to deploy the weapon known as the 'mother of all bombs' on Iran. No market reaction was reported in the batch.

headline: Rubio presses Lebanon's president over seized Hezbollah explosives and urges Lebanese-Israeli military deconfliction
detail: A State Department official says US Secretary of State Rubio discussed with President Aoun the seizure of several hundred kilos of explosives from Hezbollah. Rubio urged him to hold accountable those behind the shipment and called for direct military-to-military communication between Lebanese and Israeli forces.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield ends the session 10bp lower at 5.09% as WTI crude rises 2.8%
detail: A US market close summary reports the 10-year Treasury yield down 10bp at 5.09%, with WTI crude 2.8% higher at $97.71 a barrel and spot gold up 1.8% at $4,177.27 an ounce.

headline: Fed's Hammack says she is hearing more from lower-income Americans who are struggling with inflation
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack made the remarks on 15 October. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Pentagon says its 'NATO 3.0' plan would cut US troop numbers in Europe and shift focus to the Pacific
detail: The Pentagon said the NATO 3.0 plan sets out a rebalancing of the alliance, with fewer US troops in Europe and more US attention on the Pacific and other regions. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Fed's Hammack says businesses face heavy input cost pressures and voices concern over an emerging inflation mentality
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said businesses are reporting substantial input cost pressures and that she is worried an inflation mentality could take hold. She also said anecdotal information gives important guidance on the economy.

headline: Trump considers easing curbs on Russian and Iranian 'shadow fleet' tankers to bring down fuel costs, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the White House is considering letting blacklisted vessels carrying Russian and Iranian oil return to global trade. According to the report, the aim is to lower fuel costs ahead of the US midterm elections.

headline: Fed's Hammack says financial conditions do not currently look restrictive
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said financial conditions do not appear restrictive at present. She had earlier raised concerns about input cost pressures and inflation.

headline: New Zealand manufacturing PMI rises to 56.5 in September from 53.1
detail: New Zealand's seasonally adjusted manufacturing PMI for September came in at 56.5, up from 53.1, according to the Business NZ/Bank NZ survey.

headline: New Zealand food prices are flat in September as seasonally adjusted card spending falls 0.4% m/m
detail: Stats NZ says its food price index was unchanged at 0.0% month on month in September, after 0.3% the month before. Seasonally adjusted electronic card retail sales fell 0.4% on the month, while unadjusted sales rose 0.9% year on year.

headline: Fed's Hammack says the Fed may need to raise rates more aggressively if inflation expectations deteriorate notably
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said on Thursday that a notable deterioration in public inflation expectations could call for more aggressive rate rises, Reuters reports.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says inflation from AI-driven demand overheating would be more concerning and would need addressing
detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said that inflation arising from AI-related demand overheating would be of greater concern and would have to be dealt with.

headline: Trump rules out using nuclear weapons on Iran or deploying ground troops, and says the conflict will end soon
detail: President Trump said he would not use nuclear weapons against Iran and has no plans for ground troops there, adding that the Iran conflict would end soon. He also said he is in talks with Russia and China on nuclear disarmament.

headline: US-Mexico tariff talks stall as Commerce Secretary Lutnick resists major cuts to auto and steel levies
detail: Talks have stalled after Lutnick opposed large cuts to the 25% US auto tariffs and the 50% steel and aluminium levies. Mexico is seeking auto tariffs of 15% or less, and negotiations are continuing.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield falls 13bp to 5.06% in Asian trade as markets await Fed Chair Warsh's remarks
detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield is reported 13bp lower at 5.06% in Asian hours, with oil slipping to $97.38 and gold near $4,154. Markets are awaiting remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh for signals on possible rate rises.

headline: Japan's 10-year government bond yield rises 2bp to 2.940%
detail: The 10-year JGB yield is reported 2bp higher at 2.940% in Tokyo trading.

headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at 6.7220 per dollar, its strongest fixing since 2 February 2023
detail: The People's Bank of China fixed the yuan midpoint at 6.7220 against the dollar, compared with a market estimate of 6.6947. It also injected 60bn yuan via 7-day reverse repos at an unchanged 1.40%.

headline: Trump says allies can buy US munitions once stocks are replenished and that there are other targets besides refineries
detail: The US President said allies would be allowed to buy munitions once US stocks are built up. He added that there were plenty of targets to hit other than refineries.

headline: BoE's Bailey says second-round inflation effects look subdued so far and Middle East news is the main driver of gilt yields
detail: BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said the effect of higher energy prices on wider UK prices appears limited so far, but it is too early to draw firm conclusions. He also said the UK economy has been more resilient than forecast, though growth is not strong enough; said he is frustrated that inflation remains above target; and said prospects for international alignment on AI testing have improved.

headline: IMF's Georgieva says price stability must stay central banks' main focus and debt cannot fall without fiscal action
detail: Speaking alongside Fed Chair Warsh in Bangkok, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said growth alone cannot bring debt down fast enough without fiscal discipline. She also urged northern countries to rebuild fuel reserves before winter.

headline: US Treasury official Browne says Japan's currency and monetary policy must adjust to the post-deflation environment
detail: US Treasury official Browne also called on the IMF to do more to identify global imbalances.

headline: Fed Chair Warsh gives no signal on the October decision and says the October and December meetings will set policy direction
detail: Speaking at an IMF session in Bangkok, Fed Chair Warsh said he does not prejudge rate decisions. He said each meeting would be judged on its merits and that developments since the September FOMC have broadly followed the Fed's outlook. He also said price stability remains a firm commitment and inflation is a global problem, not just a US one. Markets expect rates to be held at the 27-28 October meeting.

headline: US Treasury's Browne says Washington and Tokyo coordinate closely on orderly markets and warns disorderly FX moves can spread
detail: US Treasury official Browne said the US and Japan are working closely together to support orderly markets. He said disorderly currency moves risk spreading volatility to other financial markets.

headline: BoC Governor says the impact of energy prices gets harder to ignore the longer they stay high, even without a rate hike
detail: The Bank of Canada Governor said that the longer energy prices stay high, the harder it is to look past their impact, even if no rate hike is made.

headline: Fed Chair Warsh doubts the Fed can predict its actions at the remaining 2026 meetings as the dollar hits a two-week low
detail: Fed Chair Warsh said he was sceptical about predicting what the Fed will do at its meetings for the rest of 2026. The dollar was reported sliding to a two-week low after his comments, with gold drawing buyers.

headline: Milburn welfare review would give young people less cash but more job support, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn is finalising his review into the million young people not in education, employment or training. The plan would cut cash payments and increase job support.

headline: Trump calls Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries a disgrace in a rebuke to Zelensky
detail: US President Trump criticised Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries, in a rebuke directed at President Zelensky. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Taiwan moves to restrict AI chip exports to China under a deal with the US
detail: A market news account reports that Taiwan will limit exports of AI chips to China as part of an agreement with the United States. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Swedish seasonally adjusted unemployment falls to 8.6% in September from 8.9%, in line with forecast
detail: Sweden's seasonally adjusted jobless rate came in at 8.6% for September, matching the forecast and down from 8.9%. The unadjusted rate fell to 8.1% from 8.5%, and the trend rate was unchanged at 8.7%.

headline: China's finance minister urges a balanced view of global imbalances in talks with ECB's Lagarde and EU officials
detail: According to a ministry statement, China's finance minister met the EU economy commissioner, ECB President Lagarde and the Eurogroup president. He said China is willing to make full use of the China-EU financial dialogue and to discuss improving global economic governance and macro-policy coordination.

headline: BoJ Governor Ueda says the bank will keep raising rates gradually if the economy and prices develop as expected
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said the underlying price trend is nearing 2% and that keeping it steady around that level matters more and more. He also said financial conditions remain accommodative.

headline: BoJ Governor Ueda flags a risk that underlying inflation overshoots the 2% price target
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said there is a risk of underlying inflation rising above the bank's 2% target. This follows his earlier remarks that the bank will keep raising rates gradually if the economy and prices develop as expected.

headline: China says its talks with the EU show the two sides can manage their differences through dialogue
detail: China commented on its talks with EU officials as the EU weighs trade measures on Chinese goods, including possible quotas and a trade instrument. The post did not say which Chinese official made the statement.

headline: PBOC Governor Pan says the central bank will support development of offshore yuan markets
detail: People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng said the bank will back the development of offshore yuan markets. No further detail or market reaction was reported.

headline: PBOC Governor Pan says China will promote renminbi bonds as globally accepted, eligible collateral
detail: People's Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng said the central bank plans to promote renminbi bonds as collateral that is recognised and eligible worldwide. He made the remarks alongside earlier comments on developing offshore yuan markets.

headline: EU leaders rule out easing Russia sanctions while the war goes on; von der Leyen says a 22nd sanctions package is being prepared
detail: European Council President Costa said now is not the time for sanctions relief on Russia and reaffirmed EU backing for Ukraine. Commission President von der Leyen said work is under way on a 22nd package, that no sanctions will be lifted unless Russia stops the war, and that Russia did not observe the energy ceasefire backed by Trump.

headline: G7 finance ministers agree to run simulated AI-driven cyber attacks on banks as cyber risk concerns grow
detail: The FT reports that G7 finance ministers have agreed to hold tabletop drills to prepare banks against future cyber attacks.

headline: China plans to add AI and solar technology to its export controls
detail: A market news account reports that China plans to extend its export controls to cover AI and solar technology. No further details or market reaction were given.

headline: Estonian PM Michal says the EU will probably need to give Ukraine a new loan to cover its budget gap next year
detail: Estonia's prime minister told Reuters that a new EU loan to fund Ukraine's budget shortfall next year is probable. He also said he hopes the EU can decide on Ukraine's future financing this year.

headline: Resolution Foundation estimates fiscal headroom has halved to about £12bn in 2029-30 before Budget measures
detail: The Resolution Foundation estimates that headroom against the fiscal rules in 2029-30 is around £12bn before any policy measures. It says Chancellor Healey would need £18bn of headroom to keep a buffer equivalent to the one his predecessor Reeves had, ahead of the 28 October Budget.

headline: Eurozone final core inflation confirmed at 2.5% y/y in September, in line with forecast
detail: The final eurozone core CPI reading is 2.5% year on year. This matches the forecast and is unchanged from the previous reading.

headline: Italy's final HICP inflation is revised up to 4.2% y/y, above the 4.1% forecast
detail: Italy's final HICP is 4.2% y/y against a 4.1% forecast and previous reading, and 2.1% m/m against a 2% forecast. National CPI is confirmed at 4.2% y/y and 0.7% m/m, both in line with forecast.

headline: Eurozone final headline inflation is confirmed at 3.8% y/y in September, in line with forecast
detail: Final eurozone CPI for September showed annual inflation of 3.8%, unchanged from the previous reading and matching the forecast. Monthly inflation was 0.6%, also in line with the forecast.

headline: Eurozone trade balance swings to a €16.1bn deficit, not seasonally adjusted
detail: The non-seasonally adjusted eurozone trade balance came in at -16.1bn. The previous figure was revised to 10.7bn from 14.2bn.

headline: Real Living Wage for 2026-27 is set at £14.10 for the UK and £15.45 for London
detail: The Resolution Foundation published the revised voluntary real Living Wage rates for 2026-27: £14.10 an hour across the UK and £15.45 in London.

headline: France and Germany issue joint declaration on car industry, planning incentives for investment, R&D, EU production and supply chains
detail: The French and German governments said in a joint statement that they have agreed a common approach to securing the future of the European automotive industry. The plan includes incentives for investment, research and development, production in the EU and supply chains.

headline: Kremlin calls the latest move against European firms' local assets part of a trend and says Kyiv must take part in any settlement
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the companies affected are all from 'unfriendly countries' that are involved in illegal expropriation of Russian property. He also said Zelensky is not pursuing a peaceful resolution, that Russia and Trump share this view, and that a Ukraine settlement cannot be discussed without Kyiv.

headline: Eurozone trade balance prints a 7bn deficit against a 5bn surplus previously
detail: The release showed a trade balance of -7bn, compared with 5bn in the previous period. No forecast was given.

headline: IMF warns eurozone measures to shield consumers from high energy prices could undermine the fight against inflation
detail: The IMF said eurozone government support to cushion consumers from high energy prices could weaken efforts to bring down inflation unless it is calibrated.

headline: Chancellor Reeves pitched London to UBS as a possible new headquarters as the bank weighs Swiss capital proposals, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that the UK government approached UBS about moving its headquarters to London. The Swiss bank is reviewing its options in response to new capital proposals.

headline: US Treasuries are on course for their best week since February as AI concerns pause the bond sell-off, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that US government borrowing costs have come down from their highest levels in decades as investors move into government debt for safety.

headline: Russia's Novak says the country has enough diesel to keep exporting despite refinery repairs
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said diesel supplies are sufficient for exports while refineries are being repaired. Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries are already a running story on the blotter.

headline: Russia's Novak says contracts must be in place before diesel supplies can begin, Interfax reports
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said contracts were needed before diesel deliveries could start, according to Interfax. The post gave no further details.

headline: BoE's Bailey says firms are cutting margins and costs rather than passing higher energy costs on to consumers
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey made the remarks at an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok. He said businesses were holding back from passing on higher energy costs and were squeezing margins and cutting costs instead.

headline: Russia's Novak says freight, insurance and diesel supply issues with the US are essentially resolved
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said questions over freight, insurance and diesel deliveries to the United States had largely been settled, according to reports.

headline: PBOC Governor Pan says exchange rate adjustments alone cannot fix global imbalances and backs closer China-EU financial cooperation
detail: The People's Bank of China governor said global imbalances cannot be resolved by relying on currency moves, and that China-EU financial cooperation should be taken to a new stage.

headline: Iran has exported some LPG and jet fuel since July despite the US naval blockade, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters, citing shipping intelligence and people involved in security, reports that Iran has managed to ship some liquefied petroleum gas and jet fuel since July even though a US naval blockade is in place.

headline: Germany's upper house approves a further release of oil stocks following the G7 agreement
detail: Germany's upper house of parliament has approved a further release of strategic oil stocks, in line with an agreement among G7 countries. No volumes were given.

headline: Ukraine offers to hold up to 10 bcm of EU strategic gas reserves in its underground storage
detail: Ukraine has proposed that the EU keep up to 10 bcm of European strategic gas reserves in Ukrainian underground storage. Separately, an acting chief executive said Ukraine's own stored gas is at about 16 bcm, its highest level in six years.

headline: Zelensky says Starlink is still not fully restored and Ukraine can no longer use it in mid-range strikes
detail: Ukrainian President Zelensky said Starlink speeds are improving but the White House has not yet lifted the throttling. He said the throttling puts civilians at risk and that European allies hold enough Patriot interceptors to get Ukraine through the winter.

headline: Zelensky says US-Russia diesel deal surprised Europe and asks US for anti-ballistic missiles if there is no energy ceasefire
detail: Ukraine's president also said he wants several negotiating tracks in the peace process, that Europe is taking some steps on its own track, and he declined to confirm whether Ukraine is striking Russian refineries again.

headline: Zelensky says Russia does not want talks in any format and expects US and Ukrainian negotiators to meet soon
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Putin has no interest in ending the war and that Donbas would not satisfy Moscow. He said he hopes US-Ukraine talks will take place in the coming days.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the bank is watching the weak yen, the Middle East and AI for their effect on price trends
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said stabilising inflation at 2% is becoming more important and that the G20 discussed how the Middle East and AI affect the economy. He said his view of AI-driven inflation pressure is broadly in line with what he heard from other global policymakers.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the next meeting will consider changing the view that underlying inflation is nearing 2%
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said the bank heard nothing at this week's meetings that departed from its baseline view, and that the timing and pace of further hikes will depend on how FX, AI demand and Middle East developments affect prices. He also said financial conditions remain accommodative.

headline: Zelensky calls the US-Russia diesel deal inappropriate, expects a gas deal to follow and rejects any deal on frozen Russian assets
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Ukraine cannot risk any deals on frozen Russian assets. He also said taking Donbas would not satisfy Putin and called current efforts to end the war a parody.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation cannot be allowed to rise further above 2% and the focus is now on entrenching 2%
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda also said he wants to judge the estimate of the neutral rate after taking account of the cumulative effect of past rate rises on financial conditions and domestic prices.

headline: China's commerce ministry warns the EU it will not gain from pressure and should not underestimate China's resolve
detail: China's commerce ministry said the EU should not expect to win concessions by pressuring China, and that Beijing is determined and able to protect its interests.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says there is no evidence the neutral rate sits at any specific level
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said there is no evidence that the neutral rate is around any particular level. He also said a policy shift comes when underlying inflation is close to 2%.

headline: Canadian housing starts rise to an annualised 248.896K in September, above the 232.5K forecast
detail: Canada's September housing starts came in at an annualised 248.896K, compared with a forecast of 232.5K and 229.0K the month before.

headline: Kalshi odds of an October Fed hike fall to 13% from 55% after Fed Chair Warsh's remarks
detail: Prediction market Kalshi puts the probability of a Fed hold in October at 86%, up from 50%, following Fed Chair Warsh's comments, according to a market commentary account.

headline: US import prices rise 1.1% m/m in September and export prices jump 2.2%, both above forecast
detail: US import prices rose 1.1% m/m against a 1% forecast and 0.7% previously. Export prices rose 2.2% m/m against a 0.9% forecast and 0.6% previously.

headline: US natural gas futures drop 5% after a force majeure is lifted
detail: A market wire reports that US natural gas futures fell 5% after a force majeure was lifted. The report does not say which facility was affected.

headline: German foreign minister says accommodating Putin would be the wrong signal and warns Russia's Black Sea actions put food supplies at risk
detail: Germany's foreign minister also says the Mercosur trade deal is already delivering positive results and that EU budget negotiations must be concluded this year.

headline: Trump says the US may need to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site but rules out nuclear weapons and ground troops
detail: In a Newsmax interview reported by Reuters, President Trump said the US may target the fortified underground site near one of Tehran's main nuclear facilities. He said the US would not use a nuclear bomb and was not considering sending ground troops to Iran.

headline: Bank of Italy raises Italy's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 1% from 0.6% and its 2027 forecast to 0.7% from 0.4%
detail: The Bank of Italy has raised its 2026 growth forecast for Italy to 1%, up from the 0.6% it projected in June. It has also lifted its 2027 forecast to 0.7% from 0.4%.

headline: German foreign minister says the US is still supporting Ukraine and Kyiv and Moscow will in the end have to negotiate
detail: Germany's foreign minister was asked about relations between Trump and Ukraine. He said the US is essentially still providing support to Ukraine and that Ukraine and Russia will ultimately have to negotiate.

headline: SNB's Tschudin says Swiss inflation pressure is slightly higher than in June
detail: Petra Tschudin of the Swiss National Bank's governing board said inflationary pressure in Switzerland is a little higher than it was in June.

headline: Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will hit fiscal headroom ahead of the Budget
detail: The Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will cut fiscal headroom in the upcoming Budget. This adds to its earlier estimate that headroom has halved to about £12bn in 2029-30 before Budget measures.

headline: US industrial production rises 0.7% m/m in September, above the 0.4% forecast; capacity utilisation at 76.9%
detail: US industrial production rose 0.7% m/m in September, after 0.0% the previous month and above the 0.4% forecast. Manufacturing output rose 0.3%, in line with forecast, after -0.3%. Capacity utilisation came in at 76.9%, against a 76.5% forecast and 76.3% previously.

headline: US Treasury yields rise after economic data, with the 10-year up 3.8bp to 5.125%
detail: The US 10-year yield rose 3.8bp to 5.125% after economic data. The 30-year rose 3.04bp to 5.458%, the 2-year rose 1.45bp to 4.766%, and the 2s10s spread stood at +35.7bp.

headline: US industrial production rises 2.25% y/y in September, up from 1.42% the previous month
detail: The annual figure for US industrial production in September was 2.25%, up from 1.42% in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

headline: Russia's Novak says Russian diesel will help balance the global market and the deal with the US benefits all fuel consumers
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak made the remarks about the US-Russia diesel deal on 16 October.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says Russia and the US are discussing Arctic and LNG projects
detail: Kirill Dmitriev, the Kremlin's envoy, said Russia and the US are in talks on projects in the Arctic and on liquefied natural gas. The remarks follow the recently reported US-Russia diesel deal.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says the US Treasury asked Russia's RDIF fund to help facilitate the US-Russia diesel deal
detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the US finance ministry asked the Russian Direct Investment Fund, which he heads, to facilitate the diesel deal between the two countries. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Eurozone final CPI is confirmed at 0.6% m/m in September, in line with forecast and up from 0.4%
detail: The final September eurozone figure showed consumer prices up 0.6% on the month, matching the 0.4% previous reading's forecast path at 0.6%. The annual rate was confirmed at 3.8%.

headline: US Treasury funds take in $3.6bn in the week, their 16th straight weekly inflow, BofA says
detail: BofA, citing EPFR data, said total bond fund inflows came to $11.8bn in the week to Wednesday. Equity funds took in $64.5bn over the same period.

headline: Kremlin's Peskov says Zelensky is not seeking a peaceful settlement and Russia shares Trump's view on this
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the Ukrainian president does not want to take responsibility or pursue a peaceful resolution, and that Moscow agrees with Trump on the point.

headline: Reports say John Healey is drawing up plans to tax banks in the forthcoming Budget
detail: City AM reports that John Healey is weighing options to raise more tax from the banking industry in the forthcoming Budget. City AM says senior banking figures have warned against the plans.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says Zelensky has overplayed his hand and is an obstacle to peace as peacemaking speeds up
detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Zelensky's attacks on President Trump would have significant consequences, and described peacemaking efforts as accelerating. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Hungary's PM Magyar says Budapest is ready to help diplomatically towards a Ukraine ceasefire and will continue talks with Kyiv
detail: Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar said he agreed with Zelensky to continue talks at ministerial level and to put relations on a new footing, and he expressed solidarity with Ukraine over Russia's aggression. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Zelensky says Putin has no interest in ending the war and Donbas would not be enough for Russia; open to talks in Budapest
detail: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Putin is playing with words and does not want the war to end, and the issue goes beyond withdrawal from Donbas. He said he would not mind going to Budapest, wants several negotiation tracks, and said European allies have enough Patriot interceptors for Ukraine to get through winter.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says G20 talks did not depart from the bank's baseline and FX, AI and the Middle East will set the timing of hikes
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said nothing he heard at this week's meetings deviated from the bank's baseline view, and he saw no big gap with global policymakers on inflationary pressure from AI demand. He said the timing and pace of further rate rises will depend on the effects of currency moves, AI demand and Middle East developments on prices.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the neutral rate estimate will reflect how past hikes have fed through to financial conditions and prices
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said he wants to assess the neutral rate estimate in light of the cumulative effect of earlier rate rises on financial conditions and domestic prices. He also said underlying inflation being quite close to 2% marks the policy shift.

headline: German foreign minister says Europe is in Iran's sights and Iran's hostile activities will not be tolerated
detail: Germany's foreign minister made the remarks on Friday in the same appearance as his comments on Ukraine, the EU budget talks and the Mercosur deal. He also said it is imperative that EU budget negotiations are concluded this year.

headline: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh, the Yanbu export hub and southern Saudi Arabia
detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two cruise missiles over the Red Sea, a ballistic missile launched towards Yanbu, and three drones over the southern and Riyadh regions. Saudi Arabia said Riyadh, Yanbu and southern areas had been targeted; no market reaction was reported.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says the Graham sanctions bill blocks Russia-US investment cooperation
detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the sanctions bill sponsored by the late Senator Graham blocks Russia-US investment cooperation. He said there was growing recognition in the US that the bill was a mistake.

headline: US Energy Department seeks an exchange of up to 17m barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
detail: The US Department of Energy is offering up to 17m barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve through an exchange, according to wire headlines.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev says Russia and the US are discussing joint data centre projects and will announce more initiatives soon
detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the projects could draw on power from Russian nuclear stations. He said further joint initiatives beyond the diesel deal would be announced soon, and some would go ahead before Russia's military operation in Ukraine ends.

headline: NatWest is no longer a US Treasury primary dealer, New York Fed says
detail: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York's list shows NatWest has stopped being a primary dealer.

headline: Germany's Merz says the EU budget needs further cuts and expects another European Council meeting in November
detail: German Chancellor Merz said the European budget must be reduced further and that additional European Council meetings are expected in November. He said he hopes for a budget agreement before the end of the year but is not sure it will happen.

headline: Germany's Merz says a 90bn loan will not cover Ukraine's needs and the Commission will assess its financial aid needs
detail: German Chancellor Merz said the European Commission will assess over the coming weeks how much financial aid Ukraine needs. He said a 90bn loan would not be enough.

headline: Germany's Merz says Italy largely backs the German-French plan to phase out coal-fired power stations by 2035
detail: German Chancellor Merz said Italy is largely in agreement with a joint German-French proposal to phase out coal-fired power generation by 2035.

headline: Germany's Merz says Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy and communications targets are understandable; EU weighs Russian visa curbs
detail: German Chancellor Merz said Ukraine attacking Russian targets that hinder its war effort, including energy and communications infrastructure, is understandable. He said the EU summit is discussing restrictions on issuing visas to Russians and that there is still room for manoeuvre.

headline: UK consumer confidence slips to a five-month low in October, LSEG/Ipsos survey shows
detail: The monthly LSEG/Ipsos survey shows UK consumer confidence edged lower in October to its weakest level in five months. The post gave no index figure.

headline: Italy and the European Commission agree on a gas price cap law
detail: Italy and the European Commission have reached agreement on a law capping gas prices, according to a market news feed. The report gave no details of the terms.

headline: Kremlin says Russia's security zone will not be part of any Ukraine negotiation; Putin says 10% of Donetsk is still to be taken
detail: The Kremlin said the security zone Russia is building will not be up for negotiation with Ukraine. It also quoted Putin as saying Russian forces have yet to take 10% of the Donetsk region, and Putin said 310 populated areas have been captured since the start of the year.

headline: Putin says Russian forces fully control Luhansk; Kremlin says 450 km of a 660 km border security strip is under Russian control
detail: Putin said the Luhansk region is now entirely under the control of Russian forces and that work on the security zone along the Ukrainian border is going well. The Kremlin said the strip runs for 660 km, of which 450 km is currently held by Russia.

headline: Russia's Gerasimov tells Putin the army has begun strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities and plans to hit strategic bridges
detail: Russia's Chief of the General Staff, Valery Gerasimov, reported to President Putin that strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities have begun and that strategic bridges are also planned targets, according to reports from Russia.

headline: US lawmakers introduce a bill to block Trump's diesel deal with Russia
detail: A bill to block the Trump administration's diesel deal with Russia has been introduced in Congress. Its sponsors are mostly Democrats, with one Republican among them.

headline: France-Germany car deal seeks to dilute EU 2035 CO2 targets and opens the way for UK trusted-partner status under Made in EU rules
detail: France and Germany said on Friday that their car industry agreement would water down EU-wide CO2 emission targets for 2035. It would also open the door for Britain to be treated as a trusted partner under the EU's Made in EU rules, Reuters reports.

headline: Brent climbs to session highs and trades near $107 a barrel
detail: Market reports say oil prices rose to their highs of the session, with Brent near $107/bbl. The move came as Russian officials reported strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

headline: Putin says Russia's offensive is running along the whole front line at a faster pace and calls the capture of Dobropillya significant
detail: Russian reports say Putin described taking Dobropillya as opening the way to the DPR's borders, said taking the DPR remains a main task and called for better protection of civilian infrastructure. Russia's chief of general staff Gerasimov said the armed forces had launched massive strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities.

headline: Scottish government is set to drop its opposition to new North Sea oil and gas fields, Politico reports
detail: Politico reports that the Scottish government is preparing to drop its opposition to developing new oil and gas fields. No timing or further detail was given.

headline: Putin orders the military to keep up massive strikes on Ukraine's defence industry and logistics centres
detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin told the military to keep carrying out massive and group strikes on Ukraine's military-industrial sites and logistics centres, according to reports. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Oil extends gains as US crude climbs above $100 a barrel
detail: Oil prices extended their gains in late trading on 16 October, and US crude rose above $100 a barrel.

headline: Brent jumps more than $3 to a new session high of $109.58 a barrel
detail: Brent crude futures rose more than $3 to a session high of $109.58 a barrel. US crude futures gained more than $2 to go above $100, with reports citing ongoing Middle East supply concerns and an outage at a Russian refinery.

headline: FT says the financial sector's lobbying against a possible UK bank tax rise in the Budget may have been hurt by splits among big lenders
detail: The Financial Times reports that bankers are uneasy about a possible tax rise in the forthcoming Budget. It says the sector's lobbying may have been weakened by divisions between the large lenders.

headline: US crude futures jump more than $3 to a session high of $101.02, the highest since 21 September
detail: US crude futures rose by more than $3 to $101.02 a barrel in late trading on Friday, according to a market wire report. This is their highest level since 21 September.

headline: Trump says oil prices will come down very soon
detail: US President Trump said oil prices would fall soon. He made the remarks while discussing inflation, as US crude traded at a session high.

headline: EU leaders ask the Commission for a proposal on Ukraine's extra 2027 financing needs; Costa says Russia's actions point to escalation
detail: European Council President Costa said EU leaders have asked the European Commission to put forward a proposal covering Ukraine's additional financing needs for 2027. He also said Russia's actions indicate escalation.

headline: Trump says the US was not behind limits on Ukraine's access to the Starshield system
detail: US President Trump said the US did not restrict Ukraine's access to the Starshield system and that he does not know who ordered it.

headline: France's Macron says the US-Russia diesel deal is unhelpful and breeds doubt and defiance
detail: French President Macron criticised the US diesel deal with Russia on Friday. Ukraine's Zelensky and US lawmakers had already objected to the deal.

headline: EU's von der Leyen calls the China trade imbalance structural and unsustainable and says EU leaders are united on China
detail: European Commission President von der Leyen spoke after China's commerce ministry warned the EU against applying pressure.

headline: EU's von der Leyen says the bloc will work on new instruments to tackle the trade imbalance with China
detail: The European Commission President said on Friday that the EU would develop new instruments to address its trade imbalance with China. She spoke after an EU leaders' meeting.

headline: France's Macron says an EU budget deal is possible by year-end and argues against a March summit before the French election
detail: The French President said agreement on the EU budget could be reached by the end of the year. He said holding the budget deal summit in March, weeks before the French election, would not be a good approach.

headline: IMF head calls for global cooperation on risks from AI and the prolonged Middle East war
detail: Reuters reports that the IMF Managing Director on Friday urged global leaders to cooperate in the face of several economic risks, including rapid advances in AI and a prolonged war in the Middle East. Washington pointed to what it calls US-led economic momentum.

headline: Trump says Russia will release diesel under the US-Russia deal and calls it a deal for the world
detail: The US President was speaking to reporters on Friday about the US-Russia diesel deal. Other leaders had criticised the deal earlier in the day.

headline: EU's von der Leyen puts Ukraine's funding gap for 2027 at 70bn
detail: European Commission President von der Leyen gave the 70bn figure for Ukraine's 2027 funding shortfall. EU leaders have asked the Commission for a proposal on Ukraine's additional financing needs for that year.

headline: European Council President Costa calls for the EU long-term budget to be agreed by year-end
detail: European Council President Costa said the EU's long-term budget needs to be agreed by the end of the year.

headline: Resolution Foundation says the UK has had the equivalent of 13 years of normal inflation in five years
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the UK has had about 13 years' worth of normal inflation over the past five years. It also says the cost of living crisis hit the UK harder than other countries.

headline: Iran says it is ready to help resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen
detail: A market news account reported that Iran has offered to help settle the Saudi-Yemen conflict. The post did not say which Iranian official made the offer. The offer follows the Saudi-led coalition's report that it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and the Yanbu export hub.

headline: US fiscal 2026 deficit widens to $1.992trn from $1.775trn; gross interest on debt hits a record $1.36trn
detail: The US Treasury puts the fiscal 2026 deficit at $1.992trn, against $1.775trn in fiscal 2025, with net customs receipts of $173.22bn compared with $194.87bn. Gross interest on the debt reached a record $1.36trn, up $144bn or 12% on the previous year.

headline: EU's von der Leyen says the Commission will propose import curbs on further Chinese sectors
detail: European Commission President von der Leyen said on Friday that the Commission will propose curbs on Chinese imports that go beyond the safeguard measures agreed with Beijing to halve shipments of Chinese hybrid cars.

headline: US CENTCOM says over 100m barrels of oil were shipped through Hormuz in the past 7 days with US help
detail: US Central Command said the US has helped move more than 100m barrels through the Strait of Hormuz over the past seven days. US officials also said about 400 merchant ships transited the strait in that period.

headline: US posts a $26.9bn budget deficit for September
detail: The US Treasury reported a September budget deficit of $26.9bn, the final month of a fiscal year in which the deficit reached $1.992trn.

headline: US CENTCOM commander says the US naval blockade has halted all of Iran's maritime exports and imports
detail: The commander of US Central Command said in a post on X that Iran currently has no seaborne exports or imports because of the US naval blockade. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Brent futures reach $110 a barrel for the first time since 20 May
detail: Brent futures rose to $110 a barrel, a level last seen on 20 May, extending the day's gains.

headline: WTI crude futures settle up $3.44, or 3.51%, at $101.41 a barrel
detail: NYMEX WTI crude futures settled at $101.41 a barrel, up $3.44 or 3.51%. November diesel futures settled at $4.8991 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.2354 a gallon.

headline: Brent crude futures settle up $3.94, or 3.72%, at $109.86 a barrel
detail: Brent crude futures settle at $109.86 a barrel, up $3.94 or 3.72% on the session.

headline: US net interest payments on debt reach a record $1.05trn in fiscal 2026
detail: The US paid a record $1.05trn in net interest on its debt in the 2026 fiscal year, according to the US budget figures.

headline: US TIC data show net long-term inflows of $279.2bn, up from -$27.9bn; overall net capital flows at $199.8bn
detail: US Treasury International Capital data put net long-term transactions at $279.2bn, against -$27.9bn previously. Overall net capital flows came in at $199.8bn, compared with a revised $87.4bn the previous month.

headline: US TIC data show China's Treasury holdings fall to $591bn and Japan's to $1.068trn in August; UK holdings rise to $1.010trn
detail: US Treasury TIC data show China's holdings of US Treasuries at $591bn in August against $618bn in July, Japan's at $1.068trn against $1.104trn, and the UK's at $1.010trn against $998bn. Net foreign holdings of Treasury bonds and notes rose by $108.9bn in August after falling by $3.6bn in July.

headline: Trump says the Iran conflict will be over very soon
detail: US President Trump said the situation with Iran will end very soon. He gave no timetable or details.

headline: UK Foreign Office now advises against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia
detail: The UK Foreign Office has changed its travel advice for Saudi Arabia to advise against all but essential travel. The change follows reports earlier in the day of missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and the Yanbu export hub.

headline: Zelenskyy offers to stop strikes on Russian refineries if the US sends more interceptors and accuses Trump of pushing Ukraine to capitulate
detail: Ukraine's president proposed halting strikes on Russian oil refineries in return for more air-defence interceptors. He cited delayed Patriot deliveries, Starlink restrictions and eased Russia-related sanctions as US pressure for concessions to Russia.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says enforcement of the Graham sanctions on Russia is suspended for now, not ended
detail: Wright said extra Russian diesel exports would benefit US consumers and the world. He described the US-Russia diesel deal, agreed before Russia moved to scale back the war, as an innovative route to peace.

headline: City of London Corporation considers tax rises and service cuts to close a £70mn budget gap
detail: The FT reports that the Corporation is preparing for the government's overhaul of local authority funding, and that the Barbican Centre's future is uncertain.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation is near 2% and the Middle East conflict is adding to energy-led price pressures
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said Japan is seeing a positive cycle of rising wages and recovering prices, and that anchoring underlying inflation around 2% is becoming more important. He said strong global demand and a tight labour market are also adding to inflation; dollar/yen was reported 0.19% lower at 157.72.

headline: RBA's Kent says neutral rates appear to be rising in Australia and abroad and questions whether policy is restrictive enough
detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Kent said policy is somewhat restrictive but it is unclear whether it is restrictive enough, and the RBA faces a hard trade-off between inflation and unemployment. He said household demand is softening while business credit stays strong, and that long-term inflation expectations look well anchored.

headline: Trump says his recent Russia moves are meant to keep Moscow in peace talks and reports great progress
detail: Trump said signing a Russia document now could push Moscow out of the talks, told Russia to stay away from supporting Iran, and criticised Ukraine's strikes on Russian diesel refineries for hurting global diesel markets. Separately, the UK reaffirmed its support for tougher sanctions on Russia.

headline: Putin proposes a summit with Trump and Xi on Ukraine's future, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reported that Russian President Putin has asked Trump and Chinese President Xi for a three-way meeting to decide Ukraine's future.

headline: UK-listed company profit warnings hit their highest level in nearly two years as energy costs rise, EY says
detail: EY analysis shows London-listed companies issued 65 profit warnings over the summer, up from 59 in the second quarter, with higher energy costs linked to the Iran war among the causes cited.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the bond taper approach is unchanged and declines to preannounce timing of any emergency JGB market measures
detail: The BoJ Governor said the bank will look at market conditions, including how fast long-term rates rise and signs of instability, when deciding whether to intervene. He added that long-term rates would probably rise steadily if the bank raises its short-term rate, and that setting policy properly to reach the 2% target would help stabilise the JGB market.

headline: French 10-year bond futures fall and the euro eases after weekend rioting across France
detail: French 10-year note futures dropped in early Asian trading after unrest in France over the weekend, according to market reports. Reuters reported that the euro eased in the wake of the rioting.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says sanctions on Russian crude stay in place and the exemptions cover diesel only
detail: Wright said the recent exemptions apply only to diesel supplies under General Licence 135, issued on 9 October, which permits certain transactions in Russian-origin diesel to ease global shortages.

headline: Brent slips 1.7% to $108 a barrel and WTI falls to near $97.50 in Asian trading
detail: Market reports said traders were weighing Middle East tensions against fairly stable regional supplies, and one report linked the WTI fall to the US waiver on Russian oil sanctions. US 10-year Treasury yields held at 5.06% as expectations of an imminent Fed rate rise eased.

headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says JGB issuance will be kept at an appropriate level and she has no fixed view on an extra budget
detail: Prime Minister Takaichi said she has no preconceived position on whether the government will compile a supplementary budget. She added that building a robust economy can strengthen market confidence in the yen.

headline: China Q3 GDP grows 4.5% y/y, beating the 4.4% poll; September retail sales rise 1.1% y/y and industrial output 5.5%
detail: China's statistics bureau reports Q3 GDP up 4.5% y/y, compared with 4.3% previously, and up 1.2% q/q. In September the jobless rate eased to 5.2% from 5.3%, while fixed-asset investment for January to September fell 7.2% y/y and property investment fell 20.6%.

headline: China's new home prices fall 2.8% y/y in September, a smaller drop than August's 3.0%
detail: A source calculation based on statistics bureau data shows the 2.8% annual fall. In Shenzhen prices fell 1.0% y/y but rose 0.3% m/m, and in Guangzhou they fell 1.1% y/y and rose 0.2% m/m.

headline: BoE examines Barclays after complaint that traders understated the risk of private credit exposure, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that the Bank of England received a complaint that Barclays understated the risk of derivatives it used to finance private credit loans, and is scrutinising the lender's disclosures.

headline: US Secretary of State Rubio says Trump will consider any route to ending the Ukraine war and intelligence sharing with Kyiv continues
detail: Rubio said the US would keep looking for chances to end the conflict but did not confirm details of a proposed meeting. He also said intelligence sharing with Ukraine has not been paused.

headline: Euro stays under selling pressure against sterling as French political instability continues
detail: A market commentary headline reports continued selling of the euro against sterling, linked to political instability in France after weekend rioting. No levels were given.

headline: China's Commerce Ministry announces changes to export control work on dual-use items, effective 18 November
detail: China's Commerce Ministry has announced further changes to how it identifies and handles export control concerns for dual-use items. It says the announcement takes effect officially on 18 November.

headline: Average UK two-year fixed mortgage rate climbs to 5.55% from 5.29% a month ago, homes portal data show
detail: Data from a homes portal reported by City AM put the average two-year fixed rate at 5.55%, compared with 5.29% last month and 4.25% before the war in Iran. The report says sellers are cutting asking prices as higher rates weigh on the housing market.

headline: China expected to hold benchmark lending rates for a 17th straight month in October, Reuters poll shows
detail: A Reuters survey shows China is expected to keep its benchmark lending rates unchanged in October. Reuters says Q3 GDP came in stronger than expected, which reduced the chances of easing in the near term.

headline: Russia strikes energy facilities in 11 Ukrainian regions overnight, Ukraine's deputy energy minister says
detail: Ukraine's deputy energy minister reported overnight Russian attacks on energy infrastructure across 11 regions. Russia's chief of general staff had earlier told Putin that strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities had begun.

headline: China says it will hold talks to set up a dialogue mechanism on export controls
detail: Market headlines on 19 October report that China plans talks on an export-control dialogue mechanism. The reports do not say who the other party is. This follows its earlier announcement of changes to export controls on dual-use items, effective 18 November.

headline: CFTC data show speculators' largest net euro short since January 2016, SocGen says, with the market heavily long dollars
detail: SocGen says the latest CFTC positioning data show the biggest net short position in the euro since January 2016. It adds that the market is also holding large long positions in the dollar.

headline: Brent drops below $105 a barrel, down 2.43% on the day; WTI falls 2.21% to $96.76
detail: Brent crude fell under $105.00 a barrel in early European trading, a 2.43% fall on the day. WTI fell 2.21% to $96.76 a barrel.

headline: UBS now expects the ECB to raise rates by 25bp in March 2027 after a December hike
detail: UBS has changed its ECB call. It previously expected the hiking cycle to end in December and now also expects a 25bp increase in March 2027.

headline: US Secretary of State Rubio says Ukraine and Russia should concentrate on ending the war
detail: Rubio made the remarks on arriving in Uzbekistan for meetings with officials of the C5+1 grouping of the US and post-Soviet Central Asian states, Reuters reports.

headline: Goldman Sachs says its cross-asset sentiment and positioning gauge falls to its lowest since April
detail: Goldman Sachs says its sentiment and positioning indicator has fallen to its lowest level since April and has decoupled from strong global PMIs. The bank points to stronger fixed income fund flows, positioning in gold and the yen, and a sharp fall in hedge fund net leverage.

headline: PBOC governor says China will launch a liquidity support tool for large-scale redemptions at non-bank institutions
detail: The People's Bank of China governor announced plans for a liquidity facility to support non-bank financial institutions facing large-scale redemptions. No size or timing was given.

headline: PBOC governor widens eligibility for standing lending facilities and plans to let overseas institutions trade RMB onshore
detail: The People's Bank of China governor also announced steps to promote bond market connectivity and to make it easier for overseas financial institutions to trade renminbi in China's domestic foreign exchange market, CCTV reported. The measures were announced alongside the liquidity support tool for non-bank institutions.

headline: PBOC governor says the bank will study moving its main open market operation tenor to overnight at an appropriate time
detail: China's central bank governor said the change would aim to make interest rate regulation more precise, according to Chinese state media.

headline: Trafigura economist puts Middle East crude flows 5m-7m b/d below pre-war levels and product flows 4m b/d lower
detail: The chief economist at commodity trader Trafigura gave the estimates for reduced Middle East crude and oil product flows compared with before the war.

headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says a Russia-China-US summit would only encourage Putin to keep fighting
detail: Ukraine's foreign minister criticised the proposed summit of Russia, China and the US, saying it would encourage Putin to continue the war. This follows reports that Putin has proposed a summit with Trump and Xi on Ukraine's future.

headline: Chancellor Healey reportedly weighs income tax on family business handovers before his first Budget
