detail: City AM, citing a report, says Chancellor John Healey is considering charging income tax when owners pass companies to their children, which could nearly double the tax bill. The report says the plans are aimed at avoiding spending cuts.

headline: French borrowing costs rise 0.1 percentage point as bond selling resumes; 10-year spread over Germany back at 1.45 percentage points
detail: The FT reports that French government bonds are under renewed selling pressure today, lifting borrowing costs by 0.1 percentage point. That takes the extra yield France pays over Germany on 10-year debt back up to 1.45 percentage points.

headline: Kremlin says a proposed Putin-Trump-Xi summit has no agenda or substantive agreements yet and a Ukraine deal needs Kyiv's participation
detail: The Kremlin said there is no agenda yet for the proposed summit of Putin, Trump and Xi, and no substantive agreements have been reached. It also said a final peace settlement for Ukraine is hardly possible unless someone from Kyiv's side takes part.

headline: French PM Lecornu orders partial curfews after riots and says the finance ministry can fully fund short-time working
detail: French Prime Minister Lecornu said he had asked prefectures and some local authorities to impose partial curfews tonight, that the government will support business, and that the finance ministry can fund short-time working at 100%. He said about 80% of those still in custody will be prosecuted.

headline: Report says a breakthrough to halt US-Iran escalation is expected to be announced this week
detail: A market newswire reports that mediators are still working to narrow the points of contention between the US and Iran. The report names no source, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: French PM Lecornu says the government would declare a state of emergency if it were judged necessary
detail: France's prime minister made the remark as rioting continues across the country. French bonds have already been under selling pressure today because of the unrest.

headline: Iranian hardliners call for nuclear weapons after the killing of Supreme Leader Khamenei, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that hardliners in Iran are pushing to weaponise the enrichment programme. They say Khamenei, who had prohibited atomic bombs, has been killed.

headline: French PM says intelligence agencies warn the far left could try to disrupt the presidential election
detail: French PM Lecornu says intelligence agencies have briefed him on the risk. Separately, President Macron condemns looting and vandalism during cost-of-living protests and orders a review of intelligence and police preparedness.

headline: IRGC spokesman warns that even limited US action against Iran would set off a global energy crisis
detail: A spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards gave the warning, Sepah News reported. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Iraq's October oil exports average over 3.4m b/d so far, up from 3m b/d in September, reports say
detail: Reports put Iraq's crude exports at an average of more than 3.4 million barrels per day so far in October, compared with 3 million barrels per day in September.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK household energy bills are due to rise again in January
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the next rise in household energy bills is due in January. It notes that 46% of domestic gas use falls in the first quarter of the year.

headline: Canadian CPI rises 3.1% y/y, below the 3.2% forecast; CPI-median measure at 1.9%
detail: Canada's annual CPI came in at 3.1%, against a 3.2% forecast and up from 3.0% previously. The CPI-median core measure was 1.9%, against a 2% forecast and down from 2.0%.

headline: Canadian CPI rises 0.1% m/m in September, below the 0.2% forecast; CPI-trim slows to 1.8% and CPI-common to 2.4%
detail: Canada's September CPI rose 0.1% on the month against a 0.2% forecast, after -0.1% previously. CPI-trim came in at 1.8% (forecast 1.9%, previous 1.9%), CPI-common at 2.4% (previous 2.6%) and BoC core CPI at 2.2% y/y (previous 2.4%), with core flat on the month.

headline: Swap pricing for a Bank of Canada rate hike in October falls to 68% from 74% after Canadian CPI data
detail: Swap market data put the chance of a Bank of Canada hike in October at 68%, down from 74% before the September inflation release.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says US inflation appears to need more work again
detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said US inflation appears to need further work again. In the same remarks, he described discretionary travel as a sign that consumers feel confident.

headline: Egypt's parliament to vote this week on letting its armed forces help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
detail: Reuters reports that Egypt's parliament is expected to vote this week on authorising its military to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen's Houthis. The support would be given if Riyadh asks for it.

headline: Zelenskiy says some types of essential US supplies to Ukraine are being delayed
detail: Ukraine's president said deliveries of some categories of essential supplies from the US have been delayed. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Chinese Premier urges all sides in the Iran conflict to choose peace and return to talks soon
detail: According to Xinhua, China's Premier said all parties concerned should opt for peace and resume dialogue and negotiations at an early date. He also said Beijing is ready to advance exchanges and cooperation with Iran.

headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says Kyiv faces obstacles in getting interceptors against Russian ballistic missiles
detail: Ukraine's foreign minister said the country is running into obstacles in obtaining interceptors to counter Russian ballistic missiles.

headline: Egypt's parliament delays its vote on military support for Saudi Arabia to 26 October
detail: Lawmakers said the Egyptian parliament has pushed back to 26 October its vote on letting the armed forces help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. The vote had been expected this week.

headline: Iran's foreign minister blames the US for Strait of Hormuz tensions and says Iran-US and Ukraine disputes need negotiated settlements
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said the US bears responsibility for insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and that regional issues should be settled through diplomacy, according to state TV. He said Iran-US talks, Ukraine and the Hormuz situation came up in his discussions, and that both the Ukraine and Iran-US conflicts should be resolved by negotiation rather than war.

headline: Russia's Lavrov calls for restoring free navigation through Hormuz and says neither Ukraine nor others are ready for talks
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov called for a return to pre-crisis conditions in the Middle East, including freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and for Yemen negotiations to resume. He said Russia would prefer to reach its goals in Ukraine through talks, that it sticks to its investment and nuclear agreements with Iran, and that it has no interest in volatile energy prices.

headline: Iran's foreign minister says attacks on ships in the Caspian Sea are a serious concern and calls on Europe to drop double standards
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi also said diplomacy is the only route open to the US in the dispute with Iran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US NAHB housing market index falls to 29 in October, below the 31 forecast and down from 32
detail: The US NAHB housing market index came in at 29, against a forecast of 31 and a previous reading of 32.

headline: Iran's foreign minister accuses European countries of complicity in the US war with Iran
detail: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi also said Tehran would welcome any proposal that guarantees regional security without a foreign presence.

headline: Russia's Lavrov calls US and Israeli action against Iran baseless and offers help in resolving the crisis
detail: Russian foreign minister Lavrov said Moscow is ready to help find a way out of the crisis.

headline: China threatens to retaliate if the UK keeps restrictions on Chinese electric vehicles
detail: China's Commerce Ministry says it will firmly counter any UK move to press ahead with restrictive measures against Chinese EVs.

headline: Violent protests spread from France to Italy and Belgium, with looting and clashes in Milan, Brussels and Liège
detail: The FT reports looting and clashes with police in Milan, Brussels, Liège and Tirana as unrest spreads beyond France. No market reaction was reported.

headline: French 10-year yield climbs further to 4.94%, up 16bp on the day
detail: French 10-year government bond yields extended their rise to stand 16bp higher at 4.94%. The move follows weekend rioting across France and continuing political instability.

headline: French 10-year yields on course for their biggest one-day rise since March 2025
detail: A market newswire headline reports the move as French bond selling continues amid political unrest and rioting. No new yield level was given.

headline: Yemen's Houthi-run forces threaten Riyadh and say Saudi oil facilities are targets for their missiles
detail: A military source with the Houthi-run Yemeni armed forces said the Saudi capital would not be safe and that Saudi oil facilities are within missile range, Iran's Fars news agency reported. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Bank of Canada business survey shows a weaker outlook and higher inflation expectations after Canada-US trade talks failed
detail: The Bank of Canada's September survey of business leaders shows firms' outlook got worse. Their inflation expectations rose after Canada-US trade talks broke down.

headline: Bank of Canada Q3 business survey indicator improves to -0.33; consumers' five-year inflation expectations rise to 3.91%
detail: The Bank of Canada's Q3 Business Outlook Survey, mostly conducted before Canada-US trade talks collapsed, shows its indicator at -0.33, up from a revised -0.39 in Q2. The share of firms expecting a recession next year fell to 6% from 17%, and 41% expect inflation above 3% over the next two years, down from 44%. In the separate consumer survey, five-year inflation expectations rose to 3.91% from 3.39%, and 53.0% of Canadians expect a recession, down from 54.6%.

headline: Iran's navy says US forces have struck its Konark base
detail: Iran's navy said US forces had carried out a strike on its Konark base. No market reaction was reported alongside the claim.

headline: Iran's first vice president says Tehran has no choice but to take control of the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran's first vice president Aref, cited by state news agency IRNA, said Iran must assert control over Hormuz, and that passage through the strait can be made easier for friendly nations. The posts report no market reaction.

headline: France to impose 8pm curfew in Lille and other northern cities after riots, reports say
detail: Reports say France will bring in an 8pm curfew in Lille and other cities in the north of the country. The government had already ordered partial curfews after the riots.

headline: Houthis say they have attacked Saudi energy, airport and military targets, including an Aramco site in Yanbu
detail: Yemen's Houthi-run forces announced several military operations deep inside Saudi territory, saying the targets included energy facilities, airports and military sites, among them an Aramco site in Yanbu. The batch reports no market reaction.

headline: IRGC spokesman says new weapons and targets will be revealed in a new phase of the war with the US
detail: Fars News reported that a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards said new weapons and targets would be unveiled and that Iran would drive what is left of US power out of the region.

headline: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oilfield and on airports in Riyadh and Abha
detail: Yemen's Houthi forces say they attacked the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid airport in Riyadh and Abha airport. The posts do not report any damage to oil output or any market reaction.

headline: Adviser to Iran's supreme leader rejects claims that the Strait of Hormuz is open
detail: An adviser to Iran's supreme leader said claims that the Strait of Hormuz is open have no basis, Tasnim News reported.

headline: Netanyahu says Trump sees the final removal of the Iranian threat as the key issue
detail: Israeli PM Netanyahu referred to Trump's support ahead of Israel's elections and said the final removal of the Iranian threat to Israel is the central question, Israel's Channel 14 News reported.

headline: Scotiabank expects the Bank of Canada to raise rates by 25bp next week
detail: Scotiabank expects a 25bp Bank of Canada hike at next week's decision, a report said.

headline: Netanyahu reportedly tells Trump that Israel still has work to finish
detail: Israel Hayom reports that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told US President Trump that Israel's work is not yet complete. The report comes as US-Iran tensions continue.

headline: French authorities extend curfews to Paris, covering Place de la République and Les Halles from 2000 GMT
detail: BFM TV reports that French authorities have ordered a curfew for the Place de la République and Les Halles areas of Paris from 2000 GMT. It follows earlier curfews in Lille and other northern cities after riots.

headline: Brent turns higher on the day and WTI extends gains after Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure
detail: Brent was last up 0.15% and WTI up 1.5% after the Houthis said they had attacked Saudi infrastructure. Brent had earlier been down 2.43% on the day, below $105 a barrel.

headline: Germany's Merz says there is no rush to decide on ECB posts, though a quick decision could be reached if needed
detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said there is no need for a fast decision on ECB positions, but added that agreement on the jobs could be reached quickly if required.

headline: Lyon imposes a city-centre curfew from 9pm Monday to 6am Tuesday as French unrest continues
detail: The local prefecture announced the overnight curfew in Lyon city centre. It follows curfews already ordered in Paris, Lille and other northern cities after the riots.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says talks with the UK on releasing diesel stocks are continuing
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said on Monday that discussions with the UK on diesel stock releases are still under way. No figures or timing were given.

headline: Barclays says its £15bn private credit book meets accounting and capital rules after report of Bank of England scrutiny
detail: Barclays said its £15 billion private credit exposure was treated in line with accounting and regulatory capital requirements, Reuters reports. The statement follows a report that the Bank of England was examining whether the bank's traders had understated the risk.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the US is converting sanctioned dark tankers into legitimate vessels
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said sanctioned tankers are being converted into legitimate tankers. He added that the number converted could run from dozens to hundreds.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says Tehran is ready to settle issues with regional countries through dialogue
detail: Reports say Pezeshkian stated that Iran has no fundamental differences with countries in the region. Separately, Iran told Russia it welcomes any regional peace initiative.

headline: Bank of Japan sees inflation close to its 2% target and is preparing a policy pivot, Nikkei reports
detail: Nikkei reports that the Bank of Japan judges inflation to be near its 2% target and is getting ready for a change in policy direction.

headline: Germany's Merz says Berlin is committing more than €500bn by the end of the decade to defence and military infrastructure
detail: German Chancellor Merz described the programme as the biggest modernisation drive in Germany's recent history. In the same remarks he said Russia and its allies, from North Korea to Iran, are attacking post-war democratic values as well as Ukraine.

headline: US official denies Iran's claim that US forces struck an Iranian naval base
detail: A US official told a CNN reporter that Iran's claim that the US had struck one of its naval bases is inaccurate. Iran's navy had earlier said US forces hit its Konark base.

headline: WTI crude settles 2.22% higher at $103.66 a barrel, up $2.25
detail: NYMEX November WTI futures settled at $103.66 a barrel, up $2.25 or 2.22% on the day. November diesel futures settled at $4.9201 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.1914 a gallon.

headline: IRGC spokesman says Iran could widen its blockade beyond Hormuz to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal
detail: The Tehran Times reports an IRGC spokesman as saying Iran has not yet fully closed the Strait of Hormuz and could extend the blockade to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Israel's finance minister Smotrich calls for annexing Lebanese territory up to current Israeli lines, and further if Hezbollah attacks
detail: Israeli Finance Minister Smotrich said Israel should annex Lebanon at least up to where its forces are now positioned, and advance as far as Beirut and beyond if Hezbollah attacks again. No market reaction was reported.

headline: IRGC spokesman points to seven major undersea data cables under the Strait of Hormuz in a warning to Iran's enemies
detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards spokesman said seven major cables carrying global internet and business data run beneath the Strait of Hormuz, and told the enemy to bear this in mind, Fars News reported. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days still stands if the US accepts its conditions
detail: Iran said the offer to reopen the strait remains available on condition that Washington accepts Tehran's terms. Tensions and attacks around the waterway are continuing.

headline: Trump says the Iran situation is good, Putin is staying out of Iran and the US is negotiating with Putin on Ukraine
detail: In remarks on Monday evening, US President Trump said the situation regarding Iran was good and that Putin was leaving Iran alone. He also said Washington was negotiating with Putin on Ukraine and did not want to break off those talks.

headline: Trump says the US is negotiating with Russia on Iran and diesel and is open to a trilateral meeting with Russia and China
detail: Speaking live, the US President said he would schedule a joint meeting with Xi and Putin on the basis of denuclearisation, said Russia has been fine on Ukraine, and said he did not think Zelenskiy wants to end the war. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Trump says it may be time for someone other than Zelenskiy to negotiate on Ukraine's behalf
detail: US President Trump said Zelenskiy does not know what he is talking about, and that the US shares intelligence with Ukraine and gives it a lot but gets nothing back. In the same remarks he said Russia had done very little to help Iran and called that positive.

headline: Trump says Russia could have done much more to help Iran
detail: President Trump made the remark in comments to reporters on Monday evening, alongside further remarks on Ukraine and the protests in France. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says he would discuss Ukraine with China's Xi and calls Xi's stance on the war very fair
detail: US President Trump said he would be willing to talk to Chinese President Xi about Ukraine and described Xi's position on Ukraine as very fair. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine could halt strikes on Russian refineries if the US helps supply Patriot missiles
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv could stop hitting Russian refineries for a period in exchange for US help with Patriot missiles. He also said the Pentagon is delaying missile deliveries under the PURL programme, and called the US decisions hard to explain.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says no Russian diesel has been released so far
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said Russian diesel has not yet been released. He made the remark during continuing US talks with Russia on diesel.

headline: Iran summons the EU and German ambassadors, reports say
detail: Reports say Tehran has summoned the ambassadors of the EU and Germany. Earlier, Iran's foreign minister accused European countries of complicity in the US war with Iran.

headline: Ukrainian officials suspect the US is intermittently limiting intelligence sharing; US Secretary of State Rubio denies any pause
detail: Ukrainian officials say they suspect the US is restricting intelligence sharing on and off, leaving Ukraine without early warning of Russian missile attacks. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denies there has been any pause in support.

headline: Brent settles at $109.55 a barrel, close to a five-month high, as Middle East tensions weigh on supply
detail: Brent settled at $109.55 a barrel and moved around a five-month high on supply risks from the Middle East. Gains were reported as limited by a recovery in Hormuz flows and by technical indicators showing the market as overbought.

headline: US lawmakers oppose Trump's proposed Russian diesel deal; European diesel futures have more than doubled this year
detail: Trump's proposed deal on Russian diesel is meeting opposition from US lawmakers, and analysts question whether extra supply would bring fuel prices down. Brent is up more than 75% this year and European diesel futures have more than doubled.

headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fall to 282.7m barrels, the lowest since 1982
detail: Crude oil held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.7 million barrels last week, the lowest level since 1982.

headline: Iran's Hormuz management body adds 122 ships to its list of non-compliant vessels
detail: Iran's Strait of Hormuz Management Organization said it has added 122 ships to its non-compliance list, as Tehran continues to restrict traffic through the strait.

headline: UK finance minister Healey rules out raising capital gains tax in the 28 October Budget, the Times reports
detail: The Times reported on Monday, as cited by Reuters, that John Healey has turned down calls to increase capital gains tax in his first Budget on 28 October. According to the report, he is instead putting economic growth and business investment first.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield holds at 5.14% after a 7bp rise; French unrest weighs on European bonds and the euro
detail: A market wrap reports the US 10-year yield steady at 5.14% after rising seven basis points, with oil near elevated levels on Middle East supply risks. French political unrest was reported as adding pressure to European bonds and the euro.

headline: 10-year JGB futures fall 0.22 point in early Tokyo trade ahead of a 20-year bond sale
detail: Benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond futures fell 0.22 point in early trade. Japan is due to sell 20-year government bonds.

headline: Trump says NATO allies refused to help the US in the Iran war and the US could be forced to leave Europe
detail: The FT reports that the US President said NATO allies declined to assist in the war with Iran. He also said the US could be forced to leave Europe and called the situation very serious.

headline: Trump administration has not approved sending interceptor missiles to Ukraine, Washington Post reports
detail: According to the Washington Post, the US administration has not approved the transfer of interceptor missiles to Ukraine. Separately, US Vice President Vance said Ukraine should not join NATO.

headline: China keeps its one-year and five-year loan prime rates at 3.00% and 3.50%, as expected
detail: The People's Bank of China left its benchmark lending rates unchanged in October, in line with forecasts. Reuters reports that rates have now been held for 17 months in a row.

headline: Japan's economy minister Kiuchi says he hopes to attend this month's BoJ policy meeting if his schedule allows
detail: Kiuchi said the government respects the Bank of Japan's autonomy over monetary policy as set out in the BoJ law. He also said he has never considered asking for a vote at a BoJ meeting to be postponed.

headline: PBOC to offer up to 1 trillion yuan a day in overnight reverse repos from 21 October to 2 November
detail: China's central bank announced the overnight reverse repo operations for the period. It carried out no 7-day reverse repos on Tuesday.

headline: Trump says the US and Mexico are very close to a trade deal
detail: US President Trump said on Monday that Mexico and the United States are very close to agreeing a trade deal, Reuters reports.

headline: Japan's finance minister Katayama says no decision has been made on how to fund the expected rise in defence spending
detail: Katayama said the government is still discussing defence spending and will look at ways to secure stable funding while keeping a focus on fiscal sustainability.

headline: UK Treasury expected to study options for closer long-term ties with the EU, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Treasury is expected to carry out a study of Britain moving closer to the EU, with Andy Burnham preparing to set out options for the UK's longer-term relationship with the bloc.

headline: Bank of England and Bank of Korea widen their partnership on tokenisation
detail: Yonhap reports that South Korea's central bank and the Bank of England have broadened their cooperation on tokenisation.

headline: China sells 10-year government bonds at a 1.6057% yield
detail: Traders say China's finance ministry auctioned 10-year bonds at a yield of 1.6057%, and offered 2-month bills at 1.0316%.

headline: Japan's 40-year JGB yield falls 6bp to 4.05%
detail: Japan's 40-year government bond yield is reported 6bp lower at 4.05% in Tokyo trading on 20 October.

headline: PBOC considers using the overnight rate as the main anchor of China's monetary policy
detail: Reports say the People's Bank of China is exploring a shift to the overnight rate as its main policy anchor. An expert quoted by a PBOC-backed news outlet says the change does not signal monetary easing and should not be seen as a rate cut.

headline: French PM says targeted curfews kept the peace overnight; local authorities will impose more tonight where needed
detail: France's prime minister said the targeted curfews helped keep the peace overnight. He said curfews would be imposed again tonight wherever the situation requires, with local authorities making those decisions on the ground.

headline: BoJ expected to hold rates in October and signal a possible hike as early as December, sources say
detail: Sources say the Bank of Japan is likely to keep rates on hold at its 29-30 October meeting while signalling room to raise them as soon as December. The same sources say its quarterly report may nudge up the fiscal 2027 inflation forecast slightly.

headline: UK regular pay growth picks up to 3.7%, above 3.6% forecast; employment rises 13K against an expected 8K fall
detail: UK average earnings excluding bonuses rose 3.7%, compared with a 3.6% forecast and 3.5% previously. Employment rose 13K after a 26K fall in the previous release, and the unemployment change was 30.3K, up from 27.8K.

headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says she does not expect to seek a mandate after the two-year tax cut
detail: Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi also denied reports that an income limit of 3M yen had been set for benefits.

headline: UK unemployment rate falls to 4.7% against a 4.9% forecast; employment up 102K on the quarter
detail: UK labour market data show the unemployment rate at 4.7%, compared with a forecast and previous reading of 4.9%. Employment rose 102K over three months, against a 5K forecast and 67K previously, and average weekly earnings growth including bonuses slowed to 3.7% from 3.9%, below the 3.8% forecast.

headline: German producer prices rise 6.7% year on year, above the 6.3% forecast
detail: German PPI rose 1.9% month on month against a 1.6% forecast and 1.1% previously. The annual rate rose to 6.7% from 4.6%, against a 6.3% forecast.

headline: UK total pay growth slows to 3.7%, below 3.8% forecast; private-sector regular pay at 3.0%, in line; claimant count up 30.3K
detail: ONS figures for the three months to August show average weekly earnings including bonuses up 3.7% year on year, against a 3.8% forecast and 3.9% previously. Private-sector regular pay rose 3.0%, as expected, after 2.9%. The claimant count rose 30.3K after 27.8K, with the claimant count rate unchanged at 4.4%.

headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says she does not intend to put pressure on prices to come down
detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said she has no intention of exerting pressure to lower prices. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Saudi Arabia commits to supplying France with 95k tons of diesel a month
detail: Saudi Arabia has committed to supply France with 95k tons of diesel per month, according to a market news post. No further terms or timing were given.

headline: UAE commits to supplying France with 100k tons of diesel a month; Bahrain and UAE deliveries due in coming weeks
detail: The United Arab Emirates has committed to provide France with 100k tons of diesel a month, following an earlier Saudi commitment. Deliveries from Bahrain and the UAE to France are reported to start in the coming weeks.

headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says the EU is working with Turkey, India and others on a Black Sea deal
detail: Kallas said a Black Sea arrangement would protect lives and supplies. No market reaction was reported.

headline: BoJ may lift its inflation forecast for next fiscal year and keep rates on hold this month, sources say
detail: Four sources familiar with the Bank of Japan's thinking told Reuters it may raise its inflation outlook for the next fiscal year in forecasts due this month. The sources linked this to higher oil prices keeping price pressures in place for longer than expected.

headline: Iran says excessive US demands are holding up progress in negotiations
detail: Iran repeated its position that US demands are blocking progress in talks between the two sides. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Eurozone seasonally adjusted current account surplus narrows to €8.7bn in August from €27.6bn
detail: ECB data show the seasonally adjusted eurozone current account surplus at €8.7bn for August, down from €27.6bn the month before. The unadjusted figure was €7.70bn, against a revised €35.90bn previously.

headline: South Korea's finance ministry says it will consider cutting bond issuance further if needed
detail: South Korea's finance ministry said it would consider a further cut to government bond issuance if necessary. It gave no figures or timing.

headline: Saudi civil defence issues an early alert in Riyadh as sirens sound in the capital
detail: Saudi civil defence issued an early warning in Riyadh, and sirens were reported in the city. It follows Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure; no market reaction has been reported so far.

headline: Saudi civil defence says the danger in Riyadh has passed after the earlier alert
detail: Saudi civil defence said the threat in the capital had ended, following its earlier alert when sirens sounded in Riyadh. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: Iran's foreign ministry says Egypt's readiness to help Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis is worsening the situation
detail: A spokesman for Iran's foreign ministry said Egypt's stated readiness to back Saudi Arabia against the Houthis is making the conflict worse. The remarks come after the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.

headline: German ZEW economic sentiment falls to 28.1, below 30 forecast; current conditions improve to -35.9
detail: German ZEW economic sentiment came in at 28.1, down from 34.7 and below the 30 forecast, while current conditions rose to -35.9 from -47.1, beating the -44.5 forecast. Eurozone ZEW expectations fell to 18.5 from 25.8.

headline: UK 10-year gilt auction yields 5.418% with 3.61 times cover, up from 5.383% and 3.34 at the previous sale
detail: The 10-year gilt auction produced an average yield of 5.418%, against 5.383% at the previous sale of the line. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.61, up from 3.34 last time.

headline: Eurozone construction output rises 1.8% on the month after a flat previous reading
detail: Eurozone construction output grew 1.8% month on month, following 0.0% in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say mines hit two oil tankers south of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving them on fire and stopped
detail: The IRGC navy said two tankers struck mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, caught fire and were brought to a halt. Tasnim carried the report, which gave no date for the incident. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Kremlin hopes Putin can meet US envoy Witkoff in Russia soon and calls for urgent resumption of US nuclear stability talks
detail: The Kremlin said it hoped a meeting between President Putin and Trump envoy Steve Witkoff could be organised in Russia in the near future, and that US negotiators could brief Putin on the Ukrainian and European positions. It also said dialogue with the US on strategic nuclear stability needs to resume urgently.

headline: Kremlin says Russia values the work of US negotiators highly
detail: The Kremlin said on 20 October that Russia rates the efforts of US negotiators highly. No market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB policymaker Rehn says the French-German bond spread has widened somewhat
detail: Olli Rehn, Bank of Finland governor and member of the ECB Governing Council, said the gap between French and German government bond yields has widened to some extent.

headline: IEA chief Birol says the agency will consider further releases from emergency oil stocks if needed
detail: Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, said the agency would look at releasing more oil from emergency stocks if required. No volumes or timing were given.

headline: Most Gulf stock markets fall after Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military sites
detail: Reuters reports that most Gulf bourses fell in early trade on Tuesday after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets on Monday.

headline: UK will fly missions to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
detail: A market newswire reports that the UK will fly missions to help defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Rubio says an India trade deal is close and US policy on Ukraine, including intelligence sharing, is unchanged
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said only a few items remain on a trade deal with India. He said he spoke with President Zelenskiy for 45 minutes, that nothing has changed on Pentagon support or intelligence sharing for Ukraine, that the US is not deliberately denying interceptors to Ukraine, and that the US is taking steps to help Saudi Arabia.

headline: Rubio says a batch of PURL interceptors for Ukraine may not have been delivered and warns Russia-Ukraine war could escalate
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said Trump is disappointed at the lack of progress in Russia-Ukraine talks, that the conflict risks spreading to other places, and that it could be accurate that a batch of interceptors bought for Ukraine under the PURL programme has not been delivered. He also said the US will talk with Reliance about refining more Venezuelan crude.

headline: Rubio says the war must end through negotiation and backs US, China and Russia arms control talks
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the war must be ended through negotiation and that arms control talks between the US, China and Russia would benefit the world. He also linked energy to national security and said Indian refining of Venezuelan crude would be discussed.

headline: Rubio says Trump is frustrated by accusations that he is harming Ukraine
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said President Trump is frustrated by accusations that he is harming Ukraine. Separately, Ukraine's President Zelenskiy has arrived in Oslo for talks with US negotiators.

headline: Rubio says India has made substantial progress in diversifying its oil purchases
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said India has made substantial progress in diversifying where it buys its oil. He made the remarks while the US and India are working on a trade deal.

headline: UK MoD says RAF Typhoons will fly defensive missions only over Saudi Arabia and will not strike the Houthis
detail: The UK Ministry of Defence says RAF Typhoon jets will fly defensive counter-air missions to help protect Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from aerial attack. It says the aircraft will not carry out offensive strikes against the Houthis.

headline: European benchmark gas price rises above €90 for the first time since 2022
detail: Europe's benchmark gas contract has traded above €90 for the first time since 2022, according to a market report. Middle East supply tensions are already on the blotter.

headline: Starmer's spokesman rejects the idea that the UK risks being drawn into the Saudi-Houthi war
detail: The Prime Minister's spokesman said the government does not accept that the UK risks being pulled into the Saudi-Houthi conflict. This follows the UK's decision to fly defensive missions over Saudi Arabia.

headline: Google Cloud outage disrupts UK banks including Halifax and Revolut
detail: The FT reports that a Google Cloud outage has hit several businesses, including UK lenders Halifax and Revolut. Google says a power outage caused the failure of its Cloud services.

headline: Russia's deputy foreign minister Ryabkov says Moscow still views a possible US-Russia diesel deal positively
detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Moscow still sees the possible diesel deal between Russia and the United States in a positive light. US lawmakers have opposed the proposed deal, and the US Energy Secretary has said no Russian diesel has been released so far.

headline: Russia's Ryabkov says Moscow's Ukraine stance does not hinge on Trump postponing severe new sanctions on Russia
detail: Russia's deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov said Moscow's approach to resolving the war in Ukraine does not depend on the US president's decision to delay what have been described as very severe sanctions on Russia.

headline: Gilts outperform G7 peers as investor concern over the UK Budget fades, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that UK government bonds sold off heavily when the Iran war began but have since done better than other G7 markets. It says traders' focus has moved to France.

headline: US ADP weekly private payrolls average 18.5K, slowing from 24.75K previously
detail: ADP says private employers added an average of 18.5K jobs a week in the four weeks to 3 October, down from 24.75K in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

headline: Russian diesel exports head back to former main buyers after the US-brokered lifting of Moscow's export ban
detail: Reuters reports that Kpler and LSEG shipping data show at least two tankers signalling voyages to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, after Russia's diesel export ban was lifted with US involvement.

headline: US housing starts fall to 1.221M in September, short of the 1.305M forecast
detail: US housing starts came in at 1.221M for September, against a forecast of 1.305M and down from 1.275M the previous month.

headline: US building permits come in at 1.4M in September, above the 1.385M forecast; housing starts fall 5.2% on the month
detail: US September building permits were 1.4M against a 1.385M forecast and 1.403M previously, a 0.2% monthly fall versus an expected 1.3% drop. Housing starts fell 5.2% on the month against a forecast rise of about 2%.

headline: Putin floats a US-China-Russia summit with Trump and Xi to negotiate an end to the Ukraine war, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Russia's President Putin raised the possibility of a three-way summit with the US and Chinese leaders on a deal to end the war in Ukraine, as reported by Semafor. Semafor said Trump already faces criticism from Republicans over his approaches to Putin, including the waiving of sanctions on Russia.

headline: All 100 economists in a poll expect a Fed rate hike in December; 94 see a hold at the 27-28 October meeting
detail: In the poll, 94 of 100 economists expect the fed funds rate to stay at 3.75%-4.00% this month and the rest expect a hike to 4.00%-4.25%. 94 of 100 see 4.00%-4.25% by the end of 2026, compared with 29 of 76 in the September poll.

headline: New EU Arctic strategy aims to keep oil, coal and gas in the ground, including in Arctic regions
detail: The European Commission says it will work with partners to prevent hydrocarbon reserve developments that threaten the Arctic ecosystem. Commission President von der Leyen says the EU must change its strategic posture in the Arctic.

headline: Qatar and Pakistan put forward a compromise proposal in US-Iran talks, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports
detail: Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, citing sources familiar with the mediation, reports that Qatar and Pakistan have presented a compromise proposal intended to meet both US and Iranian demands. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US-Iran compromise proposal carried by Pakistan's army chief has US and Iranian approval, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports
detail: Al-Araby Al-Jadeed cites sources as saying the new proposal aims to head off escalation and restart talks. It also partly meets Iran's demand over its frozen funds.

headline: Iran accepts secret IAEA site inspections as part of the compromise proposal in US talks, Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports
detail: Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reports that Iran has agreed to secret inspections of sites by the IAEA under the compromise proposal in US-Iran negotiations. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Google restores full service in its London cloud region after an outage that disrupted UK banks
detail: Alphabet's Google said on Tuesday that full service is back in its London-based cloud region, after a power event disrupted several cloud services, Reuters reports.

headline: Italy's PM Meloni condemns the US diesel deal with Russia
detail: A market commentator reports that Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has strongly condemned the US diesel arrangement with Russia. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says US bond market and auctions are performing well and sees no spillover from France
detail: In a TV interview, the US Treasury Secretary said recent bond auctions had been strong, that investors are buying bonds at a price, and that the US is getting past a temporary energy price shock. He also said the US must grow its way out of debt and that he is not seeking another job.

headline: Bessent calls for US spending control and faster growth to tackle debt, links higher rates to the energy shock
detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said spending must be brought under control and growth raised to overcome debt. He also said rates are up because of the energy shock, housing has slowed and he expects mortgage rates to come down. He added that any action on Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac would not widen agency debt spreads, and that ownership may be addressed next year.

headline: Bessent says Iran's currency has collapsed and panic is setting in, and calls the energy price spike temporary
detail: In live remarks, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran's economy would at some point go non-linear and that things were going well despite what he called a temporary spike in energy prices. He also said the US is working hard to end its reliance on Chinese critical minerals, that losing chip supply from Taiwan would be devastating, and that Putin has not yet replied to the G20 invitation.

headline: French borrowing costs rise further towards 5% as social unrest weighs on the bond market, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that French government borrowing costs rose again today to close to 5%, amid social unrest in France and fallout in the bond market.

headline: China's commerce ministry firmly opposes the US order on DeepSeek and calls it discriminatory
detail: China's commerce ministry says the US order on DeepSeek is discriminatory, politicises tech and trade issues under the pretext of national security, and ignores the consensus reached between the two countries' heads of state.

headline: China tells the US to revoke restrictions on Chinese firms and vows necessary measures to defend its interests
detail: China's commerce ministry called on the US to immediately reverse what it described as discriminatory restrictions on Chinese companies. It said China would take necessary measures to protect its interests.

headline: US Energy Under Secretary Haustveit says diesel prices are too high and the US is working with refiners to raise output
detail: US Energy Under Secretary Haustveit said current diesel prices are higher than anyone would want and that officials are working with refiners on ways to increase production.

headline: US pending home sales drop 7.3% on the month in September against a forecast 0.5% fall; index slides to 66.0
detail: US pending home sales fell 7.3% month on month, compared with a forecast fall of 0.5% and a 0.3% rise previously. The pending homes index came in at 66.0, down from 71.2.

headline: US-Iran compromise proposal would send Iran the interest on $6bn of its funds frozen in Qatari banks, Israel's Channel 12 reports
detail: Israel's Channel 12 reports that the proposal, which Pakistan's army chief presented to senior Iranian officials, partly meets Iran's demand for the return of its frozen funds. It says the US has approved the plan and Iran has given preliminary agreement.

headline: Netanyahu says he discussed overthrowing Iran's regime with Trump on Monday
detail: Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu said he spoke with President Trump on Monday about eliminating the Iranian regime, and said the regime must be overthrown. The remarks come as US-Iran talks on a compromise proposal continue.

headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says a trade deal with the US is very close but some issues remain
detail: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said a trade agreement with the United States is very close, though some issues are still to be resolved.

headline: Canada's US trade minister says trade talks with the US are continuing and expects a deal eventually
detail: Canada's minister responsible for US trade said Ottawa is still holding trade talks with its US counterparts. The minister said a deal serving the whole Canadian economy will be reached at some point, but gave no timing.

headline: US single-family housing starts fall sharply in September; single-family permits drop to a three-and-a-half-year low
detail: Reuters reports that US single-family homebuilding fell sharply in September. It says permits for future single-family construction fell to their lowest in three and a half years as higher mortgage rates held back demand.

headline: Trump administration recently came close to approving a strike on Iran, i24NEWS reports
detail: Israeli broadcaster i24NEWS reports that the US administration recently came close to authorising a strike on Iran. The report comes as US-Iran talks over a compromise proposal continue; no market reaction was reported.

headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says USTR and the Commerce Department are positive on a US-Mexico trade deal
detail: Mexico's President Sheinbaum said the US Trade Representative and the Commerce Department hold a positive view of the trade deal with Mexico. Earlier she had said a deal was very close but that some issues were still open.

headline: Iran-US talks are still going on and reports that a deal is close are wrong, says a person familiar
detail: An unnamed person said negotiations between Iran and the US continue but denied reports that an agreement is near. The denial follows earlier reports of a compromise proposal put forward by Qatar and Pakistan.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says diesel prices could fall meaningfully if Europe agrees to a coordinated release
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said Europe joining a coordinated release could bring meaningful relief on diesel prices. He also said more work is needed on refining and on Defense Production Act funding.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says any Russian diesel imported to the US would most likely go to New England
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said Russian diesel coming to the US under the proposed US-Russia diesel arrangement would probably be sent to New England. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Rubio expects the US-India trade deal within weeks rather than months, with only technical details left
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said he expects to see the trade deal with India in a matter of weeks, and that only some technical details remain to be settled.

headline: Rubio says oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are close to pre-war levels
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said on 20 October that the volume of oil passing through Hormuz is nearly back to where it was before the war. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the US is working with India to lift refining output and get more products to market
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said the US is working with India to raise refining output so that more products reach the global market. Separately, Secretary of State Rubio said Reliance has an opportunity to help India keep diversifying its energy supply chain.

headline: Bank of Israel expected to hold rates on Wednesday after three straight cuts, ahead of the 27 October election, Reuters poll shows
detail: A Reuters poll shows the Bank of Israel is expected to leave short-term interest rates unchanged on Wednesday after three successive reductions. Respondents expect policymakers to pause before next week's election even though inflation is stable.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf sets seven conditions the US must meet to win Tehran's trust
detail: Iran's Mehr news agency reported the remarks by parliament speaker Ghalibaf while US-Iran talks continue, on the day Pakistan's army chief met President Pezeshkian in Tehran to discuss mediation. The reports did not list the conditions and gave no market reaction.

headline: Iran tells Pakistan it has nothing new to say to the US, Mehr reports
detail: Iran's Mehr news agency reports that Tehran has told Pakistan, which has been mediating, that it has no new message for the US. Earlier reports said a compromise proposal carried by Pakistan's army chief had been put forward in the US-Iran talks.

headline: France's 20-year bond spread over Germany is already 170bp, says economist Robin Brooks
detail: Economist Robin Brooks says France's 20-year spread over Germany has reached 170bp. He argues that the 10-year tenor usually watched is the one most affected by ECB action to cap yields.

headline: Iran's Security Council secretary says none of Iran's enriched nuclear material will be sent abroad
detail: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported the remarks by the secretary of Iran's Security Council while US-Iran talks continue.

headline: France to send troops to back up police for protests planned on 24 October, and admits failures over weekend unrest
detail: Reuters reports that the French government announced a large security operation for Saturday's protests. The government said its response to last weekend's violence had failed.

headline: Iran's security chief rules out talks with the US until Washington builds trust
detail: Iran's Security Council secretary Rezaei set the condition after meeting Pakistan's army chief, according to Iranian state media IRNA. Separately, Tasnim reported that he said all of Iran's enriched nuclear material will stay in the country.

headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says a supertanker carrying more than 2 mln barrels of crude exploded after hitting a mine near Hormuz
detail: Iranian media, including IRIB News, carried the Revolutionary Guards navy's account. It said the tanker, which it called 'violating', exploded after striking a mine south of the Strait of Hormuz and was carrying over 2 mln barrels of crude. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warn ships off unauthorised routes in the Gulf and Sea of Oman and vow decisive action over Hormuz violations
detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say vessel owners and crews are responsible if they use unauthorised routes in the Persian Gulf and Sea of Oman, and that breaches of security in the Strait will be dealt with decisively. The warning follows the Guards' report of a supertanker hitting a mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz.

headline: Lavrov says Russia will hear US envoys Witkoff and Kushner's proposals but will make no political concessions
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Moscow will look at what US envoys Witkoff and Kushner put forward, but will not make political concessions.

headline: BoE's Greene says wage disinflation has stalled above 2%-consistent levels and second-round inflation risk is greater than thought
detail: MPC member Megan Greene said forward-looking data point to pay growth closer to 3.5%, the economy has been surprisingly resilient and labour market slack may have peaked. She said she still believes the MPC should lean proactively against the risk of second-round inflation effects.

headline: Iran's top security official Rezaei tells Pakistan's army chief Munir there will be no talks with the US until Tehran's conditions are met
detail: Iran's top security official gave the message to Pakistan's army chief, who has been carrying a compromise proposal in the US-Iran talks.

headline: Zelenskyy offers to stop strikes on sensitive Russian energy sites if Russia does the same, and seeks a trilateral leaders' meeting
detail: After talks with US envoy Witkoff and Norway's prime minister, Ukraine's President Zelenskyy said Kyiv is ready for a mutual halt to strikes on sensitive energy infrastructure and wants to move towards a three-way meeting at leaders' level. He said Witkoff travels to Russia tomorrow, while Norway's prime minister called the talks good and constructive and Finland's President Stubb said there had been genuine progress.

headline: Russia extends its strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities to western Ukraine, causing waves of blackouts
detail: Reuters reports, citing Ukrainian energy ministry officials and local authorities, that Russian attacks on energy facilities now reach western Ukraine and have caused repeated blackouts.

headline: US envoy Witkoff to meet Russian leadership in St Petersburg tomorrow after Oslo talks with Zelenskyy and Nordic leaders
detail: Norway's prime minister said Witkoff flies to St Petersburg tomorrow, and Finland's president said elements of peace found at the meeting will be taken forward there. Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for negotiations and wants to see de-escalation, that security guarantees were discussed, that territorial questions need to be settled at the highest level, and that he hopes to speak to Rubio within 48 hours.

headline: Turkey sends defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to parliament for ratification
detail: Three parliamentary sources told Reuters the pact has been submitted, bringing Turkey closer to a formal mutual defence commitment with Riyadh while Saudi Arabia faces Houthi attacks.

headline: Zelenskyy says the US has set out strong security guarantees in a document that will be shared with Russia
detail: Speaking at a press conference in Oslo with Nordic leaders, Zelenskyy said US intelligence on missile strikes is working again and that he expects positive results from talks with Rubio on Patriot missiles. Norway's prime minister said Europe needs to be part of talks on the European security order, and Finland's president said it is very important that the US stays engaged.

headline: IEA chief says the agency is ready to coordinate further emergency oil stock releases if needed
detail: The head of the International Energy Agency said on Tuesday that the agency stands ready to coordinate more emergency oil releases by member countries, while it pushes for diesel to be released under existing plans to ease surging prices, Reuters reports.

headline: Finland's President Stubb says the Ukraine peace process is back on track after a week of quiet progress
detail: Finnish President Alexander Stubb said significant progress had been made out of public view over the past week or so and called the day a good one for peace.

headline: PM Burnham plans legislation to reduce the UK benefits bill, possibly as early as April, Telegraph reports
detail: The Telegraph reports that Prime Minister Burnham plans to bring in legislation to cut the benefits bill, which could be introduced as soon as April. No figures for the savings were given in the reports.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian tells Pakistani mediator the US must lift all pressure, threats and sanctions before any negotiations
detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian set this precondition for talks with Washington in remarks to the Pakistani mediator, according to a report. No market reaction was reported.

headline: BoE's Greene questions the Bank's estimate of pay growth consistent with target, putting it at 3% wage growth for 2% inflation
detail: MPC member Megan Greene said she has concerns about the Bank of England's estimate of target-consistent pay growth, and said 3% wage growth is consistent with 2% inflation.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says he believes the US will attack again if Tehran negotiates
detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian said he believes the US would launch another attack if Iran entered negotiations, Tasnim reported. Pakistan's army chief Munir has left Tehran, Nour News reported.

headline: BoE's Greene says people take notice of inflation once it is above 3% and expects supply shocks to keep coming
detail: MPC member Megan Greene said public awareness of inflation picks up when it goes above 3%, and that the economy will continue to face many supply shocks. The comments follow her earlier remarks that wage disinflation has stalled.

headline: BoE's Greene says there is reason to worry policy is not restrictive enough, with inflation expectations anchored but above norms
detail: MPC member Megan Greene said there is a need to be concerned that the policy stance is not tight enough. She described inflation expectations as anchored but sitting above their usual levels.

headline: US to propose a face-to-face meeting between Putin, Zelenskyy and Trump, Politico reports
detail: Politico reports that the US will offer Russia's President Putin in-person talks with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy and President Trump. No market reaction has been reported.

headline: US Energy Department commits about $967m in extra funding for power grid upgrades to curb rising electricity costs
detail: Reuters reported on Tuesday that the US Department of Energy will invest roughly $967 million in additional funding to modernise critical energy infrastructure. The department said the aim is to lower surging electricity costs.

headline: Trump says he must make a final decision on Iran, winning either the nice way or the not-so-nice way
detail: The US President said Washington has to decide one way or the other on Iran. He also said he has to choose how the US wins against Tehran, by friendly means or otherwise.

headline: Rubio says a deal with Iran is extremely hard to reach because hardliners control Tehran
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said reaching an agreement with Iran is extremely difficult because hardliners are in control there. He spoke as US-Iran talks continue through Pakistani and Qatari mediation.

headline: BoE's Greene repeats her call for higher rates, citing bigger-than-expected inflation risks from the Iran war energy shock
detail: Reuters reports that MPC member Megan Greene said the risk of broader inflation from the energy price shock linked to the Iran war is greater than the Bank expected. She repeated her view that interest rates should rise.

headline: Rubio says Iran's actions against commercial shipping are unlike anything seen since the Second World War
detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described Iran's conduct towards commercial vessels as unmatched since the Second World War.

headline: Trump says Russia wants to reach a deal after the latest talks on Ukraine
detail: US President Donald Trump said Russia would like to get a deal done following the latest round of talks on ending the war in Ukraine.

headline: Trump presses Ukraine to agree a deal with Russia, saying the US has given a lot and received nothing back
detail: US President Trump said Ukraine has to want to settle the war, that the US wants Zelenskyy to make a deal and that Europe is tired of the conflict. He said it is time for Ukraine and Russia to reach a deal.

headline: Netanyahu vows Israel will remove the threat from Iran, citing the killing of Nasrallah
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said Israel had eliminated Hezbollah leader Nasrallah and would also eliminate the threat posed by Iran.

headline: Trump says Putin and Zelenskyy need not meet in person to sign a Ukraine peace deal, and calls for the war to end
detail: US President Trump said it is difficult for the Russian and Ukrainian leaders to be in the same room and that an agreement could be signed another way. He also said it was time for the two sides to end the war. No market reaction was reported.

headline: No Canada-US trade deal is expected before the US midterm elections, CBC reports
detail: Canadian broadcaster CBC reports that a trade agreement between Canada and the US is not expected before the US midterms. Earlier, Canada's trade minister for US relations said talks were continuing.

headline: Trump says the Iran war will be over very soon and the US could pull out now having done a great job
detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Tuesday evening. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Trump says the US is pretty close to a trade deal with India
detail: US President Trump spoke on Tuesday evening, after Secretary of State Rubio said earlier that the US-India deal was expected within weeks.

headline: Trump says oil prices will fall sharply once the Iran war ends
detail: The US President made the comment during remarks at the White House on 20 October, which have now ended. No market reaction was reported.

headline: France's 10-year spread over Germany moves above 150bp
detail: Economist Robin Brooks reports that France's 10-year yield spread over Germany rose above 150bp on 20 October. He also says the 30-year spread is above 170bp.

headline: Kyiv rebukes Trump over his openness to meeting Russian and Chinese leaders, and says the US has cut military intelligence sharing
detail: Semafor reports that the rift between Washington and Ukraine has widened after Trump said he was open to meeting his Russian and Chinese counterparts. Ukraine says the US has scaled back the military intelligence it shares.

headline: Iranian general says Iran's armed forces hold operational control of the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Major General Yazidi said Iran's armed forces have operational control of the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: US Defence Secretary Hegseth says the US has not withdrawn anything from Ukraine's satellite service
detail: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the US has not pulled back any of Ukraine's satellite service and wished Ukrainians success. Kyiv had earlier said the US had cut military intelligence sharing.

headline: US official says the US, Ukraine and Europe are strongly aligned at working level on next steps, ahead of Witkoff's Wednesday talks with…
detail: A US official said Ukraine put forward new proposals and the talks covered parts of a comprehensive peace framework, including security guarantees. Envoy Witkoff is due to meet President Putin on Wednesday, with Kushner joining virtually, to discuss the proposals with Russia.

headline: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi says the US cannot be trusted at all in negotiations
detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said there should be no trust in the US during the negotiation process. Speaking to Iraq's Al Ekhbariya through an interpreter, he also said Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis have not yet responded to Tehran's mediation initiative.

headline: Yemen's Houthis say a ground attack on Saudi Arabia is an option, Iranian media report
detail: Iran's Sepah News reported that Yemen's Houthis said a ground attack on Saudi Arabia is being considered. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Brent settles below $109 a barrel as US-Iran diplomacy continues; longer-dated Treasuries outperform
detail: A market wire reports that Brent crude settled below $109 a barrel as diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran went on, and that longer-dated US Treasuries outperformed. It also cites falling oil prices as one reason US stocks rose; it gives no percentage move for oil.

headline: Iran's Araghchi says talks with US continue via Pakistan and Qatar, and the US sought added clauses after agreeing Hormuz terms
detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said indirect negotiations with the US through intermediaries including Pakistan and Qatar are ongoing. He said the Strait of Hormuz was to be fully reopened on the sixth day of the agreed period, and that the US had accepted those terms but then asked to add further clauses.

headline: Iran's Araghchi rejects the extra US conditions and says Tehran will not negotiate through Washington's network
detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi was responding to the additional conditions the US sought in talks. Iran is negotiating with the US through intermediaries.

headline: UK ministers set to approve the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea on Wednesday, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that ministers will give the go-ahead on Wednesday to the Jackdaw gas project, which lies about 150 miles east of Aberdeen.

headline: Qatar steps up LNG exports as gas prices surge, with at least 20 cargoes through Hormuz since early September
detail: Semafor reports that Qatar is increasing liquefied natural gas exports, with at least 20 shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz to other destinations since early September. One tanker is now sailing towards Poland.

headline: Iran's Araghchi says Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have not responded to Tehran's offer to mediate
detail: In a television interview aired on Tuesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran has had no reply from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker talks to end the fighting between them, Reuters reports.

headline: RBA's Hauser says the inflation outlook looks slightly worse than forecast and the board's decision is still uncertain
detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Hauser said forecasts are still being finalised and he is uncertain about the board's decision. He said companies name cost pressures as their main concern.

headline: RBA's Hauser notes some easing in jobs and housing data but says inflation has stayed high for an extended period
detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said monetary policy is working but the inflation outlook has worsened, and inflation expectations must stay anchored to target. He also said some easing has been seen in labour market and housing data.

headline: Brightmine: UK median pay awards rise to 3.1% in the three months to September from 3.0%
detail: Brightmine says median UK pay settlements rose to 3.1% in the three months to September, from 3.0% in the periods to July and August. It says wage trends show little sign of shifting and most deals are no bigger than awards a year earlier.

headline: RBA's Hauser expects quarterly trimmed mean inflation above expectations and says capacity constraints are tighter than thought
detail: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser says the September labour report was somewhat weaker than expected and the labour market is softening, though unemployment is still low. He adds that the bank must respond to supply shocks to keep inflation expectations anchored.

headline: City leaders lobby Chancellor Healey against higher bank taxes at the Budget
detail: City AM reports that senior City figures, including the head of the CBI, are making a final push against a planned rise in bank taxes at the Budget. They warn that the move would cost jobs and growth outside London.

headline: UK government approves the Jackdaw North Sea gasfield
detail: The Guardian reports that the government has approved gas drilling at the Jackdaw field in the North Sea, and that PM Burnham now faces a climate backlash over the decision.

headline: US envoy Witkoff to present Putin with a peace plan after his talks with Zelenskyy, Axios reports
detail: Axios reports that US envoy Witkoff will put a Ukraine peace plan to Putin, following his talks with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy.

headline: Brent rises to $110 a barrel and US crude tops $99 as attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz add to supply worries
detail: Market reports in Asian trading say Brent rose to $110 a barrel and US oil futures went above $99. The WSJ links the gains to attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and reports that gold weakened as oil rose.

headline: Japan's Finance Minister Katayama says the economy is close to a phase of sustained inflation driven by wages
detail: Speaking on Wednesday, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said higher import costs are currently pushing up Japanese prices, and that the economy is close to moving into a period of sustained inflation driven by rising wages, Reuters reports.

headline: 20-year JGBs rise after an auction draws record demand
detail: The WSJ reports that Japanese 20-year government bonds gained after the auction drew record demand. The 10-year JGB yield was unchanged at 2.895%, and the 30-year yield fell 0.5bp to 3.935%.

headline: Sterling slips below $1.3400 ahead of UK inflation data
detail: In Asian trading, GBP/USD fell below 1.3400 as markets waited for the UK inflation release, a market report says.

headline: Israel's PM Netanyahu presses for renewed strikes on Iran, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that the Israeli military drew up plans for an extensive operation earlier this month but held back because President Trump has ruled out an attack before the US midterm elections. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Chancellor Healey drops plans for a visa for wealthy investors in the Budget, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that the Chancellor has ruled out an investor visa scheme in the forthcoming Budget, although plans for it had been well advanced under Keir Starmer.

headline: UK's top banking regulator to set targets in a five-year strategy, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that the UK's main banking regulator will set targets as part of a new five-year strategy. No further detail was given in the posts.

headline: BoJ Deputy Governor Himino says underlying inflation is near 2% and warns that delaying policy changes risks higher inflation
detail: Himino said underlying inflation is close to the 2% target, medium- and long-term inflation expectations are still rising, and upside risks to prices are elevated. He also said financial conditions remain accommodative, real rates are low, bank lending is growing fast and strong AI demand is driving capex and exports.

headline: ECB chief economist Lane argues for euro liquidity lines to foreign countries
detail: Speaking in China on Wednesday, Lane said offering liquidity safety nets abroad would let the ECB strengthen the euro's global role and extend the reach of its monetary policy, Reuters reports.

headline: Japan considers winter electricity and gas subsidies as heating costs rise, Kyodo reports
detail: Kyodo reports that the Japanese government is considering subsidies for household electricity and gas over the winter to soften the impact of higher heating costs.

headline: APEC finance ministers agree to step up macroeconomic policy coordination against external risks, China's Lan says
detail: China's Finance Minister Lan Foan said on Wednesday that finance ministers from APEC member economies have agreed to strengthen communication and coordination on macroeconomic policy to deal with external risks and challenges, Reuters reports.

headline: Trump says new large data centres must generate their own electricity and supply any surplus to local communities or the grid
detail: US President Trump said he has mandated that new large data centres produce their own power and give or sell excess electricity back to local communities or the grid. He gave no timing or further detail on how the requirement would be applied.

headline: UK PPI output prices rise 4.6% year on year, above the 4.4% forecast and up from 3.7%
detail: Official figures put UK producer output price inflation at 4.6% year on year, against a forecast of 4.4% and 3.7% previously. Output prices rose 0.8% month on month, against a forecast of 0.6% and 0.7% previously.

headline: France's Finance Minister Lescure says the government can pass a budget using constitutional powers
detail: France's Finance Minister Lescure said the government has the constitutional tools it needs to get a budget passed.

headline: UK CPI inflation rises to 3.5% in September, above the 3.4% forecast; services CPI climbs to 3.7%
detail: ONS September data show headline CPI at 3.5% year on year from 3.1% (0.4% month on month vs 0.3% expected), services at 3.7% vs 3.6% expected and 3.4% previously, and core at 2.8% as forecast, up from 2.6%. CPIH is 3.6% vs 3.5% expected, and RPI is 3.9%, in line with forecasts.

headline: UK public sector net borrowing is £24.5bn in September, above the £24.0bn forecast
detail: ONS data show September PSNB excluding public sector banks at £24.5bn against a forecast of £24.0bn. The central government net cash requirement is £16.9bn, up from £10.0bn.

headline: UK PPI input prices rise 8.3% year on year in September, above the 7.6% forecast and up from 6.1%
detail: ONS data show September input prices up 1.5% on the month against 1.4% expected and 0.3% previously. Output prices rise 0.8% on the month against a forecast of 0.6%.

headline: Trump ruled out an Israeli strike on Iran before the US midterms, blocking a planned offensive, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu told the military this month to plan a major new offensive against Iran. According to the report, the operation did not go ahead because President Trump ruled out a strike before the midterm elections.

headline: UK core CPI rises to 2.8% in September, in line with forecast; CPIH reaches 3.6% and monthly CPI is 0.4%
detail: ONS data show core CPI at 2.8% year on year in September, matching the 2.8% forecast and up from 2.6%. CPIH rose to 3.6% against a 3.5% forecast and 3.3% previously, and CPI rose 0.4% on the month against a 0.3% forecast.

headline: UK RPI inflation rises to 3.9% in September, in line with forecast and up from 3.4%
detail: ONS data show RPI at 3.9% year on year in September, matching the 3.9% forecast, with a monthly rise of 0.1%. RPI excluding mortgage interest payments rose to 3.9% from 3.3%.

headline: Reuters poll: all 100 economists expect a Fed rate hike in December; 94 see a hold at the 27-28 October meeting
detail: A Reuters poll finds all 100 economists surveyed expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates in December. 94 of the 100 expect the target range to stay at 3.75%-4.00% at the 27-28 October meeting.

headline: UK public sector debt reaches about £3 trillion in September, a week before the Budget
detail: Official data released on Wednesday show UK public sector debt close to £3 trillion in September, City AM reports. Debt had first passed £2 trillion in June 2020.

headline: Brent climbs back above $110 a barrel as US-Iran talks show little progress
detail: Brent rose above $110 a barrel on Wednesday after mixed reports on US-Iran diplomacy, City AM reports. The FTSE 100 extended its losses for the week.

headline: UK Energy Secretary Fahnbulleh confirms again that there will be no new North Sea drilling licences
detail: The UK Energy Secretary again ruled out new North Sea drilling licences on Wednesday. The statement came on the same day the government approved the Jackdaw gasfield.

headline: EU's von der Leyen says the Commission will propose new measures to shield the EU market from cheap imports
detail: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Wednesday that the Commission will propose new tools to protect the EU from unfair competition from cheap imports, Reuters reports.

headline: France's 10-year bond yield nears 5%, which would be the highest since 2002
detail: The FT reports that concerns over France's public finances and political stability have pushed 10-year OAT yields up from 3.2% in late February to close to 5%, a level last seen in 2002.

headline: S&P Global's UK consumer sentiment index drops to its lowest level since July 2023
detail: S&P Global's UK consumer sentiment index has fallen to its lowest since July 2023, according to data released earlier this week. GfK's separate consumer confidence survey has recently shown stronger readings.

headline: German Chancellor Merz says some states use economic dependencies as weapons and calls Russia a threat
detail: Germany's Chancellor Merz said some states are using economic dependencies to strengthen their position, and described Russia as a threat to Germany.

headline: ONS: UK annual house price growth slows to 0.9% in August from 1.2%; private rents rise 3.8% in year to September
detail: The ONS says UK house prices rose 0.9% in the year to August, down from 1.2% in the year to July. Average private rents rose 3.8% in the year to September, the same rate as in August.

headline: Germany's Merz warns countries distorting markets will face a response, but says ideally the EU would not need new trade tools
detail: German Chancellor Merz says countries that distort market conditions through excessive imbalances, undervalued currencies or other means should expect a response. He adds that in the best case the EU would not use its new trade tools.

headline: Germany's Merz says China's overcapacity and trade surplus must be tackled, seeking a new trade balance without conflict
detail: German Chancellor Merz said China's excess capacity and trade surplus need to be addressed. He said the aim is a new trade balance with Beijing rather than conflict, and that Germany remains committed to open markets and a fair trade order.

headline: Russia's Deputy PM Novak says Russia may fully restore diesel exports by year-end
