detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said full restoration of diesel exports was possible by the end of the year, Tass reported.

headline: Germany's Merz says the EU will stay open to trade with China, in contrast to the US
detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the EU would keep trading with China, setting its approach apart from that of the US.

headline: France's 10-year bond yield reaches 5% for the first time since 2002
detail: The French 10-year yield has hit 5%, its highest level since 2002, according to a market report early on Wednesday.

headline: Putin begins talks with US envoy Witkoff and thanks Trump for his attention to a Ukraine settlement
detail: Interfax reports that Russia's President Putin has started a meeting with US envoy Witkoff. Putin thanked President Trump for his attention to a Ukraine settlement and asked about Witkoff's meeting in Norway.

headline: Putin tells US envoy Witkoff that Russia wants to restore economic ties with the US and can help resolve the Iran conflict
detail: Russian President Putin made the remarks in his talks with US envoy Witkoff, according to Interfax. He said Russia is interested in restoring economic ties with the US and is ready to help with a resolution on Iran.

headline: Russia's Foreign Ministry calls Japanese drone supplies to Ukraine a hostile step and says Russia will respond
detail: Russia's Foreign Ministry said it regards Japan's supply of drones to Ukraine as a hostile step. It said Russia will respond but gave no details.

headline: US envoy Witkoff calls Oslo talks productive and hopes Putin will consider resuming Russia-US-Ukraine talks
detail: US envoy Witkoff said the talks in Oslo had been productive and that he hoped Putin would consider resuming three-way talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine, Interfax reported. He also thanked Putin for a diesel deal.

headline: US envoy Witkoff says he has brought Putin documents setting out options for a Ukraine settlement
detail: Interfax reports that US envoy Witkoff said this during his talks with Russian President Putin in Moscow.

headline: Putin says Russia could increase its fertiliser supplies to the US
detail: Interfax reports that Russian President Putin made the remark during his talks with US envoy Witkoff, which have focused on restoring economic ties with the US.

headline: France's Macron says securing diesel and gas supply is the priority and that energy supplies have been secured to avoid shortages
detail: French President Macron said the priority is securing diesel and gas supply. He added that France has secured its energy supplies so that shortages are avoided.

headline: Putin offers to discuss a possible meeting with Trump in China during talks with US envoy Witkoff
detail: Russian President Putin offered to discuss the possibility of meeting US President Trump in China. He also proposed that US envoy Witkoff discuss restoring bilateral ties and economic cooperation.

headline: France's Macron says France has secured 2 terawatt-hours a month of Qatari gas for the winter
detail: French President Macron said France has secured 2 terawatt-hours of gas per month from Qatar for the winter period. He had earlier said energy supplies were secured to avoid shortages.

headline: German government says Ukraine cannot have peace unless Ukrainians are involved
detail: A German government spokesperson made the statement on Wednesday, as US envoy Witkoff holds talks with Putin on a Ukraine settlement.

headline: German government says contacts with the US suggest Washington is interested in a Ukraine negotiation process
detail: A German government spokesperson said German and European contacts with the US suggest the Americans are interested in a negotiation process on Ukraine. The spokesperson added that Germany's foreign policy adviser represented Germany at the Oslo talks.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says more tightening may be needed if inflation stays high, but higher market yields call for caution
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said further tightening could be needed if inflation remains high, and noted that markets are already adding some tightening. He said higher yields may slow the economy and that he does not see conditions for excessive wage demands.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says the US cannot blockade and threaten Iran and still expect dialogue
detail: Iranian state news agency IRNA reported the remarks by President Pezeshkian. Reuters reported that most major Gulf stock markets were subdued in early Wednesday trading after Iran said it would not hold talks with Washington to end the war until its demands are met.

headline: US offers to lend up to almost a third of its 1m-barrel Northeast home heating oil reserve
detail: The US Energy Department says companies must give back the borrowed heating oil, plus a premium, before the 2027 to 2028 winter. A US government source says the administration will consider whether more loans from the reserve should follow.

headline: Russia says its first diesel tanker to the US, carrying 40,000 tons, will sail on 22 October
detail: According to reports, Russia's Deputy Prime Minister announced the first shipment of Russian diesel to the US, a cargo of 40,000 tons leaving on 22 October.

headline: Kremlin says Russia will study the US proposals on Ukraine but that a great deal hinges on Ukraine
detail: The Kremlin made the comment after Putin's talks with US envoy Witkoff, at which Witkoff presented documents setting out options for a Ukraine settlement.

headline: Brent gains more than $2 to a session high of $111.25 a barrel as Iran denies diplomatic progress
detail: Brent crude futures are reported more than $2 higher at a session high of $111.25 a barrel, with Iran's denial of diplomatic progress and falling US oil inventories cited. WTI Midland futures also rise more than $2 to a session high of $99.88 a barrel.

headline: Kremlin says a step forward on a Ukraine settlement is theoretically possible and warns Kyiv to make decisions
detail: The Kremlin says Putin-Trump talks will be serious and long, that Ukraine's position will worsen if it does not make the necessary decisions, and that Russia is ready for nuclear talks with the US and China. Tass reports a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting is possible but has no agenda yet.

headline: Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is open to diplomacy but will defend itself and has no trust in US peace intentions
detail: Iran's foreign minister said Tehran is ready for diplomacy but will defend itself, according to the FT, and separately said Iran has no trust at all in the US administration's stated wish for peace. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's foreign minister sees little prospect of progress with the US, citing no US willingness to reach an understanding
detail: Iran's foreign minister said the US had shown no willingness to reach an understanding, so there was little reason to expect progress now, according to the FT. He also said Iran was ready for diplomacy but would defend itself.

headline: Zelenskyy says any Ukraine peace deal would need a referendum and calls a trilateral meeting the minimum requirement
detail: In an interview, Ukraine's President Zelenskyy said Ukraine would have to back any potential deal, that a deal would require a referendum, and that Ukraine must take part in any meeting, preferably with European participation. He also said US Secretary of State Rubio told him he would work on resolving limits on Starlink access.

headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine needs a freeze in fighting first, followed by talks and US security guarantees
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy set out the order in an interview with Fox News, saying a freeze must come before negotiations and US security guarantees. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Kremlin says Putin freed Hubbard as a goodwill gesture
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said President Putin released Hubbard as a gesture of goodwill. He said this as US envoy Witkoff was in talks with Putin on a Ukraine settlement.

headline: UK PM Burnham says the government is considering scrapping standing charges on gas bills
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said the government is looking at removing standing charges from household gas bills. He gave no timing or cost.

headline: Putin's talks with US envoy Witkoff on a Ukraine settlement end, TASS reports
detail: Russian state news agency TASS reports that the meeting between President Putin and US envoy Witkoff has ended. No outcome was reported.

headline: Middle East oil exports return to above pre-war levels as Gulf shipments use alternative routes, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that daily shipments from Gulf producers now average 24.6mn, against 23.3mn before the conflict. Tankers are using alternative routes.

headline: Kremlin says Norway and Finland have joined the Ukraine peace process
detail: The Kremlin said Norway and Finland are now involved in the peace process on Ukraine, according to TASS. The statement follows talks between Putin and US envoy Witkoff on a settlement.

headline: France's 10-year spread over Bunds stands at 157bp and widens to 175bp at the 30-year tenor
detail: An economist's analysis of the French bond sell-off puts the 10-year spread over German Bunds at 157bp today and the 30-year spread at 175bp, so the gap is wider at the long end of the curve.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says Trump has openly stated the US wants Iranian oil and gas
detail: In remarks carried by reports, Iran's President Pezeshkian also said Iran has held firm despite pressure and war and will keep doing so.

headline: China and the EU pledge to uphold fair competition in global markets
detail: China and the EU committed to fair competition in global markets, according to a newswire headline. This follows the European Commission's plan to propose new measures to protect the EU market from cheap imports.

headline: UK Energy Secretary is leaning towards rejecting the Rosebank oilfield, the Guardian reports
detail: The Guardian reports that the UK Energy Secretary is inclined to reject the Rosebank oilfield development. No final decision has been reported.

headline: Russian wealth fund head Dmitriev calls Putin's meeting with US envoy Witkoff productive
detail: Kirill Dmitriev, head of Russia's sovereign wealth fund, described the Putin-Witkoff talks on a Ukraine settlement as productive, TASS reports. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US authorises an exchange of supplies from its Northeast home heating oil reserve
detail: The US has given formal approval for an exchange from the Northeast home heating oil reserve, according to a market news wire. This comes after its earlier offer to lend up to almost a third of the reserve's 1m barrels.

headline: Canada's Carney and Ontario's Ford are expected to announce support for steel and auto sectors hit by tariffs, CTV reports
detail: Canadian broadcaster CTV reports that Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford are expected to unveil tariff support measures for the steel and auto industries. The report gives no figures or timing.

headline: WEF could name ECB President Lagarde as its chair as early as November, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters cites four people close to the World Economic Forum as saying the appointment could come next month. That would mean Lagarde stepping down early as ECB President.

headline: Kremlin says Putin is ready in principle to resume three-way Ukraine peace talks in mid-November
detail: After Putin's talks with US envoy Witkoff, the Kremlin said reopening Russia-US-Ukraine talks was discussed, as was implementing the Russia-US diesel deal. It added that Witkoff's briefing on the Oslo talks offered nothing of real use for a settlement.

headline: Kremlin says China is preparing a possible three-way meeting of Putin, Xi and Trump
detail: The Kremlin said its Chinese counterparts are working on the preparations for a trilateral meeting. It also said Putin told Witkoff there is still room for diplomacy on Iran and that an agreement with Tehran is needed.

headline: BoE Governor Bailey refers to today's UK inflation figures in an interview with OMFIF
detail: An economics journalist reported that Bailey mentioned the September inflation data during the OMFIF interview. No details of his remarks were given.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says a post-war security system for Russia and Ukraine is the main topic for resuming talks
detail: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia is prepared to resume negotiations chiefly on building a security system for Russia and Ukraine once the conflict ends. He spoke after Putin's talks with US envoy Witkoff.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Putin and US envoy Witkoff discussed a plan to possibly resume Russia-US-Ukraine talks
detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Putin and US envoy Witkoff discussed a plan for possibly resuming three-way negotiations with representatives of Russia, the US and Ukraine. He added that Putin said he was interested in continuing joint work with the United States.

headline: Kuwait Petroleum Corp CEO says Kuwait is exporting more than 1.1m barrels a day of crude
detail: The chief executive of Kuwait Petroleum Corporation said Kuwait's crude oil exports are running above 1.1m barrels per day.

headline: Zelenskyy tells Fox News he would accept freezing the current front lines, followed by talks and security guarantees
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy was asked about a deal leaving Ukraine in control of 75% or more of its territory. He told Fox News he would accept a freeze along the current lines, followed by negotiations and security guarantees.

headline: Aramco's Yanbu and Shaybah facilities are undamaged after Houthi claims of an attack, Argus reports
detail: Argus reports that Saudi Aramco's Yanbu and Shaybah facilities were not damaged following Houthi claims of an attack on them. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Israel's Netanyahu says Iran is again pursuing nuclear weapons and that only regime change in Tehran would remove the threat
detail: Reports quote Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu as saying Iran is trying again to develop nuclear weapons under Mojtaba Khamenei. He said overthrowing the Iranian government was the only way to remove the threat.

headline: Kremlin says the next round of Russia-US-Ukraine three-way talks could be held in Abu Dhabi
detail: The Kremlin named Abu Dhabi as a possible venue for a new round of trilateral talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine, Russian state broadcaster Vesti reports. No date was given in the report.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says the war in Ukraine is nearing an end
detail: Russian media (Vesti and Interfax) report that Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the Ukraine conflict is moving towards an end. The remarks follow Putin's talks with US envoy Witkoff on a Ukraine settlement.

headline: NIESR analysis says UK CPI inflation could rise above 5% in early 2027
detail: In a blog by Huw Dixon, NIESR points to energy and global supply shocks as the main pressures. The analysis notes that annual CPI rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1% in August, with prices up 0.4% on the month.

headline: Kremlin aide says Putin told US envoy Witkoff that Russia is ready to resume three-way Ukraine talks on 10 November
detail: A Russian presidential aide said Putin told US envoy Witkoff that Russia is ready to resume the Russia-US-Ukraine talks on 10 November. The Kremlin had earlier pointed to mid-November.

headline: France's Macron says Saudi Arabia has agreed to extend additional diesel supplies
detail: French President Macron said Saudi Arabia has agreed to extend extra diesel deliveries, AFP reports. Earlier he had said securing diesel and gas supply was the priority.

headline: Russian wealth fund head Dmitriev says Moscow sees the US suspension of the Lindsey Graham Act as an important step
detail: Russian wealth fund head Kirill Dmitriev said Russia had noted the US suspension of the act linked to Senator Lindsey Graham and regards it as an important step, according to reports. Russia designates Graham as a terrorist and extremist.

headline: LGA says council budgeted spending on homelessness services is up 170.1% since 2019/20 and calls for Autumn Budget action
detail: The Local Government Association says councils' budgeted spending has risen since 2019/20 by 42.3% in children's social care, 29.9% in adult social care and 170.1% in homelessness services. It is calling on the Autumn Budget to address rising demand.

headline: Trump wants Zelenskyy and Putin to sign a Ukraine peace deal at the G20 summit in Miami, reports say
detail: Reports carried by a market news account say US President Trump wants the Ukrainian and Russian leaders to sign a peace deal at the G20 summit in Miami. No official confirmation or market reaction was reported.

headline: Egypt's Sisi says Egyptian military involvement is solely to defend Saudi Arabia and does not mean an offensive against Yemen
detail: Egyptian President Sisi said Egypt's military role is limited to defending Saudi Arabia and does not include offensive action against Yemen. A presidency statement added that Egypt's military efforts do not reach beyond the borders of Egypt or of allied nations whose security it has committed to protect.

headline: US official says Russia has accepted a US proposal for a three-way meeting with Ukraine
detail: A US official said Russia has agreed to the US proposal for trilateral talks with Ukraine. This follows US envoy Witkoff's talks with Putin. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US natural gas futures drop 5% to a five-week low
detail: A market newswire reported that US natural gas futures fell 5% to their lowest level in five weeks on 21 October.

headline: Reuters says hotter-than-expected UK inflation has strengthened market bets on a Bank of England rate rise
detail: Reuters reports that Wednesday's UK inflation data came in above expectations and reinforced bets on the BoE raising interest rates. The FTSE 100 was little changed, with oil majors gaining as crude prices firmed.

headline: US Treasury announces new Iran-related sanctions
detail: The US Treasury Department has issued a new round of sanctions related to Iran. No details of the targets were included in the initial report.

headline: US Treasury issues Iran general licence HH allowing cargo to be offloaded from some blocked vessels
detail: The US Treasury Department has issued Iran-related general licence HH, which authorises the offloading of cargo involving certain blocked vessels. It follows new Iran-related sanctions the Treasury announced earlier.

headline: US issues licence permitting talks on the sale of Lukoil International GmbH
detail: US authorities have published a licence that permits talks on the sale of Lukoil International GmbH, the international arm of the Russian oil company.

headline: US adds vessels to its Iran sanctions list
detail: The United States has added vessels to its Iran-related sanctions list, according to a market news post. The post gave no figures and reported no market reaction.

headline: US envoy Witkoff says Russia-US-Ukraine talks are continuing at technical level and that work remains
detail: US envoy Witkoff said three-way talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine are continuing at technical level and that there is still work to do. US officials also said a technical-level meeting of the three countries has been accepted.

headline: Italy's energy minister expects energy price measures agreed with the EU to take effect in January
detail: Italy's energy minister said he expects the measures agreed with the EU to curb energy prices to come into force in January.

headline: US 20-year Treasury when-issued yield is 5.460% ahead of $13bn auction
detail: The when-issued 20-year US Treasury yield stood at 5.460% before the $13 billion reopening auction, a market post reported.

headline: US $13bn 20-year Treasury auction tails 0.9bp at 5.469% with bid-to-cover of 2.73
detail: The 20-year auction priced at a high yield of 5.469%, compared with 5.420% previously, and the bid-to-cover rose to 2.73 from 2.570; indirect bidders took 58.2%, directs 31.6% and primary dealers 10.3%. After the auction the 20-year yield pared its decline and was last down 1.25bp at 5.467%.

headline: US FinCEN subpoenas a Greek bank over possible Iran ties and seeks information on banks' links to Iranian lenders
detail: The US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network said it is issuing an administrative subpoena in an investigation into a Greek bank's potential ties to Iran. It also said it has issued several requests for information on banks' relationships with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions.

headline: EU leaders will try to agree funding for Ukraine's €70bn of unmet 2027 needs at a special summit on 26-27 November
detail: Reuters reports, citing an EU official involved in the preparations, that the special summit will also discuss the EU's next long-term budget.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says Iran will not start a war but will not give in to force
detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian said Iran has never sought war and does not intend to start one, but will not yield to pressure, Press TV reported.

headline: China and Russia agree to back companies in expanding their oil cooperation, Xinhua reports
detail: China's state news agency Xinhua reports that China and Russia have agreed to support companies in widening oil cooperation between the two countries. No figures or timetable were given.

headline: Yemen's Houthis say talks with Saudi Arabia are at a dead end and they are preparing for wider escalation
detail: Yemen's Houthis said all negotiations have stalled, blaming Saudi Arabia for trying to impose its demands, and said they are preparing for an all-round escalation of conflicts. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's Araghchi offers diplomacy another chance if the US shows sincerity, and warns that choosing war would mean greater US failure
detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said Tehran would give diplomacy another chance if it saw strong evidence that the US sincerely wants to build trust and reach a fair solution. He said that if the US chose war over diplomacy, it would suffer an even greater strategic failure.

headline: Kuwait Petroleum Corp CEO says Kuwait is producing well over 2m barrels a day of crude
detail: The chief executive of Kuwait Petroleum Corp put Kuwait's crude production at well over 2m barrels a day. This follows his earlier statement that exports are above 1.1m barrels a day.

headline: Kuwait Petroleum Corp CEO says crude exports are back at pre-war levels, with buyers now coming into the Gulf to load
detail: The chief executive of Kuwait Petroleum Corp said Kuwait's crude exports have returned to pre-war levels and that customers are now sending ships into the Gulf to collect cargoes. He also repeated that production is well over 2m barrels a day.

headline: Kuwait Petroleum Corp CEO reports significant progress in talks on pipelines
detail: The chief executive of Kuwait Petroleum Corp said a lot of progress is being made in pipeline talks, adding to earlier remarks on Kuwait's crude output and exports. No further details were given.

headline: Kuwait Petroleum Corp CEO says there is plenty of crude supply and that refined fuels are the bottleneck
detail: Barron's reports the Kuwait Petroleum Corp chief executive describing crude supply as ample and pointing to refined fuels as the constraint. This follows his earlier comments on Kuwait's production and exports.

headline: US Treasury accepts $750M of $4.751B offered in buyback of coupons maturing 2028-2036
detail: In its debt buyback operation, the US Treasury accepted $750M of the $4.751B offered, buying 8 of the 27 eligible issues. The operation was aimed at coupon securities maturing between 2028 and 2036.

headline: Zelenskyy backs US proposal for negotiator-level trilateral talks and hopes they meet by early November
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy says he supports the US proposal for three-way talks between negotiators as soon as possible. He says the teams could meet in early November and hopes the meeting happens no later than that.

headline: Canada and Ontario announce C$9bn joint package for steel and auto sectors affected by US tariffs
detail: Canada's PM Carney said the package will also support critical minerals supply chains, and that Canada will tighten enforcement against foreign steel dumping. He said Canada is still ready to negotiate a fair trade deal once the US is willing to talk in good faith.

headline: Canada's Carney says Canada is ready for a fair US trade deal when Washington negotiates in good faith, and will tighten anti-dumping…
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Carney made the remarks as Canada and Ontario unveiled a joint C$9bn package for the steel and auto sectors hit by US tariffs. He said Canada would strengthen enforcement against foreign steel dumping.

headline: Minutes show India's rate-setters see room for further hikes but are cautious about an aggressive tightening cycle
detail: Minutes of the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee meeting, released on Wednesday, show members indicated more rate rises may be needed to curb inflation. They stopped short of backing aggressive tightening because of risks to growth, Reuters reports.

headline: US prepares to order some staff and families out of its embassies across the Gulf, US officials say
detail: US officials say the State Department is getting ready to order the departure of some personnel and their family members from US embassies in the Gulf region. No market reaction is reported.

headline: Canada's Carney says he held a lengthy call with Trump on Wednesday covering trade and Iran
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he spoke with US President Trump on Wednesday about a wide range of issues, including Iran and some trade matters. He gave no details of any outcome.

headline: Saudi Energy Ministry says air defences intercept a drone aimed at a facility at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield
detail: The Saudi Energy Ministry said air defences intercepted a drone that was trying to hit a facility at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. The ministry statement made no mention of damage.

headline: Aramco says Shaybah oilfield operations are unaffected by drone attack; Saudi official says two people killed
detail: Saudi state news agency SPA, citing an Energy Ministry official, reports two deaths in the drone attack on the Shaybah oilfield in the Eastern region. A statement says the attack had no impact on Saudi Aramco's operations at the field.

headline: EU set to delay its push for cheaper UK university fees for EU students as it works to finalise reset deal
detail: The Financial Times reports the EU is set to put off its demand on UK tuition fees for students from the bloc. The concession could help the two sides complete a 'reset' deal at a summit next month.

headline: Trump says the US is getting closer to a settlement of Russia's war with Ukraine
detail: US President Trump said on Wednesday evening that a settlement of the Russia-Ukraine war is getting closer. It follows Kremlin comments that three-way talks with the US and Ukraine could resume in November.

headline: US orders non-emergency government staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks increase
detail: The US State Department has issued an ordered departure for non-emergency government employees and their families, covering Saudi Arabia only. A State Department spokesperson said Iranian-backed Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including on civilian airports and critical infrastructure.

headline: Morningstar says leading gilt investors expect Healey's 28 October Budget to avoid fuelling gilt market volatility
detail: Research firm Morningstar said on Wednesday that major investors in UK government bonds expect the finance minister, John Healey, to avoid triggering gilt market volatility in his Budget on 28 October.

headline: US waives record-keeping requirements on red diesel tax to attract buyers
detail: US authorities have waived record-keeping requirements linked to red diesel tax in an effort to draw in buyers, a market news account reported.

headline: Trump says he does not know of any move to pull US embassy staff from the Middle East
detail: Asked about reports that US government staff had been told to leave posts in the Gulf, President Trump said he did not know that they were. He also said he has the right to impose sanctions on any day.

headline: Trump says the US continues to beat Iran and that he cannot say whether a denuclearisation meeting will happen
detail: US President Trump made the remarks to reporters on Wednesday evening. He also said he can impose sanctions on any day.

headline: Senior Iranian security official says Iran expects a US-Israeli attack and treats US diplomatic gestures as invalid
detail: Iran's Fars news agency reported the remarks from an unnamed senior Iranian security official on Wednesday evening. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran warns it will target US political figures if strikes on Iran resume, Fars reports
detail: Iran's Fars news agency reports that Iran has threatened to target US political figures if strikes on the country resume. No market reaction is reported.

headline: US troops and diplomats are leaving posts in the Middle East, NBC reports, citing two US officials
detail: NBC reports that US troops and diplomats are being evacuated from posts in the Middle East, citing two US officials. This comes after earlier reports that the US was preparing to order some staff and families out of its embassies across the Gulf.

headline: US troops moved from Middle East posts include some in Jordan, Qatar and Kuwait, NBC News reports
detail: NBC News reports that the US troops repositioned in the region include forces in Jordan and some in Qatar and Kuwait. This adds detail to its earlier report that US troops and diplomats are leaving posts in the Middle East.

headline: New Zealand Q3 CPI rises 3.7% on the year, below the 3.8% forecast and down from 4.1%
detail: New Zealand consumer prices rose 0.7% in Q3 from the previous quarter, against a forecast of 0.8% and 1.5% before, while non-tradables inflation was 3.3% on the year and 1.0% on the quarter. The New Zealand dollar fell to $0.5692 after the release.

headline: France's 10-year bond yield rises above 5% for the first time in nearly a quarter of a century
detail: Reuters' market wrap reports that the French 10-year yield went above 5% on Wednesday, with European markets livelier than calm US bond, currency and energy markets.

headline: US and Israel are drawing up a plan for new strikes on Iran after the US election, NYT reports
detail: The New York Times reports that US Defense Secretary Hegseth met Israel's Netanyahu this week to discuss new strikes on Iran.

headline: Trump says the US inflicted a crushing defeat on Tehran and wants lasting results in Iran
detail: US President Trump made the remarks early on 22 October UTC.

headline: Japan's 10-year JGB yield falls 2bp to 2.87% in early Tokyo trade
detail: Benchmark 10-year JGB futures opened 0.17 point higher and the 5-year yield fell 1bp to 2.285%, while Nikkei futures were down 0.7%.

headline: Bank of Korea holds base rate at 3.00% in unanimous vote and says it will decide the timing and pace of further hikes
detail: The hold matched the 3.00% forecast. The Bank of Korea says inflation will stay above target for an extended period. It expects growth this year and next to come in well above its August forecasts of 3.3% and 2.9%, and next year's CPI and core CPI to exceed its August forecasts of 2.3% and 2.5%.

headline: Brent and WTI futures rise about 1% after the US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia
detail: Crude futures rose about 1% after the US ordered staff to leave Saudi Arabia. The WSJ says concern is growing that conflict in the Middle East will flare up again.

headline: Japan's 30-year government bond yield falls 3bp to 3.895%
detail: The 30-year JGB yield fell 3bp to 3.895% in Tokyo trade. The WSJ reports that the Japanese yield curve is flattening amid concern about AI-related credit risks.

headline: BoK Governor Shin says growth and inflation pressure are stronger than in August and the restrictive stance should stay
detail: After the Bank of Korea held its rate at 3.00%, Governor Shin said it would keep acting until inflation pressure eases to target. He also said the bank does not have to follow market forecasts of the peak policy rate, and that next year's government budget could add 0.5 percentage point to GDP growth.

headline: RBNZ sectoral factor model puts New Zealand's Q3 core inflation at 2.8% on the year
detail: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's sectoral factor model, a core inflation measure, shows 2.8% annual inflation in the third quarter. It was published after the Q3 CPI print of 3.7%.

headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says seven ships were hit in the Gulf and warns US bases could be targeted
detail: The IRGC Navy said four vessels it accused of illegal oil transfers were struck and set on fire in the northern Gulf, and three more hit mines west of the Strait of Hormuz overnight. It warned its response could extend to US bases in the region if Washington keeps urging ships to cross the mined waterway.

headline: Brent rises to $110.90 a barrel on concerns over supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia
detail: Brent crude climbed to $110.90 a barrel as the risk of attacks on Saudi Arabia added to supply concerns. Separately, the WSJ said crude was rising as geopolitical risks came back into focus.

headline: BoK Governor Shin says the inflation target may be reached in 2028 and the bank need not follow market terminal rate pricing
detail: Bank of Korea Governor Shin said hitting the inflation target may be feasible in 2028 and that the bank does not necessarily need to follow financial markets' expectations for the terminal policy rate. He also said South Korea is at an early stage of internationalising the won.

headline: Japan's 40-year JGB yield falls 3.5bp to 4.015%
detail: The 40-year Japanese government bond yield fell 3.5bp to 4.015% in Tokyo trade.

headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says concessions to Moscow will not end the war after a Russian strike on Kyiv that followed US talks
detail: Ukraine's foreign minister spoke after a Russian strike on Kyiv, which came after talks with the US. He said that placating Russia would not bring the war to an end.

headline: Japan's 20-year JGB yield falls 2.5bp to 3.68% while the 2-year yield holds at 1.9%
detail: In Tokyo trade, the 20-year Japanese government bond yield fell 2.5bp to 3.68% and the 2-year yield held steady at 1.9%.

headline: Oil rises more than $2 a barrel as further Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raise fears of wider Middle East escalation
detail: Reuters reports oil prices up by more than $2 a barrel on Thursday after further Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. The move reflects concerns over wider conflict and further disruption to crude supplies from the region.

headline: IMF warns further disruption to energy output and trade routes could push up energy prices, weaken growth and raise inflation
detail: The IMF says further disruption to energy production and trade routes could lift energy prices, slow growth and add to inflation.

headline: French manufacturing confidence rises to 105 in October, above the 101 forecast; overall business climate at 97
detail: INSEE's October survey puts manufacturing confidence at 105 against a forecast and prior reading of 101, and the overall business climate at 97 against a forecast of 95.5 and 96 previously. The production outlook indicator rises to -8 from -9, and own-company production outlook rises to 19 from 15.

headline: Goldman Sachs estimates crude freight costs on Middle Eastern routes are above $35 a barrel as the Hormuz crisis continues
detail: Goldman Sachs estimates that global average crude freight rates are above $20 a barrel, compared with about $3 a year ago, and that rates on Middle Eastern routes are above $35 a barrel.

headline: BoJ likely to say inflation has hit its 2% target but hold off on back-to-back hikes in October, Nikkei reports
detail: Nikkei reports the Bank of Japan's October meeting is likely to put off consecutive rate increases, even though the bank is expected to say inflation has reached its 2% target. USD/JPY was reported 0.7% lower at 157.11 shortly afterwards.

headline: Japan's Rengo union group targets 6% pay rises in 2027 wage talks and sets first medium-term goal of 15% by 2030
detail: Rengo, Japan's largest labour union group, puts the centre of its 2027 wage increase target at 6% and keeps its benchmark of 5% or more. It also sets its first medium-term target, a 15% wage increase by 2030.

headline: Aramco CEO says the company wants to work with other countries to build up strategic oil reserves
detail: Saudi Aramco's chief executive, Amin Nasser, said the company is looking for partnerships with other countries to increase strategic reserves. No volumes or partner countries were given.

headline: SNB minutes say current monetary conditions are appropriate and a greater readiness to intervene in FX is no longer needed
detail: Minutes of the Swiss National Bank's latest meeting say medium-term inflationary pressure is only slightly higher than at the June assessment, while inflation is likely to rise somewhat in the short term because of higher energy prices. Board members flagged second-round effects as a risk to inflation, said uncertainty remains high and expect moderate growth in the coming quarters.

headline: SNB minutes find no second-round inflation effects and say a weaker franc has eased monetary conditions since June
detail: The Swiss National Bank's minutes of its September meeting say core inflation has risen only slightly, inflation expectations are stable and medium-term inflation pressure is only a little higher than at the June review. They also say the franc's fall outpaced the rise in interest rates, leaving monetary conditions easier, and that a worsening in the Middle East would hit global activity harder.

headline: Treasuries extend rally as higher oil prices drive a global risk-off move; eurozone bonds come under pressure
detail: The FT reports that US Treasuries are rallying again and eurozone bonds are weaker as rising oil prices prompt a risk-off move. China's CSI 300 index falls 1.8% and European equities are lower.

headline: Brent futures climb more than 3% to $112.55 a barrel, highest level since May
detail: Brent crude futures rose by more than 3% to $112.55 a barrel, their highest level since May, according to a market report.

headline: Global equities slide as oil prices rise; China's CSI 300 falls 1.8% and European shares lower
detail: The Financial Times reports a broad fall in global stock markets as oil prices climb, with China's CSI 300 index down 1.8% and European equities also lower.

headline: Iran warns the conflict could widen over what it calls illegal transit through the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran said the scope of the conflict may expand in response to transit through the Strait of Hormuz that it describes as illegal. No market reaction was reported alongside the statement.

headline: Aramco CEO says he sees oil demand rising to 3 million barrels a day after the Iran war as Saudi Arabia seeks stockpile partners
detail: Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser told Al Arabiya Business TV on Thursday that Saudi Arabia and Aramco want to work with other countries to expand their strategic oil stockpile. He put oil demand after the Iran war at 3 million barrels per day, Reuters reports.

headline: Kremlin says Russia has not yet picked its representative for trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine
detail: The Kremlin also said more European diplomatic activity on a peaceful settlement in Ukraine was a positive development. It added that the US is doing a lot for a settlement while the EU is doing nothing.

headline: France's 10-year bond yield climbs to 5.084%, above US Treasury yields for the first time since 2013
detail: France's 10-year government bond yield reached 5.084%, moving above US Treasury yields for the first time since 2013, according to a market report. Earlier in the session it had risen above 5% for the first time in nearly a quarter of a century.

headline: Kremlin envoy Dmitriev says a diesel fuel deal with the US will start being put into effect tomorrow, reports say
detail: Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev announced that work to implement a diesel fuel deal between Russia and the United States begins tomorrow, according to reports relayed on social media. The reports gave no further terms.

headline: Resolution Foundation says lower net migration will reduce fiscal headroom in the coming Budget
detail: The Resolution Foundation said on 22 October that lower net migration is expected to weigh on the government's fiscal headroom at the upcoming Budget. It gave no figures in its post.

headline: European Parliament approves a three-year delay to the EU's methane emissions rules
detail: The European Parliament voted to approve putting back the EU's methane regulation by three years, according to a market news wire. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Houthis say they will announce several military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia in a statement at 3:00 PM
detail: The Yemeni Armed Forces, the Houthis' military, say the statement will also set out their position on what they call a Saudi threat to Yemeni tribes. The announcement follows further Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia that have been linked to rising oil prices.

headline: France's 10-year bond risk premium widens to 175bp
detail: A market newswire reports that France's 10-year government bond risk premium has risen to 175bp. Earlier, France's 10-year yield moved above 5% for the first time in nearly a quarter of a century.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK household energy bills are due to rise again in January
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the January rise in energy bills comes in the coldest part of the year, when 46% of domestic gas use takes place in the first quarter.

headline: German 10-year Bund yield drops 6.5bp to 3.3486%, its lowest since 4 September
detail: The German 10-year government bond yield fell 6.5bp to 3.3486%, its lowest level since 4 September, according to a market wire report.

headline: France's 10-year spread over Bunds widens 16bp to 176bp
detail: The spread between France's 10-year government bond yield and the German Bund widened by a further 16bp to 176bp, according to a market wire report.

headline: IMF forecasts Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan GDP shrinking 1.3% in 2026 because of the Iran war
detail: On Thursday the IMF forecast that output in the region will contract by 1.3% this year and then grow by 6.6% in 2027. It warned that further disruption to energy production could make the outlook worse.

headline: Iran's national security council chief says Tehran is in talks with Gulf states on a security framework to prevent conflict
detail: The head of Iran's National Security Council said Iran is talking to Gulf states about a regional security architecture aimed at preventing conflict.

headline: French yields rise about 10bp while US Treasury yields fall about 10bp as the two markets diverge
detail: An FT markets journalist reports that French government bond yields are up about 10bp while US yields are down about 10bp. This comes after France's 10-year yield moved above US Treasury yields earlier in the session.

headline: Gulf stock markets fall in early trade after new Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia raise fears of wider regional conflict
detail: Reuters reports that the main Gulf stock markets fell early on Thursday after fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis. The report says the strikes added to fears of a broader escalation in the region.

headline: India's trade minister says the India-EU trade deal will be signed before year-end and could take effect within 4–5 months
detail: India's trade minister made the comments during a visit to Germany. He said the agreement could become operational 4–5 months after it is signed.

headline: Markets price only 3.5bp of Fed tightening for the 28 October meeting, consistent with the Fed holding
detail: A market economist reports that pricing for the Fed's 28 October decision shows just 3.5bp of tightening, which he reads as markets expecting the Fed to stay on hold. He links this to the sell-off in global bond markets.

headline: France's 30-year spread over Germany reaches 190bp, wider than the 175bp gap at the 10-year tenor
detail: An economist notes that the French spread over German debt is 190bp at the 30-year tenor today, against 175bp at 10 years.

headline: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi defence ministry in Riyadh, Aramco site in Yanbu and King Fahd airport in Dammam
detail: Yemen's Houthis say they have attacked the Saudi defence ministry in Riyadh, an Aramco facility in Yanbu and King Fahd Airport in Dammam. The UAE foreign ministry condemns the airport attack as a violation of Saudi sovereignty.

headline: France's 10-year risk premium over Bunds hits a fresh 15-year high, back at euro zone debt crisis levels
detail: Reuters reports that the premium investors demand to hold French 10-year government bonds over German Bunds has reached its highest level in 15 years.

headline: US initial jobless claims fall 6K to 194K in week to 17 October, below the 200K forecast
detail: US initial jobless claims came in at 194K against a 200K forecast, and the previous week was revised to 200K. Continuing claims rose 25K to 1,728K in the week to 10 October, above the 1,710K estimate.

headline: German tax panel raises its 2026-30 total tax revenue projection to €43.4bn above the May forecast
detail: The panel puts federal revenue for 2026-30 €3.3bn above the May forecast, with this year €3.0bn below and next year €4.1bn above; the ministry projects 2026 tax at €379.1bn. Germany's finance minister says there will be no new fiscal room in 2027 and that budget consolidation must continue.

headline: German finance minister Klingbeil says further budget cuts are needed to create new fiscal room
detail: German Finance Minister Klingbeil said more budget cuts are required to open up fiscal room. His remarks came as the German tax panel published updated revenue projections, putting this year's state tax revenue €0.1bn above the May forecast.

headline: US 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields are both down 10bp on the day
detail: A market wire reports that US 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields have each fallen 10bp on the day, so the rally covers both the short and long end of the curve.

headline: Eurozone flash consumer confidence falls to -17.9 in October, below the -17 forecast
detail: The flash eurozone consumer confidence reading was -17.9, compared with a forecast of -17 and a previous reading of -16.5.

headline: UK ASHE data shows the share of workers in low pay did not fall, the first time in 15 years, says Resolution Foundation
detail: According to the Resolution Foundation, the ONS Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings released today shows the low-pay share of the workforce did not fall for the first time in 15 years. The survey covers the labour market from earlier this year.

headline: Canada and Turkey agree to begin free trade agreement talks before the end of the year
detail: Turkish President Erdogan said after meeting Canadian PM Carney that the two countries will start free trade talks before year-end. Carney said negotiators will hold a first round in Ankara next month as part of a new strategic partnership with a three-year action plan covering trade, defence, energy and people-to-people ties.

headline: Turkey and Canada aim to lift bilateral trade to $5bn and then $10bn, from $3bn; Carney says trade talks start next month
detail: Turkish President Erdogan said the aim is to raise trade with Canada to $5bn and then $10bn, up from $3bn, as the two countries upgrade ties to a strategic partnership. Canadian Prime Minister Carney said negotiators will meet next month to discuss trade.

headline: US Treasury rally deepens: 5-year yield falls 14.33bp to 4.827% and 3-year falls 13.93bp to 4.771%
detail: The US 5-year Treasury yield touched 4.825%, its lowest since 23 September, and was last down 14.33bp at 4.827%. The 3-year yield touched 4.768%, its lowest since 18 September, and was last down 13.93bp at 4.771%.

headline: French 5-year CDS go above 100bp for the first time since October 2012
detail: LSEG data shows French 5-year credit default swaps rose above 100bp for the first time since October 2012, and were last quoted at 97.75bp. This comes as France's spread over Bunds widens further.

headline: 20-year gilt yields fall to about a one-month low, heading for their best three-day run since June
detail: A UK markets commentator says 20-year gilt yields are close to their lowest level in a month. They are on track for their strongest three days since June. No figures were given.

headline: Kansas City Fed composite index slips to 11 in October, below the 12 forecast
detail: The Kansas City Fed composite index came in at 11, compared with a forecast of 12 and 14 previously.

headline: Kansas City Fed manufacturing index falls to 16 in October from 20
detail: The Kansas City Fed's manufacturing index came in at 16 for October, down from 20 the previous month. No forecast was given.

headline: Bank of Italy Governor Panetta says there is no evidence that bigger banks lead to tighter credit supply
detail: Bank of Italy Governor Fabio Panetta, an ECB Governing Council member, said there was no evidence that larger banks tighten credit supply. The remarks did not address interest rates.

headline: US Treasury says 26 October 2-year auction could trigger an unscheduled 5-year note reopening if high yield is 4.875%-4.999%
detail: The US Treasury said the result of the 2-year note auction on 26 October could lead to an unscheduled reopening of 5-year notes if the auction's high yield falls between 4.875% and 4.999%.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield falls below 5% for the first time since 23 September, down 14.97bp at 4.996%
detail: The 10-year US Treasury yield was last down 14.97bp at 4.996%, below 5% for the first time since 23 September, as the Treasury rally extended.

headline: Trump accuses Iran of inventing attacks and mines to push up oil prices before the US midterm elections
detail: In posts on Truth Social, US President Trump said Iran was fabricating hits and mines to drive up the price of oil ahead of the midterm elections.

headline: Saudi Aramco orders staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters and work remotely, sources say
detail: Reuters, citing six people with knowledge of the matter, reported that Saudi Aramco told staff to leave its Dhahran headquarters and work remotely. The move comes a day after an attack on a nearby airport killed two people.

headline: UK agrees deal for gas supply from Belgium ahead of winter, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Britain has agreed a last-minute deal to secure gas supply from Belgium before winter. The report says the deal follows years of falling UK domestic gas production.

headline: Average US 30-year fixed mortgage rate eases to 7.32% in week to 22 October from 7.40%, Freddie Mac says
detail: Freddie Mac's weekly survey puts the average US 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.32% in the week to 22 October, down from 7.40% the week before.

headline: French 10-year yield moves 50bp above Italy's for the first time
detail: The French 10-year bond yield spread over Italian equivalents reached 50bp for the first time, market reports said. The move comes as France's premium over Bunds hits 15-year highs.

headline: Qatar says it is seeking more LNG deals with buyers outside the Middle East
detail: Qatar said it is looking for additional liquefied natural gas supply deals beyond the Middle East region. No volumes or counterparties were given.

headline: Russian government says gasoline and diesel output has risen and fuel reserves are being built up
detail: Interfax reported the Russian government's statement that gasoline and diesel production has increased and that fuel reserves are being built up. The statement gave no figures.

headline: ECB's Pereira calls for Europe to deepen its single market
detail: ECB official Pereira said the European single market needs to be deepened. The reported remarks did not touch on interest rates.

headline: Resolution Foundation says fuel prices have risen again since September's CPI reading, when UK inflation reached 3.5%
detail: The Resolution Foundation says higher fuel prices made the largest contribution to the rise in UK CPI inflation to 3.5% in September, its highest rate in almost a year. It adds that fuel prices have risen further since the September CPI data were collected.

headline: US 5-year Treasury yield extends its fall to 15bp on the day, at 4.80%
detail: The US 5-year Treasury yield is down 15bp on the day at 4.80%, a deeper fall than the 14.33bp drop to 4.827% reported earlier in the session.

headline: Senior Iranian security official says Tehran will treat Netanyahu and Trump alike in any military escalation
detail: A senior Iranian security official said Iran would make no distinction between the Israeli prime minister and the US president if the conflict escalates militarily. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Senior Israeli officers see no reason to strike Iran ahead of the US elections, Ynet reports
detail: Israeli outlet Ynet reports that senior Israeli military officers see no reason for a strike on Iran before the US elections. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Traders stop fully pricing a Fed rate hike before the end of 2026
detail: Market commentary reports that money markets no longer fully price a Federal Reserve rate increase before year-end, as the US Treasury rally continues.

headline: US $26bn 5-year TIPS auction tails 0.7bp at 2.367% high yield, bid-to-cover 2.41
detail: The US Treasury sold $26bn of 5-year TIPS at a high yield of 2.367%, against a when-issued level of about 2.36% before the sale, with bid-to-cover at 2.41. Indirect bidders took 62.0%, direct bidders 32.4% and primary dealers 5.5%.

headline: Rubio reaffirms US commitment to Qatar's security and to freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz
detail: The US State Department says Secretary of State Rubio restated US support for Qatar's security and for free passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The readout refers to Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine is ready for peace talks at the G20 but has had no invitation so far
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv is prepared to hold peace talks at the G20 and has not yet been invited. He also said he hopes to discuss Starlink with US Secretary of State Rubio in the coming days.

headline: Finland's prime minister rules out gas deals with Russia while the war continues
detail: Finland's prime minister said there can be no gas deals with Russia for as long as the war in Ukraine goes on.

headline: Brent extends its rally to a $4 a barrel gain, hitting a five-month high as Houthi attacks raise Middle East supply fears
detail: Oil futures pushed further ahead late on Thursday, with Brent crude up $4 a barrel on the day at a five-month high. The rise is reported to be driven by worries over Middle East supply after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

headline: Canada's chief negotiator on US trade says tariff-free trade with the US is not expected to return
detail: Canada's US trade negotiator, Charette, said Canada should not expect a return to tariff-free trade with the United States. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Egypt urges talks on Yemen as its parliament prepares to vote on military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis
detail: Egypt's foreign minister said Cairo favours pursuing every diplomatic option to end the Yemen conflict, Reuters reports. The parliament votes next week on whether to authorise the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

headline: Putin describes eastern Ukraine as historically Russian territory
detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin made the remark about eastern Ukraine. Ukraine has said it is ready for peace talks, and the Kremlin has not yet named its representative for trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine.

headline: WTI crude settles up 2.39% at $99.47 a barrel
detail: NYMEX December WTI futures settled $2.32 higher at $99.47 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.9321 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.1765 a gallon.

headline: Putin says Russia has no plans to go to war with Europe
detail: The Russian president said Russia does not plan to wage war on Europe, according to a wire headline.

headline: Putin says trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine will cover Russian and Ukrainian security, and European security too
detail: Russia's president said the planned trilateral talks involving the US and Ukraine would focus on security guarantees for Russia and Ukraine. He added that European security should also be on the agenda.

headline: Brent crude futures settle 4.00% higher at $113.17 a barrel, up $4.35
detail: Brent futures closed the session $4.35, or 4.00%, higher at $113.17 a barrel, after Houthi attacks earlier in the day raised fears over Middle East supply.

headline: Lebanon-Israel talks in Florida end with no breakthrough, US official says
detail: A US official told Al Arabiya that the meetings in Florida between Lebanon and Israel ended without a breakthrough. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK Chancellor plans to cut back business asset disposal relief, Telegraph reports
detail: The Telegraph reports that the Chancellor is set to scale back business asset disposal relief. No further details or figures were given.

headline: Trump signs executive order on US housing costs that seeks to cut mortgage insurance premiums
detail: The White House says President Trump has signed an executive order aimed at lowering housing costs for Americans. Reports say the order seeks to reduce mortgage insurance premiums.

headline: Romanian president says Russia looks more focused on escalating the Ukraine war than on pursuing peace
detail: Romania's President Nicușor Dan questioned whether Moscow is ready for a deal despite US-led diplomacy. He urged NATO members to raise their readiness while avoiding further escalation, as EU members prepare for possible Russian hybrid threats.

headline: Russia agrees to resume trilateral peace talks with the US and Ukraine, with technical talks possibly in Abu Dhabi in mid-November
detail: The agreement came during a visit by US envoy Steve Witkoff, who also secured the release of US detainee Stephen Hubbard and discussed Russian diesel shipments, according to a market news account. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump executive order directs US trade negotiations on wind turbine imports
detail: A White House executive order released on Thursday tells the Commerce Secretary and the US Trade Representative to pursue negotiations on wind turbine imports, Reuters reports. They must report back to the President on progress within 180 days.

headline: UK relaxes 'fit and proper' rules for holding bankers to account, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK is loosening the regulatory regime that requires bankers to be fit and proper. The regime was central to past actions against former Barclays chief executive Jes Staley and hedge fund owner Crispin Odey.

headline: Trump warns the US may carry out further strikes on Iran
detail: US President Trump says the US has already struck Iran hard and may strike again. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Trump invokes the Defense Production Act to expand US petroleum capacity
detail: The US president invoked the Defense Production Act for petroleum capacity, waived the Act's section 303 rules to expand oil capacity and sent a memo on the matter to Defense Secretary Hegseth, according to market news posts.

headline: UK banking watchdog to review how financial regulation affects investment, capital and growth, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that the new UK banking watchdog will examine the effect of its rules on competitiveness, with more focus on transparency and on an objective to promote competition.

headline: UK GfK consumer confidence drops to -24 in October from -13, its biggest monthly fall since 2020
detail: GfK's October survey shows the major purchases index at its lowest since September 2024, while the inflation outlook component rose.

headline: Japan's September core CPI rises to 2.1% year on year from 1.7%, matching forecasts
detail: Japanese government data show headline CPI at 2.1% against 1.9% previously, and the measure excluding fresh food and energy at 2.4%. Reports say core inflation is above 2% for the first time since December 2023.

headline: Australia's October flash composite PMI drops to 47.7 from 51.3 as services fall to 47.8
detail: S&P Global's flash readings show the services PMI down to 47.8 from 51.9, while manufacturing edged up to 49.7 from 49.6.

headline: Chancellor Healey says next week's Budget will target entrepreneurs, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that the Chancellor intends to aim next week's Budget at entrepreneurs, as the number of UK founders choosing to sell their businesses rather than scale them reaches an eight-year high.

headline: US Treasury proposes tighter curbs on investment in sensitive Chinese technology, FT reports
detail: According to the FT, the proposed restrictions would cover investment in areas including AI, hypersonic weapons and biotech.

headline: US has strike plans against Iran ready with Israel, including energy facilities, CNN reports citing US officials
detail: CNN, citing US officials, reports that Trump's advisers have drawn up plans for strikes on Iran coordinated with Israel that could proceed as soon as he approves. Targets would include nuclear infrastructure, missile and drone depots and energy facilities, and the officials say using the largest US conventional bomb is one option under consideration.

headline: JGB yields fall in early Tokyo trade, with the 10-year down 7bp at 2.810%
detail: The 5-year JGB yield fell 8bp to 2.210% and the 20-year fell 6bp to 3.620%, while 10-year JGB futures gained 0.6 point. Asia-Pacific equities opened lower amid moves into safe-haven assets.

headline: UK grid operators expect adequate gas and electricity supply this winter, with peak gas supply at 592 mcm
detail: Britain's energy grid operators project that peak daily gas demand this winter will be 493 mcm, against peak supply of 592 mcm. They expect electricity supply to be sufficient.

headline: Japan's October flash manufacturing PMI falls to 53.3 from 54.1 while services rise to 52.0
detail: In S&P Global's October flash survey, Japan's composite PMI was unchanged at 52.3. The services PMI rose to 52.0 from 51.3.

headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at 6.7180 per dollar, the strongest fixing since 2 February 2023
detail: The People's Bank of China set its daily yuan reference rate at 6.7180 per dollar. Market estimates had put the fixing at 6.6758.

headline: Treasuries post their biggest daily rally in more than three years as a tech sell-off drives a move into safe havens
detail: Reuters reports that worries over the funding needs of AI hit technology stocks and pushed investors into sovereign bonds and safe-haven currencies, cutting bets on rate hikes. The FT reports the yen rallying as Asian stocks followed Wall Street lower.

headline: 2-year JGB yield falls 6bp to 1.840%
detail: Japan's 2-year government bond yield fell 6bp to 1.840% in Tokyo trade on Friday.

headline: US envoy Waltz says the US can keep its Iran blockade in place for the foreseeable future and presses Tehran for a nuclear deal
detail: In an interview with the FT, Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN, said the US is ready for a long stand-off with Iran. He warned that Tehran must reach a meaningful agreement on its nuclear programme.

headline: India's October flash composite PMI rises to 56.7 from 55.9 as services reach 56.2
detail: The HSBC flash composite PMI for India beat the 56.1 forecast, and services rose to 56.2 from 55.2 against a 55.5 forecast. Manufacturing slipped to 54.9 from 55.1, just below the 55.0 forecast.

headline: Iran threatens wider attacks on economic and civilian sites in retaliation for US strike, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Iran has warned it could widen its attacks to economic and civilian targets in response to a US strike. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Chancellor Healey to pledge cuts to paperwork for small UK firms, with savings put at £800mn a year, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Chancellor will promise to remove unnecessary paperwork for small companies. The government says the deregulation drive could reduce business costs by £800mn a year.

headline: UK retail sales growth slows to 0.8% year on year, short of the 1% forecast, as core sales fall 0.7% on the month
detail: Official UK retail sales rose 0.8% year on year, below the 1% forecast and down from 2.4% previously. Core sales also grew 0.8% year on year against a 1.4% forecast and 2.7% previously, and fell 0.7% month on month against a forecast fall of 0.1% and a previous rise of 0.6%.

headline: UK retail sales fall 0.4% on the month in September, a bigger drop than the 0.1% forecast
detail: Including fuel, September retail sales fell 0.4% on the month after a 0.5% rise previously. Excluding fuel, annual growth was 0.8% against a 1.4% estimate and 2.7% previously.

headline: BoJ Financial Stability Report finds Japan's financial system broadly stable, with no major imbalances
detail: The Bank of Japan published its latest Financial Stability Report, which judged the financial system broadly stable and found no major imbalances.

headline: BoJ says Japanese banks can withstand stress from oil and AI risks, and flags energy costs squeezing SME profits
detail: The Bank of Japan's Financial Stability Report says higher raw material and energy prices appear to be weighing on profits, particularly at SMEs, and that some firms are relatively exposed to higher crude prices. It also says the Middle East situation, AI-related investment, non-bank developments, asset prices and growing concentration in private funds' portfolios all need close monitoring.

headline: Tanker with 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel heads for New York following a Putin-Trump agreement, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports, citing LSEG shipping data, that a Malta-flagged tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is bound for New York following an agreement with US President Trump.

headline: China pledges to respond to US restrictions on research ties and demands an end to measures against its research bodies
detail: China's Commerce Ministry said it would take action after the US imposed curbs on research ties, and called on Washington to stop what it described as discriminatory measures against Chinese research institutions. No market reaction was reported.

headline: French flash services PMI drops to 48.4 in October from 51.2, well below the 50.7 forecast
detail: France's October flash services PMI came in at 48.4, against a forecast of 50.7 and a previous reading of 51.2.

headline: French flash manufacturing PMI slips to 49.3 in October from 50.6 and the composite falls to 48.4, both short of forecasts
detail: S&P Global's October flash survey shows French manufacturing at 49.3 against a 50.5 forecast. The composite PMI came in at 48.4, below the expected 50.7, down from 51.2.

headline: German flash composite PMI falls to 52.8 in October from 53.8 as services slip to 51.7, while manufacturing rises to 54.2
detail: Germany's October flash composite PMI came in at 52.8, below the 53.4 forecast, and services fell to 51.7 from 52.9 against a 52.5 forecast. Manufacturing beat expectations at 54.2, up from 53.9, with 53.5 forecast.

headline: Eurozone flash composite PMI falls to 51.9 in October from 53.1, short of the 52.7 forecast, with services at 51.7
detail: The eurozone flash services PMI fell to 51.7 from 53.0, against a 52.5 forecast. Flash manufacturing slipped to 52.4 from 52.9, below the 52.8 forecast.

headline: ECB consumer survey shows 12-month inflation expectations rise to 3.1% in September; 3-year expectations stay at 2.9%
detail: The ECB's consumer expectations survey has 12-month-ahead inflation expectations at 3.1% in September, up from 3.0% in August. Expectations three years ahead are unchanged at 2.9%.

headline: BoJ sees rates still far from neutral and is expected to keep raising them quickly, with December in focus, sources say
detail: Sources say the Bank of Japan thinks inflation needs to settle near its target and that interest rates remain well short of neutral. The sources also say the central bank is expected to keep raising rates rapidly, with attention on December.

headline: Brent hits $114 a barrel for the first time since May as AI worries weigh on global stocks, FT reports
detail: The FT reports oil has reached $114 a barrel for the first time since May, while global equities have been hit by concerns over the AI boom. European and US markets are reported to be steadier.

headline: Iran says it has halted 'illicit' shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Fars reports
detail: Iran says it has stopped vessel traffic in the Strait of Hormuz that it calls illicit, according to the Fars news agency. The report gives no further details and no market reaction has been reported.

headline: UK flash services PMI rises to 53.1 in October from 52.1, well above the 51.8 forecast
detail: The flash UK services PMI for October came in at 53.1, against a forecast of 51.8 and a previous reading of 52.1.

headline: Treasury minister Murray says UK fiscal rules support stability as the Budget comes amid global uncertainty
detail: Treasury minister Murray said the fiscal rules underpin the UK economy's stability and that the Budget comes during a period of unprecedented global economic instability. She added that the government is focused on entrepreneurs and on helping businesses grow.

headline: UK flash composite PMI climbs to 53.1 in October from 52.0, beating the 51.7 forecast; manufacturing rises to 52.8
detail: The October flash composite PMI came in at 53.1, against a forecast of 51.7 and 52.0 the previous month. The flash manufacturing PMI rose to 52.8 from 51.9, also above the 51.8 forecast.

headline: GfK links October slump in UK consumer confidence to the cost of living, inflation and Iran; morale and big-purchase gauges lead the fall
detail: The drop in GfK's UK consumer confidence index came mainly from its general economic outlook and major purchase components. A post noted that a fall this large has happened in only six months over the past 52 years.

headline: UK October flash PMI shows employment rising for the first time in more than two years
detail: An economist reviewing the October flash PMI says the survey records the first increase in jobs in over two years. He adds that the employment balance is moving back into line with output growth.

headline: Trump administration ends programme that rewarded allies for aligning with US export controls
detail: A market news account reports that the US administration has halted a programme that rewarded allied countries for aligning with US export controls. No further details or market reaction were reported.

headline: Kremlin says three-way Ukraine talks with the US are set for Abu Dhabi in early November
detail: The Kremlin said the talks on Ukraine will take place in Abu Dhabi in early November in a three-party format, Interfax reported. An earlier report had pointed to technical talks possibly in mid-November.

headline: Germany says an electricity tax cut is on the agenda but depends on budget financing; revenue cost put at about €5bn a year
detail: A German government spokesperson said a cut to electricity tax is under consideration, subject to sufficient budget financing being found. A ministry spokesperson said it would reduce annual tax revenues by about €5bn.

headline: Markets stop pricing a Fed rate hike in December as AI sell-off shifts rate expectations, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters says markets no longer expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates in December. It links the change in rate expectations to the sell-off in AI-related stocks.

headline: Bank of Russia holds its key rate at 14%, as forecast
detail: The Russian central bank left its key interest rate unchanged at 14%, in line with the 14% forecast and the previous level.

headline: France awaits a Moody's ratings verdict today after a week of heavy selling in French government bonds spread to Italy
detail: Reuters reports France faces the risk of a Moody's downgrade on Friday while its government struggles with social unrest and strained public finances. Economist Robin Brooks says French government debt sold off sharply this week and the selling spread to Italy, while yields fell in most other markets, especially the US and Japan.

headline: Reuters dealer poll sees 2026/27 gilt sales raised by £3.4bn to £249.6bn, with long-dated share lowest since 1990
detail: Bond dealers polled by Reuters ahead of the Budget also see 2026/27 T-bill sales up £5bn to £10bn, public sector net borrowing up about £15bn in both 2026/27 and 2027/28, and headroom of £15bn.

headline: EU ministers seek deals with Beijing to limit Chinese imports in chemicals, machinery and pharmaceuticals
detail: EU ministers said on Friday that the bloc should pursue agreements with China to curb imports in several sectors, calling the goods trade deficit with China unsustainable and damaging, Reuters reports.

headline: Sterling rises to a fresh 17-month high against the euro after mixed UK data
detail: Reuters reports that sterling edged up to its highest level against the euro in 17 months on Friday. It is on course for a fourth straight weekly gain after UK data sent mixed signals on the economy.

headline: WTI crude extends gains, rising more than $2 to $101.62 a barrel on worries over Middle East escalation
detail: US WTI futures climbed by more than $2 a barrel to $101.62, adding to gains as concern grew over rising tension in the Middle East. In the previous session WTI settled at $99.47 and Brent at $113.17.

headline: Canadian retail sales rise 1.2% on the month in August, just under the 1.3% forecast; core sales also up 1.2%
detail: Headline retail sales rose 1.2% month on month in August against a 1.3% forecast, after -0.7% previously. Core retail sales also rose 1.2%, ahead of the 1.1% forecast, after -0.7% previously.

headline: USTR proposes extending suspension of its Section 301 probe into China's maritime and shipbuilding sectors to 9 January 2027
detail: The Office of the US Trade Representative proposed a further suspension of its Section 301 investigation into China's targeting of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors, running to 9 January 2027.

headline: Algeria tells urea fertiliser producers to halt supplies to France as France raises Algerian trade curbs at EU level, sources say
detail: Sources say Algeria has instructed urea producers to stop supplying France, following an informal ban on imports of French products in place since July. France has taken the issue of Algerian trade restrictions to EU level, according to the same sources.

headline: White House says Russia and Ukraine agree a local ceasefire in Oleshky, starting 29 October, brokered by Melania Trump
detail: The White House says Russia and Ukraine will temporarily halt all military action in the city of Oleshky so humanitarian aid can enter and a civilian evacuation can be prepared through a safe corridor. It credits Melania Trump with securing the deal and says the ceasefire begins on 29 October.

headline: US flash services PMI slips to 57.9 in October from 58.8, near the 58 forecast; manufacturing edges up to 56
detail: S&P Global's US flash services PMI came in at 57.9 against a forecast of 58 and a previous 58.8. The flash manufacturing PMI rose to 56, above the 55.5 forecast and up from 55.9.

headline: French foreign minister Barrot warns renewed Iran-US escalation would hurt everyone and push oil prices higher
detail: France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said any new escalation between Iran and the United States would leave no winners and would raise oil prices. The remarks follow US strikes on Iran and threats of retaliation from Tehran.

headline: US University of Michigan final October consumer sentiment comes in at 48, above the 46.3 forecast
detail: The final October reading of University of Michigan consumer sentiment was 48, against a forecast of 46.3. The expectations index was 48.8, above the 47.1 forecast and up from 47.3 previously.

headline: US Energy Department authorises emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude from the SPR
detail: The US Department of Energy authorised an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. It is to address a crude supply disruption affecting the Phillips 66 Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.

headline: US University of Michigan final October 5-year inflation expectations hold at 3.5%, in line with forecast
detail: The final October University of Michigan survey puts 5-year inflation expectations at 3.5%. That matches both the forecast and the previous reading.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine has agreed to a team-level trilateral meeting after a call with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner
detail: Ukraine's president said he had spoken with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner, and that a trilateral meeting at team level had been agreed. Russia had already agreed to resume trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine.

headline: Zelenskiy says Russia has started its winter attacks and US Patriot interceptor deliveries are still delayed
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Russia has already begun its winter campaign of attacks. He said delivery of missile interceptors is still delayed and that he hopes the US will deliver Patriot interceptors.

headline: EU trade chief Sefcovic says the EU's trade deficit with China could exceed the 2022 record
detail: EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic said the bloc's trade deficit with China could surpass its 2022 record. He spoke as EU ministers seek deals with Beijing to limit Chinese imports.

headline: German foreign minister says Germany, France and the UK are ready to negotiate with Iran, stressing urgency to avoid escalation
detail: Germany's foreign minister said there is great urgency to avoid a new escalation, and that Germany, France and the UK stand ready to negotiate with Iran. He also called for support for Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government in their defence, and said there was agreement to do everything possible to allow Russian and Ukrainian grain exports.
