headline: Senior Ukrainian official says Oleshky ceasefire will take effect soon, with humanitarian corridors to follow in coming days
detail: A senior Ukrainian official said the ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky will be established soon and that humanitarian corridors out of the town will be set up in the coming days.

headline: Turkish foreign minister says no one backs a fresh attack on Iran and that diplomacy is the only route
detail: Turkey's foreign minister spoke after talks with regional and European counterparts. No market reaction was reported.

headline: German foreign minister says Russia is being urged to agree a new Black Sea security deal
detail: Germany's foreign minister said he and his counterparts are jointly urging Russia to agree a new security arrangement for the Black Sea. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says the US could end the Iran war quickly and claims control of the Strait of Hormuz and its oil
detail: US President Trump said the US could bring the Iran war to a rapid end and that the question is whether to finish it or let it wither. He also said the Strait of Hormuz belongs to the US, that the US is taking out as much oil as it wants and that it could take all of Iran's oil.

headline: Trump says he discussed opening up North Sea oil in a call with the UK prime minister
detail: US President Trump said he talked about opening up North Sea oil with UK prime minister Burnham today. Some earlier posts described the call as being with the British foreign minister.

headline: Trump says the US is very close to a trade deal with Mexico and that Canada is working hard on one
detail: US President Trump said a deal with Mexico was close. In the same remarks he said Canada was working hard to reach a deal with the US.

headline: Kremlin says Russian and Ukrainian militaries are still setting the dates for the Oleshky ceasefire
detail: The Kremlin said civilians who want to leave Oleshky will be allowed to go. It praised Melania Trump for coordinating the humanitarian agreement and said Putin and Trump had discussed it in a recent phone call.

headline: Zelenskiy says any peace deal would need strong security guarantees and 10 years of funding for Ukraine's army
detail: Ukraine's president set out the conditions for any peace agreement with Russia: strong security guarantees and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army. The comments come as the Kremlin says three-way talks with the US are planned for early November.

headline: Trump says the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections and that talks are under way
detail: US President Trump said the US would not strike Iran before the midterms and that talks with Tehran are in progress. The posts do not report any market reaction.

headline: October marks the worst month on record for attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Reuters reports the figure from data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017.

headline: Russian military says Oleshky ceasefire begins at 04:00 local time on 27 October for a humanitarian operation
detail: Russia's defence ministry says the ceasefire in Russian-controlled Oleshky in the Kherson direction starts at 04:00 local time on 27 October, Interfax reports. Chief of the general staff Gerasimov says Russian forces will make sure a humanitarian convoy can move safely to Alekseyevka with essential goods.

headline: Poll finds most economists expect the Bank of Canada to raise its overnight rate to 2.50% on 28 October
detail: A poll found 19 of 34 economists expect a rise to 2.50% on 28 October, and 16 of 29 expect two rises by the end of March. In the August poll, 17 of 34 had forecast no change until mid-2027.

headline: German oil stockpiling agency EBV launches tender to sell diesel, heating oil and crude from its reserves
detail: Germany's oil stockpiling agency EBV issued a tender on Friday to sell diesel, heating oil and crude oil from its reserves. The post gave no volumes.

headline: Iran has drawn up detailed plans to strike Gulf undersea cables if the war resumes, officials say
detail: A market news account reported the claim, citing unnamed officials. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Ukraine and Russia sign agreement setting out details of Oleshky humanitarian mission, Kyiv ombudsman says
detail: Ukraine's ombudsman Lubinets says the multi-stage mission will cover demining roads to Oleshky, food deliveries and evacuations. He says Kyiv is working to extend the mission to other settlements.

headline: Trump has told CENTCOM to draw up a plan for striking Iran, with no deadline set, Israel's Kan reports
detail: Israeli public broadcaster Kan reports that the US president directed Central Command to prepare a strike plan against Iran, and that no deadline was attached. The report comes after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections.

headline: Trump is expected to lift some US tariffs on Canada, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that President Trump is expected to remove some tariffs on Canada. The report links the move to an effort to help Senator Susan Collins.

headline: US could offset any cut in tariffs on Canada by raising other levies, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that the US may balance tariff reductions for Canada with increases in other levies. This follows its earlier report that President Trump is expected to lift some US tariffs on Canada.

headline: China's energy regulator tells oil and gas firms to raise output capacity and speed up national strategic supply bases
detail: China's National Energy Administration has told the country's oil and gas companies to expand production capacity and to speed up building national strategic oil and gas supply bases, Reuters reports. It also said the firms should take responsibility for safeguarding national energy security.

headline: Trump removes US tariffs on nine categories of Canadian goods, Senator Collins' office says
detail: US Senator Collins' office says nine product categories from Canada will be exempted from US tariffs, including blueberries, potatoes, apples and seaweed. Collins says Trump has removed the tariffs on these goods.

headline: Downing Street says PM Burnham and Trump discussed the energy secretary's approval of the Jackdaw gas field
detail: Downing Street's readout of the call between the UK prime minister and the US president says the two discussed the energy secretary's decision to approve the Jackdaw North Sea development. It also says Burnham stressed that Ukraine needs full access to Starlink.

headline: Downing Street says Burnham backed Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks and raised Argentina's Falklands measures in call with Trump
detail: Downing Street's readout of the Burnham–Trump call says the prime minister restated UK support for Saudi Arabia in the face of Houthi attacks. It also says he raised the economic consequences for the UK and US of Argentina's coercive measures over the Falkland Islands, and that the two leaders agreed approving the Jackdaw field will benefit the UK.

headline: WTI crude futures settle at $103.27 a barrel, up $3.80 or 3.82% on the day
detail: US crude oil futures settled at $103.27 a barrel on Friday, a gain of $3.80 or 3.82%. Earlier in the session the gains had been linked to worries over escalation in the Middle East.

headline: Brent crude futures settle at $116.72 a barrel, up $3.55 or 3.14% on the day
detail: A market commentator reports that Brent crude futures settled $3.55, or 3.14%, higher at $116.72 a barrel. WTI also settled higher earlier in the session.

headline: Iraq's prime minister sets a goal of gradually lifting oil output to 10 mln bpd by 2032
detail: Iraq's prime minister said the country plans to raise oil production step by step to 10 million barrels per day by 2032. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran says the blockade of its southern ports has cut its imports by 25%, ISNA reports
detail: Iran's Students News Agency (ISNA) reports that Iran puts the fall in its imports caused by the blockade of its southern ports at 25%. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two tankers hit naval mines on an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iranian state media carried the Revolutionary Guards' statement that two tankers struck naval mines while using an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: Trump says the US may carry out another operation against Iran and doubts Tehran is ready to negotiate seriously
detail: US President Trump made the remarks at a rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on 23 October. He said he does not expect Iran to agree to get down to business.

headline: White House changes the list of Canadian goods under Section 338 tariffs from 30 October, swapping plywood and paper for valves and carpets
detail: The White House said plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery, refrigeration equipment and packing crates and boxes are being taken out of the Section 338 tariffs. It said they will be replaced by certain valves, carpets, waste products and other goods, with both changes taking effect on 30 October 2026.

headline: Trump says the US is close to ending the Russia-Ukraine war, though he adds that it is only a hope
detail: US President Trump said he hopes the end of the Russia-Ukraine war is close. He spoke after the White House announced a local ceasefire in Oleshky. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US Treasuries and stocks fall together as higher oil prices revive inflation concerns
detail: A US market wrap posted at the close reports that both US bonds and equities fell, with the surge in oil prices renewing inflation worries. No yield levels were given.

headline: Moody's France review says slower growth and higher deficit have increased debt burden; projects 2027 deficit at 5.2% of GDP
detail: In its periodic review of France, Moody's says slower growth and a higher deficit have pushed the debt burden up since its last review, and it projects a deficit of 5.2% of GDP in 2027. The agency says France's Aa3 rating assumes that a deficit-reducing budget for 2027 is adopted.

headline: Moody's says the recent sharp rise in French government bond yields adds to the risk of debt affordability weakening further
detail: The ratings agency made the point in its review of France, after a week of heavy selling in French government bonds. No yield figures were given.

headline: French finance minister Lescure says Moody's decision acknowledges the strength of the French economy
detail: France's finance minister Lescure responded on Friday evening to Moody's ratings review of France. The post did not say what Moody's decided.

headline: Canadian dollar reaches five-week high against US dollar as bets on a Bank of Canada rate rise next week build
detail: Reuters reports that the Canadian dollar firmed to a five-week high against the US dollar on Friday. It says higher oil prices and domestic retail sales data supported expectations that the Bank of Canada will raise rates next week.

headline: UK will not join the Canada-led Defence Security and Resilience Bank and will back a separate UK-led initiative
detail: The FT and Reuters, citing a source familiar with the matter, report that Britain will stay out of the Canada-led defence bank. Reuters adds that the UK and Canada said they would build a framework for cooperation between their defence-funding initiatives.

headline: European gas prices hit their highest level since 2022 as trading opens
detail: European gas prices reached their highest level since 2022 at the start of trading, according to a market report. No percentage move was given.

headline: Chancellor Healey expected to announce a 3.9% rise in the full state pension, The Times reports
detail: The Times reports that Chancellor John Healey is expected to announce a 3.9% increase to the full state pension.

headline: UK government commits a further £432mn to end rough sleeping ahead of the Budget
detail: The government has committed a further £432mn to ending rough sleeping. The FT reports that PM Burnham is promising Budget money for the goal, while Chancellor Healey is preparing a fiscal statement intended to reassure markets.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says US-Canada trade deal is very close; Trump says tariff dispute will be settled soon
detail: Hassett said Commerce Secretary Lutnick is still negotiating, although US officials cautioned that progress was uncertain because Canada had not offered enough concessions. Speaking at a Michigan border rally, Trump said the dispute would be resolved soon but did not say what a deal would involve.

headline: RBA signals interest rates could go higher; Australian dollar weakens
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia signalled that higher interest rates are possible. The Australian dollar still weakened, according to reports early on Monday in Asia.

headline: Saudi-led coalition destroys Houthi missile launchers in Sanaa after intercepting ballistic missile fired at Riyadh
detail: The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh. It then destroyed two launch platforms in Sanaa, one of them used in that attack, and said its operation against the Houthi ballistic missile network is continuing.

headline: China's onshore yuan strengthens to 6.6682 per dollar, strongest since June 2022, after PBOC sets firmest fixing since 2023
detail: The PBOC set the yuan midpoint at 6.7162 per dollar, against 6.7180 previously, its strongest fixing since 2 February 2023. The onshore yuan then rose to 6.6682 in early trade, its strongest level since 9 June 2022.

headline: Houthis claim drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pumping stations and Riyadh airport; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed
detail: Yemen's Houthi group said on Monday it had targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, with no immediate Saudi confirmation. Reuters reported that oil prices slipped on Monday from near six-month highs, while the attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus.

headline: Fed to keep raising rates quarterly after reversing its 2025 insurance cuts, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Federal Reserve plans to keep its rate increases on a quarterly pace now that the insurance cuts made in 2025 have been reversed.

headline: Crude oil falls as Qatar pursues mediation efforts, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that crude oil prices are falling as Qatar pursues mediation. No price levels were given.

headline: EU leaders aim to finalise €45bn Ukraine loan backed by the EU budget before year-end
detail: EU leaders are seeking to complete a €45 billion loan to Ukraine, guaranteed by the EU budget, before the end of the year.

headline: Swedish producer prices rise 3.4% on the month, taking the annual rate to 11.2% from 6.8%
detail: Swedish PPI rose 3.4% month on month, up from 0.9% previously, and annual producer price inflation reached 11.2% against 6.8% before. No forecast was given.

headline: PM Burnham says he is not proposing that the UK rejoin the EU in this parliament and rules out an early election
detail: Prime Minister Andy Burnham made the remarks in an ITV interview on 26 October. He said he was not proposing EU membership during the current parliament and ruled out calling an early general election.

headline: PM Burnham says Healey will set out on Wednesday how the UK meets NATO commitments; signals savings from youth job support
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said Chancellor Healey would set out the path to meeting the UK's NATO commitments on Wednesday, and that youth job support needs changing in a way that can save money. Speaking on the same occasion, he also said he would like to see the UK rejoin the EU in his lifetime.

headline: Markets price only 12% odds of a Fed rate rise at this week's meeting
detail: An economist reports that markets see a 12% chance of a Fed hike at this week's meeting. He contrasts this with July, when markets pushed for a rise from Chair Warsh.

headline: French 10-year yield falls 5.3bp to 4.9685% after Moody's keeps France's sovereign rating unchanged
detail: France's 10-year government bond yield falls 5.3bp to 4.9685% in early trading. The move follows Moody's decision on Friday to leave France's sovereign rating unchanged.

headline: Iran says Monday's talks will take in Israel, Lebanon and Palestine; warns of a crushing response to any aggressors
detail: Iran said the talks on Monday will cover Israel, Lebanon and Palestine. Separately, it said its forces would respond with crushing force to aggressors.

headline: Singapore agrees with Saudi Aramco to store Saudi oil in rock caverns, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the deal with Saudi Aramco is meant to secure energy supplies for south-east Asia while the Middle East war disrupts supply.

headline: Chancellor Healey expected to deliver a cautious first Budget this week, putting gilt market stability first, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that Chancellor John Healey is expected to favour bond market stability over large spending increases in this week's Budget. The report contrasts this with the bigger spending plans PM Burnham discussed when he took office.

headline: EU plans import curbs on Chinese chemicals and furniture, which could be presented as early as Q1 2027
detail: Reports say the EU is planning import restrictions on Chinese chemicals and furniture and is also looking at caps or quotas on Chinese furniture. The new trade measures could be presented as early as the first quarter of 2027.

headline: German Ifo business climate index comes in at 90.2, above the 89.9 forecast and the previous reading
detail: The Ifo institute's German business climate index came in at 90.2 against a forecast of 89.9. The previous reading was also 89.9.

headline: German Ifo expectations rise to 91.6, beating forecast, while current conditions slip to 88.8, below forecast
detail: The October Ifo expectations index came in at 91.6, against a 90 forecast and 90.4 previously. The current conditions index was 88.8, against an 89.8 forecast and 89.5 previously.

headline: Chancellor Healey reportedly plans to borrow billions for military investment in Wednesday's Budget
detail: City AM cites reports that the Chancellor will fund defence investment with borrowing in the Budget. UK defence shares rose in early Monday trading, with Rolls-Royce up nearly 2% and Melrose up 1.4%.

headline: Healey pledges more than £1bn extra for social and affordable housing as figures show a sharp fall in housebuilding
detail: City AM reports that the extra funding will be confirmed in Wednesday's Budget and will extend the government's 10-year social and affordable housing programme. New figures show a sharp fall in housebuilding, raising doubts over the 1.5m homes target.

headline: Kalshi traders price a 93% chance the Fed holds this week and a 6% chance of a hike; Goldman expects a December rise
detail: Kalshi prediction-market pricing shows a 93% chance the Fed holds this week and 6% for a hike. Goldman Sachs expects a hold now and a 25bp rise in December.

headline: Kremlin says Oleshky truce could be a model for other local ceasefires; renewed talks with Ukraine and US do not limit fighting
detail: The Kremlin said the local ceasefire in Oleshky, agreed with US help, could set a precedent for similar ceasefires elsewhere. It added that the agreement to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US places no restrictions on either Moscow or Kyiv continuing military action.

headline: ECB survey finds euro zone firms are struggling more to get bank credit as fuel and other costs rise
detail: A European Central Bank survey published on Monday showed firms in the euro zone finding it harder to obtain credit from banks, while higher fuel and other costs squeeze their finances, Reuters reports.

headline: Pakistan's central bank lifts its key rate to 12%, citing inflation risks from the Gulf conflict
detail: Pakistan's central bank raised its key policy rate to 12%. It pointed to inflation risks from the conflict in the Gulf.

headline: Ministers plan apprenticeship funding overhaul that would make training over-25s more expensive, Guardian reports
detail: The Guardian reports that ministers are planning to change apprenticeship funding so that training workers over 25 costs more. Employers warn the change could undermine the government's plan to tackle youth unemployment.

headline: Fed policymakers have signalled no rate rise this week, but investors expect the pause to be short, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that Federal Reserve officials have indicated they will leave US short-term rates unchanged at this week's meeting. It also reports that, with inflation still the main concern, investors do not expect the pause to last long.

headline: UK CBI distributive trades balance improves to -10, well above the -48 forecast and the previous -55
detail: The CBI distributive trades survey's reported sales balance came in at -10, against a forecast of -48 and a previous reading of -55.

headline: Large gilt investors want reassurance from Healey's Budget and caution against changes to the fiscal rules, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that big bond investors want the new Chancellor's Budget on Wednesday to reassure the gilt market. They warn against adjusting the key fiscal rules.

headline: Egypt's foreign minister says a military solution with Iran cannot last and Cairo is working to prevent a full-scale war
detail: Egypt's foreign minister said Cairo talks every day with both Iran and the US, and that it is trying to avoid another full military conflict. He added that a military solution would not be sustainable.

headline: Saudi Arabia backs opening negotiation channels as Mecca pact talks take place in Tehran, aiming to end the conflict
detail: Saudi Arabia said the negotiations were meant to prevent escalation and open the way to an agreement ending the conflict. It made the comments against the background of Mecca pact talks in Tehran.

headline: Healey's Budget to exempt nearly one million state-pension-dependent retirees from income tax, City AM reports
detail: City AM reports that Chancellor Healey's Autumn Budget this week will exempt low-income pensioners who rely on the state pension from income tax. A former pensions minister has warned that the plan could create a £200m cliff edge and a growing bill for future governments.

headline: Banks face an expected tax raid in Wednesday's Budget; London mayor Khan urges them to keep investing in the UK
detail: City AM reports that the banking sector is expected to face higher taxes in Chancellor Healey's Budget. On Monday, London mayor Sadiq Khan urged the biggest banks to stay in London but would not say whether he opposed the measure.

headline: US natural gas futures drop 5% to lowest since April 2026 on higher output and weaker demand forecasts
detail: US natural gas futures extended losses to fall 5%, reaching their lowest level since April 2026. The decline was attributed to higher output and forecasts of lower demand.

headline: US Chicago Fed National Activity Index rises to 0.07 for September, above the -0.095 forecast
detail: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for September came in at 0.07, against a forecast of -0.095 and a previous reading of -0.04.

headline: French 10-year yield extends its fall, down as much as 10.56bp on the day to 4.9158%
detail: The French 10-year yield fell as much as 10.56bp on the day to 4.9158%, a bigger drop than the 5.3bp decline reported earlier after Moody's left France's sovereign rating unchanged.

headline: Egypt's parliament authorises the military to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom asks for support
detail: Egyptian MPs voted to approve military support for Saudi Arabia's defence, to be given on a Saudi request. The vote follows Houthi missile and drone attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Senior Iranian official says Tehran talks with Mecca pact members exclude Iran's nuclear programme
detail: A senior Iranian official said the talks with Mecca pact members in Tehran do not include the nuclear issue. The official added that Iran will not discuss its nuclear programme until Tehran's demands are met.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian tells Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish delegations that Tehran is ready to deepen cooperation and settle differences
detail: The Iranian presidency reported the remarks from Pezeshkian's meeting with the three delegations in Tehran. Iranian state broadcaster IRIB separately reported that Iran is ready to back any understanding on regional unity.

headline: German Chancellor Merz meets Knot and Hernández de Cos, seen as favourites for top ECB post, Handelsblatt reports
detail: Handelsblatt reports that Merz held meetings with the two candidates, who are described as front-runners for the top job at the ECB.

headline: UK 20-year gilt yield falls 6bp to 5.678%, its lowest since 23 September
detail: The 20-year gilt yield was down 6bp on the day at 5.678%, its lowest level since 23 September, a market feed reported at 14:21 UTC.

headline: US Dallas Fed manufacturing index rises to 13.4 in October, above the 8.8 forecast
detail: The Dallas Fed manufacturing business index came in at 13.4 for October, against a forecast of 8.8 and a previous reading of 9.8.

headline: Slovak foreign minister says Russia told him it stands ready to honour agreed energy contracts
detail: Slovakia's foreign minister made the remarks after meeting Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov. He added that Slovakia will keep working with Russia in areas that sanctions do not cover.

headline: Iran's president repeats that Tehran is not seeking nuclear weapons
detail: Iran's president said again on Monday that Tehran is not trying to acquire nuclear weapons. The statement came during the Mecca pact talks being held in Tehran.

headline: US Treasury plans to buy back up to $6bn of longer-dated debt on Tuesday
detail: The US Treasury will hold a buyback operation on Tuesday for up to $6bn of longer-dated securities.

headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks drop to 282.6 million barrels, the lowest level since 1982
detail: Crude held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.6 million barrels last week, the lowest level since 1982, according to a market news feed.

headline: Iran is at an advanced stage of planning attacks on Americans, Fox News reports
detail: Fox News reported on Monday that Iran is at an advanced stage of planning attacks on Americans. The batch reports no market reaction and no official confirmation.

headline: US 3-month bill auction clears at 4.05% and 6-month at 4.21%; 6-month cover falls to 2.63
detail: The US Treasury sold $95bn of 3-month bills at a high yield of 4.050% with bid-to-cover of 3.07, up from 2.770, and 82.29% of bids at the high were allotted. It also sold $82bn of 6-month bills at 4.210%, against 4.220% previously, with cover of 2.63, down from 2.840, and 61.74% of bids at the high allotted.

headline: Iran, Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agree to keep talking after Tehran meeting, Iranian state media reports
detail: Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reports that Iran, Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to continue talks. The four met in Tehran on Monday in talks aimed at ending the conflict.

headline: Brent crude recovers its earlier losses and trades close to $117 a barrel
detail: A market newswire reports that Brent has turned around its earlier fall and is trading near $117 a barrel. Crude had fallen earlier in the day while Qatar was pursuing mediation efforts.

headline: Trump administration challenges US wind projects, putting a bipartisan energy permitting deal in doubt, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the administration's new challenge to wind power projects ends a truce on renewables. That truce was aimed at winning bipartisan support for a permitting bill.

headline: Federal Reserve bids for US 2-year notes total $7.7bn
detail: Federal Reserve bids for US 2-year Treasury notes come to $7.7bn, a market commentator account reports.

headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says further Russia sanctions are being prepared and warns of a serious risk of renewed Iran-US escalation
detail: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said more sanctions on Russia are being prepared. She also said there is a serious risk of renewed escalation between Iran and the US.

headline: US 2-year when-issued yield stands at 4.705% ahead of $69bn Treasury auction
detail: The when-issued US 2-year note yield was 4.705% shortly before the US Treasury's $69bn 2-year note auction.

headline: US $69bn 2-year note auction clears at 4.708%, tailing by 0.3bp; bid-to-cover slips to 2.59
detail: The US Treasury sold $69bn of 2-year notes at a high yield of 4.708%, against 4.705% when-issued before the sale and 4.787% at the previous auction. Bid-to-cover was 2.59 against 2.63 previously; primary dealers took 13%, directs 41.32% and indirects 45.68%.

headline: Healey to raise minimum wage by nearly 4% in Budget but slow increase for young workers, The Times reports
detail: The Times reports that Chancellor Healey will announce an increase of nearly 4% in the minimum wage, with a slower rise for younger workers. The Budget is due on Wednesday.

headline: Saudi Arabia reportedly offers Houthis $1bn in Iran-brokered deal to end attacks, Israel Hayom reports
detail: Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom reports that Saudi Arabia has offered the Houthis $1bn under a deal brokered by Iran to stop their attacks. The report has not been confirmed.

headline: UK National Living Wage for over-21s reportedly set to rise 3.9% from £12.71 to about £13.20
detail: A report carried by a market news feed says the National Living Wage, which covers workers aged 21 and over, is expected to go up from £12.71 to around £13.20, a 3.9% increase. It adds figures to earlier reports that the minimum wage will rise in Wednesday's Budget.

headline: Government expected to publish a fiscal devolution roadmap for England alongside Wednesday's Budget
detail: Centre for Cities says the government is expected to publish a roadmap for fiscal devolution in England on Wednesday alongside the Budget.

headline: Canada says partners will sign founding articles of new Defence, Security and Resilience Bank in Luxembourg on 30 November
detail: Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said in a statement on Monday that Canada and its partners will meet in Luxembourg on 30 November to sign the articles of agreement that establish the bank.

headline: EU Council adopts eight European Peace Facility decisions for Ukraine, taking total EPF support to €10.8bn
detail: The EU Council says €4.7bn will reimburse member states for military aid to Ukraine and €230m will go to the EU military assistance mission for Ukraine (EUMAM). The decisions take the EU's overall European Peace Facility support for Ukraine to €10.8bn.

headline: Reform UK leader Farage says banks should not face new taxes in this week's Budget, partly reversing his earlier stance
detail: City AM reports that Farage has come out against new bank taxes in Wednesday's Budget. Earlier this year he had pledged to scrap the interest lenders receive on their deposits at the Bank of England.

headline: US official warns Iran it must change its behaviour or face completion of the mission, Al Jazeera reports
detail: Al Jazeera cites an unnamed US official issuing the warning to Tehran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: New York Fed's Williams forecasts no Fed rate rises in 2027, against market expectations
detail: New York Fed President John Williams projects no rate increases in 2027, according to a market news report that says his view differs from market pricing. It comes ahead of this week's Fed policy meeting.

headline: Poll finds 22 of 27 economists expect RBNZ to raise cash rate 25bp to 3.00% on 28 October
detail: In a poll of economists, 22 of 27 said they expect the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to raise its cash rate by 25bp to 3.00% at its 28 October decision.

headline: Poll: 13 of 23 economists see RBNZ cash rate at 3.00% by year-end, while 9 expect a rise to 3.25% in December
detail: In a poll of economists, 13 of 23 expect the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's cash rate to end the year at 3.00%. Nine expect a further increase to 3.25% in December.

headline: US and Canada reportedly work on deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and car imports
detail: Unnamed sources say the US and Canada are working on an agreement that would ease US tariffs on imports of Canadian steel and cars. The reports give no timing or terms.

headline: Iran is open to a shorter timeline on the US proposal if conditions are met, state TV reports
detail: Iranian state television reported that Tehran is willing to accept a shorter timeline for the US proposal, provided certain conditions are met. The report did not say what the conditions were.

headline: UK reportedly in talks with the EU on a return to free movement, The Times reports
detail: The Times reports that the UK is holding talks with the EU on a return to free movement. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Canadian PM Carney says Canada will not sign the trade terms the US offered in August
detail: Canada's prime minister said Ottawa is not prepared to accept the US trade terms put forward in August. This follows reports that the two countries are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and car imports.

headline: Canadian PM Carney says any progress in US trade talks reflects the US moving towards Canada's position
detail: Canada's Prime Minister Carney commented on the state of trade negotiations with the US, saying any progress made has come from the US shifting closer to Canada's stance.

headline: Healey's Budget to centre on everyday cost-of-living fixes with limited giveaways and first-time buyer help, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Healey is set to offer limited measures to ease living costs as energy costs rise, along with support for first-time homeowners, in Wednesday's Budget.

headline: UK BRC shop price inflation rises to 2.1% in the year to October from 1.4% in September
detail: The British Retail Consortium's figures put annual shop price inflation at 2.1% in October, up from 1.4% in September. Retailers told the Chancellor that discounting is no longer holding back price rises, City AM reports.

headline: USTR Greer warns EIB loan to Airbus may breach the US-EU trade truce and aircraft agreement
detail: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the European Investment Bank's loan to Airbus may violate the US-EU trade truce. He said US concerns need to be resolved quickly to avoid breaching the large civil aircraft agreement, the FT also reports.

headline: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in Oleshky takes effect; Russia suspends strikes on Kherson
detail: The local ceasefire in Oleshky came into force, according to reports. Russia's Defence Ministry said it has suspended strikes on Ukraine's Kherson.

headline: South Korea Q3 GDP grows 1.0% q/q and 3.4% y/y, beating poll forecasts
detail: The Bank of Korea's advance estimate shows Q3 GDP up 1.0% on the quarter against a 0.7% poll, and up 3.4% on the year against 3.0%. Private consumption fell 0.2% q/q. A BoK official said the Q3 figure adds 0.35 percentage points to this year's growth forecast.

headline: China industrial profits rise 14.4% y/y in September, up from 4.2% in August; year-to-date growth eases to 15.5%
detail: China's statistics bureau says industrial profits for January to September are up 15.5% on a year earlier, compared with 15.7% for the year to August. September profits alone rose 14.4% year on year.

headline: Japan corporate services prices rise 3.7% y/y in September
detail: Data published on Tuesday show Japan's corporate services price index, a key gauge of service-sector inflation, up 3.7% on a year earlier in September. Reuters says the figure points to mounting price pressures.

headline: People's Bank of China injects 1 trillion yuan through overnight reverse repos
detail: China's central bank said in a statement that it had added 1 trillion yuan of liquidity through overnight reverse repurchase operations.

headline: Japan's finance minister Katayama says government is ready to take decisive action in the currency market
detail: Katayama said officials are watching market moves with heightened urgency, that the yen should move in line with fundamentals, and that clear communication aims to keep market confidence in the yen and in the Takaichi administration's fiscal policy.

headline: Bank of England orders Section 166 review of Revolut's product approval processes, FT reports
detail: According to the FT, the order was made earlier this year and focuses on risks from the rapid launch of new financial products.

headline: Taiwan central bank calls its policy stance tightening and forecasts 5.82% GDP growth for next year
detail: The central bank named geopolitical risks and climate conditions as the main uncertainties for inflation, said bank loan quality was stable, and reported that the Taiwan dollar fell 1.25% against the US dollar in the first half.

headline: Brazil's real suffers its worst day in more than 25 years as Lula faces calls for budget cuts, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that investor worries about how the economy is being managed drove falls in the real and the Bovespa index after the president's re-election.

headline: HSBC third-quarter profit rises 32% and the bank announces a buyback of up to $1bn
detail: The bank said higher rates supported net interest income, and it expects banking NII of at least $46bn in 2026. Pre-tax profit of $9.63bn and revenue of $18.6bn were both below estimates.

headline: India's oil minister says Washington is not pressing India to cut its Russian crude imports
detail: India's oil minister said the US is not putting pressure on India to reduce its imports of Russian crude. He also said US cargoes now make up 67% of India's LPG imports.

headline: Japan's 30-year JGB yield rises 1.5bp to 3.820%
detail: Japan's 30-year government bond yield rose 1.5bp to 3.820% in early trading on 27 October.

headline: China's December 30-year government bond futures rise 0.4% to a record 118.56
detail: China's 30-year government bond futures for December delivery rose 0.4% to a record high of 118.56.

headline: China's foreign ministry urges EU not to misuse trade remedy tools as Brussels plans trade measures
detail: Responding to EU plans for trade measures, China's foreign ministry said it regards China-EU trade ties as a partnership. It said it hopes the EU will not abuse its trade remedy tools.

headline: French retailers will not replenish the diesel stocks they have released, Politico reports
detail: Politico reports that retailers in France do not plan to refill diesel stocks that have been released. The report gives no volumes and no market reaction.

headline: French consumer confidence drops to 80 in October, its lowest since June 2013
detail: France's October consumer confidence index came in at 80, against a forecast of 85 and down from 86 in September. It is the lowest reading since June 2013.

headline: Merz says a US-Russia-China understanding on Ukraine that leaves out Kyiv would be unacceptable
detail: German Chancellor Merz, speaking in Singapore, said it would be wholly unacceptable for the US, Russia and China to try to reach an understanding without Ukraine's involvement.

headline: UK business minister says Britain and EU are making progress on concerns over the bloc's proposed 'Made in Europe' rules
detail: UK business minister Jonathan Reynolds said on Tuesday that London and Brussels are working through concerns over the EU's planned 'Made in Europe' rules, according to Reuters. The rules have caused uncertainty for UK manufacturers and investors.

headline: Saudi Arabia says it has contained a fire near the Ras Tanura oil hub after an attack
detail: Saudi Arabia reports that a fire near its Ras Tanura oil hub, which broke out after an attack, has been contained. The report gave no details on damage to oil supply and no market reaction.

headline: France-Germany 10-year yield spread widens 6bp to 160bp
detail: The gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields widened by 6bp to 160bp on Tuesday morning, according to a market wire.

headline: Eurozone M3 money supply grows 3.5% y/y, slightly above the 3.4% forecast; lending growth holds steady
detail: Eurozone annual M3 growth was 3.5%, unchanged from the previous reading and against a 3.4% forecast. Loans to non-financial firms grew 4.2% and loans to households grew 3.1%, both the same as the previous month.

headline: OPEC+ reportedly set to keep oil output targets unchanged at Sunday's meeting
detail: Sources say OPEC+ is expected to hold its oil production targets steady when it meets on Sunday.

headline: French finance minister Lescure says France must answer protesters without adding to spending
detail: In an FT interview, Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the government can find creative solutions without widening the budget deficit. He also said an unwinding of carry trades had added to pressure on short-dated French debt during this month's volatility.

headline: Iran's Gulf strait authority says Sinokor Shipping vessels will face legal action from 1 November
detail: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said all vessels belonging to Sinokor Shipping will be met with legal action starting 1 November.

headline: Kremlin says no breaches of the Oleshky ceasefire have been reported so far
detail: The Kremlin said on 27 October that no violations of the Oleshky ceasefire agreement with Ukraine had been reported so far. It also said no date has yet been set for US-Ukraine talks in the UAE, TASS reports.

headline: Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre hold phone call with Putin on efforts to end the war in Ukraine
detail: Finland's presidential office says President Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Støre started the call with President Putin to discuss Russia's war against Ukraine and diplomatic efforts to end it. The office says the call related to upcoming meetings in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Gulf stock markets rise after Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials meet Iran in Tehran to ease escalation
detail: Reuters reports that major Gulf stock markets rose in early trade on Tuesday. The gains came a day after senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran to try to ease military escalation.

headline: Qatar's foreign ministry says Iran must halt threats to Gulf states and reopen the Strait of Hormuz for mediation to work
detail: A spokesperson for Qatar's foreign ministry said Iran needs to demonstrate good intentions and stop threatening Arab Gulf states. The spokesperson also said Tehran must open the Strait of Hormuz for mediation efforts to succeed.

headline: Kremlin says Putin, Stubb and Støre discussed the Oleshky ceasefire and agreed to keep direct contact
detail: The Kremlin said the leaders of Finland and Norway requested the call, which covered settling the war in Ukraine, the Oleshky ceasefire and upcoming meetings in Abu Dhabi, TASS reported. Denmark's prime minister was reported as saying she is very sceptical about Norway and Finland talking to Putin.

headline: Kremlin says Russia-US-Ukraine talks will resume in Abu Dhabi in November to address postwar security
detail: The Kremlin said the three-way talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine will restart in Abu Dhabi in November. It said the talks will cover postwar security arrangements.

headline: German 2-year Schatz auction clears at 3.08% with bid-to-cover of 1.3
detail: The German 2-year Schatz auction produced an average yield of 3.08%, compared with 3.1% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.3, up from 1.1 last time.

headline: Kremlin says Putin told Stubb and Støre peace needs Russia's interests met in full and EU and NATO policies prolong the war
detail: The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders of Finland and Norway that peace can only come if Russia's interests are taken into account fully and without conditions. It said he also told them that confrontational EU and NATO policies are dragging out the conflict.

headline: Iran's supreme leader calls for conditions to be met to end the war and discusses Hormuz management with Rezaee
detail: Iran's supreme leader called for the conditions for ending the war to be met. Separately, he discussed national unity and the management of the Strait of Hormuz with Rezaee. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK sells £4.5bn of 5-year gilts at an average yield of 5.036%, the highest since 2008
detail: The UK sold £4.5bn of 5-year debt at an average yield of 5.036%, the highest since 2008. New OBR forecasts are due tomorrow; in March the OBR forecast that debt servicing would soon cost 3.8% of GDP.

headline: Houthis claim a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery
detail: Yemen's Houthi forces said they hit the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province with a ballistic missile and that the strike caused large fires. Saudi Arabia had earlier said it had contained a fire near the oil hub after an attack.

headline: Russia's Novak says a fourth tanker of Russian diesel under the Russia-US deal leaves on 28 October
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said a fourth tanker of Russian diesel under the Russia-US diesel deal will depart on 28 October. He said three more tankers are currently en route.

headline: Russia's Novak says Moscow is ready to resume gas supplies to European countries if they want them
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia was prepared to restart gas deliveries to Europe should European countries wish. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Russia's Novak says Moscow can redirect and sell all its gas elsewhere if Europe turns down supplies
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia could reroute its gas and sell all of it if European countries reject supplies. He had earlier said Moscow was ready to resume gas deliveries to Europe.

headline: QatarEnergy extends force majeure on LNG supplies to Italy's Edison through December
detail: QatarEnergy has extended the force majeure on its LNG deliveries to Italian energy company Edison until the end of December, according to a market news account. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Oleshky ceasefire will run until 1 November, says senior Ukrainian official
detail: A senior Ukrainian official said the local ceasefire in Oleshky will remain in place until 1 November. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Three Russian diesel tankers head for the US, one of them under sanctions, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that three tankers of Russian diesel are sailing to the US under the Trump-Putin fuel deal, and that one of them is under sanctions. The FT says the arrangement exposes the companies involved to legal threats from Congress.

headline: Putin describes the sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines as direct acts of terrorism
detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin called the attacks on the Nord Stream gas pipelines direct acts of terrorism. Earlier, Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Russia was ready to resume gas supplies to Europe. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Putin warns that trying to shut Russia out of the global gas market has serious consequences and urges gas exporters to coordinate routes
detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin said global natural gas prices have risen sharply but may fall again, and that gas supply needs to increase. He proposed that gas-exporting countries work together to optimise export and transport routes.

headline: Putin says Russia is open to gas cooperation and is looking at working with US partners, including in the Arctic
detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia is open to cooperation in the gas sector and is looking into possible joint work with partners from the US, including in the Arctic. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Putin calls for ending ongoing conflicts and lifting sanctions to be considered, and warns against overdoing the green agenda
detail: Russian President Putin said ending current conflicts and removing sanctions should be considered, and that the green agenda should not be taken too far. He made the remarks in the same appearance as his earlier comments on the gas market.

headline: US ADP weekly employment change slows to 16.75K from 18.5K
detail: ADP's weekly US private-sector employment estimate showed a gain of 16.75K, down from 18.5K the previous week. No forecast was given.

headline: Norway's Støre says Moscow appears to be preparing thoroughly for the Abu Dhabi talks and calls for de-escalation of the Ukraine war
detail: Norway's prime minister said his call with Putin lasted 90 minutes and that his impression was that Moscow is preparing thoroughly for the Abu Dhabi meeting. He also said efforts must be made to de-escalate the war in Ukraine.

headline: Norway's Støre says his views on Ukraine match those of the coalition of the willing
detail: Norway's prime minister made the remark after his phone call with Putin, held with Finland's Stubb, about efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

headline: Resolution Foundation estimates fiscal headroom has halved to about £12bn in 2029-30 before Budget measures
detail: The Resolution Foundation estimates that headroom against the fiscal rules will have fallen to around £12bn in 2029-30 before any Budget measures. It says Chancellor John Healey would need £18bn of headroom to keep a buffer equivalent to the one Rachel Reeves had.

headline: Downing Street rules out a UK return to EU free movement during the current parliament
detail: The Prime Minister's spokeswoman said the UK will not return to EU free movement in this parliament. She added that the coming UK-EU summit may take concrete steps but these will not be enough.

headline: US durable goods orders rise 1.8%, just below the 1.9% forecast; core orders up 0.5%
detail: US durable goods orders rose 1.8% against a 1.9% forecast, after -0.1% the previous month. Core durable goods rose 0.5% against a 0.6% forecast, after 0.2% the previous month.

headline: Poland's Tusk says Finland's Stubb described the European position on the Abu Dhabi talks as moderately optimistic
detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Finland's president told him, after his call with Putin, that Europe is moderately optimistic about the Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

headline: Norway's Støre says his call with Putin on the Ukraine war revealed big differences
detail: Norway's prime minister said there were big differences with the Russian president during their call on the war in Ukraine. Finland's president also took part in the call.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield edges up 0.86bp to 4.995% after US data; 30-year flat at 5.304%
detail: US Treasury yields moved after the release of US economic data. The 10-year yield was last up 0.86bp at 4.995%, while the 30-year yield was last unchanged at 5.304%.

headline: Houthis say they pushed back an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb strait
detail: Yemen's Houthis say they repelled a Saudi-led advance near the Bab el-Mandeb strait and fired ballistic missiles and heavy weapons at the advancing forces. No market reaction was reported.

headline: British Business Bank and National Wealth Fund set for a boost in Healey's Budget, Observer reports
detail: The Observer reports that public finance institutions, including the British Business Bank and the National Wealth Fund, are due to get extra support in the Chancellor's Budget. The report gives no figures.

headline: US Case-Shiller 20-city house prices rise 2.65% y/y in August, above 2.61% forecast; FHFA index up 0.3% m/m
detail: The S&P Case-Shiller 20-city index rose 2.65% year on year in August, against a 2.61% forecast and 2.5% previously. The FHFA house price index rose 0.3% month on month, against a 0.2% forecast, and its annual rate eased to 2.4% from 2.6%.

headline: US set to approve three more wind projects, Punchbowl reports
detail: Punchbowl reports that the US administration will approve three more wind power projects. No other details were given.

headline: UK minister Reynolds says EU uncertainty is hurting British business and the long-term relationship must be settled
detail: The FT reports that minister Reynolds said uncertainty over the UK's relations with the EU is damaging British business and the long-term relationship needs resolving. He spoke ahead of new UK-EU talks.

headline: Economists' poll lifts global growth forecasts to 3.0% for 2026 and 3.2% for 2027; 2027 inflation views raised for 31 of 50 economies
detail: A poll of economists puts global growth at 3.0% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, up from 2.9% and 3.1% in the July poll. Forecasts for 2027 inflation were raised for 31 of 50 major economies compared with July.

headline: Houthis claim a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's defence ministry in Riyadh
detail: Yemen's Houthis say they hit the Saudi defence ministry in the capital with a ballistic missile, following their earlier claim of a strike on the Ras Tanura refinery. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the attack.

headline: US Conference Board consumer confidence jumps to 91.7 in October, well above the 81.0 forecast
detail: The Conference Board's October consumer confidence index came in at 91.7 against a consensus of 81.0. September's reading was revised up to 84.2 from 81.9.

headline: US new home sales fall 0.6% m/m, a smaller drop than the 4.5% decline forecast
detail: US new home sales fell 0.6% on the month, against a forecast fall of 4.5%. The previous month showed a 6.4% rise.

headline: US consumers' 12-month inflation expectations ease to 5.8% in October but stay elevated, Conference Board says
detail: The Conference Board's October consumer confidence report puts consumers' average 12-month inflation expectations at 5.8%, lower than the previous month. It adds that consumers still expect interest rates to be higher over the next 12 months.

headline: Finland's Stubb says he passed on Ukraine's messages to Putin and that the US and Ukraine asked Finland and Norway to do more
detail: Finnish President Stubb said he relayed messages from Ukraine during his call with Putin. He said the US and Ukraine had asked Norway and Finland to take a more active role in efforts to end the war.

headline: Dallas Fed services activity index rises to 4.0 in October, against a -2.9 forecast
detail: The Dallas Fed's services activity index for October came in at 4.0. The forecast was -2.9 and the previous reading was -1.8.

headline: Brent falls to its intraday low and trades near $114 a barrel
detail: Market reports say oil fell to its low of the session, with Brent trading close to $114 a barrel.

headline: Russia's Novak says Russia-US Arctic projects could cover gas fields or joint LNG, and refineries are restarting quickly
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak said possible Russia-US projects in the Arctic could involve developing gas fields or taking part in joint LNG projects. He also said Russian refineries are bringing units back online very quickly after maintenance.

headline: Finland's Stubb says the Putin call was prepared together with Ukraine and the US
detail: Russian media report that Finnish President Stubb said his phone call with Putin on the Ukraine war was prepared jointly with Ukraine and the United States.

headline: Russia's Novak offers to help Gulf states restore oil refineries and to supply technology and equipment
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia stands ready to help Persian Gulf countries restore their oil refineries, including by providing technology and equipment. He also said Russian refineries are bringing units back online quickly after maintenance, using mostly Russian-made equipment.

headline: Russia's Lavrov expects the Ukraine conflict to continue and probably escalate; says the Finland and Norway call with Putin offered…
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said Europe wants a role in the negotiations, and that the Finnish and Norwegian leaders brought nothing new to their call with Putin, according to Interfax. He also said the Russia-US diesel deal is a purely commercial agreement with no extra conditions.

headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says the Oleshky ceasefire could serve as a confidence-building step in peace talks
detail: Ukraine's foreign minister also said Kyiv coordinated the call that the Finnish and Norwegian leaders held with Putin.

headline: Poland's energy minister expects a schedule for releasing oil stockpiles to be ready by the end of November
detail: Polish Energy Minister Motyka said the timetable for releasing oil from stockpiles should be finalised by the end of November. No volumes were given.

headline: US Treasury sells $54bn of 52-week bills at a 4.29% high yield, down from 4.400% previously; bid-to-cover 3.15
detail: The US 52-week bill auction cleared at a high yield of 4.29%, against 4.400% at the previous sale, with bid-to-cover of 3.15 against 3.070. 65.33% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

headline: Trump says the US will accept 1 million barrels of Venezuelan oil and plans to visit a tanker carrying it in Texas
detail: US President Trump made the remarks in comments carried live on Tuesday. He said he expects to visit a tanker in Texas that is carrying Venezuelan oil.

headline: Kremlin aide says Putin told Stubb and Støre that Zelenskyy may visit Moscow and security would be guaranteed
detail: Kremlin aide Ushakov said Putin confirmed in his call with Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre that Zelenskyy may visit Moscow. According to Ushakov, Putin said all necessary conditions for such a visit, including security, would be provided.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says a Russia-Ukraine leaders' meeting would only make sense once negotiations are complete
detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said contact between the Russian and Ukrainian leaders would be appropriate after the negotiation process has finished, to sign documents. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Melania Trump says the local Ukraine ceasefire has begun and now extends beyond Oleshky within the Kherson region
detail: US First Lady Melania Trump said the localised ceasefire in Ukraine has started and has been widened beyond Oleshky to cover more of the Kherson region. No market reaction was reported.

headline: EU leans on allies as a shortfall in Ukraine funding approaches, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the EU is pressing allied governments over an approaching gap in funding for Ukraine. The report gives no figures.

headline: Kremlin's Peskov says it is too early to tell whether the Putin call with Stubb and Støre will affect the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin's phone call with Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre could, in some circumstances, influence contacts in Abu Dhabi, but that it is premature to say so yet.

headline: Russian refineries' crude processing is up 25% since drone attacks halted in mid-October, Reuters sources say
detail: Reuters sources say crude runs at Russian refineries have risen 25% since drone attacks stopped in mid-October. Earlier, Russia's Novak said refineries were restarting quickly.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian tells Putin the region can resolve its problems without the US
detail: Iran's president made the remarks during talks with Russia's president in Moscow, Tasnim reports.

headline: US 5-year Treasury when-issued yield is 4.841% ahead of the $70bn auction
detail: Ahead of the US Treasury's $70bn 5-year note auction, the when-issued yield was quoted at 4.841%.

headline: US Treasury sells $70bn of 5-year notes at a 4.845% high yield with a 0.4bp tail; bid-to-cover 2.33
detail: The high yield compares with 5.033% at the previous 5-year sale, and bid-to-cover rose to 2.33 from 2.210. Indirect bidders took 60.0%, directs 29.4% and primary dealers 10.6%.

headline: Trump says the Venezuelan oil cargo the US is taking is only the first shipment
detail: US President Trump said the shipment of Venezuelan oil bound for the US is the first of more to come. One report gave the cargo as 1 million barrels and another as 100 million barrels; the earlier blotter entry carried 1 million barrels.

headline: Trump says petrol and diesel prices will soon fall sharply as Venezuelan oil shipments begin
detail: In posts on Truth Social, the US President said the Venezuelan cargo is the first of billions of barrels to come. He also said US energy output from Alaska to Venezuela has made the Western Hemisphere the world's energy capital.

headline: Canada and the UAE sign a comprehensive trade deal
detail: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi signed the deal at a joint signing ceremony.

headline: Fiscal devolution roadmap on mayors' revenue-raising and spending is due to be published in tomorrow's Budget
detail: The Institute for Government says the government's fiscal devolution roadmap will be unveiled in the Budget on 28 October. It will set out changes to how mayors raise and spend money.

headline: US Treasury accepts $6bn of offers in a buyback of 2046-2056 coupons, taking the maximum from $10.746bn offered
detail: The US Treasury received $10.746bn of offers in a buyback aimed at coupon securities maturing between 2046 and 2056. It accepted $6bn, the maximum, across 6 of the 35 eligible issues.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says more refined products are moving out through the Strait of Hormuz
detail: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said refined product flows from the Strait of Hormuz have risen. He did not give any figures, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the suspension of sanctions on Russia is temporary and the US is ramping up LNG exports
detail: In remarks on CNBC, which have now ended, US Energy Secretary Wright also said Russia cannot currently export diesel.

headline: US is discussing Russian deals for American oil majors as part of Ukraine peace talks, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Washington is discussing deals in Russia for US oil majors within the Ukraine peace negotiations. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US and Russia propose a post-war oil venture off the Sakhalin coast, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the US and Russia have put forward a joint oil venture off Sakhalin to follow the end of the Ukraine war. Earlier, the FT reported that Russian deals for American oil majors were being discussed in the peace talks.

headline: Trump to announce looser rules on methane leaks from oil companies, Washington Post reports
detail: The Washington Post reports that President Trump will announce relaxed regulations on methane leaks from oil firms.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says Russia cannot export diesel at present and the Iran war has come at a cost
detail: The US Energy Secretary also said the Constellation Energy deal will add 1.1 gigawatts of capacity. These remarks came alongside earlier comments on US LNG exports and on flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: ECB authorises Intesa Sanpaolo to take control of Monte dei Paschi ahead of its €32bn takeover offer
detail: Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy's biggest bank, said on Tuesday that it had received European Central Bank authorisation to take control of Monte dei Paschi di Siena, Reuters reports. The approval is a major step towards launching its €32bn ($36bn) offer.

headline: Chancellor Healey is preparing a £50 cut to household gas bills, Telegraph reports
detail: The Telegraph reports that Chancellor Healey is preparing to cut household gas bills by £50. The report comes ahead of the Budget, which is due tomorrow.

headline: Kremlin's Peskov says the local Ukraine ceasefire deal at first covered only a halt in fighting around one town
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the ceasefire agreement originally provided for a period of quiet around a single town. Earlier reports said the local ceasefire had been extended beyond Oleshky in the Kherson region.

headline: US sells first Venezuelan crude cargo, received at no cost, to Citgo and Exxon Mobil, White House official says
detail: A White House official says the US government received the first Venezuelan crude cargo from NABEP at no cost under an August deal. The official says the cargo has been sold to Citgo Petroleum and Exxon Mobil.

headline: Chile's central bank says it will set the rate path meeting by meeting and will monitor inflation persistence closely
detail: Chile's central bank says it will assess the future path of interest rates at each meeting and will watch closely for signs that shocks are passing through more widely or that inflation is persisting. It says the economy may regain momentum by 2027, but current weakness could last longer than expected.

headline: Chancellor Healey is set to reverse the cuts to cash ISA limits, FT reports
detail: According to the Financial Times, Chancellor Rachel Healey plans to reverse the earlier cuts to cash ISA allowances. The report came the evening before the Budget.

headline: Healey puts energy reform at the centre of his Budget and pledges more support for businesses and households, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Chancellor will put energy reform at the centre of what it calls a 'do no harm' Budget. It also says he will pledge extra support for businesses, entrepreneurs and households.

headline: Australian CPI rises 1.3% q/q in Q3, above 1.2% forecast; September annual rate climbs to 4.3%
detail: Q3 trimmed mean was 1.0% q/q, as forecast, and 3.7% y/y against a 3.6% forecast. Monthly CPI rose 0.8% m/m in September and 4.3% y/y against a 4.2% forecast, and the Australian dollar rose 0.4% to $0.7053 after the release.

headline: RBA's Bullock says the inflation outlook has worsened and the CPI data adds to upside risks; won't signal the board's decision
detail: The RBA Governor said inflation is now expected to run above the August projections, the labour market looks tighter than previously estimated and higher oil prices will add to inflation. Deputy Governor Hauser said the CPI figures were in line with expectations but still too high.

headline: RBNZ holds its official cash rate at 2.75% on a 4-3 vote, against a forecast of 3%
detail: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand left the OCR at 2.75%, while the forecast had been for 3%. It said all committee members agreed on the overall inflation outlook and that global factors are adding to inflation pressures.

headline: UK government weighs local investment and sustainability conditions for data centres in return for priority grid access
detail: City AM reports that ministers are examining the proposals ahead of Wednesday's Budget, after missing their own deadline for new planning rules.

headline: RBNZ minutes say more OCR hikes are probable depending on the outlook; New Zealand dollar falls 1.4% to $0.5600
detail: The RBNZ minutes show Breman, Hansen, Gai and Williams voted to hold the OCR, while Conway, Gourley and Silk backed a hike. They also say international developments are adding to upside inflation risks and that high refined fuel prices and a weaker currency could spread inflation more widely. The New Zealand dollar fell 1.4% to $0.5600 after the hold.

headline: Israel's Netanyahu says the Iran mission is not complete and Israel will remove the threat together with Trump
detail: Speaking after Israel's elections, Prime Minister Netanyahu said Iran is weaker than ever but the campaign against it is not over and is only beginning.

headline: US military cost of the Iran war tops $47bn, Pentagon data show
detail: Pentagon data obtained by Reuters put US spending on the Iran war at more than $47bn so far, over 25% above the Defense Department's July estimate.

headline: RBA's Hunter says Australia is not expected to fall into recession
detail: RBA Assistant Governor Hunter said the central bank does not expect the Australian economy to slip into recession.

headline: Chancellor Healey is set to present a cautious Budget on Wednesday amid bond market pressure, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that Chancellor John Healey will set out a low-key Budget plan on Wednesday, aiming not to add to bond market pressure on Prime Minister Andy Burnham's new government.

headline: RBNZ Governor Breman says more rate hikes are probable at coming meetings and a lasting NZD fall could lift imported inflation
detail: The RBNZ Governor said policy may need to become more restrictive depending on the economy, and that the committee looked at market pricing and the fall in the New Zealand dollar. The Australian dollar rose 2% against the New Zealand dollar to NZ$1.2602, its highest since early 2013.

headline: Japanese government bond yields rise 4bp, with the 10-year at 2.825% and the 20-year at 3.635%
detail: The 20-year JGB yield rose 4bp to 3.635% and the 10-year rose 4bp to 2.825% in Asian trading on Wednesday.

headline: RBA's Bullock says inflation is unacceptably high and domestic demand still exceeds supply
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia Governor said Australian domestic demand remains above domestic supply and that inflation is too high.

headline: RBNZ's Breman says the OCR is likely to rise above its earlier forecast path and tightening may reach restrictive levels
detail: At the briefing after the decision, the RBNZ Governor said the committee discussed raising the OCR track and the risk of a fall in AI-linked asset prices. She also said wage growth is still below levels consistent with the inflation target and that partial inflation and labour data will be key in the coming weeks.

headline: US signals a possible short, sharp escalation of the Iran conflict after the midterm elections, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Washington has signalled the possibility of a brief, intense escalation in the Iran conflict once the US midterm elections are over. The report gave no market reaction.

headline: Japan's 5-year government bond yield rises 3bp to 2.260%
detail: The yield on 5-year JGBs climbed 3bp to 2.260% in Asian trading on Wednesday.

headline: Sterling edges lower towards $1.3300 ahead of the Budget and the Fed decision
detail: GBP/USD drifted towards 1.3300 in Asian trading, ahead of Chancellor Healey's Budget and the Federal Reserve rate decision, according to an FX market report.

headline: Bank of England is set to begin short-term precautionary monetary tightening in November, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Bank of England plans to start short-term precautionary tightening at its November meeting. The report came out before the UK Budget.

headline: Japan's 2-year government bond yield rises 2bp to 1.895%
detail: The 2-year JGB yield climbed 2bp to 1.895%, while the 5-year yield rose 3.5bp to 2.265%.

headline: Trump leaves open the possibility of further attacks on Iran after the election
detail: President Trump said he would not rule out more strikes on Iran once the US election is over.

headline: Trump says Ukraine peace efforts are progressing and he hopes to hold talks with Putin and Zelenskiy soon
detail: President Trump said efforts on Ukraine are moving forward and that he hopes to meet both Putin and Zelenskiy in the near future.

headline: Chancellor Healey abolishes standing charges on household gas bills
detail: A market news account reports that the UK Chancellor is scrapping standing charges on gas bills and presents the change as making payments fairer. The report comes ahead of Wednesday's Budget.

headline: German GfK consumer sentiment weakens to -30.8, below the -30.3 forecast
detail: The GfK consumer sentiment index for Germany came in at -30.8, compared with a forecast of -30.3 and -30.6 previously.

headline: Brent and US crude futures rise more than $2 as supply risks return
detail: Brent and US crude futures were reported up by more than $2 a barrel, with the rise put down to renewed supply risks.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine will not target Russian ships carrying diesel bound for the US
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Ukraine would not attack Russian vessels transporting diesel to the United States. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Russia's Ryabkov says Moscow is preparing for Ukraine negotiations and hopes US dialogue can address the conflict's root causes
detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Russia is in the preparation phase for negotiations on Ukraine. He also said Moscow hopes close dialogue with the US administration will help resolve the root causes of the conflict.

headline: China says it will pay consumption subsidies faster to support spending
detail: China announced on 28 October that it will speed up subsidy payments aimed at lifting consumption. The report gave no amounts or timetable.

headline: China urges Germany and the EU to take a rational approach on trade and supply chains
detail: China's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that it is committed to keeping global industrial and supply chains stable and secure. It was responding to German Chancellor Merz's proposal for wider EU-Asia market access to counter trade restrictions.

headline: Qatari mediators give Iran a new draft deal with a seven-day timeline; Iran's response is expected by the end of the week
detail: An official briefed on the negotiations says Qatari mediators handed Iran the draft in Tehran on Sunday. Under the draft, both sides would take confidence-building steps every day, several countries would act as guarantors, and the timeline could begin early next week.

headline: Healey's Budget is set to focus on the cost of living, with modest measures and major decisions put off, Guardian reports
detail: The Guardian reports that Chancellor Healey will frame today's Budget around the cost of living crisis at what he calls a difficult moment. It says only modest policies are expected and that important decisions will be deferred.

headline: China's commerce minister notes recent EU trade restrictions on China and calls the EU an important trade partner
detail: China's commerce minister said in a statement that China has taken note of recent EU restrictive trade measures against it, and described China and the EU as important economic and trade partners.

headline: Iran's president says the government is working to end the state of 'neither war nor peace'
detail: Iran's President Pezeshkian said the government is working to get beyond the current state of neither war nor peace. Qatari mediators have given Iran a new draft deal, and Iran is expected to respond by the end of the week.

headline: Italian producer prices rise 3.6% m/m in September
detail: Italian producer prices rose 3.6% month on month in September, according to the data release.

headline: Senior Iranian official denies Qatar has made a new proposal to end hostilities with the US and calls its ideas unacceptable
detail: A senior Iranian official said Qatar had not presented a fresh plan to end hostilities with the US, and that the ideas Qatar had put forward were unacceptable to Tehran. The official added that Iran's refusal to show flexibility on the nuclear issue is unchanged.

headline: Zelenskiy says Russia could also get security guarantees as part of a Ukraine peace deal, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Ukraine's president has acknowledged Moscow could receive security guarantees under a peace settlement. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Russia's Novak denies that Moscow is in talks with the US about American companies returning to Russian oil projects
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia is not negotiating with the US on a return to oil projects, TASS reported. This follows FT reports that the US was discussing Russian deals for American oil majors as part of the Ukraine peace talks.

headline: Germany's 10-year Bund auction averages 3.37%, down from 3.58% last time; bid-to-cover falls to 1.1
detail: The average yield at Germany's 10-year Bund auction was 3.37%, compared with 3.58% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.1, down from 1.2.

headline: US regulator proposes rules to speed up LNG projects and expand export capacity
detail: Reuters reports that a US regulator on Wednesday proposed new rules to speed up liquefied natural gas projects and expand export capacity. The proposal is part of the Trump administration's wider push on energy infrastructure.

headline: Bank of Canada is widely expected to raise its key rate by 25bp to 2.5% on Wednesday, its first hike in three years
detail: Reuters reports that most economists expect the Bank of Canada to raise its benchmark rate by 25bp to 2.5% on Wednesday. Economists see the move as protection against energy inflation spreading more widely.

headline: Healey's Budget bank tax rise is reported to be temporary, with the surcharge set below 8%
detail: Reports ahead of Chancellor Healey's Budget say the higher tax on banks will be temporary and the bank surcharge will come in under 8%.

headline: Gulf stocks fall after an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery revives fears of Middle East escalation
detail: Reuters reports that Gulf equity markets fell in early trade on Wednesday after an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia, the largest crude exporter. The attack revived concerns that the conflict in the Middle East could escalate.

headline: US secured overnight financing rate rises to 3.95% on 27 October from 3.93%
detail: The US secured overnight financing rate was 3.95% on 27 October, compared with 3.93% on 26 October.

headline: Chancellor Healey begins presenting the UK Budget
detail: Reuters is carrying a live broadcast of Chancellor John Healey presenting the Budget on 28 October.

headline: PM Burnham pledges to do all he can to secure a better EU deal for the UK
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said he would do everything he could to obtain an improved deal with the EU for the UK.

headline: US advance goods trade deficit widens to $134.9bn, more than the $130.2bn forecast
detail: The advance US goods trade balance came in at -$134.9bn, against a forecast of -$130.2bn and -$132.07bn previously. In the same release, advance wholesale inventories rose 0.6% m/m, against a forecast of 0.5% and 0.5% previously.

headline: Healey opens Budget speech saying it rests on fiscal discipline and backs British business for growth
detail: As he opened the Budget statement, Chancellor Healey said the Budget was for working people, would be built on fiscal discipline and would back British enterprise to drive growth. These were his opening remarks to the Commons.

headline: US preliminary wholesale inventories rise 0.6% m/m in September, above the 0.5% forecast
