detail: US wholesale inventories rose 0.6% m/m in the preliminary September reading, against a forecast and a previous reading of 0.5%. Advance retail inventories excluding autos rose 0.4%, after 0.0% the month before.

headline: UK Budget puts fiscal headroom against the spending rule at £15bn, slightly below the £15.2bn expected
detail: The headroom figure was reported as Chancellor Healey presented the Budget on 28 October. It compares with an expected £15.2bn.

headline: Healey says he meets the fiscal rules and will use some headroom to absorb the Iran war, with debt interest up £14bn this year
detail: In his Budget speech, the Chancellor said he would keep cutting borrowing, would not raise tax on working people and had rejected broad-based tax rises. He said the OBR names the Middle East war as a key driver of its forecasts and that debt interest spending is £14bn higher this year.

headline: OBR forecasts UK borrowing at 4.2% of GDP in 2026-27, up from 3.6% previously, falling to 1.8% by 2031-32
detail: Chancellor Healey set out the OBR's Budget forecasts. They put public sector net financial liabilities at 83.2% of GDP in 2026-27, against 82.6% in March, and net financial debt at 82.3% of GDP in 2030-31.

headline: Healey says fiscal headroom rises from £15bn to £22bn by 2030-31, with the rules met in the third forecast year
detail: The OBR's £15bn headroom against the current budget rule is down from £23.6bn in March and in line with the £15bn poll. The Chancellor said it climbs to £22bn by 2030-31 and that the fiscal rules will be met in the third year of the forecast.

headline: OBR raises its 2026 UK GDP growth forecast to 1.2% from 1.1% in March
detail: Chancellor Healey gave the upgraded OBR growth forecast in his Budget speech.

headline: Healey rules out broad tax rises and cuts to public services in the Budget
detail: The Chancellor told Parliament his Budget aims to give families and businesses breathing space. He also said he will start a radical reform of energy to bring bills down.

headline: OBR cuts its 2027 UK GDP growth forecast to 1% from 1.6%
detail: The Budget forecasts cut UK GDP growth for 2027 to 1% from 1.6%, while 2026 growth was raised to 1.2% from 1.1%.

headline: Healey announces £100 energy payment for 20mn households at a cost of £2.6bn and extends electricity VAT cut to July 2027
detail: In the Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said 20 million households will receive a £100 energy payment, at a cost of £2.6bn. He also extended the VAT cut on electricity bills to July 2027.

headline: Healey scraps the planned gas shippers obligation and moves more older renewables onto fixed-price contracts
detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey set out a new cost-controlled framework for energy bills, saying it aims to bring UK energy costs into line with Europe and reduce the effect of international gas prices on bills. He also said the UK remains committed to net zero by 2050.

headline: Budget says £1 in every £13 of government spending goes on debt interest
detail: The government's Budget statement put debt interest at £1 in every £13 of public spending.

headline: OBR raises its 2027-28 UK borrowing forecast to 3.4% of GDP from 2.9%
detail: The OBR's Budget forecast raises borrowing for 2027-28 to 3.4% of GDP from 2.9%. It also has the deficit falling to 1.8% of GDP by 2031-32.

headline: OBR forecasts UK net financial debt at 83.1% of GDP in 2029-30, easing to 82.3% by 2030-31
detail: Budget forecasts put UK net financial debt at 83.1% of GDP in 2029-30. The OBR projects the ratio easing to 82.3% by 2030-31.

headline: Healey raises the national living wage by 3.9% in the Budget
detail: Chancellor Rachel Healey announced a 3.9% rise in the national living wage in his Budget statement.

headline: Budget extends the 5p fuel duty cut to July 2027 and suspends tariffs on more than 100 supermarket products
detail: Chancellor Healey announced in the Budget that the 5p cut in fuel duty is extended to July 2027. He also announced that tariffs on more than 100 supermarket products are being suspended.

headline: Healey exempts pensioners with income up to the full state pension from income tax under a new pension allowance
detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new pension tax allowance in the Budget. Under it, pensioners whose income is no higher than the new full state pension will not pay income tax.

headline: Healey raises tax rates on income from property and savings by 2 percentage points in the Budget
detail: In the Budget speech, Chancellor Healey announced higher tax rates on property and savings income, with the increase reported as 2 percentage points. He also said the threshold for business asset disposal relief is being cut.

headline: Budget adds 3% to the bank surcharge
detail: Chancellor Healey told parliament in the Budget that banks will pay an extra 3% on the bank surcharge.

headline: Healey drops the planned cash ISA change and keeps the £20k cash ISA limit for all ages
detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey said the planned change to cash ISAs will not go ahead and the cash ISA limit stays at £20k for people of all ages.

headline: Budget lifts duty on gaming machines to 25% from 20% as Healey raises gambling taxes
detail: Chancellor Healey announced higher gambling taxes in the Budget, including a rise in gaming machine duty to 25% from 20%. He also announced tighter rules on online marketplaces so that sellers cannot avoid paying VAT.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine-Russia-US talks could take place as early as 10 November
detail: Ukrainian reports cite President Zelenskiy as saying that three-way negotiations between Ukraine, Russia and the United States could start as early as 10 November.

headline: Budget lifts the bank surcharge to 6% from 3% for 15 months starting in January
detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey's 3 percentage point increase takes the bank surcharge to 6% from 3%. The extra charge applies for 15 months from January.

headline: Healey allocates £20.4bn to the National Wealth Fund in the Budget
detail: Chancellor Healey announced £20.4bn for the National Wealth Fund in his Budget speech. He also announced a new British data centre covenant but gave no figures for it.

headline: Healey announces a founders relief within capital gains tax in the Budget
detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new founders relief in capital gains tax during the Budget speech. No further details were given in the reports.

headline: Budget sets out £140mn investment in strategic British AI companies
detail: The UK Budget includes £140mn of investment for strategic British AI firms, as announced during Chancellor Healey's speech.

headline: Healey says local authorities will keep 100% of business rates by the end of the decade as he moves to devolve tax revenues
detail: In his Budget statement, Chancellor Healey said the government is taking steps to devolve tax revenues. He said local authorities will retain all business rates by the end of the decade.

headline: Budget creates a new Good Growth Fund for local mayors
detail: Chancellor Healey announced a new Good Growth Fund for local mayors in the Budget. No funding figure was given in the reports.

headline: Healey says triple lock changes save £50bn by 2050, with a pensions double lock saving £15bn
detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said changes to the state pension triple lock will save £50bn by 2050. He also said a double lock on pensions will save £15bn.

headline: Healey says the Budget fully funds the defence investment plan
detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey said the government will fully fund the defence investment plan. No figures were given in the reports.

headline: Healey commits £10bn more in support for Ukraine in the Budget
detail: In his Budget speech, Chancellor Healey announced a further £10bn of support for Ukraine and said Britain would back Ukraine for as long as needed.

headline: Budget sets up a defence finance taskforce, with the National Wealth Fund and National Bank deploying up to £5bn on defence
detail: Healey said the government will start treaty talks with Finland, Poland and the Netherlands on a multilateral defence mechanism and will set out how it meets its NATO defence commitment. The National Wealth Fund and the National Bank will put up to £5bn of funding and investment into the defence industrial base.

headline: Canadian official says trade talks with the US have made limited progress
detail: Reuters cited a Canadian government official familiar with the talks, speaking on Wednesday.

headline: DMO sets 2026-27 gross gilt issuance at £250.6bn, above the £249.6bn poll and the April remit of £246.2bn
detail: The UK Debt Management Office published its revised 2026-27 financing remit alongside the Budget. Planned gross gilt issuance is £250.6bn, compared with £249.6bn expected in a poll and £246.2bn in the April remit.

headline: Healey sets a target of 3% of GDP for UK defence spending in 2030
detail: Chancellor Healey gave the target for UK defence spending during his Budget speech.

headline: Healey takes total government backing for council homes to £40bn and makes land sold to social housing providers VAT-free
detail: In the Budget, Chancellor Healey also announced £1.5bn for a social and affordable housing programme. He said all land sold to social housing providers will be free of VAT.

headline: Healey replaces the lifetime ISA with a first-time buyer ISA and gives £4.7bn to a 'Your first home' scheme
detail: Chancellor Healey announced both measures in his Budget speech.

headline: OBR raises UK inflation forecast to 3.1% for 2026 and 3.5% for 2027
detail: The OBR's Economic and Fiscal Outlook puts 2026 inflation at 3.1%, up from 2.3%, and 2027 inflation at 3.5% in its central forecast, up from 2% in March.

headline: DMO cuts long conventional syndication to £12.5bn and raises index-linked syndication to £7.8bn for 2026-27
detail: The revised DMO remit sets long-dated conventional gilt syndications at £12.5bn, down from £15bn in April. Index-linked syndications rise to £7.8bn from £7bn, and index-linked auctions fall to £15.6bn from £16bn.

headline: OBR cuts headroom against the debt rule to £24bn from £27.1bn
detail: The OBR says Budget policies add £3.5bn to borrowing in 2027-28 and cut it by £11.7bn in 2031-32. Reported calculations show £65bn more borrowing over 2026-27 to 2030-31 than in the March forecast.

headline: OBR calls fiscal margins very small and says a 1% rate move shifts debt interest by £16bn
detail: The OBR describes the UK fiscal position as very challenging and says a higher, longer energy price peak could lift 2027-28 borrowing £17bn above its central forecast. It adds that productivity growth 0.5 percentage points higher or lower could leave borrowing £50bn lower or £40bn higher.

headline: World Bank forecasts global energy prices up 32% in 2026, a four-year high, on Middle East war
detail: The World Bank expects global oil supply to fall 5.2% in 2026 and overall commodity prices to rise 23% before falling 7% in 2027. It warns that further Middle East escalation or damage to Russian oil infrastructure could lift energy prices further.

headline: OBR raises 2026-27 UK borrowing forecast to £133.2bn from £115.5bn, and 2027-28 to £112bn from £96.5bn
detail: The OBR's Budget forecast puts government borrowing at £68.3bn in 2031-32. Net borrowing over 2026-31 is reported as £65bn higher than in the previous forecast.

headline: OBR expects UK CPI inflation to peak at 3.75% on a quarterly basis in early 2027
detail: The quarterly peak is in the OBR's central forecast, published alongside the Budget.

headline: European benchmark gas price hits €100/MWh, its first time at that level since December 2022
detail: The European benchmark gas price is reported reaching €100/MWh, a level last seen during the 2022 energy crisis.

headline: OBR puts the chance of meeting the fiscal mandate at 56%, down from 59% at Budget 2025
detail: The OBR also says the Budget plans slow the near-term pace of fiscal consolidation compared with the previous plans.

headline: OBR expects the UK tax-to-GDP ratio to pass its 37.2% record in 2027-28 and keep rising
detail: The OBR says the ratio rises in every year of the forecast. It also expects the bank tax increase to bring in £1bn in receipts in 2027-28.

headline: Bank of Canada raises its key rate by 25bp to 2.5%, in line with forecasts
detail: The Bank of Canada lifted its key rate to 2.5% from 2.25%, matching the 2.5% forecast. It is the bank's first rate rise in three years.

headline: OBR says headroom would be £10.2bn if fuel duty stayed frozen; cumulative cost of freezes and 5p cut reaches £139bn
detail: The OBR's Budget documents put headroom at £10.2bn if fuel duty had stayed frozen. It also says the cumulative cost of fuel duty freezes and the 5p cut has risen to £139bn.

headline: UK plans to extend its forthcoming carbon border tax to refined products, Treasury documents show
detail: Treasury Budget documents show the government plans to widen the scope of its upcoming carbon border tax to cover refined products.

headline: Bank of Canada signals further hikes may be needed and raises its inflation forecasts to 2.9% for 2026 and 3.1% for 2027
detail: The Bank of Canada's Monetary Policy Report now puts inflation at 2.9% in 2026 (2.5% in July), 3.1% in 2027 (2.0%) and 2.2% in 2028 (2.1%), above target until mid-2028. It assumes Brent averages around $100 in Q4 before easing to around $75 by end-2028. Governor Macklem said the hike was meant to stop high energy prices spreading into wider inflation, that rates may have to rise again and that the council will go carefully, deciding one meeting at a time.

headline: OBR says the government's council housebuilding ambition could cost an extra £3bn-£4bn a year
detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility put this estimate on the council housebuilding plans in its Budget documents.

headline: OBR expects the Employment Rights Act to have a negative economic impact
detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility gave this assessment of the Employment Rights Act alongside the Budget. No figures were reported.

headline: Losses on the BoE's quantitative tightening for 2027-28 are put at £5.7bn more than forecast in March
detail: The higher estimate of losses on the Bank of England's QT programme for 2027-28 was reported on Budget day. It is £5.7bn above the March forecast.

headline: Kremlin says Europeans will not join the trilateral Ukraine talks and a date will be announced soon
detail: Kremlin aide Ushakov said European representatives are not being invited to the negotiations on Ukraine, Interfax reported. The Kremlin also said the date of the trilateral talks would be announced soon.

headline: OBR puts UK headroom before Budget measures at £12.5bn in 2029-30
detail: The OBR estimates fiscal headroom in 2029-30 at £12.5bn before the Budget measures are taken into account.

headline: DMO says its standing repo facility for Treasury bills will start in January
detail: The UK Debt Management Office says a standing repo facility covering Treasury bills will begin operating in January.

headline: Gilts extend rally as UK 30-year yield drops 5bp to a day low of 5.70%
detail: Market wire reports UK gilts extending gains during the Budget, with the 30-year yield down 5bp at an intraday low of 5.70%.

headline: DMO expects to price Treasury bill repo facility 20bp below Bank Rate and sets up £250mn collateral pool per bill
detail: The DMO said its Treasury bill standing repo facility is likely to be priced at 20bp below BoE Bank Rate, subject to review. It is also introducing a collateral pool holding £250mn of each Treasury bill.

headline: Government says England's regions will keep a share of locally raised income tax and business rates
detail: Reuters reports the government's fiscal devolution plan, published on Wednesday alongside the Budget, will let England's regions retain part of the income tax and business rates raised in their areas.

headline: UK plans reform of electricity standing charges, Treasury Budget documents show
detail: Treasury documents published with the Budget say the government will reform electricity standing charges. No further details were given in the report.

headline: ADNOC tells clients its new pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz will start in early 2027
detail: Abu Dhabi's national oil company has told clients that its new pipeline route avoiding the Strait of Hormuz is due to begin operating in early 2027, according to a market commentary account. The post did not report any price reaction.

headline: OBR says the welfare cap will be missed by £2.8bn, putting the government technically in breach of one fiscal rule
detail: The OBR's Budget documents show social security spending on course to exceed the welfare cap by £2.8bn, a technical breach of that rule.

headline: OBR forecasts real household disposable income per person still more than ¾% below its March path in 2030-31
detail: The Resolution Foundation, reading the Budget documents, says the OBR has real household disposable income falling this year and real earnings growth at zero in 2027 and 2028. The Guardian reports the living standards outlook was downgraded partly because of the Middle East conflict.

headline: Healey makes online marketplaces responsible for collecting VAT owed by sellers on their platforms
detail: Reuters reports that the Chancellor said on Wednesday that online marketplaces will have to collect the VAT owed by retailers who sell through them.

headline: Foreign banks are not exempt from the higher UK bank surcharge
detail: A market commentary account reports that foreign firms get no exemption from the higher bank surcharge announced in the Budget.

headline: Macklem says the Bank of Canada's policy rate is still low enough not to restrain growth, even after the hike
detail: At his press conference after the rate rise, Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said hiking will limit how much higher oil prices pass through to inflation. He also said investment in the energy sector is rising and investment estimates may be conservative.

headline: Macklem says the Bank of Canada has no set path for rates and inflation now looks less likely to stay well contained
detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said after the 25bp hike that raising rates will limit how far higher oil prices pass through, and that businesses are planning to pass on high input costs. He also said changing direction is always a difficult decision.

headline: Budget commits to ringfencing preventative spending at the 2027 Spending Review
detail: The Institute for Government reported that the Chancellor will ringfence preventative spending at the 2027 Spending Review, a Budget measure the IfG had argued for.

headline: Macklem says US trade and Middle East uncertainty could change the BoC outlook; Rogers calls housing forecast subdued
detail: Speaking after the rate decision, Bank of Canada Governor Macklem said uncertainty over US trade and the Middle East could alter the outlook. Senior Deputy Governor Rogers said uncertainty over the economy and borrowing rates is weighing on housing, and called the bank's housing forecast subdued.

headline: Zelenskiy hopes for Ukraine-US-Russia talks between 6 and 10 November and no later than end-November
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv hopes the trilateral talks with the US and Russia will take place between 6 and 10 November, and that they should happen no later than the end of November.

headline: BoC's Rogers says policymakers broadly agreed inflation risks had risen and discussed both holding and raising rates
detail: Bank of Canada Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers said there was strong consensus that inflation risks were rising. She said the Governing Council discussed whether to hold or raise rates, which she called common practice.

headline: Zelenskiy expects clarity on peace talks after the US elections and will discuss territory only at leaders' level
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said he expects clarity on talks with Russia and the US after the US elections. He said territory would only be discussed at leaders' level and called for European unity to help end the war.

headline: Dutch PM says no European ally is willing to buy Russian energy
detail: The Dutch prime minister said no European ally is prepared to buy Russian energy and described doing so as a foolish decision.

headline: Zelenskiy says the energy ceasefire is not holding and Ukraine is hitting Russian energy sites in response to attacks
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said the energy ceasefire is not working. He said Ukraine now responds to Russian attacks on its energy infrastructure by striking Russian energy infrastructure.

headline: BoC's Rogers says the Bank does not see a Middle East resolution as imminent
detail: Bank of Canada Senior Deputy Governor Rogers made the remark at the press conference following the Bank's 25bp rate rise to 2.5%. The press conference has now ended.

headline: UK markets react calmly to Healey's first Budget after pledge to keep to borrowing rules
detail: Reuters reports that UK markets took the chancellor's first Budget calmly on Wednesday. Investors drew comfort from the government's commitment to stick to its borrowing rules.

headline: IFS says current budget surplus by 2029-30 is still on track but smaller, with day-to-day borrowing likely in 2028-29
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says the government remains on track for a current budget surplus by 2029-30, but a smaller one, with more of the fall in borrowing coming in later years. It says the government is now likely to be borrowing for day-to-day spending in 2028-29.

headline: Mexico's Sheinbaum says US trade deal talks continue and Mexico is weighing whether a deal before the midterms is possible
detail: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said talks with the US on a trade deal are continuing. Mexico is assessing whether an agreement can be reached before the US midterm elections.

headline: Budget's cost of living package centres on a £100 council tax rebate for Band A–D homes to help with winter energy bills
detail: According to the Resolution Foundation, the main measure in the Chancellor's cost of living package is a £100 council tax rebate for households in Bands A to D, aimed at rising energy bills this winter.

headline: Healey says the main UK minimum wage rate will rise by 3.9%
detail: Chancellor John Healey announced on Wednesday that the main minimum wage rate will increase by 3.9%, Reuters reports.

headline: US crude futures rise $3 a barrel as fighting in Yemen raises Middle East supply concerns
detail: A market newswire reports US crude prices up $3 a barrel. The move is attributed to concerns over Middle East supply after fighting in Yemen.

headline: Budget documents show mayors' share of income tax will cover basic-rate receipts only
detail: Government Budget documents show that the devolved income tax share for mayors will be limited to basic-rate revenues, an economist noted. Higher and additional rate receipts are not included.

headline: Meloni says Italy's 2027 budget includes €26bn of tax cuts and spending increases
detail: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the 2027 budget contains tax cuts and spending increases worth €26bn.

headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR forecasts put 2020s income growth as the weakest of any decade on record
detail: The Resolution Foundation said the OBR's latest forecasts show incomes ending the decade only 1.4% higher in 2030 than in 2020.

headline: Senior US official says any Iran strike does not depend on Israeli politics and Trump aims to remove threats to Hormuz
detail: Israel Hayom quotes an unnamed senior US diplomatic official as saying a strike on Iran does not depend on Israel's political process. The official also says Trump is still determined to fully neutralise Iran's military nuclear programme and remove military threats to the Strait of Hormuz and to Iran's neighbours.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright expects diesel prices to fall sharply as Gulf exports rise and China resumes shipments
detail: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said diesel exports from the Arabian Gulf are likely to increase and China is likely to resume exporting diesel. He said diesel prices will drop significantly.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says Russia can benefit from diesel exports only by ending the war in Ukraine
detail: The US Energy Secretary tied any Russian gain from diesel exports to an end to the war. He repeated that he expects diesel prices to fall significantly and Gulf diesel exports to rise.

headline: Markets price about a 93% chance that the Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00% ahead of today's decision
detail: A market commentator said a hold at 3.75%–4.00% is about 93% priced for the Federal Reserve decision at 2:00pm ET, with Chair Warsh's press conference due at 2:30pm ET.

headline: IFS says OBR sees UK growth slowing markedly next year, with GDP level back to its March path by 2030-31
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says the OBR puts next year's slowdown down to higher energy prices and interest rates. The OBR expects GDP to fully regain its March-forecast level by 2030-31, with energy prices and inflation forecast to return to pre-war levels.

headline: IFS says OBR cuts forecast for household income growth this parliament to 0.4% a year from 0.7%
detail: The IFS says the OBR's revised forecast would make this the second weakest parliament for household income growth since 1979. It would still beat the last parliament, when disposable incomes fell.

headline: Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is still giving diplomacy a chance and is working with intermediaries to speed up its 7-day plan
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran's armed forces are ready to defend the country but Tehran will keep pursuing diplomacy. He said Iran is in ongoing contact with intermediaries over ideas that could put its 7-day plan into effect in less than a week.

headline: Long-dated gilt yields fall to a one-month low as Budget borrowing figures match gilt dealers' forecasts
detail: Reuters reports that the 2026-27 gilt issuance rise of £4.4bn to £250.6bn was close to the £249.6bn Reuters poll. The 2027-28 PSNB forecast of £112bn was in line with the poll.

headline: Budget says 10 new English devolution agreements are in their final stages
detail: A post on the Budget says that, if the 10 agreements are completed, devolution deals would cover over 90% of England's population.

headline: IFS says Budget measures raise the long-run tax take only modestly, much less than the parliament's two earlier Budgets
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies said in its Budget 2026 analysis that the Chancellor's measures produce a modest increase in the long-run tax take, significantly smaller than the increases in the previous two Budgets of this parliament.

headline: HMRC draws up list of 200 billionaires as part of a tax compliance drive on the UK's wealthiest
detail: The FT reports that HMRC has identified 200 billionaires and is inviting each of them and their representatives to a voluntary early or pre-filing discussion.

headline: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00% on a 10-2 vote
detail: The Federal Reserve left its target range for the federal funds rate at 3.75%–4.00%, as expected, with two FOMC members dissenting. The Fed said gathering more information will help it decide the appropriate policy stance.

headline: Fed's Cook and Hammack dissent in favour of a 25bp hike; statement says inflation remains elevated and growth is strong
detail: The Fed statement says activity is expanding at a strong pace, inflation remains elevated and more information will help determine the policy stance. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack backed a 25bp hike, and short-term US rate futures were reported rising after the decision.

headline: Axios reports US and Israel anticipate a week of strikes on Iran after the midterms if nuclear talks fail
detail: According to Axios, possible strikes would target Iran's leadership, energy and nuclear sites, Iran is being pressed to make nuclear concessions, and the Israeli military and the US are coordinating. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Traders keep pricing a 90% chance of a December Fed hike after the hold; short-term rate futures rise
detail: Short-term US interest rate futures rose after the Fed left rates at 3.75%–4% and traders still price a 90% chance of a December hike. The dollar index fell 0.08% to 102.26 and the euro rose 0.15% to $1.114.

headline: Axios says possible post-midterm strikes on Iran could target its leadership as the US and Israel coordinate
detail: Axios cites Israeli and regional sources as saying Iran is under pressure to make nuclear concessions, and that the Israeli military and the US are coordinating ahead of any attacks.

headline: UK to tax sovereign wealth funds on their UK property investments
detail: The Financial Times reports the change will affect countries such as the Gulf states, which are large property investors in Britain.

headline: Traders now price an 80% chance of a December Fed hike
detail: Market pricing for a December Fed hike stands at 80%, according to a market commentary feed. This follows the Fed's hold earlier today.

headline: Arab mediators press Iran for a deal on IAEA inspections and US sanctions relief, Axios says
detail: Axios reports that Arab mediators are pushing Tehran towards an agreement covering IAEA inspections and relief from US sanctions.

headline: Resolution Foundation says global developments since March add £11bn a year on average to OBR underlying borrowing forecast
detail: The Resolution Foundation says global news since March has raised the OBR's underlying borrowing forecast by £11bn on average across the next five years.

headline: IFS says OBR expects 10.8 million higher or additional rate income taxpayers by March 2031
detail: The IFS says this is 6 million more than if the higher rate threshold had risen with CPI inflation since 2022, and 250,000 more than the OBR forecast in March.

headline: Canadian 2-year yield reaches a two-year high after the Bank of Canada's rate hike
detail: Reuters reports Canadian bond yields rose and the Canadian dollar edged higher against the US dollar after the Bank of Canada raised rates for the first time in more than three years.

headline: Fed Chair Warsh says inflation remains elevated and the Fed has not grown easier; sees 3Q US GDP likely above 3%
detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said economic activity is expanding strongly, business investment is likely rising at a double-digit pace and the committee wants more information to set the policy stance. He said the Fed's responsibility is to get inflation down and that he is not surprised by market volatility.

headline: WTI December crude settles up 2.88% at $102.78 a barrel
detail: NYMEX WTI December futures settled $2.88 higher at $102.78 a barrel on Wednesday.

headline: Warsh says the Fed will change its FOMC schedule, with one 2027 meeting lacking a rate vote and 6 policy-setting meetings expected in 2028
detail: At his press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed will keep 8 meetings a year, with one focused on strategy and one with no rate vote or statement in 2027, and two without a rate vote in 2028. He also said the Fed has shown it is willing and ready to act, that growth has strengthened and credit conditions have tightened, and that he would not call financial conditions tight.

headline: Fed's Warsh says tightening is starting to work and credit conditions have tightened, but he will not call financial conditions tight
detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed removed some accommodation in September, that swap-based inflation compensation is moving the right way and that he is not surprised by market volatility. He said the committee is focused mainly on price stability, will not tolerate inflation above the 2% target, and that the period ahead is rich in information.

headline: Warsh says swap-based inflation compensation is moving the right way and the Fed removed some accommodation in September
detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the period ahead would bring plenty of information and he was comfortable with the signposts. He added that the conclusions of the Fed's five task forces are unlikely to feed into policy at this point, and that he may speak at a task force field hearing on 16 November.

headline: Warsh says the Fed's 2% PCE goal is not a soft target and longer-term inflation expectations remain anchored
detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said near-term inflation expectations have risen but longer-term measures still show confidence in price stability. He called the FOMC meeting a family fight that reached the right decision, and said market interest rates have turned lower despite a usually stable link with rising oil prices.

headline: Warsh says he will not give forward guidance outside a crisis or prejudge December, and that politics played no part in the decision
detail: At his post-decision press conference, Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed may learn a lot before December and that neither the midterm elections nor politics came up in FOMC deliberations. He also said rates have affected investment inside and outside the technology sector since early September, that capex strength has broadened, that credit spreads have widened for some assets, and that he has noted the rise in oil futures.

headline: Warsh says balance sheet task force will report to the FOMC early in Q1 and most Fed colleagues do not see the economy running too hot
detail: Fed Chair Warsh said any balance sheet changes would follow serious consideration of the task force's recommendations and are unlikely to affect the current policy juncture. He also said productivity has been rising, higher growth does not mean it is causing inflation, and he does not think the Fed has to throw people out of work.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises 4.11bp to 5.034% during Warsh's press conference
detail: The 10-year Treasury note yield was last reported up 4.11bp at 5.034% while Fed Chair Warsh was speaking after the Fed's decision to hold rates.

headline: Warsh ends press conference saying he is comfortable with the Fed tightening financial conditions; Fed not involved in Cook proceedings
detail: Fed Chair Warsh said tighter financial conditions show that policy is working and that he is not uncomfortable with them. Asked about the proceedings involving Governor Cook, he said the Fed is not involved as far as he knows, and then ended the press conference.

headline: Iran and mediators weigh Turkey meeting before 4 November on new proposal covering Hormuz reopening, Al Arabiya says
detail: Al Arabiya, citing sources, says Iran and mediators are discussing a meeting in Turkey before 4 November. It says the timeline in the new proposal includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the siege.

headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR sees UK welfare bill rising by £38bn by 2031-32 while reform waits on reviews
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the OBR expects welfare spending to increase by £38bn by 2031-32, led by the State Pension and by health and disability benefits for people of working age. It says welfare reform is paused until the Milburn and Timms reviews report.

headline: US CENTCOM says US forces have cleared sea mines from the main transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz
detail: US Central Command says all internationally recognised primary transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared of sea mines by US forces and remain clear. It says thousands of commercial vessels have used the lanes safely and are still using them today.

headline: Zelenskiy acknowledges for the first time that Russia needs security guarantees, as US-led peace diplomacy picks up
detail: The Ukrainian president acknowledged Russia's need for security guarantees, a change in Kyiv's position. He said ending the war and securing Ukraine must still come first.

headline: US CENTCOM rejects Iranian media claims that commercial ships are hitting sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: US Central Command said claims carried by Iranian-controlled media in recent days and weeks, that commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz were striking sea mines, are false.

headline: Iran proposal also covers lifting the blockade, the nuclear issue and the return of inspectors, Al Arabiya says
detail: Al Arabiya reports that the schedule of the new proposal under discussion with Iran covers reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the blockade, dealing with Iran's nuclear programme and calling in inspectors. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Healey asks BoE to review banks' capital requirements and says the bank tax rise will have a time limit in law
detail: In post-Budget remarks, Chancellor Healey said she has asked the Bank of England to look at banks' capital requirements and that legislation for the higher bank tax will include a time limit. She also said the government will press ahead with the financial services and markets bill and that business costs were a Budget priority.

headline: US proposal reportedly combines Iran's seven conditions with US nuclear demands in phases; Iran wants its conditions met first
detail: An Al Jazeera reporter says the US proposal pairs Iran's seven conditions with US demands on highly enriched uranium and inspections, to be implemented in phases. The reporter says Iran insists its conditions are met before any nuclear negotiations, while indirect US-Iran messages continue.

headline: US Vice President Vance writes to a senior Iranian hard-liner in an attempt to restart peace talks, WSJ reports
detail: The WSJ reports that Vance sent the letter to the secretary of Iran's top security body, a former long-serving IRGC commander. One person said the letter was sent at Trump's direction and that Trump knows about the continuing outreach.

headline: Germany will let offshore wind developers hand back auctioned sites if they pay a penalty
detail: German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said on Wednesday that companies may return offshore wind sites they won at auction, as long as they pay a penalty to the transmission system operators. Reuters reports that the sector is under growing economic pressure.

headline: Trump signs proclamation on US imports of robotics and industrial machinery but imposes no immediate tariffs
detail: The White House says President Trump has signed a proclamation adjusting US imports of robotics, industrial machinery and their parts and components. It says these imports pose national security risks, but no tariffs take effect immediately.

headline: Bessent says US faces an energy supply shock and the Fed should keep an open mind; says bonds have done much of the tightening
detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said he expects a strong US third-quarter GDP figure, that the Fed is very attentive to inflation having been above target for a long time, and that yields and oil prices are closely correlated. He also said he and Trump have a lot of confidence in Fed Chair Warsh.

headline: Bessent says the Iran operation is working and Tehran is cut off from dollars; sees no problem in AI-related borrowing
detail: In a CNBC interview, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said Operation Outcast on Iran is succeeding, that Iran cannot get dollars and that funding for its proxies is falling. He also said he does not regard AI borrowing or wider spreads on AI-issuer debt as a problem, and described France as having a tough hand.

headline: Global bond sales hit an annual record of $6.61 trillion
detail: Market reports on 28 October said global bond issuance this year has reached a record $6.61 trillion.

headline: Bessent says US trade deals are largely locked in and consumer and business behaviour is strong
detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC that much of Trump's economic agenda, including tax cuts, is already in place, and that the trade deals are mostly locked in. He also said France has a tough hand. His CNBC appearance has now ended.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK plans a much larger fiscal consolidation than other high-income OECD countries
detail: In its post-Budget analysis, the Resolution Foundation said the government's planned fiscal consolidation is much bigger than those of other high-income OECD countries. It added that it is not yet clear whether the plans will be delivered.

headline: Budget confirms £1.5bn of devolved loans for mayoral authorities plus extra funding for social housing and rough sleeping
detail: Inside Housing reports that the Chancellor's Budget repeats the Prime Minister's earlier announcement giving mayoral authorities access to £1.5bn of devolved loans. The Budget also confirms more funding for the Social and Affordable Homes Programme and for rough sleeping.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says timing of Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine depends partly on the battlefield situation
detail: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said the date for the negotiations in Abu Dhabi will depend on factors including the situation on the battlefield and the wider situation. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Fitch says US fiscal pressures will persist whatever the midterm election result
detail: Fitch Ratings said pressure on US public finances is set to continue regardless of the outcome of the midterm elections. The post reported no rating action.

headline: Trump says he did not instruct Vance to write to Iran
detail: President Trump said he had not told Vice President Vance to send the letter to Iran. The WSJ had reported that Vance wrote to a senior Iranian hard-liner to try to restart peace talks.

headline: BoC's Macklem says Canada's neutral rate estimate could rise and the inflation forecast assumes fuel costs pass through
detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said the estimate of the neutral interest rate may be revised up and the bank's inflation forecast rests on fuel costs passing through to prices. He added that a new model lets the bank break inflation down by component, and described earlier core CPI forecasts as a shortcut.

headline: Hong Kong Monetary Authority leaves its base rate at 4.25%
detail: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority kept its base rate unchanged at 4.25% after the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates.

headline: RBNZ Governor Breman says the chance of a December rate hike is high
detail: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman said on Thursday that the likelihood of the bank raising the official cash rate in December is high.

headline: South Korea's finance minister says Seoul will act promptly on market turbulence and review November bond issuance
detail: South Korea's finance minister said the government will respond quickly to any jump in market volatility, will carefully assess the size of November treasury bond issuance and will buy back treasury bonds if needed.

headline: JGB yields rise ahead of the BoJ policy announcement, with the 5-year up 1.5bp at 2.28%
detail: The 5-year Japanese government bond yield rose 1.5bp to 2.28% as investors waited for the Bank of Japan's policy decision, WSJ reported.

headline: US 30-year Treasury yield falls 5bp to 5.311% in Asian trading
detail: The long bond yield fell 5 basis points to 5.311% during Asian hours on Thursday, while US equity futures sold off.

headline: Budget scorecard assumes approval of North Sea discovery drilling producing more than a billion barrels
detail: City AM reports that the Budget scorecard assumes the government will approve North Sea discovery drilling projects producing over a billion barrels of oil and gas, following Jackdaw and Rosebank.

headline: Bank of Korea board member Hwang says it is time to focus on inflation and the won is moving faster than expected
detail: Hwang said the Bank of Korea is watching the FX market closely and that high borrowing costs are limiting gains for small and medium firms. He cited an upward revision to the 2026 current account surplus to $500bn from $450bn.

headline: China's onshore yuan strengthens to 6.6621 per dollar, its strongest since 7 June 2022
detail: The onshore yuan rose to 6.6621 per US dollar in Asian trading on Thursday, its strongest level since 7 June 2022.

headline: China opposes US move to put Chinese firms on a Xinjiang-related entity list and vows to protect its interests
detail: China's commerce ministry said the US listing of Chinese companies goes against the consensus reached by the two heads of state. It called on Washington to stop immediately and said China will take the steps needed to protect its interests.

headline: Swedish GDP growth slows to 2.8% year on year in advance estimate, just below the 2.9% forecast
detail: Sweden's advance GDP estimate showed annual growth of 2.8%, against a forecast of 2.9% and down from 3.3% previously.

headline: Swedish Q3 GDP rises 0.4% on the quarter, above the 0.3% forecast; September GDP indicator falls 0.7% on the month
detail: Sweden's Q3 GDP indicator rose 0.4% quarter on quarter, against a 0.3% forecast and 1.4% previously. The monthly indicator for September fell 0.7% after a 1.1% rise, and its annual rate slowed to 2.1% from 3.5%.

headline: Swedish retail sales fall 0.4% in September and consumer confidence drops to 94.3 in October
detail: Swedish retail sales fell 0.4% month on month in September after a revised 0.9% rise, and annual growth slowed to 5.5% from a revised 7.2%. Consumer confidence fell to 94.3 in October from 102.2, while manufacturing confidence rose to 111.5 from 106.3.

headline: Healey commits to cutting welfare spending before the next election, with plans due by the end of the year
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Chancellor, having delivered her first Budget, has promised to publish plans by the end of the year to reduce a welfare bill she called unsustainable.

headline: China's commerce ministry says it will take all necessary measures if the EU imposes discriminatory restrictions on Chinese goods
detail: China's Ministry of Commerce issued the warning about any EU curbs on Chinese products on 29 October. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Lloyds Q3 net interest income comes in at £3.81bn, just below the £3.83bn estimate
detail: Lloyds reported Q3 2026 loan-loss provisions of £313.0m (estimate £311.8m) and operating costs of £2.37bn (estimate £2.39bn). Total deposits were £502.8bn, against an estimate of £502.41bn.

headline: India's trade minister says the US trade deal will protect farmers and all stakeholders and leave India at a strong comparative advantage
detail: India's trade minister said that no sensitive interest of farmers or any other stakeholder would be compromised by the planned trade deal with the US. He added that India would hold a strong comparative advantage once the deal is completed.

headline: EU energy commissioner says the bloc uses 18% less gas than in 2022 and is better placed for the current crisis
detail: The EU energy commissioner said the bloc is better able to handle the current energy crisis than in 2022 because gas use is 18% lower. The commissioner also said the crisis is made worse by its impact on oil products.

headline: South Korea sets November treasury bond issuance at 12tn won
detail: South Korea will issue 12tn won of treasury bonds in November. The finance minister had earlier said Seoul would review November issuance in response to market turbulence.

headline: Lloyds Q3 pre-tax profit rises nearly 99% to £2.3bn as costs fall and there are no major impairment charges
detail: Lloyds Banking Group reported third-quarter pre-tax profit of £2.3bn, ahead of expectations. City AM said the rise came from a lower cost base and the absence of any major impairment charges.

headline: EU energy commissioner says the threat to jet fuel supply security seen this summer has passed
detail: The EU's energy chief said there had been a risk to the security of jet fuel supply this summer and that the risk is no longer present.

headline: Saudi Aramco sets its November butane price at $780 a tonne
detail: Saudi Aramco has set its contract price for November butane at $780 per tonne, according to a market wire headline.

headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says three oil tankers hit mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iranian reports cite the IRGC navy as saying three tankers caught fire after hitting mines over the past 24 hours while using an unauthorised route off the southern side of the strait. US CENTCOM had earlier rejected Iranian media claims of ships hitting mines and said main transit routes had been cleared.

headline: Trump administration is in continuing talks on a temporary peace deal, Semafor reports
detail: Semafor reports that the US administration is in ongoing talks on a temporary peace deal. The report did not say which conflict the talks cover.

headline: Italian unemployment rate rises to 6.3%, above the 6.2% forecast
detail: Italy's unemployment rate came in at 6.3%, against a forecast of 6.2% and a previous reading of 6.2%.

headline: UK consumer credit rises £1.914bn and mortgage lending £3.866bn, both below forecasts, BoE data show
detail: Bank of England figures show consumer credit of £1.914bn against a £2bn forecast and £2.464bn previously. Net mortgage lending was £3.866bn against a £4.2bn forecast, with the previous month revised to £4.174bn from £4.410bn.

headline: UK 10-year gilt yield falls 3bp to 5.29%, a five-week low
detail: The benchmark 10-year gilt yield fell 3bp to 5.29% in morning trading, its lowest level in five weeks.

headline: UK mortgage approvals fall to 53.4K in September, below the 54K forecast; M4 money supply grows 0.1% on the month
detail: Bank of England data put September mortgage approvals at 53.443K against a forecast of 54K, with August revised to 54.814K. M4 money supply rose 0.1% on the month and 3.9% on the year, down from 4.4%, and M4 excluding intermediate OFCs grew at a 1.6% three-month annualised rate, down from 2.8%.

headline: Haskel says ONS productivity revisions came too late for the OBR forecast; OBR raised total factor productivity for AI
detail: Speaking at a Resolution Foundation event, former MPC member Jonathan Haskel said recent ONS revisions that lift output per hour arrived too late to go into the OBR forecast and do not change the outlook for productivity growth. He noted that the OBR raised its total factor productivity assumption because of the effect of AI.

headline: ECB President Lagarde tells staff she plans to step down on 7 February
detail: Reports on 29 October say ECB President Christine Lagarde has told staff she intends to leave her post on 7 February. The reports give no reason for her departure and name no successor.

headline: Lagarde's successor at the ECB is to be appointed by the European Council under the EU treaty nomination process
detail: The European Council will appoint the next ECB President using the nomination procedure in Article 283 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. This follows Lagarde telling staff she plans to step down on 7 February.

headline: EU's Costa says the search for Lagarde's successor as ECB President begins today and will go ahead without delay
detail: European Council President Costa said Lagarde had told him she intends to leave the ECB presidency on 7 February 2027. He said the appointment process for her successor starts today.

headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says subsidies to curb electricity and gas bills will run from December to February
detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said the government will introduce support measures for household electricity and gas bills starting in December and running until February.

headline: Japan's PM Takaichi says the target pump price for petrol will rise by 5 yen per litre each month from December
detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi said the target petrol price will go up by 5 yen per litre each month from December into the spring. She also confirmed the decision to subsidise power and gas bills from December.

headline: Healey says preventative spending will be ringfenced at the 2027 spending review
detail: According to the Institute for Government, John Healey has announced that the government will put a ringfence around preventative spending at the 2027 spending review.

headline: ECB formally confirms Lagarde has resigned as President, effective 7 February
detail: The European Central Bank said in a statement on Thursday that President Christine Lagarde has resigned and will leave on 7 February. This follows earlier reports that she had told staff of her plans.

headline: IFS says Budget plans for public service spending are very tight and doubts the government will deliver them
detail: At its post-Budget briefing, the Institute for Fiscal Studies questioned whether defence spending can reach 3% of GDP entirely within existing spending envelopes. It also said repeated small changes from Budget to Budget have left the tax system overly complex.

headline: Resolution Foundation says the OBR forecast higher borrowing and debt than in March before Budget measures
detail: In its Budget analysis 'Spread thin', the Resolution Foundation says the OBR's pre-measures forecast had government borrowing and debt above its March projections. No figures were given in the post.

headline: Lagarde resigned from the ECB because she could no longer stay neutral on French politics, a source says
detail: An unnamed source gave this as the reason for ECB President Lagarde's resignation, which takes effect on 7 February. The ECB had already formally confirmed that she is leaving.

headline: Italian consumer confidence falls to 90.3, below the 91 forecast; manufacturing confidence holds at 91.9
detail: Italy's October consumer confidence came in at 90.3, against a forecast of 91 and down from 91.2 previously. Manufacturing business confidence was 91.9, the same as the previous reading and just below the 92 forecast.

headline: Resolution Foundation says 2020s set to be the worst decade on record for real household disposable income growth
detail: In its post-Budget analysis 'Spread thin', the Resolution Foundation says real household disposable income will end the 2020s only 1.4% higher than at the start of the decade.

headline: Budget shields low-income pensioners from income tax as state pension rises; report says some face a 53% effective rate
detail: City AM reports that new Budget rules from Chancellor Healey exempt low-income pensioners from income tax on the state pension. The report says hundreds of thousands of pensioners would pay an effective 53% rate on part of their retirement income.

headline: RBC analysts say NatWest, Nationwide and Lloyds take the biggest profit hit from the Budget's doubled bank surcharge
detail: City AM reports RBC analysts' view that UK-focused lenders are more exposed than HSBC and Barclays to the Budget's doubling of the bank surcharge.

headline: Resolution Foundation says the forecast for the level of GDP in 2030 is unchanged after the Budget
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the GDP growth forecast picks up after a hit in the near term. It adds that other population assumptions make up for lower migration, so the 2030 level is unchanged.

headline: US Q3 GDP grows 3.4% in advance estimate, above the 3.2% consensus
detail: The advance estimate puts US third-quarter GDP growth at 3.4%, compared with a consensus of 3.2%.

headline: US continuing jobless claims fall to 1.701M, below the 1.72M forecast
detail: US continuing jobless claims came in at 1.701M, down from 1.728M previously and below the 1.72M forecast.

headline: Germany's Merz says the search for Lagarde's successor at the ECB will be finished by the end of the year
detail: The German Chancellor said the process to choose the next ECB President will be completed by year-end. Lagarde's resignation takes effect on 7 February.

headline: US September PCE prices rise 0.5% on the month and core 0.3%, both as forecast; core annual rate at 3.1%
detail: US data show headline PCE prices up 0.5% on the month (previous 0.3%) and core up 0.3% (previous 0.2%), both matching forecasts. Core PCE is 3.1% year on year against a 3.1% forecast; reports of the headline annual rate differ. Personal income rose 0.2% against a 0.3% forecast, spending rose 0.5% against 0.6%, and real consumption was flat against a 0.1% forecast.

headline: US Q3 GDP price index rises 2.3%, below the 3.2% forecast; quarterly core PCE prices up 2.5%
detail: The US advance Q3 GDP report puts the GDP price index at 2.3% against a 3.2% forecast and 3.5% previously. Core PCE prices rose 2.5% against a 2.4% forecast and 3.3% previously, and headline PCE prices rose 2.1% after 5.0%.

headline: US initial jobless claims hold at 194K, below the 198K forecast
detail: US weekly initial jobless claims were 194K, unchanged from the previous week and below the forecast of 198K.

headline: PM Starmer's spokesman says Burnham and Healey both think the welfare bill needs to fall
detail: The Prime Minister's spokesman said Burnham and Healey share the view that welfare spending should be reduced. This follows Healey's commitment to cut welfare spending before the next election, with plans due by the end of the year.

headline: Kremlin aide warns large Ukrainian attacks over 4 November celebrations could shift Russia's stance on trilateral talks
detail: A Kremlin aide said, according to Interfax, that major Ukrainian attacks during the 4 November celebrations could affect Russia's attitude towards the trilateral negotiations on Ukraine.

headline: Resolution Foundation says typical household energy bills this year are close to 2022-23 levels
detail: The Resolution Foundation said the typical UK household will pay nearly as much for energy this year as it did in 2022-23.

headline: US September PCE supercore inflation rises to 3.596% year on year from 3.493%; monthly pace at 0.367%
detail: US PCE supercore prices rose 3.596% on the year in September, up from 3.493% the previous month. The monthly rate was 0.367%, compared with 0.373% previously.

headline: EUR/GBP falls to its lowest level since April 2025 as sterling firms against the euro
detail: A market commentary account reported that the euro fell against sterling to its lowest level since April 2025. The post gave no exchange rate.

headline: France's Macron thanks Lagarde and says the ECB leadership handover must be orderly and balanced, prepared with European partners
detail: French President Macron thanked Christine Lagarde after the ECB confirmed her resignation as President, effective 7 February. He said the transition at the top of the ECB should now be prepared with European partners in an orderly and balanced way.

headline: ECB holds rates as expected, with the deposit facility rate at 2.50% and the main refinancing rate at 2.65%
detail: The ECB kept its October policy rates unchanged. The deposit facility rate stays at 2.50% and the main refinancing rate at 2.65%, both in line with forecasts, including the Reuters poll.

headline: UK PM Burnham says Britain is working to de-escalate and reopen the Strait of Hormuz fully, and to cut the welfare bill
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said the UK is doing all it can to de-escalate and to support a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and that Iran must have no nuclear capability. On the same occasion he said the government is working to reduce the welfare bill as soon as possible.

headline: ECB says a larger, longer energy shock is likely to push inflation up and growth down; keeps meeting-by-meeting approach
detail: The ECB's statement says energy prices have kept rising, posing upside risks to inflation and downside risks to growth, while underlying inflation has stayed broadly stable and wages show no material response so far. It says financing conditions have tightened since the last meeting, it will not pre-commit to a rate path, and APP and PEPP holdings continue to shrink with no reinvestment.

headline: Euro falls 0.4% to $1.11095, its lowest since May 2025, as traders cut ECB hike pricing to 68bp by end-2027
detail: The euro slipped after the ECB's decision to hold rates and was last down 0.4% at $1.11095, its lowest since May 2025. Market pricing for ECB rate hikes was pared to 68bp by the end of 2027.

headline: BoE opens consultation on rules for central counterparties accepting tokenised collateral
detail: The Bank of England said on Thursday it is consulting on the requirements central counterparties must meet before they can accept tokenised collateral. The Bank said this could make margin calls and wider collateral management easier, Reuters reports.

headline: French-German 10-year yield spread narrows 4bp to 150bp after ECB decision
detail: A market newswire reports that the gap between French and German 10-year government bond yields tightened by 4bp to 150bp after the ECB's rate decision.

headline: Treasury lowers its 2031-32 day-to-day spending assumption by £5.5bn in Budget plans
detail: An economics journalist reports that the Treasury trimmed its assumption for day-to-day departmental spending in 2031-32 by £5.5bn. No department yet has a budget set for that year.

headline: UK September mortgage approvals are the lowest since December 2023; unsecured lending growth is the fastest since 2018
detail: Reuters reports that lenders approved the fewest mortgages since December 2023 last month as borrowing costs rose. Unsecured lending to households grew at its fastest annual pace since 2018.

headline: Lagarde says the eurozone economy expanded in Q3 and growth stays supported, but higher energy prices hurt consumer confidence
detail: At her press conference after the ECB's decision to hold rates, President Lagarde said incoming data show the economy grew in the third quarter and that growth should remain supported in the near term. She said the new rise in energy prices is weighing on consumer confidence.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says Trump believes rates can be lower but respects Fed independence
detail: Speaking to Fox Business, Hassett said inflation came in close to expectations, that GDP is moving towards 4% growth and that a supply-side boom is pushing prices down. He said Trump thinks rates can be lower and respects the Fed's independence.

headline: France lowers diesel stockholding requirements to release supply
detail: A French official said the government has reduced the mandatory diesel stocks it requires so that more supply can reach the market.

headline: Lagarde says ECB wage tracker points to 2.5%-2.8% growth for rest of 2026 and energy prices have risen beyond baseline
detail: At the ECB press conference, Lagarde said underlying inflation stayed largely steady, early stages of the pricing chain show upward pressure, wage pressures are moderate and most long-term inflation expectation gauges are near 2%. She said AI investment and public spending should support growth, and that fiscal measures should be temporary, focused and tailored.

headline: Lagarde says eurozone growth risks are to the downside and inflation risks to the upside, with financial conditions tighter
detail: At the ECB press conference, President Lagarde said financial conditions have tightened since the last meeting. She added that fiscal uncertainty and weaker market sentiment could tighten financing conditions further and dampen demand.

headline: Lagarde sees no material risk of second-round inflation effects now, though indirect energy price effects have intensified
detail: At her post-decision press conference, ECB President Lagarde said she sees no sign of second-round effects beyond the ECB's projections, although the indirect impact of the energy price surge has intensified. She also said long-term borrowing costs have risen since September.

headline: Lagarde says ECB Governing Council discussed whether a rate rise would be appropriate but kept its measured approach
detail: ECB President Lagarde said at the post-decision press conference that the Governing Council debated a hike, but that a measured approach is still suitable for now. She said the ECB is unanimously seen as well positioned and strong enough to wait for further data.

headline: Budget changes how self-assessment income taxpayers make payments on account
detail: Chancellor Healey confirmed in the Autumn Budget that the government will change how income tax self-assessment taxpayers make their advance payments on account, City AM reports. Tax advisers have raised concerns about the effect on cash flow for the self-employed.

headline: Lagarde says long-end yields have risen worldwide and high-debt countries must plan for rates staying higher
detail: At her press conference, ECB President Lagarde said the ECB is watching the 10-year and the whole bond curve, and that borrowing by hyperscalers is one reason yields have risen. She also said the ECB will probably prepare scenarios in December.

headline: QatarEnergy CEO says it is buying US LNG to hedge against future Hormuz disruption and rules out bypass pipelines
detail: The QatarEnergy chief executive said the company expects to sign more long-term LNG purchase deals with the US and other suppliers by the end of 2026, aiming for well above 7 million tonnes a year. He said pipelines that bypass Hormuz are ruled out because any infrastructure in the region could be targeted.

headline: QatarEnergy CEO says two LNG trains hit in Iranian attacks need about three years to repair, cutting capacity by 17% meanwhile
detail: The QatarEnergy chief executive said full LNG output could restart within a week of a peace deal if ships are available, that Pearl GTL is due back by Q1 2027, and that the 142 MTPA expansion plan is unchanged. He also said LNG from new purchase agreements cannot be offered to long-term customers as a Hormuz backup.

headline: Lagarde says the ECB's direction of travel on rates is clear barring a surprise and it has tools for transmission disruptions
detail: Speaking at the ECB press conference, President Lagarde also said there is no plan to limit the number of meetings.

headline: OBR cuts its five-year housing delivery forecast by 190,000 homes, citing weak demand and rising costs
detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility expects 190,000 fewer homes to be delivered over the next five years than in its March 2026 forecast, Inside Housing reports.

headline: FT reports Hernández de Cos and Knot are frontrunners to succeed Lagarde as ECB President
detail: The Financial Times reports that Pablo Hernández de Cos and Klaas Knot lead the race to become the ECB's fifth president, after Lagarde confirmed she will step down on 7 February.

headline: QatarEnergy aims to lift outside LNG purchases well beyond 7 million tonnes a year by end-2026
detail: QatarEnergy is reported to be securing long-term LNG supplies from the US and elsewhere to hedge against future Hormuz disruption, and plans to expand those purchases to well beyond 7 million tonnes a year by the end of 2026.

headline: Lagarde says ECB QT continues mechanically with no plan to change, and she is leaving early to speak freely on non-monetary issues
detail: At her post-decision press conference, ECB President Lagarde said the approach to bond repayments under quantitative tightening is unchanged and there is no plan to readjust it. She also said she is stepping down early so that she has freedom of expression on matters other than monetary policy.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says the Fed would probably act if October inflation comes in very high
detail: White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said the Federal Reserve would likely respond if October inflation proves very high. He made the remarks in a live appearance on 29 October.

headline: Lagarde says ECB business will continue with full continuity ahead of her departure
detail: ECB President Christine Lagarde said the central bank will carry on its work with complete continuity. She said this after confirming she will step down on 7 February.

headline: Iran has received a letter from US Vice President Vance but has not replied, and still insists on its seven conditions, Tasnim says
detail: Iran's Tasnim news agency reports that Tehran has received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance and has not yet responded. Tasnim says Iran is holding to its seven conditions for the US and will not accept any position that contradicts them.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says October CPI and PCE figures should show the Fed what action to take
detail: White House economic adviser Hassett said the October consumer price and PCE inflation data should make the appropriate Fed policy response clear.

headline: Greek PM Mitsotakis calls for an urgent global maritime truce and says attacks on commercial shipping are unacceptable
detail: Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis said targeting civilian commercial shipping is unacceptable and that a global maritime truce is urgently needed.

headline: Netherlands releases its final 700K barrels of oil products to the market
detail: The Netherlands is releasing a last tranche of 700K barrels of oil products from its stocks to the market, according to a market newswire report.

headline: Trump weighs further military strikes on Iran after the midterms but is open to more diplomacy, Semafor reports
detail: Semafor reports that President Trump is seriously considering more military operations against Iran after the US election while appearing willing to give diplomacy another chance. The report says many inside the administration doubt the case for resuming strikes.

headline: Chancellor Healey pledges to set out benefit cuts before the end of this year
detail: The FT reports that the Chancellor made the commitment while answering criticism that Wednesday's Budget relies on unrealistic spending assumptions.

headline: IMF backs Fed Chair Warsh's focus on price stability
detail: The IMF said it fully supports Fed Chair Warsh's comments on focusing on price stability and that the Fed is right to watch the data closely.

headline: Cheniere says Europe needs an extra 69 million tonnes of LNG this winter and will have to draw cargoes away from Asia
detail: Cheniere's chief commercial officer, Anatol Feygin, said Europe will need an additional 69 million metric tons of LNG over the coming winter. He said the region will have to pull cargoes from Asia to meet it.

headline: ECB policymakers see a December rate hike followed by a pause, sources say
detail: Sources say new ECB staff estimates show the rise in bond yields reducing growth by a cumulative 100bp and inflation by 90bp over 2027-28 compared with the September baseline.

headline: US 4-week bill auction sells $115bn at 3.91% high yield, with bid-to-cover at 3.1
detail: The US Treasury's 4-week bill sale cleared at a high yield of 3.91%, compared with 3.945% at the previous auction. Bid-to-cover was 3.1, up from 2.820, and 16.96% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

headline: Trump says Vance's outreach to Iran was about helping it obtain medical supplies
detail: US President Trump says Vice President Vance's contact with Iran was about medical supplies, Reuters reports. US media had reported that Vance wrote to Iran's top security official to revive peace talks.

headline: Russia is set to extend its diesel export ban to the end of the year, sources say
detail: Sources say Russia is preparing to keep its ban on diesel exports in place until the end of the year. The report gives no market reaction.

headline: US and Hungary sign a pipeline framework agreement, Hungary's foreign minister says
detail: Hungary's foreign minister said the US and Hungary have signed an agreement on what is being called the 'Trump Peace Pipeline Framework'. No further terms were given.

headline: Japan to start scaling back gasoline subsidies from December, PM Takaichi says
detail: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the government will raise its target pump price for gasoline by 5 yen per litre each month from December into the spring. She said the aim is to contain the growing cost of fuel oil subsidies, Reuters reports.

headline: UK public's long-term inflation expectations ease to 4.0% in October from 4.3%, Citi/YouGov survey shows
detail: The Citi/YouGov survey puts the UK public's long-term inflation expectations at 4.0% in October, down from 4.3% in September.

headline: UK public's year-ahead inflation expectations fall to 4.2% in October from 4.5%, Citi/YouGov survey shows
detail: The Citi/YouGov survey shows the public's year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.2% in October, down from 4.5% in September. Citi economists said there was no obvious explanation for the fall and that they were wary of reading it as more than normal volatility.

headline: EU states reaffirm accelerated release of 42.6 million barrels of oil stocks, half of it diesel, says Commissioner Jorgensen
detail: EU Energy Commissioner Jorgensen says member states have recommitted to an accelerated release of 42.6 million barrels from oil stocks, and half of the releases in the coming months will be diesel. He says the EU does not expect problems with oil and gas supply security but that citizens are struggling to pay their bills.

headline: Federal Reserve bids for US 7-year notes come to $4.9bn
detail: A market news account reported that the Federal Reserve's bids for US 7-year notes came to $4.9bn.

headline: Saudi civil defence issues danger alerts for Riyadh, Al Kharj and Najran
detail: Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority warned of potential danger in Najran, then in Riyadh and Al Kharj, in two alerts minutes apart. It gave no details of the threat, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: UK welfare bill will not fall during this parliament, according to a market headline
detail: A market news feed reported at 17:00 GMT that the UK welfare bill will not come down this parliament; the post did not name a source. Earlier, ministers said the welfare bill needs to fall.

headline: US $44bn 7-year note auction stops on the screws at 4.894%, with bid-to-cover at 2.46
detail: The high yield of 4.894% matched the when-issued level, against 5.085% at the previous auction, and bid-to-cover rose from 2.420. Indirect bidders took 57.77%, direct bidders 32.82% and primary dealers 9.41%.

headline: Iranian media report Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Aramco
detail: Fars News reported that Yemen's Houthi-run army had targeted Saudi Aramco in a broad wave of missile attacks, and other Iranian outlets carried similar reports. Saudi civil defence separately said the danger had passed in Najran city.

headline: Saudi civil defence lifts danger alerts for Riyadh, Al Kharj and Najran
detail: Saudi civil defence said the danger had passed in Riyadh, Al Kharj and Najran. It had issued the alerts earlier, after reports of Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Aramco.

headline: Trump says the Federal Reserve is reluctant to cut interest rates
detail: US President Trump said the Fed dislikes cutting interest rates, according to a market headline. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf says talks can progress only once mediators accept Iran's seven conditions
detail: Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran has set out its conditions to mediators many times and that pressure combined with incentives will not work on Iran. He said progress depends on all seven conditions being agreed.

headline: Dallas Fed trimmed mean PCE inflation rises to 2.8% annualised in September from 2.0% in August
detail: The Dallas Fed's trimmed mean PCE price index rose at a 2.8% annualised rate in September, compared with 2.0% in August.

headline: Putin says Russia is ready for war but does not want one, and backs steps to restore relations with European countries
detail: Russian President Putin was speaking about his call with the leaders of Norway and Finland, who he said had made clear they were not representing the EU. He also said there would be no winners if things went too far, and that Russia does not want a Strait of Hormuz-type situation to arise in the Baltic Sea.

headline: Trump says US military operations against Iran are going very well and repeats that the conflict will end very soon
detail: US President Trump made the remarks on 29 October. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Trump says the US had to strike Iran to stop it obtaining a nuclear weapon
detail: US President Trump said military action against Iran was needed to prevent it from acquiring a nuclear weapon. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Centre for Social Justice says a £33bn rise in UK benefits spending from 2027 to 2032 would offset frozen tax threshold gains
detail: Analysis by the Centre for Social Justice, reported by City AM, finds that the £33bn increase in benefits spending between 2027 and 2032 would broadly match the rise in projected receipts from frozen income tax thresholds.

headline: Trump says the US is working with Venezuela to produce millions of barrels of oil for the US
detail: US President Trump said the US is working with Venezuela on oil production for the US, citing millions of barrels. He gave no timetable or further detail.

headline: Trump pledges $5,000 payment to every adult US citizen if Republicans win the House and Senate, at a cost of about $1tn
detail: Trump puts the cost of the proposed $5,000 payment at about $1 trillion and says tariff revenue would help pay for it. He says recipients would have to spend the payments in the US.

headline: Reuters says Chancellor Healey's first Budget passes with little market reaction, though some details leaked beforehand
detail: Reuters reports that markets barely moved on Chancellor John Healey's first Budget. It contrasts this with the leaks, U-turns and bond market jitters seen around earlier budgets, while noting that this one was not entirely free of leaks.

headline: US is planning to strike Iran after next week's elections, Newsmax reports, citing officials
detail: Newsmax, citing unnamed officials, reports that the US plans strikes on Iran after next week's US elections. The batch gives no market reaction.

headline: Trump says Canada has been treating the US very well lately, amid the two countries' tariff dispute
detail: Reuters reports that US President Trump told a rally on Thursday that Canada has recently been treating the US very nicely. The US has been in a tariff war with Canada.

headline: Top US Middle East commander briefs Trump in person on Iran military options as US weighs resuming major combat, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials and others with direct knowledge, says the commander briefed Trump at the White House on Thursday. The report describes the in-person visit as rare.

headline: Think-tanks question whether Chancellor Healey's Budget deficit-reduction pledge is credible, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that leading think-tanks see the pledge to cut the deficit as unlikely to be met. They point to pressures on public services and households.

headline: Houthis claim several separate military operations deep inside Saudi territory
