detail: Yemen's Houthi movement says it has carried out a number of distinct military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia. This follows earlier Iranian media reports of Houthi missile attacks aimed at Saudi Aramco.

headline: Houthis say they hit Aramco's Abqaiq site and the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries; Saudi Arabia has not yet confirmed
detail: In statements, Yemen's Houthis said they attacked an Aramco facility at Abqaiq, the Ras Tanura and Rabigh oil refineries, and King Khalid airport in Riyadh and King Fahd airport in Dammam. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation, and no market reaction has been reported.

headline: US Energy Department says companies will borrow 16.75m barrels of crude from the SPR out of 17m offered
detail: The US Energy Department said five companies, including Trafigura, Gunvor and Vitol, are taking loans of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. They will borrow 16.75 million of the 17 million barrels offered.

headline: US Energy Department awards contracts to exchange more than 40m barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve
detail: The US Department of Energy said in a statement that it has awarded contracts for an exchange of more than 40m barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

headline: Greek PM backs continued sanctions on Russia; says Greek shipowners would resume Black Sea trade if safe passage is assured
detail: Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis restated his support for economic sanctions on Russia. He also said Greek shipowners are ready to resume Black Sea trading if safe passage is guaranteed, and urged the EU to send more naval assets to its Aspides mission in the Red Sea.

headline: US bonds rally as a tech share selloff drives broad rotation across markets
detail: A US market wrap reports that bonds rallied on Thursday as a selloff in technology stocks set off a wider rotation. No yield figures were given.

headline: US Q3 GDP growth is the fastest in a year; September PCE inflation rises 0.5%, the largest monthly gain in six months
detail: A market news account reports that US GDP expanded in the third quarter at its quickest pace in a year. September PCE inflation rose 0.5% on the month, the biggest increase in six months.

headline: LGA publishes briefing on the local government measures in the 28 October Autumn Budget
detail: The Local Government Association has released a briefing that summarises the Budget announcements relevant to councils and gives its initial view. The Chancellor delivered the Budget on 28 October 2026.

headline: US Treasury yields fall to seven-week lows as market odds of a December Fed hike ease to 70%
detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell 8.5bp to a seven-week low, and the 2-year yield fell further to 4.5648%, also a seven-week low, in Asian trading. Fed funds futures gained as the implied odds of a December rate rise eased to 70%.

headline: Ukraine pauses strikes on Russian oil refineries after US pressure, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports, citing people with knowledge of the operations, that Ukraine's military has paused strikes on Russian refineries after pressure from President Trump. The pause is expected to last until after the US midterm elections and possibly further into November.

headline: Japanese government bond yields slide, with 10-year at 2.775% and 20-year at 3.620%, ahead of BoJ
detail: The 10-year JGB yield slid to 2.775% and the 20-year to 3.620% in Asian trading as traders waited for the Bank of Japan decision.

headline: Australia Q3 producer prices rise 1.1% q/q, down from 1.3%; September private credit up 0.6%
detail: Australian producer prices rose 1.1% quarter on quarter in Q3, down from 1.3%, and the annual rate held at 3.6%. Private-sector credit rose 0.6% m/m in September against a 0.5% forecast, with housing credit up 0.4%, according to the central bank.

headline: BoJ holds short-term rate at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote; Takata dissents in favour of a rise to 1.5%
detail: The Bank of Japan said underlying inflation is in line with its target, risks to prices are tilted to the upside and it will keep raising rates. Board medians are 2.5% for fiscal 2026 core CPI, 2.7% for fiscal 2027 core-core CPI and 0.7% for fiscal 2026 real GDP growth.

headline: Brent and WTI rise $2 a barrel on growing US-Iran geopolitical risk
detail: Market reports say crude rebounded in Asian trade as doubts grew over the prospects of a peace deal, with both Brent and WTI up $2 a barrel.

headline: Bonds head for their largest monthly gain in nearly three years as Asian tech shares slump on AI spending worries
detail: Reuters says investors moved into safe havens on Friday, with the yen rising and tech stocks falling on worries about returns on AI spending. Japan's 5-year JGB yield fell 5bp to 2.220%, the Nikkei dropped 3% and Taiwan's Taiex 3.5%.

headline: Sterling rises in Asian trade on a hawkish BoE outlook and broad dollar weakness
detail: A market report says sterling gained on expectations of a hawkish Bank of England and a broadly weaker US dollar; no levels were given.

headline: BoJ will speed up ETF sales to about 860bn yen a year from about 330bn yen, starting January 2027
detail: The Bank of Japan says the new pace would take about 43 years to run down its ETF holdings, compared with about 112 years before. With its rate hold, the BoJ also says Japan now faces a risk of inflation overshooting, and that it will weigh the timing and pace of rate rises; dollar/yen was last down 0.37% at 157.115.

headline: BoJ says it will keep raising rates if conditions allow; estimates proposed food tax cut would lower fiscal 2027 core CPI by 1.3pp
detail: Alongside its hold, the Bank of Japan said further rate rises would depend on how the economy and prices develop and named Middle East tensions, AI demand and currency swings as risks. Its projections leave out the proposed food consumption tax cut, which it estimates would lower fiscal 2027 core CPI by 1.3 percentage points and core-core CPI by 1.4 points.

headline: Yen firms and 5-year JGB yield falls 3.5bp to 2.235% after BoJ hold described as hawkish
detail: The yen strengthened against the dollar after the Bank of Japan's decision, which market commentary called a hawkish pause, as attention moved to Governor Ueda. 10-year JGB futures gave back some earlier gains but were still up 0.34 point, and the 5-year JGB yield fell 3.5bp to 2.235%.

headline: Japan finance minister Katayama expects BoJ to work closely with government to reach 2% inflation target
detail: Japan's finance minister Katayama said she expects the Bank of Japan to keep coordinating closely with the government on the 2% inflation target. She declined to comment on the day's BoJ decision.

headline: Japan's 20-year JGB yield falls 6.5bp to 3.605% after BoJ decision
detail: The 20-year Japanese government bond yield dropped 6.5bp to 3.605% following the Bank of Japan's decision to hold rates. Market reports also said the yen strengthened and the Nikkei fell further after the decision.

headline: BoJ raises its inflation forecast while keeping rates on hold
detail: Reuters reports that the Bank of Japan revised up its inflation forecast on Friday and said again that it was ready to keep raising borrowing costs to head off growing inflation risks.

headline: ECB's Simkus says risk of energy spillover has risen but second-round effects are not yet visible
detail: ECB Governing Council member Simkus said the likelihood of energy prices spilling over into wider inflation has increased. He added that second-round effects are not yet visible.

headline: Sterling moves above $1.3350 in early trade
detail: A market report said sterling rose past 1.3350 against the dollar but stayed below its 100-day moving average.

headline: French GDP shrinks 0.1% q/q in preliminary Q3 estimate, below 0.1% forecast; consumer spending falls 0.5% m/m
detail: Preliminary French GDP fell 0.1% q/q against a forecast rise of 0.1% and 0.0% previously, and was down 0.1% y/y against a forecast 0.3% and 0.5% previously. Consumer spending fell 0.5% m/m against a forecast rise of 0.1%, matching the previous -0.5%.

headline: BoJ Governor Ueda expects Japan's economy to keep growing moderately; puts mid- to long-term inflation expectations at around 2%
detail: The BoJ Governor made the remarks after the bank kept its short-term rate at 1.25%. He said medium- to long-term inflation expectations are around 2%.

headline: French GDP falls 0.1% y/y in preliminary Q3 estimate against 0.3% forecast; September consumer spending down 0.4% y/y
detail: The annual GDP figure compares with growth of 0.5% in the previous quarter. Consumer spending fell 0.4% y/y in September, against a forecast rise of 0.4% and a previous reading of 0.8%.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation is near the 2% goal and financial conditions remain accommodative; flags FX, AI and Middle East risks
detail: At his post-decision press conference, Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said rates will rise further depending on economic, inflation and financial conditions, and that policy adjustments depend on outlook risks. He also said the BoJ will keep J-REIT sales at the current pace.

headline: Ueda says BoJ will keep raising its policy rate as activity, prices and financial conditions evolve; credits government measures
detail: At his post-decision press conference, Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said government measures had boosted economic activity and helped bring the 2% price goal within reach. He also said core CPI inflation is broadly in line with the 2% target and is expected to stay near that level.

headline: 30 of 32 economists in a poll expect the RBA to raise its cash rate to 4.85% on 3 November
detail: In a poll of economists, 30 of the 32 surveyed said the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise its cash rate to 4.85% at its 3 November decision.

headline: Poll: 27 of 29 economists say a 4.85% RBA cash rate will be the peak for the year
detail: A poll of economists finds 27 of 29 expect an RBA cash rate of 4.85% to mark the high point for the year.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says economic and inflation trends will be examined at each meeting, with closer monitoring of risks
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said policymakers will check the data to judge whether underlying inflation is stable and will assess how well inflation expectations align with the 2% target. He added that economic and financial risks need closer monitoring to guide policy.

headline: BoJ's Ueda stops short of declaring the 2% inflation target met; sees overshoot risks little changed from a month ago
detail: At his post-decision press conference, the Bank of Japan Governor said inflation must sit stably and sustainably around 2% before the target is deemed met, and that the BoJ will not make a formal announcement when it is achieved. He added that the risk of inflation exceeding the target is not significantly higher than a month ago, and that whether wage growth is sustainable remains an important consideration.

headline: French finance minister Lescure says economy has stalled in 2026 and calls for a budget to support confidence
detail: France's finance minister said the economy came to a standstill in 2026 and that the country needs a budget to boost confidence and growth. His remarks came after preliminary Q3 GDP data showed a contraction.

headline: German import prices rise 10.4% y/y in September, above 10.3% forecast; up 2.1% m/m
detail: German import prices rose 10.4% from a year earlier, against a 10.3% forecast and 8.3% previously. On the month they rose 2.1%, against a 2% forecast and 1.0% previously.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says inflation expectations remain only weakly anchored around 2%; declines to discuss revising government accord
detail: At his post-decision news conference, BoJ Governor Ueda said inflation expectations are still weakly anchored around 2%. He would not say whether the accord between the BoJ and the government needs revising.

headline: Nationwide UK house prices flat m/m in October against -0.2% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.5%
detail: Nationwide's October index shows UK house prices unchanged on the month, after -0.2% in September, against a -0.2% forecast. Annual growth (NSA) eases to 0.5% from 0.8%, below the 0.6% forecast.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says a rate rise will be considered at every meeting, the next one included
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said the bank will weigh a rate increase at each policy meeting, including the next one. He spoke after the BoJ held its short-term rate at 1.25%.

headline: China's most-active 30-year government bond futures contract drops 1.00% intraday to 117.34 yuan
detail: The most-active TL contract on 30-year Chinese government bonds fell 1.00% during the session to 117.34 yuan.

headline: BoJ's Ueda expects faster ETF sales to have only a limited market impact; says upside risks need an appropriate response
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda spoke after the decision to speed up ETF sales. He said the faster pace should have only a limited effect on markets and that the bank must respond appropriately to upside risks.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says he wants to bring the policy rate to a neutral level in an appropriate way
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said this at his press conference after the BoJ held its short-term rate at 1.25%.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the policy rate is still below neutral and will be adjusted at the right time to stop risks materialising
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said at his post-decision press conference that work remains because the policy rate is below the neutral level. He also said rate adjustments would be timed to prevent risks from materialising.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the BoJ is watching spring wage talks closely, which must make 2% inflation built in
detail: Speaking after the BoJ's policy decision, Governor Ueda said the bank is watching next spring's wage negotiations closely and that annual wage talks need to reach a point where 2% inflation is built in. He added that the BoJ still needs to watch whether the price trend becomes anchored.

headline: French producer prices rise 1.7% m/m in September, up from 1.0% the previous month
detail: French PPI rose 1.7% month on month, compared with 1.0% in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

headline: French flash October HICP rises 3.8% y/y, above 3.6% forecast and up from 3.4% in September
detail: France's preliminary October harmonised inflation came in at 3.8% y/y and 0.4% m/m, against forecasts of 3.6% and 0.3%. National CPI rose 3.4% y/y against a 3.3% forecast (previously 3.1%), and 0.4% m/m against a 0.2% forecast (previously -0.3%).

headline: ECB's Dolenc says the energy shock is not yet feeding broader price pressures but warns inflation may stay above 2% for years
detail: ECB Governing Council member Dolenc said the energy shock had not yet spread into wider price pressures, but that higher energy prices risk more persistent inflation. He added that inflation could remain above 2% in the coming years.

headline: Spanish flash October HICP eases to 4.9% y/y, in line with forecast and down from 5.0%; up 0.5% m/m
detail: Spain's flash October HICP rose 4.9% y/y, matching the 4.9% forecast, after 5.0% the month before. On the month it rose 0.5%, also in line with forecast, after 0.6% previously.

headline: Spanish Q3 GDP grows 0.6% q/q in line with forecast, slowing from 0.7%; annual growth picks up to 2.7%
detail: Spain's preliminary third-quarter estimate shows 0.6% growth on the quarter, as forecast and down from 0.7% previously. Annual growth is 2.7%, matching the forecast and up from 2.6%.

headline: Spanish flash October national CPI holds at 4.9% y/y as forecast; monthly rise of 0.6% is below the 0.7% forecast
detail: Spain's flash national CPI for October is unchanged at 4.9% y/y, in line with forecast. On the month, prices rise 0.6%, against a 0.7% forecast and 0.3% previously.

headline: Germany's Merz says he is working to end the Iran war quickly, citing its heavy impact on Europe
detail: German Chancellor Merz said the Iran war is having a major impact on Europe and that this is why he is holding intensive talks on his Asia trip. He also said the US is shifting its foreign policy and Germany must do likewise.

headline: Dutch Q3 GDP grows 0.6% q/q, above 0.3% forecast; annual growth picks up to 2.1%
detail: Preliminary figures show Dutch GDP grew 0.6% q/q in the third quarter, against a 0.3% forecast and matching the previous quarter's 0.6%. Annual growth came in at 2.1%, compared with a forecast of 1.3% and 1.6% previously.

headline: Saxony's October CPI slows to 2.8% y/y from 3.4%, with prices down 0.2% m/m
detail: Figures for the German state of Saxony show annual inflation easing to 2.8% in October from 3.4% the previous month. Prices fell 0.2% m/m, after a 0.6% rise previously; no forecast was given.

headline: ECB's Rehn says growth and inflation outlook remains highly uncertain and upside inflation risks are still elevated
detail: ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn said the outlook for growth and inflation is still very uncertain and that risks of higher inflation remain clearly elevated. He added that policymakers need to stay vigilant about second-round effects.

headline: German unemployment rises by 4k in October, below 5k forecast; jobless rate holds at 6.4% as expected
detail: German seasonally adjusted unemployment rose by 4k, against a 5k forecast and 12k previously. The unemployment rate was 6.4%, in line with the forecast and unchanged from the previous month.

headline: Japan's Katayama says the budget process will consider how much surplus the BoJ's ETF sales produce and how to handle it
detail: Japan's finance minister Katayama said the government would consider the specific amount of surplus from the BoJ's ETF sales, and how to treat it, when drawing up the budget.

headline: German Q3 GDP grows 0.2% q/q, above 0.1% forecast; annual growth picks up to 1.2%
detail: Germany's preliminary Q3 GDP rose 0.2% on the quarter against a 0.1% estimate, after 0.3% in the previous quarter. Annual growth came in at 1.2%, above the 1.1% estimate and up from 1.0%.

headline: Bavaria's October CPI slows to 2.8% y/y from 3.2%
detail: Annual inflation in the German state of Bavaria eased to 2.8% in October from 3.2% the previous month.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Russia, the US and Ukraine have agreed to resume trilateral negotiations
detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the three countries had agreed to restart trilateral talks, responding to media reports about Europe's possible involvement in the negotiations.

headline: Italian Q3 GDP flat q/q in preliminary estimate, below 0.1% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.8%
detail: Italy's preliminary third-quarter GDP was unchanged on the quarter, against a 0.1% forecast and after 0.2% growth previously. Annual growth eased to 0.8% from 1.0%.

headline: North Rhine-Westphalia's October CPI slows to 2.7% y/y from 3.3%
detail: Annual inflation in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's most populous state, slowed to 2.7% in October from 3.3% in September, ahead of the national flash estimate.

headline: Kremlin says European negotiators' role in US-Ukraine-Russia talks has not been discussed; Putin open to contacts
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said there had been no discussion of European negotiators joining the trilateral talks between the US, Ukraine and Russia. He added that Putin is open to contacts with everyone in pursuit of a peaceful settlement of the conflict in Ukraine.

headline: PBOC sets its overnight reverse repo rate at 1.25%; open market operation changes take effect 2 November
detail: The People's Bank of China has set its overnight reverse repo rate at 1.25%. It says the changes to its open market operations take effect on 2 November.

headline: EU carbon price climbs to €90 a tonne, its highest level since January
detail: A market commentator reported that EU carbon allowances reached €90 per tonne on Friday morning, the first time at that level since January.

headline: Merz to pass Asian partners' concerns over EU 'Made in Europe' protectionism risk on to Brussels
detail: Reuters reported that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Friday he would take to Brussels concerns from key Asian trading partners that the EU's Made in Europe initiatives could become a new form of protectionism.

headline: UK Decision Maker Panel puts firms' year-ahead CPI expectations at 3.4% in October
detail: The October Decision Maker Panel survey of UK businesses shows firms expect CPI inflation of 3.4% over the year ahead.

headline: ECB's Nagel sees no significant second-round effects yet but says a price rise in the coming weeks cannot be ruled out
detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel said the decision to hold rates had not been easy. He also said medium-term inflation expectations must stay firmly anchored.

headline: ECB's Nagel says the ECB will act decisively if needed
detail: Bundesbank President and ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said the central bank is prepared to take decisive action if required. He spoke after earlier saying that a price rise in the coming weeks cannot be ruled out.

headline: BoE survey finds no sign of an inflation premium in pay awards and limited pass-through of cost pressures to prices
detail: A Bank of England survey reports no evidence that pay awards include an inflation premium. It also finds that firms are passing only a limited share of cost pressures through to prices.

headline: Eurozone Q3 GDP grows 0.4% q/q in flash estimate, above 0.2% forecast; annual growth picks up to 1.3%
detail: The preliminary flash estimate shows euro area GDP up 0.4% q/q, against a 0.2% forecast and down from 0.6% previously. Annual growth is 1.3%, above the 1.1% forecast and up from 1.2%.

headline: Italian flash October HICP jumps to 5.6% y/y, well above 4.6% forecast and up from 4.2%
detail: Italy's preliminary October HICP rose 1.2% m/m against a 0.4% forecast. National CPI rose 5.4% y/y against a 4.6% forecast, and 0.9% m/m against a 0.1% forecast.

headline: ECB's Panetta says the price outlook is worsening and further rate rises could prove necessary
detail: ECB Governing Council member Panetta said inflation is expected to stay above 2% for several quarters and core inflation could rise more sharply early next year. He also said the rise in long-term yields must be taken into account as policy is calibrated, and that the ECB can adjust its stance quickly if the international situation improves or financial tensions weigh on inflation.

headline: ECB's Kocher says inflation risks have risen and action will be needed if the situation does not improve quickly
detail: ECB Governing Council member Martin Kocher said inflation risks have clearly increased. He added that neither moving too early nor sitting and waiting would secure price stability.

headline: Kremlin calls the Oleshky situation an isolated case that should not be applied to the wider Ukraine settlement process
detail: The Kremlin said the incident in Oleshky should not be taken as representative of the overall peace process in Ukraine.

headline: Qatari mediators are in Tehran to discuss the latest US proposal for peace talks, Axios reports
detail: Axios reports that Qatari mediators are in Tehran for talks on the latest US peace talks proposal. The report gives no further detail.

headline: BoE surveys show firms expect to raise pay by around 3.5% in 2027, similar to current rates
detail: Bank of England business surveys released on Friday show firms expect pay growth of around 3.5% next year, broadly in line with current settlements, Reuters reports.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Moscow has noted Zelenskyy's stated willingness to discuss territorial issues
detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russian officials had heard the Ukrainian president's remarks about being open to talks on territory, following agreement to resume trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia negotiations.

headline: China's Xi calls the EU a partner and says differences can be resolved through equal dialogue
detail: Chinese President Xi Jinping said China sees the EU as a partner, according to state broadcaster CCTV. He added that the two sides can always resolve their differences and problems if they keep to that partnership and to equal dialogue.

headline: US Centcom commander says the Strait of Hormuz transit route has been cleared of sea mines
detail: The commander of US Central Command said the transit route through the Strait of Hormuz had been cleared of sea mines, and that 1.5 billion barrels of crude had been exported through the strait since the summer. He added that he saw no IRGC presence when he visited the strait earlier this week.

headline: Kremlin says European representatives will need to take part in Ukraine settlement talks at some point
detail: The Kremlin said European participation in talks on a peaceful settlement in Ukraine will be required at some stage. No market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB's Makhlouf says keeping rates on hold does not mean the ECB has finished
detail: ECB Governing Council member Makhlouf said the decision to hold rates should not be read as a sign that the ECB is done.

headline: Trump says the Iran war will end very soon, one way or another
detail: US President Trump said the war with Iran would be over very soon, without giving further detail. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says Iran must make a deal and the US needs a guarantee that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon
detail: In a KCMO radio interview, US President Trump said he expects the Iran war to be wrapped up soon. He also said it is unclear who to talk to on the Iranian side because many of its leaders are gone.

headline: Trump was briefed on Thursday on possible military options in Iran, Fox reports
detail: Fox reports that US President Trump received a briefing on Thursday on potential military options against Iran.

headline: ECB's Makhlouf calls the current inflation situation uncomfortable
detail: ECB Governing Council member Makhlouf said the current inflation situation is uncomfortable.

headline: Kremlin says Kyiv is disregarding Trump's calls to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries
detail: Kremlin aide Ushakov said on Friday that Ukraine has not heeded Trump's repeated demands to stop attacking Russian refineries.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Kyiv probably could not have attacked Russian oil refineries without European backing
detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Ukraine was unlikely to have carried out strikes on Russian oil refineries without support from Europe.

headline: Iran's IRGC navy says it stopped two oil tankers south of the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said on Friday that two oil tankers were involved in incidents and were stopped south of the Strait of Hormuz. It said the tankers had ignored radio warnings and tried to use what it called an unauthorised route through the waterway, Reuters reports.

headline: Exxon CEO Woods says Hormuz crude flows are nearing pre-war levels and calls diesel the key crunch point
detail: In a CNBC interview, ExxonMobil chief executive Darren Woods said crude moving through the Strait of Hormuz is getting back close to pre-war levels. He named diesel as the main pressure point, saying demand remains high despite available capacity.

headline: Iranian state media says a supertanker exploded after striking a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran's IRIB News said the supertanker hit a mine about an hour before its report, on what it called an unauthorised route through the strait, and Fars also reported the mine strike. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US Q3 employment cost index rises 0.8%, in line with consensus; wages and salaries slow to 0.7% from 0.9%
detail: US Q3 employment costs rose 0.8%, down from 0.9% in Q2 and matching consensus. Wages and salaries rose 0.7% and benefit costs 0.9%, after 0.9% and 1.0% respectively in Q2.

headline: Iran's IRGC says three oil tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Friday; burning supertanker carrying over 2m barrels abandoned
detail: The IRGC says the latest vessel was the third oil tanker to strike a mine on Friday, and Iranian state broadcaster IRIB says a supertanker holding more than 2 million barrels has been abandoned and is on fire at the mouth of the Strait. Separately, the FT reports that attackers in a speedboat hit a tanker with limpet mines on Thursday, the first such incident since 2019.

headline: Canadian GDP flat m/m in August against 0.2% forecast; StatCan flash estimate points to a 0.1% fall in September
detail: Statistics Canada said August GDP was unchanged on the month, missing the 0.2% forecast, and July was also flat. Its flash estimate suggests GDP most likely fell 0.1% in September.

headline: Russia's Novak says Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after a pause, hitting three refineries and a chemical plant
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Ukrainian drones attacked three Russian oil refineries and one petrochemical complex, with minor damage at one site. He said the attacks resumed after a period of pause.

headline: ECB asks EU leaders to begin the search for a successor to chief economist Lane
detail: The ECB has asked EU leaders to start the process of finding a successor to Philip Lane on its Executive Board.

headline: US Treasury yields hold most of their losses after US data; 10-year down 6.22bp at 4.927%, 2-year down 7.05bp at 4.586%
detail: US Treasury yields mostly held their declines after the release of US economic data. The 10-year yield was last 6.22bp lower at 4.927% and the 2-year yield 7.05bp lower at 4.586%.

headline: Russia plans to extend its diesel export ban, with some exceptions, to the end of January
detail: Interfax reports that Russia plans to extend the diesel export ban, with certain exceptions, until the end of January. TASS cites Deputy Prime Minister Novak as saying Russia plans to export 510,000 tonnes of diesel in October and 2.15m tonnes in November.

headline: German flash October CPI slows to 2.8% y/y from 3.3%, below 3% forecast; HICP also 2.8% against 3.1% forecast
detail: Germany's preliminary October CPI fell 0.2% m/m against a forecast 0.1% rise, after 0.6% in September. Flash HICP dropped 0.1% m/m against a forecast 0.1% rise, and its annual rate slowed from 3.3%.

headline: Kremlin says Ukrainian refinery strikes will not derail upcoming Ukraine talks and will not be raised in Abu Dhabi
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said Russia will not bring up Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries at the upcoming Abu Dhabi meeting. Interfax reported the Kremlin as saying the strikes do not put the negotiations in doubt.

headline: OBR chair Haskel says revised ONS productivity figures leave the UK productivity puzzle unresolved
detail: OBR Chair Jonathan Haskel made the remarks about the ONS's revised productivity numbers at a Resolution Foundation event on 29 October, the think tank reports.

headline: Fed's Barkin says the Fed's direction of travel is clear and the open question is the pace, with a gradual approach signalled
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said in a SiriusXM interview that the Fed has signalled a gradual approach. He added that the Fed will see what it learns over the coming period.

headline: Fed's Barkin says AI investment is driving demand-side inflation that the Fed can lean against, and cost pressures are hitting firms
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the AI investment surge has strained supply chains and that many cost pressures are hitting US businesses. He said years of elevated inflation make it easier for firms to justify price rises, and that consumer spending has held up surprisingly well despite fairly flat incomes.

headline: Fed's Barkin says business demand stays solid, with weakness only in housing and non-profits, and firms plan to pass on price rises
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said businesses describe broad cost pressures and plans to raise prices, adding that consumer spending has been surprisingly resilient given broadly flat incomes. He made the remarks at a business briefing, which has now ended.

headline: US Chicago PMI falls to 55.3 in October, below 56.0 forecast and down from 58.8
detail: MNI's Chicago Business Barometer came in at 55.3 for October, short of the 56.0 consensus, after 58.8 in September.

headline: Chevron CEO Wirth says crude oil and refined product prices are elevated worldwide
detail: Chevron chief executive Mike Wirth said in a CNBC interview that prices for both crude oil and refined products are running high around the world.

headline: China's commerce ministry opposes US FCC curbs on Chinese testing labs and says further countermeasures will follow if the US continues
detail: China's commerce ministry says the FCC vote restricting Chinese testing labs breaches a consensus agreed between the two heads of state and seriously disrupts the stability of global supply chains. It says Beijing had repeatedly proposed talks on a mutual recognition pact but the US stance was extremely negative, and that China will take further countermeasures if the US continues.

headline: OBR estimates £3bn-£4bn a year in extra grant needed to return council housebuilding to 1980s levels
detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility estimates that returning council housebuilding to 1980s levels could need £3bn to £4bn a year of extra grant funding on top of SAHP money, Inside Housing reports.

headline: Exxon estimates half of Russia's refining capacity is offline; CEO sees global refining starting to recover next year, possibly later
detail: Exxon estimates that half of Russia's refining capacity is out of action. Its chief executive says global refining capacity could start to recover next year but warns it may take longer.

headline: US officials say Thursday's Iran meeting focused on a blockade and economic pressure, not strikes, Axios reports
detail: Axios cites several US officials as saying more than 20 people attended Thursday's meeting on Iran, which discussed a blockade and economic pressure at length. The officials said strikes remain possible straight after the midterms.

headline: Exxon says UAE oil production is back in line with historical output
detail: Exxon said on Friday that output in the UAE has recovered to levels consistent with its historical production.

headline: Russia's Novak says attacks on oil refineries will hurt diesel supplies to the global market
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said strikes on Russian oil refineries will have a negative effect on global diesel supply. He had earlier said Ukraine had resumed such strikes.

headline: Fitch says the UK budget keeps broad policy continuity but leaves a large delivery challenge, and still expects significant fiscal slippage
detail: Fitch Ratings says the UK fiscal consolidation plan becomes much harder to deliver from 2027 and expects significant slippage against spending plans. It also sees moderately more policy risk as the next general election approaches.

headline: Russia's Novak says October oil output is above September's, with December diesel export plan due at the end of November
detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak says Russian oil production in October was higher than in September. He adds that Russia will set its plan for December diesel exports at the end of November.

headline: European Commission proposes Council approval of the remaining €45bn Ukraine loan tranche for 2027
detail: The European Commission has proposed that the EU Council approve the remaining €45bn of the Ukraine loan for 2027.

headline: Resolution Foundation puts real per-person public services spending growth at 1.7% a year from 2023-24 to 2028-29
detail: In its Budget analysis, the Resolution Foundation says day-to-day spending is rising moderately in this Parliament. It puts real per-person growth in public services spending at 1.7% a year between 2023-24 and 2028-29, close to the two latest periods under Conservative governments.

headline: Fed's Daly says AI is important to how policymakers think about policy in the near and medium term
detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said artificial intelligence is a significant factor in how the Fed approaches policy over the near and medium term.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Russia and the US are coordinating dates for a three-way meeting in Abu Dhabi in November
detail: Ushakov said Russia has sent the US its thoughts on dates for the trilateral talks with Ukraine and is waiting for a reply. He said the meeting will be held in Abu Dhabi in November.

headline: ECB's Lane says AI is lifting euro area activity, with AI-related price pressures visible but limited effect on headline inflation
detail: ECB chief economist Lane said artificial intelligence is driving growth and credit trends and could significantly raise productivity, and that AI companies are more sensitive to monetary policy. He said AI-related price pressures can be seen but have had limited impact on headline inflation.

headline: ECB's Lane says AI adoption is still at a fairly early stage, and the scale and timing of its economy-wide impact are very uncertain
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane added this point to his earlier remarks on AI and the euro area economy. He did not mention interest rates.

headline: Fed's Musalem says the Fed will raise rates again soon, and earlier hikes lower the risk to the wider economy
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said inflation is still elevated with risks tilted to the upside, policy and financial conditions remain accommodative, and gradual moves are better than sudden ones. He also said higher expected policy rates are driving elevated long-term bond yields, while inflation expectations are steady and the economy and labour market are robust.

headline: Canada and EU agree to define by 2027 summit an 'ever-closer association' for Canada that stops short of membership
detail: The commitment is in a joint statement issued at the EU-Canada summit. The statement was signed by Prime Minister Carney, European Council President Costa and Commission President von der Leyen.

headline: Canada and EU sign political agreement on digital trade deal as Carney launches strategic alliance
detail: Canada and the European Union signed a political agreement on an EU-Canada digital trade agreement and agreed a strategic alliance, leaving the definition of their new relationship until 2027. Canadian Prime Minister Carney called it a historic day and said the world is becoming more dangerous and divided.

headline: Carney says Canada aims to be the EU's first associate member, with talks to be concluded at June European Council meetings
detail: Canada's Prime Minister Carney said he has accepted European Council President Costa's invitation to attend the June meetings to conclude negotiations, and that the substance, scale and scope of the new form of membership will be set over the coming months. He described it as the deepest possible partnership short of accession, and said a new Canada-EU competition agreement is being concluded alongside the digital trade deal.

headline: Canada seeks to take part in the EU's €90bn support loan for Ukraine, joint statement says
detail: A joint Canada-EU statement says Canada is set to contribute to the EU's €90bn loan to Ukraine. The two sides also launched a new alliance that includes deals on minerals and AI.

headline: Fed's Musalem says public understanding of how the Fed thinks matters, and policy rules are useful for monetary policy
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem also said that communication is not necessarily the same thing as forward guidance. He made the remarks in further comments on Friday afternoon.

headline: Budget includes a fiscal devolution roadmap promising fundamental change to mayoral funding, Institute for Government says
detail: In a commentary piece, the Institute for Government calls the roadmap the main reform in the budget. It says the roadmap sets out a fundamental change in how mayors are funded.

headline: Fed's Musalem says he is focused on preventing second-round inflation effects, such as in services
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said his focus is on stopping inflation from feeding through in second-round effects, naming the service sector as an example.

headline: UK approves a 2 gigawatt undersea power cable
detail: A market news account reported that the UK has given approval for a 2 gigawatt undersea electricity cable. The post did not give further details.

headline: Von der Leyen says the EU and Canada have agreed that Canada will take part in the EU's loan for Ukraine
detail: European Commission President von der Leyen said Canada's participation in the EU loan for Ukraine has been agreed. Earlier, a joint statement said Canada wanted to join the €90bn support loan.

headline: Carney says Canada will contribute €500m to the EU's Ukraine support loan
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a €500m contribution to the EU's loan for Ukraine. This follows the earlier EU-Canada agreement on Canada joining the loan.

headline: Carney says Canada's alliance with the EU will make its financial sector more competitive
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the new strategic alliance with the EU will boost the competitiveness of the financial sector. He spoke after Canada and the EU signed a political agreement on a digital trade deal.

headline: Fed's Logan says the Fed needs at least two more 25bp rate hikes, after which a pause would be reasonable
detail: Dallas Fed President Logan said policy should move gradually and stay moderately restrictive, and called it unacceptable for inflation not to return to the 2% target. She said a pause after 50bp of increases would be reasonable, that growth is robust, that the labour market is balanced and may be tightening slightly, and that higher long-term rates have weighed on the economy less than expected.

headline: Pakistan's military says it is cautiously optimistic about its Iran-US mediation
detail: The Pakistani military spokesman spoke to Reuters on Friday in his first interview since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week.

headline: Gilts rally with core bonds in a risk-off move as sterling holds steady
detail: A UK market commentator reports that gilts are rallying alongside other core government bonds amid risk-off trading on Friday, with sterling steady. No yield levels were given.

headline: WTI crude futures settle up 2.08% at $104.12 a barrel
detail: NYMEX December WTI crude futures settled $2.12 higher at $104.12 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.7905 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.3120 a gallon.

headline: US orders non-emergency government staff to leave Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks on airports and infrastructure
detail: The US embassy in Riyadh said on Friday that non-emergency government employees and their families have been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia, effective 23 October, because of safety risks, Reuters reports. The embassy cited Houthi attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure.

headline: Brent crude futures settle up 2.4% at $117.64 a barrel
detail: Brent crude futures settled $2.76 higher at $117.64 a barrel, a gain of 2.4%.

headline: US Treasury report finds the blockade and sanctions are crippling Iran's economy, Axios reports
detail: Axios cites a US Treasury report saying the US blockade and sanctions are inflicting severe damage on Iran's economy. The report adds to the running US-Iran pressure campaign story.

headline: Qatari mediators hold 12 hours of talks in Tehran aimed at securing a US-Iran deal, Axios reports
detail: Axios reports that Qatari negotiators spent 12 hours in talks in Tehran trying to unlock a deal between the US and Iran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: White House pushes back hearing on mortgage fraud allegations against Fed Governor Cook to December, Hassett says
detail: Kevin Hassett, President Trump's top economic adviser, said the White House hearing into mortgage fraud allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has been delayed until December, Reuters reports. On Friday, Cook's lawyers would not confirm that any date had been agreed.

headline: Canadian dollar reaches six-week high against the US dollar as higher oil prices support bets on more Bank of Canada tightening
detail: Reuters reports the Canadian dollar extended its monthly gain on Friday as the oil price jump lifted expectations that the Bank of Canada will tighten further. The move outweighed weaker-than-expected Canadian GDP data.

headline: Fourth tanker explodes after striking a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's IRGC says via state broadcaster
detail: Iran's IRGC, as reported by Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, says a fourth tanker exploded after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC says the tanker had ignored warnings not to use an 'unauthorised route' through the strait.

headline: Trump says talks with Iran are continuing and the US is in no hurry
detail: US President Trump says talks with Iran are ongoing and that the US has time. He also says the US is spending very little money on Iran.

headline: Trump says the US is not considering lifting sanctions on Russia's sovereign wealth fund
detail: US President Trump says lifting sanctions on Russia's sovereign wealth fund is not under consideration.

headline: Lavrov says Russia's stance is unchanged ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Moscow's position had not changed before the negotiations in Abu Dhabi. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Poland's Sikorski calls for a Black Sea ceasefire and ties any Russian energy sales to Europe to a fair end to the Ukraine war
detail: Polish Foreign Minister Sikorski said G20 members discussed food security, freedom of navigation and energy. He said Poland wants a Black Sea ceasefire so Ukrainian and Russian food supplies can be shipped out, and that the war in Ukraine must end fairly if Russia wants to sell energy to Europe again.

headline: Lavrov says core US-Russia issues remain unresolved as sanctions stay in place and arms keep flowing to Ukraine
detail: Russia's foreign minister said sanctions are still in force and weapons are still being supplied to Ukraine. He also said it is unclear what Ukraine will bring to new settlement talks, and called Zelenskiy's references to long-range strikes unhelpful.

headline: US approves $2.1bn sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine
detail: The Financial Times reports that the US has approved a $2.1bn sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine. President Zelenskyy had accused the Trump administration of holding up the weapons as relations between the two countries worsened.

headline: US-Iran talks make positive progress and mediators work to close remaining gaps, Axios reports; oil falls more than 1%
detail: Axios cited a diplomat involved in the US-Iran talks as saying talks had progressed positively and mediators were working on the remaining differences. Oil prices were later reported down more than 1% as the Iran-Qatar talks sought to end the US-Iran war.

headline: Trump says the US is very near a trade deal with Canada after Carney reports a good call on trade
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Carney said on Sunday he had a good conversation with President Trump on future trade between the two countries, which have been in a trade war. Trump said a deal with Canada was very near and also said he had held a productive discussion with Israel's Netanyahu that covered Iran.

headline: Brent and WTI fall a further $2 a barrel in Asian trade as efforts to restart Middle East talks gather pace
detail: Brent and WTI crude were each reported down $2 a barrel early on Monday. The WSJ linked the fall to efforts to get Middle East parties back to negotiations, and Reuters said high oil prices were limiting demand for sovereign bonds as a safe haven.

headline: Japan's Katayama says the US-Japan FX statement still applies and Tokyo will act against disorderly moves
detail: Japan's finance minister Satsuki Katayama said the joint currency statement with the US remains in force and that stable FX markets are crucial. She declined to comment on specific yen levels and said Prime Minister Takaichi sees yen weakness as a problem.

headline: South Korea and Taiwan October manufacturing PMIs fall; Japan's final reading holds at 53.3
detail: S&P Global's October manufacturing PMI fell to 51.3 from 53.9 in South Korea and to 54.9 from 56.7 in Taiwan. Japan's final reading was unchanged from the flash estimate at 53.3.

headline: Brent drops to $109.52 in Asian trade, heading for its lowest level in more than a week; WTI nears $100
detail: Brent was reported down more than $3 at $110.37 a barrel. It then fell nearly 2% more to $109.52, while WTI dropped about 2% towards $100 after earlier sliding more than $3 to $101.11.

headline: US pushes to restore Russian gas flows to Europe through Ukraine as part of a Moscow-Kyiv energy truce, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Washington is seeking to resume Russian gas shipments to Europe via Ukraine. The aim is an energy truce between Russia and Ukraine.

headline: China's RatingDog manufacturing PMI eases to 52.0 in October, above the 51.6 forecast
detail: China's RatingDog manufacturing PMI fell to 52.0 in October from 52.1 in September. The forecast was 51.6.

headline: BoJ says rate rises should ease inflation and support consumption, and notes higher real yields at the long end
detail: The Bank of Japan says underlying inflation has risen to about 2% and is becoming embedded at that level. It also says real interest rates have climbed recently, especially for long and super-long maturities, while median real rates stay low, and that it is watching equity and currency moves as part of a broad review of financial conditions.

headline: ADNOC CEO says Hormuz disruption has taken nearly 1bn barrels out of global inventories
detail: ADNOC's chief executive said disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has drawn global inventories down by nearly 1 billion barrels and the world has used up its available supply reserves. He added that some markets report diesel stocks at their weakest seasonal levels in 35 years.

headline: China's Xi warns against the Middle East and Gulf becoming a battleground for great power rivalry
detail: China's President Xi said, according to state broadcaster CCTV, that China will keep pursuing political and diplomatic settlement of disputes. He also said Beijing is willing to step up dialogue and cooperation with Arab nations to restore regional peace and stability soon.

headline: BoJ Governor Ueda has all but locked in a December rate rise, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda has all but committed to a rate rise in December. The report says investors remain uncertain how much further the BoJ could tighten once rates near neutral.

headline: Goldman Sachs now expects a 25bp BoE rate rise in February 2027 on top of a quarter-point hike next week
detail: Reuters reports that Goldman Sachs has added a February 25bp Bank of England rate rise to its forecast, alongside its existing call for a quarter-point increase next week. The bank cited higher energy prices and stronger economic data.

headline: German real retail sales fall 2% in September, against a 0.4% rise forecast
detail: German real retail sales dropped 2% month on month in September, after a 1.3% rise the previous month. They were down 2.3% year on year, compared with a -0.2% forecast and -0.4% previously.

headline: Iran says its seven-step proposal underpins diplomacy with the US and could be implemented within days
detail: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Baghaei said Iran's seven-step proposal is the basis for its diplomacy with the US. He said there is a chance it could be implemented over the next few days.

headline: Iran says it is still exchanging messages with the US and has set out its demands, with a deputy foreign minister in Doha
detail: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei says message exchanges with the US are continuing and that Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi was in Doha to help them along. Iran also says it has passed what it calls legitimate demands to the US.

headline: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz cannot reopen until US sanctions are lifted
detail: Iran said on Monday that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen before US sanctions are lifted. The statement came as efforts to restart US-Iran talks continued.

headline: Draft proposal from the Doha talks goes out for feedback and a follow-up meeting is possible, source says; Iranian negotiators have left
detail: An official briefed on the Doha talks said a draft proposal has been circulated for feedback and that a follow-up meeting is possible. A separate source said Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday and that their departure was not caused by problems in the talks.

headline: Start of US-Iran negotiations depends on the naval blockade ending, report says
detail: A market news account reports that opening negotiations between Iran and the US is conditional on an end to the naval blockade; the post does not name the source of the statement. No market reaction is reported.

headline: Poland's October manufacturing PMI rises to 50.0, above the 49.4 forecast; Hungary's reading is 53.1
detail: Poland's manufacturing purchasing managers' index came in at 50.0 for October, against a forecast of 49.4. Hungary's manufacturing PMI for October was 53.1.

headline: Iran says a letter from US Vice President Vance gives no new basis for talks and its demands have not changed
detail: Iran's response to the letter from US Vice President Vance was reported in a market headline. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Spain's October manufacturing PMI rises to 52.2, above the 50.5 forecast
detail: Spain's manufacturing PMI came in at 52.2, against a forecast of 50.5 and a previous reading of 51.0.

headline: Iran says the US must change its approach for talks to go ahead and nuclear negotiations have not yet been reached
detail: Iran said the US needs to change its approach before talks can proceed, and that it is not yet at the point of nuclear negotiations with Washington. Foreign ministry spokesperson Baghaei said Iran's seven-step proposal remains the basis for diplomacy and could be put into effect over two days.

headline: Brent falls 3% intraday to $108.34 a barrel and WTI drops below $99
detail: Brent crude was reported down 3.00% intraday at $108.34 a barrel, with WTI also down 3.00% and trading below $99 a barrel.

headline: France's final October manufacturing PMI comes in at 49.5, above the 49.3 forecast
detail: France's final manufacturing PMI for October was 49.5, against a forecast and prior reading of 49.3, and remains below the 50 mark that separates expansion from contraction.

headline: Eurozone final October manufacturing PMI is revised up to 52.7, above the 52.4 forecast and flash reading
detail: The final eurozone manufacturing PMI for October came in at 52.7. The forecast and the previous reading were both 52.4.

headline: Germany's final October manufacturing PMI is confirmed at 54.2, in line with forecast
detail: The final German manufacturing PMI for October was 54.2. This matches both the forecast and the previous reading.

headline: ECB's Kazimir says the debate is now about how much further ECB action is needed, not whether it is
detail: ECB Governing Council member Peter Kazimir said further policy action is increasingly a question of scale rather than whether it will happen.

headline: PBOC to run swap facility operations for securities, fund and insurance firms on 3 November
detail: China's central bank said it will carry out swap facility operations for securities firms, fund managers and insurers on 3 November.

headline: PBOC says 31 firms applied for its swap facility, with an allotment of 100bn yuan
detail: China's central bank said 31 firms had applied to its swap facility for securities, fund and insurance firms, with 100bn yuan allotted.

headline: UK 10-year gilt yield falls 5bp to 5.23%, its lowest level since September 2023
detail: Market reports say the 10-year gilt yield fell 5bp to 5.23%, the lowest level since September 2023.

headline: ECB's Kazimir says waiting for inflation to rise before acting is unwise and markets may not fully grasp the path ahead
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazimir said action is needed before high inflation becomes entrenched, and that waiting for firms to pass on costs would be a mistake. He also said markets may not fully understand the policy path that is needed.

headline: Brent's fall widens to 4% as hopes build for an end to the US-Iran conflict
detail: A market commentary account reports that Brent crude is down 4%, more than the 3% intraday fall recorded earlier. It links the drop to growing hopes that the US-Iran conflict can be resolved.

headline: Kyiv says Russia has resumed attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region now that the truce has ended
detail: According to Ukrainian authorities, Russian attacks on the Kherson region restarted after the truce expired.

headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR forecasts make the 2020s the weakest decade for income growth on record
detail: Citing the latest OBR forecasts, the Resolution Foundation says incomes will finish 2030 only 1.4 per cent above their 2020 level.

headline: UK final October manufacturing PMI confirmed at 52.8, in line with forecast and the previous reading
detail: The final UK manufacturing PMI came in at 52.8, matching both the 52.8 forecast and the prior figure.

headline: Kremlin says current conditions on the ground rule out restoring Russian gas flows to Europe via Ukraine for now
detail: The Kremlin was responding to a WSJ report that the US is pushing to restore Russian gas transit to Europe through Ukraine as part of a Moscow-Kyiv energy truce.

headline: Kremlin says no further humanitarian ceasefires like Oleshky are planned so far, after Ukraine accuses Russia of regrouping
detail: Ukraine's General Staff said Russian forces used last week's humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky to reinforce their positions. The Kremlin replied that both sides could regroup during a ceasefire and called this normal practice.

headline: UAE energy minister declines to give current oil export levels and says the country will be better prepared whatever happens in the war
detail: The UAE's energy and infrastructure minister would not say how much oil the country is exporting now. He said the course of the war cannot be predicted but the UAE will be more prepared than before.

headline: UK 30-year gilt yield falls more than 7bp on the day to 5.648%, its lowest since 7 August
detail: The 30-year gilt yield dropped by more than 7bp on the day to 5.648%, its lowest level since 7 August, according to a market report. Earlier, the 10-year yield fell 5bp to 5.23%.

headline: China's Wang Yi urges all sides in the Middle East conflict to pursue political solutions rather than renewed fighting
detail: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi made the call on Monday during a meeting in Beijing with an Iranian national security official, Reuters reports.

headline: ECB's Vujcic names AI valuations as a financial stability risk and says sovereign bond markets need monitoring
detail: ECB Vice-President Vujcic said AI valuations are among the risks set out in the ECB's financial stability review. He also said the sovereign bond market must be monitored.

headline: IRGC says 11 tankers have burned in the Strait of Hormuz since 25 October
detail: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps gave a count of 11 tankers burned in the Strait of Hormuz since 25 October. No market reaction was reported with the statement.

headline: Belgian PM De Wever offers resignation after budget talks fail; King holds decision in reserve
detail: The Belgian Royal Palace says Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his resignation after budget negotiations failed. The King has not yet decided and will begin consultations with majority party leaders tomorrow.

headline: Russian Foreign Ministry voices extreme concern over signals that new military action against Iran is planned
detail: Russia's Foreign Ministry said signs of planned fresh military action against Iran were causing it extreme concern, Tass reported. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Gazprom's daily gas exports to China through Power of Siberia reach a record
detail: Gazprom's daily gas exports to China through the Power of Siberia pipeline have hit a record high, according to a market news post. The post gave no volume.

headline: China proposes looser foreign exchange rules for current account transactions
detail: Chinese authorities have put forward proposals to ease foreign exchange rules on current account transactions. The post gave no further details.

headline: Trump says Iran wants a deal with the US but it remains to be seen whether one is reached
detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Iran in comments reported on 2 November, and also said the US has knocked out two of Iran's regimes. No market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB's Makhlouf says the French government must repair its public finances
detail: ECB Governing Council member Makhlouf said on Monday that France needs to put its public finances in order. The post reported no market reaction.

headline: Trump says oil rose less than he expected during the Iran war and predicts US petrol prices will drop below $2 a gallon
detail: US President Trump made the comments on 2 November and also said the US is receiving millions of barrels of oil from Venezuela. No market reaction was reported.

headline: TotalEnergies CEO says Europe will not face a gas shortage this winter
detail: The chief executive of TotalEnergies said he expects no shortfall in European gas supply over the coming winter.

headline: Resolution Foundation says the Budget keeps Local Housing Allowance frozen into 2027-28, affecting over a million families
detail: The Resolution Foundation said the Local Housing Allowance freeze is extended into 2027-28, leaving more than a million families worse off, 91% of them in the bottom half of the income distribution. It said the Budget's Your First Home scheme will help a small number of renters buy.

headline: Equinor CEO says Europe enters winter more vulnerable than usual, with gas storage at its lowest in 15 years
detail: The Equinor chief executive said European gas storage is at the lowest level the company has seen in 15 years, leaving the region more exposed than normal going into winter. He also said more customers are seeking long-term Norwegian gas contracts, with pipeline gas deals now running to 15 years and beyond.

headline: Israel's Netanyahu urges Trump to carry out new strikes on Iran
detail: A wire headline reports that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is pressing US President Trump for renewed military strikes against Iran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Equinor CEO says shipping costs have changed rapidly and the efficient market of the past is gone
detail: The Equinor chief executive said shipping costs have shifted quickly and that the efficient market the industry was used to no longer exists. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Equinor CEO says European industrial gas demand is 30% below its five-year average
detail: Equinor's chief executive said demand for natural gas from European industry is running 30% below the five-year average.

headline: PBOC cuts its stock buyback relending rate to 1% from 1.25%
detail: The People's Bank of China lowered the rate on its stock buyback relending facility to 1% from 1.25%.

headline: European gas prices drop as much as 5.3% to €98.49/MWh
detail: European benchmark gas fell by up to 5.3% to €98.49/MWh on Monday, according to a market wire report. The move came as Brent was also reported trading lower.

headline: Vitol CEO says oil demand will be about 3m bpd lower by end-2026 and the system has low inventories and no spare capacity
detail: The Vitol chief executive said oil demand will take a year to get back to its 2025 level and that the world could not cope with a bigger disruption than the current one. He also said the market could face a difficult spring.

headline: Vitol CEO warns of a potentially difficult spring for oil and says demand will need a year to get back to 2025 levels
detail: Vitol's chief executive made the further comments on the outlook for the oil market on Monday, after his earlier remarks on demand, inventories and spare capacity.

headline: India tells liquor firms it will honour the India-UK trade pact and settle the Scotch tariff dispute, sources say
detail: According to sources, India told a meeting with the drinks industry that bulk Scotch imports are among the concessions in the India-UK trade deal and that it will resolve the tariff dispute.

headline: UK October manufacturing PMI shows the strongest output growth in more than two years, alongside fast-rising costs
detail: Reuters reports that the October manufacturing survey published on Monday showed British factory output growing at its fastest pace in more than two years, with input costs rising quickly. The survey comes in the same week as the Bank of England's rate decision.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says the Supreme Leader has given the government some powers over negotiations
detail: Iran's ISNA news agency reported the remarks by President Pezeshkian. They come as efforts to restart US-Iran talks continue.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian rejects what he calls false claims and excessive demands from Iran's enemies
detail: Iranian state outlet Press TV reported the remarks by President Pezeshkian on Monday, as efforts to restart US-Iran talks continue.

headline: Brent drops to a fresh intraday low near $106 a barrel
detail: Brent was reported trading near $106 a barrel at its intraday low on Monday afternoon. Earlier on Monday it had fallen 3% to $108.34 as hopes grew for an end to the US-Iran conflict.

headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says Tehran will seek to settle the war with the US through dialogue
detail: Iranian state media reported the comments from President Pezeshkian on the conflict with the US.

headline: China's Foreign Minister calls for regional energy and shipping lane security to be safeguarded
detail: China's Foreign Minister made the call amid the Middle East conflict and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: Iran's Foreign Minister says talks via Qatari and Pakistani mediators are intensive and warns of a harsher response to any new strikes
detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said Tehran has presented its terms and plan and that reopening the Strait of Hormuz depends on Iran's conditions being accepted, according to IRNA. He said Iran is ready to work with the US if it chooses honest diplomacy, and that any deception or military operations would meet a harsher response than before.

headline: Iran's Foreign Minister says Hormuz will reopen and talks resume if the US accepts Tehran's conditions, otherwise the status quo continues
detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said Tehran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz are clear. If the US accepts them, the strait will reopen and negotiations will resume; if not, the current situation will continue. State news agency IRNA reported the remarks.

headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve falls to 282.2m barrels, its lowest level since 1982
detail: Crude stocks in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.2 million barrels last week, the lowest level since 1982.

headline: Canada's October manufacturing PMI drops to 49.6 from 51.5
detail: Canada's manufacturing PMI came in at 49.6, down from 51.5 previously. No forecast was given.

headline: UK 10-year gilt yield heads for its largest one-day drop since 20 May
detail: A market report says the 10-year gilt yield is on course for its biggest single-day fall since 20 May.

headline: US final October manufacturing PMI is revised down to 54.9 from the 56.0 flash reading
detail: S&P Global's final US manufacturing PMI for October came in at 54.9, below the 56.0 flash estimate and forecast. September's reading was 55.9.

headline: US Gulf allies are preparing for a new round of strikes on Iran and possible retaliation, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that America's Gulf allies are getting ready for further US strikes on Iran and for the blowback that could follow. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US October ISM manufacturing index rises to 55.5, above the 54.5 forecast, as prices paid ease to 75.2
detail: The US ISM October manufacturing index came in at 55.5, against a forecast of 54.5 and 54.5 the previous month. New orders were 55.5 (forecast 55, previous 55.3), employment was 52.4 (forecast 52, previous 52.7) and prices paid were 75.2 (forecast 77.2, previous 77.9).

headline: US construction spending falls 1.9% on the month, against a forecast 0.3% rise
detail: US construction spending fell 1.9% month on month, compared with a forecast rise of 0.3% and a previous reading of 0.9%.

headline: ECB's Moulin says France's situation is a cause for concern and markets are worried about it
detail: Bank of France Governor Moulin, an ECB Governing Council member, said markets are concerned about the situation in France. He also said rises in global interest rates affect every country.

headline: ECB's Moulin says France will very probably get a budget and markets may be overreacting to the French situation
detail: Bank of France Governor Moulin said France's budget position is poor and must be dealt with. He also said the country is very likely to pass a budget and that markets may be overreacting.

headline: ECB's Escrivá says a lack of fiscal adjustment is not limited to France
detail: Bank of Spain Governor Escrivá said the absence of fiscal adjustment extends beyond France. He spoke on the same day as other ECB policymakers' comments on French public finances.

headline: ECB's Escrivá says the outlook for interest rates is highly complex
detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said the rates scenario is marked by high complexity. He gave no figures.

headline: ECB's Escrivá says the oil and gas price shock is bigger than expected but there are no signs yet of second-round effects
detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said the energy price shock had proved larger than expected. He added that second-round effects on inflation had not yet appeared.

headline: ECB's Moulin says inflation is well above the 2% target but the impact on the wider economy is moderate for now
detail: ECB official Moulin said inflation is clearly above the ECB's 2% objective. He said the effect on the broader economy has so far been fairly moderate.

headline: Oil flows through Kazakhstan's Atyrau-Samara pipeline are halted
detail: A market newswire reports that oil flows on the Atyrau-Samara pipeline from Kazakhstan have stopped. It gave no cause and no expected duration.

headline: ECB's Escrivá says rates at 2% are a reasonable level to hold inflation around 2%
detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said a policy rate of 2% is reasonable for keeping inflation at around 2%.

headline: ECB's Moulin says the current inflation episode cannot be compared with 2022 as the macro backdrop is very different
detail: ECB official Moulin said inflation is clearly above the ECB's objective, but that the current macroeconomic situation differs greatly from 2022 and the two periods are not comparable.

headline: ECB's Escrivá says markets have been fairly insensitive to price risk in recent years
detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá made the remark on Monday, in further comments alongside his earlier statements on rates and inflation.

headline: ECB's Escrivá says AI valuations are clearly high
detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said valuations linked to artificial intelligence are obviously elevated. The comment came on the same day as his other remarks on rates and inflation.

headline: ECB's Escrivá says he is optimistic about AI and sees large productivity gains
detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá made the remarks on Monday, in the same set of comments in which he called AI valuations clearly high.

headline: Iran threatens US bases in Europe if the US carries out new airstrikes, The Times reports
detail: The Times reports that Iran has threatened to target US bases in Europe in response to any new US airstrikes. No market reaction was reported in the post.

headline: Brent futures drop by more than $8 a barrel on hopes of progress towards ending the Iran war
detail: Brent crude futures were reported down by more than $8 a barrel on the day, as hopes grew for progress towards ending the US-Iran conflict.

headline: European gas prices extend their fall to as much as 10%, reaching €93.55/MWh
detail: European gas prices fell by as much as 10% to €93.55/MWh, a bigger fall than the earlier drop of up to 5.3% to €98.49/MWh. The move comes as hopes build for an end to the US-Iran conflict.

headline: US Treasury sells $95bn of 3-month bills at 4.040% and $82bn of 6-month bills at 4.150%
detail: The 3-month bill sale drew a bid-to-cover of 2.88, against 3.07 at the previous sale, and its high yield was 4.04% against 4.05% previously. The 6-month bill drew cover of 2.89, against 2.63, with a high yield of 4.15% against 4.21% previously.

headline: USTR plans to suspend South Africa and Rwanda from duty-free US market access under AGOA
detail: The US Trade Representative said in a statement that it intends to suspend both countries' duty-free access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act. USTR Greer said Trump had found that the two governments' practices do not meet AGOA's eligibility criteria.

headline: Sterling holds steady against the dollar and euro as markets turn to Thursday's BoE decision, where a hike is expected
detail: Reuters reports the pound was broadly steady on Monday as attention moved from last week's UK Budget to the Bank of England decision on Thursday. A rate rise there would be the Bank's first since August 2023.

headline: Italy runs a €20.8bn budget deficit in October
detail: Italy's state budget showed a deficit of €20.8bn for October, according to a market news post. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US-Iran talks reach a breakthrough after Qatari mediation clears procedural hurdles, Al-Jadeed reports
detail: Lebanese broadcaster Al-Jadeed, citing diplomatic sources, reports that Qatari mediation overcame procedural obstacles in the US-Iranian negotiations. No official confirmation or market reaction has been reported.

headline: Brent's fall widens to more than $9 a barrel and WTI drops $8 on hopes of a deal to end the Iran war
detail: Oil futures fell further late on Monday, with Brent down by more than $9 a barrel and US WTI down $8. The moves were reported as driven by hopes of a deal to end the Iran war.

headline: Israel says it will back whatever the US decides on Iran and that a nuclear strike is not under discussion
detail: Israel's UN envoy Danon told Al Arabiya that Israel will support the US decision on Iran, and that Israel and the US are not discussing a nuclear strike on Iran.

headline: US Treasury yields fall to their lowest since 10 September, with the 10-year down 5.76bp at 4.871%
detail: Market reports show US Treasury yields at their lowest level since 10 September. The 10-year note yield was last 5.76bp lower on the day at 4.871%.

headline: Iran's Fars News, citing a source, says there is no new development in message exchanges with the US
detail: A source quoted by Fars News Agency said exchanges with the US through intermediaries are routine and there will be no new steps until the US meets Iran's seven conditions. The source also said the Strait of Hormuz is under Iran's full military control.

headline: UK reportedly ready to pay up to £450m a year on EU student fees in return for equal treatment under EU 'Made in Europe' plan
detail: A report says the UK would spend up to £450m a year on fees for EU students if Brussels gives British companies equal treatment under its planned 'Made in Europe' industrial programme. The report gave no source for the UK position.

headline: Qatari mediators head to Tehran for talks with Iran's foreign minister on a draft US-Iran deal
detail: An official briefed on the talks told Reuters that Qatari mediators were travelling to Tehran late on Monday to meet Foreign Minister Araghchi. The official said the talks would cover a version of a draft US-Iran deal that has been under negotiation for the past eight days.

headline: WTI December crude settles down $7.66, or 7.36%, at $96.46 a barrel
detail: NYMEX WTI December futures settled at $96.46 a barrel, down $7.66 or 7.36%. December gasoline settled at $2.9001 a gallon, diesel at $4.4216 a gallon and natural gas at $2.8560/MMBtu.

headline: Trump says oil will fall further because the US is winning with Iran, and a deal could happen
detail: US President Trump said oil prices will go down further, that Iran wants to make a deal which could happen, and that Iran has said recently it will not have a nuclear weapon.

headline: Trump tells Axios he is in no hurry to decide whether to restart the war with Iran
detail: In a phone interview with Axios, the US President said he did not need to decide quickly on resuming the war with Iran. He also said Iran had recently stated again that it will not have a nuclear weapon.

headline: Brent crude futures settle down $8.66, or 7.63%, at $104.77 a barrel
detail: Brent settles at $104.77 a barrel, down $8.66 or 7.63% on the day, amid hopes of a deal to end the Iran war.

headline: Trump says an Iran deal is coming together well, which is why oil is falling, and that the US will stop killing Iran's leaders as asked
detail: Speaking at the Reflecting Pool, President Trump said Iran had asked the US to stop killing its leaders and that the US would do so. He said things with Iran were coming together well and linked this to the fall in oil.

headline: US Treasury puts privately held net marketable borrowing at $739bn in its quarterly refunding estimate
detail: The US Treasury's quarterly refunding estimate puts privately held net marketable borrowing at $739bn for the July-September 2026 quarter, assuming an end-September cash balance of $950bn. Excluding a higher-than-expected cash balance at the start of the quarter, the estimate is $87bn above the May projection.

headline: Trump answers no when asked whether the US will strike Iran after the elections
detail: US President Trump said no when asked about striking Iran after the elections, according to a White House pool report.

headline: US Treasury expects $628bn of borrowing for October-December 2026, assuming an $850bn end-December cash balance
detail: The US Treasury published the estimate in its quarterly refunding release. The same release put privately held net marketable borrowing at $739bn, which it said was $68bn higher than the May projection, mainly because it now expects lower net cash flows.
