headline: US Treasury puts its fourth-quarter borrowing estimate at $618bn, $10bn below its August projection
detail: Reuters reports that the US Treasury now expects to borrow $618bn in the fourth quarter, $10bn less than it projected in August. The Treasury attributed the cut to a higher-than-assumed starting cash balance, partly offset by lower projected net cash flows.

headline: US VP Vance says progress has been made towards an Iran deal and no deadline has been set for resuming strikes
detail: US Vice President Vance said he feels good about the prospects of a deal with Iran, that there have been a number of good talks with Iranian officials and that some progress has been made. He also said the US has not set any deadlines for resuming strikes.

headline: Trump says Iran wants a settlement as soon as possible and that one could happen, as oil falls almost $10 a barrel
detail: In a social media post, US President Trump said oil prices had dropped almost $10 a barrel because people expect there will be no war with Iran. He added that Iran wants a settlement as soon as possible.

headline: Iranian state media reports five explosions on Qeshm Island as the IRGC claims it downed an MQ-9 drone east of Hormuz
detail: Iran's IRNA news agency reported five explosions on Qeshm Island and said their intensity suggested impacts on the island. Shortly before, Iran's IRGC claimed it had shot down an MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz with an advanced air defence system; neither report gave a source for the explosions or any market reaction.

headline: US military carries out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that the US has launched strikes against Iran's Qeshm Island. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: US to mediate Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November covering an end to the war and post-war security
detail: US envoy Witkoff and a senior US official say the working-level trilateral talks will cover ending the war, post-war security pacts, de-escalation and aid measures. US negotiators will also meet France, Germany, the UK, the EU and NATO in Brussels this week.

headline: PBOC raises the foreign exchange deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4%, effective 15 November
detail: The People's Bank of China says the 2-percentage-point increase is intended to improve the management of foreign currency liquidity at financial institutions.

headline: South Korea's October CPI rises 2.8% y/y, in line with forecasts and down from 2.9%
detail: The statistics office says prices rose 0.2% on the month, below the poll, and core CPI rose 2.8% y/y.

headline: Oil rises in early Asian trade after report of US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, then stabilises
detail: Reuters reported oil prices rising in early Asian trading on Tuesday after the Wall Street Journal said the US had struck Qeshm Island. A later Reuters report said oil had stabilised after the previous session's sharp fall, with Asian stocks lower ahead of the US midterm elections.

headline: Offshore yuan falls as much as 0.34% to 6.67 per dollar after PBOC raises FX deposit reserve ratio
detail: The offshore yuan fell 0.26% to 6.6642 per dollar, its largest daily drop since June, before extending losses to 0.34% at 6.67. The move followed the PBOC's increase in the foreign currency deposit reserve ratio to 6% from 4%. The PBOC fixed the yuan midpoint at 6.7150 per dollar.

headline: RBA raises cash rate 25bp to 4.85% in 6-3 vote, citing a material upward revision to its inflation outlook
detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its rate from 4.60%, as forecast. Three board members preferred no change. Staff forecasts put CPI at 4.5% and trimmed mean CPI at 3.6% in Q4 2026, and the Australian dollar fell 0.35% to $0.6974 after the decision.

headline: RBA's Bullock gives no guidance on the next move after the hike and says pausing to assess incoming data is probably best
detail: At her press conference after the rate rise, the RBA Governor said the increase was needed to bring inflation down, that growth must stay subdued and unemployment rise further, and that she sees no wage-price spiral. She said board members who favoured a hold were not ruling out higher rates and that this hike might not be enough; Reuters reported the Australian dollar dipped after the decision.

headline: Washington calls its Qeshm Island strikes defensive, aimed at protecting US military assets in the Middle East
detail: The FT reports the US described Monday night's strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz as a defensive move, and says the attacks appear limited in scope.

headline: RBA's Bullock says it is unclear how high rates may need to go and no decision has been made on further hikes
detail: The RBA Governor said the latest hike may not be enough but further increases are not clearly needed, and that unemployment remains relatively low and she does not see the economy weakening. The Australian dollar was reported near a two-week low after the decision, which took the cash rate to an 18-year high in the fifth hike of the year.

headline: IEA says global LNG supply could post a record annual decline because of the Iran war
detail: The International Energy Agency said the Iran war could cause global liquefied natural gas supply to fall by a record amount this year, the WSJ reports.

headline: China halts IPOs and share offerings in a bid to stabilise weak markets, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that China's securities regulator has privately told investment banks in recent days to pause initial public offerings.

headline: Aramco CEO says the company is looking at more export routes and overseas capacity, including a possible East-West pipeline expansion
detail: Saudi Aramco's chief executive said the company is exploring additional export routes and capacity abroad, among them a potential expansion of its East-West pipeline. No timing or volumes were given.

headline: Senior Iranian official says Tehran's conditions must be met before Hormuz reopens, with nuclear talks only to follow
detail: A senior Iranian official said Tehran will reject what it called excessive US demands and is ready to respond forcefully to any US strikes, in the region and beyond. The official added that mediators are working to narrow the gaps between Tehran and Washington.

headline: Turkey's October CPI rises 29.77% y/y, above the 29.5% forecast, with prices up 2.58% on the month
detail: Turkish annual inflation came in at 29.77% against a 29.5% forecast and 29.73% previously. Monthly inflation was 2.58%, against a 2.4% forecast and 1.84% previously.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker Qalibaf says Tehran has sent Washington its response and the next move is for the US
detail: Iranian state media reported Parliament Speaker Qalibaf as saying Tehran had given the US a strong and rational response, leaving the next step to Washington. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's foreign minister Araqchi says talks with Saudi Arabia on new regional security arrangements are continuing
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on X on Tuesday that Tehran is in ongoing talks with Riyadh, seeking regional security arrangements without foreign military involvement, Reuters reports. Reuters also reports that fighting in Yemen is intensifying.

headline: Iran and the US are reviewing the mediators' latest proposals, a diplomat says
detail: A diplomat said both sides are studying the latest suggestions from mediators. The report follows Monday's talks in Tehran between Qatari mediators and Iran.

headline: US crude futures rise $2.14 to $98.60 a barrel as Iran and the US weigh mediators' latest proposals
detail: US oil futures are trading $2.14 higher at $98.60 a barrel in early trade. A diplomat says Tehran and Washington are reviewing new proposals from the mediators after Qatari officials held talks in Iran on Monday.

headline: ECB's Radev says the October pause does not mark the end of tightening as the economic environment becomes more challenging
detail: ECB Governing Council member Radev said the economic environment is getting more challenging and that the ECB's pause in October does not mean tightening has finished.

headline: ECB's Radev says current rates are not adequate and the ECB should act without waiting for second-round effects
detail: ECB Governing Council member Radev said core inflation is stable and the energy shock is not feeding through to wages, but argued that the ECB should move now rather than wait for second-round effects. He also said the economic environment is becoming increasingly difficult.

headline: Swiss October CPI rises 1.5% y/y, above the 1.2% forecast and up from 1.0%; core steady at 0.5%
detail: Swiss consumer prices rose 0.2% on the month, against a forecast of 0% and 0.0% previously. Core inflation was 0.5% y/y, in line with forecasts and unchanged from the previous reading.

headline: French year-to-date budget balance comes in at -159.173bn, compared with -159.60bn previously
detail: France's latest state budget balance figure is -159.173bn, against -159.60bn in the previous release. No forecast was given.

headline: German Chancellor Merz calls for a cut to electricity tax in the 2027 budget and says he has ideas on how to deliver it
detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said a reduction in electricity tax needs to be secured in Germany's 2027 budget. He did not say how it would be paid for.

headline: Aramco CEO warns energy markets face pressure this winter and says preliminary engineering on a pipeline expansion has begun
detail: Saudi Aramco's chief executive said energy markets will come under pressure in the coming winter. He added that the company has started preliminary engineering work on a pipeline expansion.

headline: Aramco CEO says global refining has lost 5m b/d of supply and tanker attacks have removed 15% of effective capacity
detail: Saudi Aramco's chief executive said the global refining market has lost 5m barrels a day of supply and that attacks on tankers have taken out 15% of effective capacity. He also said oil demand will recover more strongly.

headline: Iran's armed forces chief sets out five principles for regional peace, including an end to war on all fronts and full sanctions relief
detail: Iran's armed forces chief Abdollahi lists Tehran's conditions for a lasting regional peace, according to reports including Tasnim. They include an end to the war on all fronts, including Lebanon and Gaza, full sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets.

headline: Iran's armed forces chief seeks recognition of Tehran's sovereignty over Hormuz and an end to the US security umbrella
detail: Further principles set out by Iran's armed forces chief, as reported by Tasnim and other outlets, include war reparations, guarantees against further aggression and security arrangements led from within the region. He also calls for recognition of Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and for the US security umbrella to be replaced.

headline: ECB's Machado calls for strong bank capital standards to be kept, including an output floor
detail: ECB official Machado said it is important to keep strong capital standards for banks and to retain an output floor. The remarks were about bank regulation, not interest rates.

headline: Iran's president, parliament speaker and foreign minister press the military to engage with Qatar's proposal
detail: President Pezeshkian, parliament speaker Qalibaf and foreign minister Araqchi have urged Iran's armed forces to engage with the Qatari mediation proposal on a US-Iran deal. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iranian assessments increasingly see a return to war as likely, report says
detail: A newswire headline reports that assessments inside Iran increasingly see a return to war as likely. The report gives no source for the assessments and no market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB's Kocher says it is crucial to stop inflation becoming entrenched
detail: ECB Governing Council member Martin Kocher said on Tuesday that the ECB must make sure inflation does not become entrenched.

headline: Iran says it would regard any action it takes as legitimate self-defence
detail: Iran says any action it takes would be legitimate self-defence. The statement comes as the US and Iran review mediators' proposals after US strikes on Qeshm Island. The report does not name the official who made it.

headline: Iran's Gharibabadi says Tehran would respond if a nuclear weapon were used against it
detail: Iranian official Gharibabadi told ISNA that Iran's hands would not be tied if it were the target of a nuclear weapon. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Kremlin confirms three-way Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi next week, with Putin aide Medinsky leading Russia's delegation
detail: The Kremlin confirmed the tripartite talks on Ukraine due in Abu Dhabi next week and named presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky as Russia's lead negotiator. It said all sides broadly agree the meeting would be useful.

headline: Kazakhstan restarts oil flows through the Atyrau-Samara pipeline after drone attacks took it offline
detail: Kazakhstan's energy ministry said on Tuesday that it had resumed oil transit through the Atyrau-Samara pipeline, Reuters reports. Drone attacks had forced the pipeline to shut the previous day.

headline: China says it will keep a moderately loose monetary policy and sets out five focus areas for financial policy
detail: Xinhua reports that China will continue its moderately loose monetary policy and has named five main areas of focus for financial policy. These include stopping illegal financial activity and looking into the use of AI in financial oversight.

headline: UK 10-year gilt auction clears at 5.268% with cover of 3.38, compared with 5.418% and 3.61 at the previous sale
detail: The 10-year gilt auction gave an average yield of 5.268%, down from 5.418% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.38, against 3.61 last time.

headline: Qatar says its mediators are back in Doha from Tehran and US-Iran talks are continuing
detail: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson says the mediation team that went to Tehran on Monday night has returned, and both the US and Iran are reviewing the mediators' proposals. The spokesperson also says Gulf states agree on avoiding escalation.

headline: Iranian state broadcaster says three oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday
detail: Iran's state broadcaster IRIB reported on Tuesday that three oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. The report gave no cause, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: Qatar reports progress in US-Iran mediation and says both sides are evaluating the proposal
detail: A spokesperson for Qatar's foreign ministry said the US and Iran are both committed to the mediation and are assessing the proposal, adding that Qatar remains hopeful of a deal that sets the stage for further negotiations. The spokesperson also said regional leaders are coordinating closely to find a solution and avoid escalation.

headline: Qatar says freedom of navigation is not up for negotiation and rejects threats to its carriers as US-Iran talks go on
detail: A spokesperson for Qatar's foreign ministry said Doha rejects any threat to Qatari carriers and others. The spokesperson also said Iran and the US remain committed to negotiations and that Qatar is working towards a deal that builds trust.

headline: German 5-year Bobl auction clears at 3.14% with cover of 1.4, compared with 3.22% and 1.1 at the previous sale
detail: Germany's 5-year Bobl auction came in at an average yield of 3.14%, down from 3.22% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover was 1.4, up from 1.1.

headline: ECB's Moulin says the ECB has to stop inflation from spreading beyond energy
detail: ECB official Moulin said the central bank needs to keep energy-driven inflation from spilling over into wider prices. No market reaction was reported.

headline: SNB's Schlegel says inflation pressure in September was slightly higher than in June and expects moderate Swiss growth
detail: Swiss National Bank Chairman Schlegel said inflation pressure in September was slightly higher than in June. He also said the Swiss economy should grow moderately after a strong second quarter.

headline: Russia's Lavrov says reports of US strikes on Iran after the US vote have not been confirmed
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said talk of US strikes on Iran after the US elections has not been confirmed, according to TASS.

headline: IFS director criticises the Budget's Founders Relief tax break for entrepreneurs at Treasury Committee hearing
detail: Helen Miller, head of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, told the Treasury Committee she did not see how Treasury officials could have concluded from the evidence on entrepreneurship that the Founders Relief tax break was good policy.

headline: Resolution Foundation chief tells Treasury Committee the Budget's household living standards forecasts are dire
detail: Resolution Foundation chief executive Ruth Curtice gave evidence to the Treasury Select Committee on Tuesday morning about last week's Budget. She singled out the forecasts for household living standards as particularly bad.

headline: Iran's president says the supreme leader has authorised talks on issues previously treated as non-negotiable
detail: Iran's president made the statement on Tuesday as Iran and the US consider the mediators' latest proposals. The report did not say which issues are covered or describe any market reaction.

headline: Qatari mediators expect US and Iranian responses to their new proposal within 36 hours
detail: An official briefed on the talks told Reuters that Qatar's mediators expect feedback from both Washington and Tehran within 36 hours on a new proposal intended to move the talks forward.

headline: Iran's supreme leader warns foreign forces in the Persian Gulf that they belong only at the bottom of its waters
detail: Iran's supreme leader said in a statement that outside powers acting from thousands of kilometres away in the Gulf have no place there, as the US and Iran weigh Qatar's mediation proposals. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Kremlin says security guarantees for both Russia and Ukraine will be on the table at the three-way Abu Dhabi talks
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said security guarantees for Russia and Ukraine will be discussed at the three-way talks in Abu Dhabi. The talks are due on 10-11 November with US mediation.

headline: UK PM's spokesman rules out a return to EU freedom of movement during this parliament
detail: The Prime Minister's official spokesman said on Tuesday that the UK will not return to EU freedom of movement in the current parliament.

headline: Brent crude drops below $105 a barrel to session lows
detail: Brent crude was reported trading below $105 a barrel, its lowest level of the session, while Iran and the US review the mediators' latest proposals.

headline: UK to make a guaranteed lifetime retirement income the default option for private sector pensions
detail: Plans unveiled by the UK government on Tuesday will make a guaranteed income for life the default retirement option for private sector workers, so that savers do not have to manage their pension pots themselves, Reuters reports.

headline: Kremlin's Peskov says Russia will in time need to talk to Europe about a future security system, but who it talks to matters
detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia would eventually have to discuss a future European security system with Europe, and stressed the importance of who its counterparts would be. He spoke ahead of the US-mediated three-way Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says the overnight US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island have not affected oil flows
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said the overnight US strikes on Iran, including the attack on Qeshm Island, have not affected the flow of oil.

headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says more refined products are coming out of the Arabian Gulf and India's output will rise
detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said refined product exports from the Arabian Gulf are increasing and that more refined output is expected from India. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says the US is halting $4b of aid to Israel under a deal agreed months ago and will not raise payments
detail: US President Trump said in a Fox News interview that he would not increase payments to Israel and that a deal reached months ago means $4b of aid is being stopped. Asked about Iran after the elections, he said only that it remained to be seen.

headline: Trump says the US successfully hit a recently built Iranian anti-aircraft facility overnight
detail: In a Fox News interview, the US president said the strike last night had worked, that he is not trying to cause mass casualties in Iran, but that the US would kill people there if it had to. He said Iran would see what happens after the elections.

headline: Trump says Canada will supply fertiliser to the US tariff-free and a broader deal with Canada is close
detail: Speaking in a Fox News interview, the US president said the US is close to a fertiliser deal with Canada and expects to reach a wider deal soon.

headline: US approves Qatar's draft memorandum of understanding with Iran, and Saudi Arabia and UAE also back it, reports say
detail: Al Jazeera reports that Washington approved the draft MoU that the Qatari delegation presented for Iran yesterday. Sources close to the mediation team say Saudi Arabia and the UAE were briefed and approved it, and that the US and Iran made concessions on the nuclear file and frozen assets.

headline: Trump says the US could balance its budget if the Fed cut interest rates
detail: Trump made the remarks in a Fox News interview, in which he also said Israel does not need the $4 billion in US aid.

headline: US and Iran have made concessions on Tehran's nuclear programme and frozen funds, Al Araby Al Jadeed reports
detail: Al Araby Al Jadeed, citing unnamed sources, reports that Washington and Tehran have each made concessions on Iran's nuclear programme and its frozen funds. The two sides are reviewing the mediators' latest proposals.

headline: Germany's Merz says Russia risks further escalation with Black Sea attacks and a worldwide food crisis
detail: After talks with Ukraine's President Zelenskiy, German Chancellor Merz said Ukraine can continue to rely on Germany and that Russia risks further escalation with its Black Sea attacks. He also said a coalition of the willing summit will be held in Berlin later this month.

headline: Brent falls to $102 and European gas drops 8% to €86.9/MWh on reports of US-Iran concessions
detail: Brent and WTI futures turned negative and fell nearly 3% after President Trump said the US would stop paying Israel after year-end. Brent was then reported at $102 a barrel and European gas 8% lower at €86.9/MWh, as sources close to the mediators said Washington and Tehran had made concessions on nuclear issues and frozen assets.

headline: Trump says the US should pay the lowest interest rates in the world
detail: President Trump made the remark in a Fox News interview. Earlier in the same interview he said the US could balance its budget if the Fed cut rates.

headline: US-Iran mediation turns to how to announce an interim deal: Iranian nuclear concession for release of some frozen funds, report says
detail: Al Araby, citing sources close to the mediators, reports that talks now focus on a first step and on how to announce an interim agreement, with both sides then returning to negotiations. Under the reported plan, Tehran would announce a concession on its nuclear programme and Washington would announce the release of part of Iran's frozen funds.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine has offered Russia a longer, wider ceasefire and wants an energy ceasefire and Black Sea truce discussed in Abu Dhabi
detail: Ukraine's president said Kyiv had offered Russia an extended and expanded ceasefire after the humanitarian operation in Oleshky. He said a ceasefire on energy targets and a Black Sea truce should be discussed at the Abu Dhabi talks.

headline: Germany's Merz says Russia must commit seriously to a ceasefire and a later peace agreement at the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: German Chancellor Merz commented on the upcoming three-way Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US-Iran deal would be announced in stages with both sides acting at the same time, Al Araby reports
detail: Al Araby, citing sources close to the negotiating team, reported on how a US-Iran deal would be announced. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Zelenskiy hopes US-mediated talks lead to a leaders' meeting and calls Russia's invitation to Moscow destructive
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said he hopes the US-mediated talks open the way to a meeting of leaders. He also described Russia's invitation for him to come to Moscow as destructive.

headline: Germany's Merz says third countries should not discuss Ukraine at the G20 meeting in Miami without Ukraine present
detail: German Chancellor Merz said it would be unacceptable for third countries to talk about Ukraine at the G20 meeting in Miami without Ukraine taking part.

headline: Russian crude exports climb to 3.65m b/d as attacks on its refineries resume
detail: A market news account reports that Russia's crude exports have risen to 3.65 million barrels a day amid renewed attacks on Russian refineries. No price reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's Rezaee says the US response falls short and Hormuz reopens only if Washington meets Iran's seven conditions
detail: Iranian official Rezaee said the US reply on Iran's demands was unconvincing. He said the Strait of Hormuz will reopen only once the US explicitly addresses and acts on Iran's seven conditions.

headline: UK moves ahead with its digital bond pilot and gives key roles to six banks
detail: A market news account reports that the UK has advanced its digital bond pilot and assigned key roles to six banks. The post did not name the banks or give a timetable.

headline: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman says any understanding with the US requires a firm commitment to end the war on all fronts, including…
detail: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei also said Tehran is taking part in diplomacy with maximum caution because of past US breaches of agreements. Separately, security chief Rezaee repeated that the US response to Iran's seven conditions was not convincing.

headline: Russia launches a large-scale attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, hitting power plants and substations in nine regions
detail: The Financial Times reports that Russian missiles and drones struck power plants and substations across nine Ukrainian regions, and that Ukraine's air force struggled to intercept them. The attack comes ahead of the three-way talks in Abu Dhabi, where Ukraine has asked for an energy ceasefire to be discussed.

headline: ECB's Moulin calls France's 0.4% growth forecast optimistic and says a downgrade is likely
detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said France's 0.4% GDP growth forecast is optimistic and will probably need to be revised down. He described euro area growth as fairly resilient.

headline: US JOLTS job openings rise to 7.523m in September, above the 7.164m forecast
detail: US job openings were 7,523K in September, against a forecast of 7,164K and 7,079K in the previous reading.

headline: US factory orders rise 1.8% m/m, above the 1.2% forecast; revised core durable goods steady at 0.5%
detail: US factory orders rose 1.8% on the month, against a 1.2% forecast and 0.1% previously. Revised core durable goods orders came in at 0.5%, in line with the forecast and the previous reading.

headline: US Treasury yields rise after US data; 10-year up 5.36bp at 4.948%, 2-year up 3.13bp at 4.614%
detail: US Treasury yields moved higher after the release of US factory orders and JOLTS job openings data. The 10-year yield was last up 5.36bp at 4.948% and the 2-year was up 3.13bp at 4.614%.

headline: US September durable goods orders revised up to 1.9%, against a 1.8% forecast and initial reading
detail: The revised US durable goods orders figure for September is 1.9%. The forecast and the previous reading were both 1.8%.

headline: Iran's negotiating team says no new progress has been made towards an agreement with the US
detail: Iranian state broadcaster IRIB quotes the spokesman for Iran's negotiating team as saying there has been no new development on an agreement with the US. The statement follows earlier reports of concessions by both sides on Tehran's nuclear programme and frozen funds.

headline: Iran denies reports that it is close to a deal with the US, state broadcaster IRIB says
detail: Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reports that Tehran rejects reports of a near agreement with the US. The denial follows earlier reports of US and Iranian concessions on the nuclear programme and frozen funds.

headline: Gulf oil exports fall in October from September, their highest level since the Iran war began, ship-tracking data show
detail: Reuters cites data from two ship-tracking companies showing Gulf oil exports fell in October from September's levels. Both companies said the October figures could be revised up as more shipment details come in.

headline: BoC's Macklem says the inflation outlook has worsened and further rate hikes may be needed, with decisions taken meeting by meeting
detail: The Bank of Canada Governor said higher oil prices linked to the Middle East war are lifting costs, and CPI inflation is expected to rise to 3.5% by year-end, stay at or above 3% through much of 2027 and return near 2% by mid-2028. He put Q2 GDP growth at 3.3% and Q3 at around 2%, and projected growth of 1% in 2026 and about 2% in both 2027 and 2028, with a Q4 slowdown due to new US tariffs.

headline: Senior Iranian official says there is no deadline for exchanging messages with the US through mediators or reviewing responses
detail: The comment was reported on Tuesday as Qatari-mediated US-Iran talks continue.

headline: BoC's Macklem says he does not see fiscal policy currently making it harder to bring inflation down
detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said that, in present circumstances, he does not believe fiscal policy is complicating efforts to lower inflation. He made the remark after earlier saying further rate hikes may be needed.

headline: Iranian official says mediators are working to close the gap between Tehran and Washington
detail: An Iranian official said mediators are trying to narrow the differences between Iran and the US as talks on a possible deal go on. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Resolution Foundation says Budget headroom fell from £24bn to £15bn as energy prices top the OBR's central forecast
detail: The Resolution Foundation says oil and gas prices have gone above the OBR's central forecast since its forecast window closed in mid-August, and are nearer its severe scenario. It says gilt yields are still in line with the OBR's central forecast.

headline: Zelenskiy says Russia would not survive fully enforced sanctions and urges pressure rather than dialogue alone with Putin
detail: Ukraine's president said Russia could not survive if all sanctions were fully applied with no exemptions for some oligarchs. He also said Putin responds to pressure and strong steps, and that Europe is several times stronger than Russia.

headline: Russia summons Norway's chargé d'affaires to protest over the seizure of Russian assets requested by Ukraine
detail: Russian reports say the foreign ministry lodged a protest with Norway's chargé d'affaires after Russian assets were seized following a request from Ukraine.

headline: Russia's foreign ministry says it will seek removal of sanctions on Russian assets in Norway and invokes the Svalbard Treaty
detail: Russian reports cite the foreign ministry as saying Moscow will try to have the sanctions on Russian assets in Norway lifted. The ministry also demands that Oslo comply fully with international law, including the Svalbard Treaty.

headline: Israel tells the US that Iran is considering chemical weapons use, NYT reports, and US officials are divided on the claim
detail: The New York Times, citing US and regional officials, reports that Israel has shared intelligence with the US asserting that Iran is weighing the use of chemical weapons against its adversaries. Some US officials reacted with alarm and others with deep scepticism, and some see it as part of an Israeli push for the US to return to major combat operations against Iran.

headline: ECB's Nagel says a December rate hike is very likely needed as inflation pressures near the adverse scenario
detail: Bundesbank President and ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said September inflation pressures were higher than expected and approaching the ECB's adverse scenario. He said the ECB must stop the energy price spike from feeding into broad-based inflation.

headline: Greenland's parliament ratifies security deal with the US that allows a larger US military presence on the island
detail: Reuters reports that Greenland's parliament ratified on Tuesday the security agreement signed by US President Trump and the leaders of Greenland and Denmark, which may resolve the standoff over the island. Some opposition members questioned the deal.

headline: ECB's Sleijpen says the Iran shock is proving more persistent than previously thought
detail: Olaf Sleijpen, Dutch central bank governor and ECB Governing Council member, said the shock from the Iran war is lasting longer than earlier expected.

headline: ECB's Sleijpen sees no clear second-round inflation effects yet but says tightening is slowing Europe's economy
detail: ECB Governing Council member Sleijpen said second-round effects are not yet really visible, that rising energy risks carry knock-on effects for inflation, and that policy tightening is slowing the European economy.

headline: ECB's Nagel says he is confident France will sort out its budget problems and that this is not a job for monetary policy
detail: Bundesbank President and ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel commented on France's fiscal position on 3 November. He said dealing with the budget is not a task for monetary policy.

headline: ECB's Sleijpen says France's problems have to be resolved by Paris
detail: ECB Governing Council member Sleijpen said France's problems need to be solved in Paris. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's Araghchi says Tehran will not give up its independence under economic pressure and says the US misreads Iran's leadership
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi made the comments in an interview with Al Jazeera, while mediated US-Iran talks continue.

headline: ECB's Kocher says a December rate hike is likely unless the situation changes and inflation risks are still elevated
detail: ECB Governing Council member Martin Kocher said risks to inflation are still elevated and that the ECB will keep responding to inflation where needed. He said a rate hike in December is likely if conditions do not change.

headline: New Zealand unemployment rises to 5.7%, above the 5.5% forecast, as employment falls 0.1% q/q
detail: New Zealand's unemployment rate was 5.7%, against a 5.5% forecast and 5.6% previously. Employment fell 0.1% q/q, against a forecast rise of 0.4% and 0.5% previously, and the participation rate fell to 70.4% from 70.7%, below the 70.7% forecast.

headline: Australia's final services PMI rises to 48.5 from 47.8 and the composite PMI to 48.2 from 47.7
detail: Australia's final October services PMI came in at 48.5, up from 47.8.

headline: Canada's Carney says trade talks with the US have made progress but are not finished, with red lines still to be resolved
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said negotiations with the US will become more intensive, and that key issues and some red lines still have to be addressed. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Canada's Carney says the US is asking for fewer concessions and offering more, and some Canadian red lines have been dropped
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said some of Canada's limits in the US trade talks have been removed and discussions will intensify, though no deal has been reached yet. He added that lines of communication remain open even when negotiators are not meeting the USTR.

headline: Trump tells the FT the US has no immediate plan to strike Iran and describes the stand-off with Tehran as brilliant
detail: In an interview with the Financial Times hours before the midterm polls closed, the US president said he was content with the stand-off with Iran but signalled he was ready for more war if needed.

headline: US Treasury yields ease in Asian trading; 10-year down 5bp at 4.9167% and 30-year at 5.2964%
detail: US Treasury yields moved lower early in the Asian session as US midterm election results came in.

headline: Australia's household spending rises 0.6% m/m in September, with volumes up 0.7% q/q
detail: Australian data showed seasonally adjusted household spending up 0.6% on the month in September and spending volumes up 0.7% on the quarter.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield falls 6bp to 4.573% in Asian trading as fed funds futures edge higher
detail: Market reports say the US 2-year yield fell 6bp to 4.573%, while fed funds futures posted modest gains.

headline: China's October services PMI drops to 50.8, below the 51.7 forecast; composite PMI eases to 52.0
detail: China's RatingDog services PMI fell to 50.8 in October from 51.6 in September, against a forecast of 51.7. The composite PMI fell to 52.0 from 52.4.

headline: PBOC steps up re-lending support for stock buybacks as applications pass 200bn yuan
detail: China's central bank said it is expanding re-lending policies that support share buybacks and increased holdings, with applications above 200bn yuan. Separately, it injected 257.5bn yuan through overnight reverse repos at 1.25%.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield falls to two-month low of 4.551% as fed funds futures extend gains
detail: The US 2-year yield dropped to 4.551% in Asian trading while fed funds futures rose further. The move came as US networks including CNN and NBC projected that Democrats would win control of the House in the midterm elections, and the euro rose 0.5% to $1.125.

headline: Democrats win control of US Senate and House in midterms; global stocks and the dollar slide
detail: Media projections show Democrats flipping Senate seats in Texas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia, and enough Republican-held seats to take the House. The FT and WSJ report that global stocks and the dollar fell on the results, and the WSJ says a weaker dollar and lower US bond yields lifted demand for gold.

headline: Iran's IRGC says four tankers are destroyed by naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz and two more ships are seized
detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the four oil tankers hit mines while using a route it calls prohibited south of the strait and were still on fire, and that two other vessels had been detained.

headline: Japan's 10-year government bond yield rises 4bp to 2.81%
detail: Japan's 10-year yield gained 4bp to 2.81% in Asian trading, while the Nikkei was still down 1.65% after coming back from its session lows.

headline: Trump links Republican midterm losses partly to the Iran war and petrol prices but says he does not regret starting it
detail: Trump said voters were probably not willing to bear the short-term cost of higher petrol prices tied to Iran. The WSJ reports he accepted that the war was one reason for Republican losses but said he does not regret starting the conflict earlier this year.

headline: India's October services PMI is revised down to 55.8 from a 56.2 flash; composite PMI falls to 56.2
detail: The final HSBC/S&P Global services PMI for India came in at 55.8 for October, below the flash reading of 56.2. The composite PMI fell to 56.2 from 56.7 the previous month.

headline: Japan's deputy chief cabinet secretary Kihara says Tokyo is watching market moves with a high sense of urgency
detail: Japan's Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Kihara said markets move on various factors and that the government is monitoring market moves with a high sense of urgency.

headline: Asian markets fall sharply as Democratic midterm gains raise fears of AI regulation
detail: Asian markets were reported plunging on Wednesday morning after Democratic gains in the US midterm elections, with the drop linked to fears of tighter regulation of artificial intelligence. No index levels or figures were given.

headline: Italy's services PMI rises to 52 in October, above the 51.5 forecast
detail: Italy's services PMI came in at 52, up from 51.7 previously and ahead of the 51.5 forecast.

headline: Italy's October composite PMI eases to 50.8, in line with forecasts
detail: Italy's composite PMI fell to 50.8 in October from 51.0 in September, matching the 50.8 forecast. The services PMI rose to 52.

headline: France's final October services PMI is revised down to 46.2 from a 48.4 flash; composite PMI cut to 46.6
detail: France's final October services PMI came in at 46.2, against a forecast and flash reading of 48.4. The composite PMI was 46.6, also against a forecast and preliminary reading of 48.4.

headline: Eurozone final October services PMI is revised down to 51.4 from 51.7; composite PMI cut to 51.7
detail: The eurozone's final October services PMI was 51.4, below the 51.7 flash reading and forecast. The composite PMI came in at 51.7, against a flash reading and forecast of 51.9.

headline: Germany's final October services PMI is revised up to 52.5 from a 51.7 flash; composite PMI rises to 53.4
detail: Germany's final October services PMI came in at 52.5, compared with a 51.7 flash reading and forecast. The composite PMI was 53.4, up from a preliminary 52.8 and above the 52.8 forecast.

headline: ECB projects wage growth of 2.8% in the second quarter of 2027, slowing to 2.4% in the third quarter
detail: The European Central Bank's latest wage projections put wage growth at 2.8% in 2Q 2027 and 2.4% in 3Q 2027.

headline: Gold rises 3% as the dollar and yields fall after Democrats win the US midterms
detail: A market wire reports gold up 3%, with the dollar and yields lower after the Democrats won control of Congress in the US midterm elections.

headline: UK final October services PMI is revised down to 52.8, against a 53.1 forecast and earlier reading
detail: The UK's final services PMI came in at 52.8. Forecasts and the previous reading were both 53.1.

headline: UK final October composite PMI is revised down to 52.9 from a 53.1 flash, below the 53.1 forecast
detail: The final October composite PMI came in at 52.9, below the preliminary reading and forecast of 53.1. The services PMI was revised down to 52.8 from 53.1.

headline: NIESR expects the MPC to raise Bank Rate by 25bp to 4% at tomorrow's decision
detail: NIESR said its Monetary Policy Dashboard shows a growing case for a change in policy, and that it expects a 25bp increase to 4% at the MPC decision on 5 November.

headline: Eurozone flash October inflation rises to 4% y/y, in line with forecasts; core inflation holds at 2.5%
detail: Eurozone flash headline CPI came in at 4% year on year, up from 3.8% and matching the 4% forecast. Core CPI was 2.5%, unchanged and in line with expectations, and prices rose 0.4% month on month, down from 0.6% and in line with the forecast.

headline: Gilts extend gains as the 10-year yield falls 5bp to 5.21%
detail: UK government bonds add to earlier gains on Wednesday morning, with the 10-year gilt yield down 5bp at 5.21%, according to a market report.

headline: Germany's 15-year Bund auction yields 3.57%, up from 3.5%, with bid-to-cover falling to 1.3 from 2
detail: Germany sold 15-year Bunds at an average yield of 3.57%, compared with 3.5% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.3, down from 2 last time.

headline: Iran's Khamenei warns that any further attacks will bring a far wider response
detail: In a message, Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei said Iran must become ever more powerful to achieve absolute deterrence, and warned that further attacks would draw a far wider response. Separately, an IRGC adviser told Tasnim that in a war, Iran's retaliation would not be limited to the source of the attack.

headline: Khamenei calls Iran's Hormuz action a response to US aggression and says the US midterm result will not change Washington's hostility
detail: In a message, Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei said the US wants Iran's unconditional surrender and that any move towards submission would embolden the enemy. He said people who expect changes in the party holding power in the US to end Washington's hostility towards Iran are badly mistaken.

headline: Resolution Foundation says typical UK household energy bills this year are close to their level in the 2022 energy shock
detail: The Resolution Foundation estimates that the typical household will spend nearly as much on energy this year as it did during the 2022 shock. The think tank gave no figures in the post.

headline: S&P Global survey shows UK businesses adding staff for the first time in more than two years
detail: City AM reports that S&P Global's survey figures showed headcount rising for the first time in over two years, alongside stronger services activity. Analysts cited by the paper expect the Bank of England to raise rates several times in the coming months.

headline: Chancellor Healey confirms a further 2% rise in tax on savings income from April 2027
detail: City AM reports the Budget measure takes the savings tax rate to 44% for some, and that thousands of workers will face an effective rate of 64% on cash savings.

headline: France's finance minister Lescure sees no reason to revise the 5.4% 2026 deficit goal
detail: Lescure also said France has to meet its 5% deficit target for 2027 if it is to remain credible.

headline: Kremlin hopes the US midterm results will not affect Trump's peace efforts on Ukraine
detail: The Kremlin made the comment after Democrats won control of Congress, and Tass also reported that Russia hopes Trump will continue his peace efforts.

headline: EU trade commissioner Sefcovic says it is vital that the US-EU trade deal is upheld
detail: EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic said that respecting the trade agreement between the US and the EU is of the highest importance. The remarks follow the Democrats' wins in the US midterm elections.

headline: Brent is reported at $102, down from $118 at the end of last week, after the US midterm results
detail: An economist puts Brent crude at $102 a barrel, against $118 at the end of last week, and says the oil market's direction depends on whether the US eases or steps up the war with Iran after the midterms.

headline: Resolution Foundation says Budget plans cut departmental capital spending in 2029-30 compared with the March forecast
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the Budget again scaled back planned investment, leaving capital departmental spending lower in 2029-30 than in the March forecast. Defence investment is the exception.

headline: ECB's Knot expects core inflation and second-round effects to pick up, says ECB may more often approach 2% from above
detail: ECB Governing Council member Knot said core inflation and second-round effects are likely to rise and that small shocks lifting inflation will keep occurring. He said the ECB may more often have to approach its 2% target from above.

headline: ECB's Knot says AI will lift productivity growth and that Europe is caught up in the US-China rivalry
detail: ECB Governing Council member Knot made the remarks in further comments on 4 November. He did not give any new figures or guidance on rates.

headline: ECB's Knot says the ECB would respond with a somewhat hawkish policy as core inflation and second-round effects pick up
detail: Knot, a candidate for an ECB post, said the central bank would meet the expected rise in core inflation and second-round effects with a somewhat hawkish policy stance.

headline: UK prime minister's spokesperson says de-escalation in the Middle East is the priority
detail: The prime minister's spokesperson said the government's priority is de-escalation in the Middle East. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US ADP private payrolls rise 86,000 in October, beating the 67,000 forecast
detail: ADP data show US private employment up 86,000 in October, against a forecast of 67,000 and a previous reading of 90,000. Spot gold was reported little changed after the release.

headline: US trade deficit narrows to $105bn in September, smaller than the $107.9bn forecast
detail: US data put the September trade balance at -$105bn, against a forecast of -$107.9bn. The previous month's figure was revised to -$105.7bn from -$105.6bn.

headline: US Treasury sets quarterly refunding at $125bn, in line with estimates, and changes its guidance on future auction sizes
detail: The US Treasury set the 3-year note auction at $58bn, the 10-year note at $42bn and the 30-year bond at $25bn, and changed its guidance on future changes to auction sizes.

headline: Brent and US crude futures extend losses, down more than $2 a barrel
detail: Brent and US crude futures are reported down more than $2 a barrel as the decline extends.

headline: Iran's Larijani rules out talks with the US on war or peace and says Tehran has chosen to keep resisting
detail: Iranian reports say Larijani described the choice facing Iran in its stand-off with Washington as one between giving in and resisting, and said Iran will go on resisting. No market reaction was reported.

headline: UK October PMI shows input cost inflation picking up again, with composite output at its strongest since February
detail: Details of the S&P Global UK PMI survey for October show input cost inflation rising again and the employment component positive for the first time since the first Budget of Chancellor Reeves. The composite output index was at its highest level since February.

headline: WTI crude falls 3% to $93.25 a barrel
detail: US WTI crude futures are reported down 3% at $93.25 a barrel, adding to the day's earlier oil price losses.

headline: Houthis say they fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh's King Khalid airport; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed
detail: A Houthi spokesperson in Yemen says the group launched a ballistic missile at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and urges international airlines not to fly over Saudi airspace. There is no Saudi confirmation.

headline: Turkey's parliament is due to ratify a defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan that includes a collective defence clause
detail: Reuters reports that Turkey's parliament is set to ratify the pact on Wednesday, which would commit Turkish forces to Saudi Arabia's defence while the kingdom faces attacks from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.

headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas hopes the new US Congress keeps backing Ukraine and keeps up pressure on Russia
detail: Responding to the US midterm results, EU foreign policy chief Kallas said US voters had made a clear choice. She said she hoped the new Congress and Senate would keep supporting Ukraine and add pressure on Russia.

headline: US final October S&P Global composite PMI falls to 55.9, below the 57.3 forecast and down from 57.6
detail: S&P Global's final US composite PMI for October came in at 55.9, against a forecast of 57.3 and a previous reading of 57.6.

headline: US final October S&P Global services PMI is revised down to 56.1 from a 57.9 flash
detail: S&P Global's final October US services PMI came in at 56.1, against a forecast and flash reading of 57.9 and 58.8 in September. The composite PMI is 55.9, down from a 57.6 flash and 58.4 in September.

headline: UK new car sales rise 26.9% y/y in October to 154,407 units
detail: Figures from New AutoMotive put total UK new car sales in October at 154,407 units, an increase of 26.9% on a year earlier.

headline: US ISM services PMI eases to 54.5 in October, just below the 54.8 forecast; prices paid falls to 73
detail: The ISM services index came in at 54.5, down from 54.9 and below the 54.8 forecast. Prices paid fell to 73 from 74.0 (74.6 forecast), new orders dropped to 55.9 from 59.8 (58.5 forecast) and employment rose to 51.4 from 50.1 (50 forecast).

headline: Canada's trade surplus widens to C$5.35bn in September, its highest since May 2022
detail: Canadian data released on Wednesday show the September trade surplus at C$5.35 billion ($3.83 billion), Reuters reports. Gold and higher energy exports, mainly to the United States, drove the rise.

headline: US Vice President Vance says the war was the reason Republicans lost the midterms, and the Israel relationship was another
detail: Vance said the war was the main reason for the Republican defeat in the US midterm elections and named the relationship with Israel as a further reason. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Brent crude drops below $100 a barrel for the first time since 7 October
detail: Brent crude futures fell below $100 a barrel, the first time since 7 October, according to market reports. The fall extends the oil price losses that followed the US midterm results.

headline: France's 10-year government bond yield extends its fall, down 12.5bp at 4.80%
detail: A market newswire reports that France's 10-year government bond yield fell further, to 4.80%, a drop of 12.5bp on the day.

headline: Brent and US crude futures extend their slide to more than $4 a barrel
detail: Market reports at 16:07 GMT show Brent and US crude futures each down by more than $4 a barrel on the day. Earlier in the session the losses were above $2.

headline: Brent crude futures extend their slide to more than $5 a barrel
detail: Market reports say Brent crude futures are now down more than $5 a barrel on the day. Earlier in the session the fall was more than $4.

headline: UK 10-year gilt yield drops 12bp to 5.143%, its lowest since 4 September
detail: The 10-year gilt yield was reported down 12bp at 5.143%, its lowest level since 4 September. This extends the earlier fall that took it 5bp lower to 5.21%.

headline: Swiss Federal Council adopts the EU's 21st package of sanctions on Russia
detail: Switzerland's Federal Council has adopted the EU's 21st Russia sanctions package.

headline: European gas prices fall by as much as 5.3% to €86.74/MWh
detail: European gas prices fell by as much as 5.3% to €86.74 per megawatt hour on Wednesday, according to a market report.

headline: Canada says the US midterm results will not change its position in trade talks with the US
detail: According to Reuters, a senior Canadian cabinet minister said on Wednesday that Ottawa's stance on trade talks with the US is unchanged after the midterms. He added that he expects to speak to his US counterparts soon.

headline: Brent crude futures extend their slide to more than $7 a barrel; US crude falls more than $5 to near $90
detail: Market reports show Brent crude futures down by more than $7 a barrel and US crude futures down by more than $5 a barrel. US crude is reported trading near $90 a barrel as the oil sell-off deepens.

headline: Brent crude falls to $95 a barrel, down 10% from Friday
detail: An economist reports that Brent crude is at $95 a barrel, 10% lower than on Friday, as the slide following the US midterm results continues.

headline: US Treasury announces new sanctions related to Iran
detail: The US Treasury Department posted new Iran-related sanctions on its website. No further details were given in the report.

headline: House Democratic leader Jeffries says Democrats will pass a bill to stop Trump's tariffs and end the Iran war
detail: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries made the pledge after the Democrats won control of Congress in the midterms. He also said he had not heard from Trump.

headline: US Treasury advisory committee finds AI-linked corporate borrowing is not crowding out demand for Treasuries
detail: The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee reached this view at its latest meeting, Reuters reports. The committee also cautioned that the AI financing boom is still at an early stage.

headline: OBR's David Miles names fiscal drag as one of three main causes of near-stagnant UK household income growth this decade
detail: David Miles of the Office for Budget Responsibility said frozen income tax thresholds, which pull more people into higher tax bands, are one of three main reasons that growth in UK households' disposable income is close to stagnant in the current decade, City A.M. reports.

headline: Brent crude slides 10% to near $93 a barrel, its lowest in two months
detail: Brent crude is reported down 10% at close to $93 a barrel, its lowest level in two months, as the oil sell-off extends through the session.

headline: US Treasury's OFAC warns industry about vessels that may be falsely flagged and names a Turkey-based firm in Iran sanctions
detail: As part of its latest Iran-related sanctions, the US Treasury designated Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services for supporting Iran's aviation sector. Its Office of Foreign Assets Control also issued a new alert to industry on the risks of dealing with vessels that may be falsely flagged.

headline: US Treasury sanctions 4 India-based individuals and 9 companies for supporting Iran's shadow fleet
detail: The US Treasury says the 4 individuals and 9 companies, all based in India, are being sanctioned for supporting Iran's shadow fleet. It is part of the Iran sanctions action announced earlier today, which also included a warning that falsely flagged vessels have no valid protection or insurance.

headline: Trump agrees the Republican midterm defeat was largely down to the Iran war
detail: US President Trump says it is largely true that the Republicans lost the midterm elections because of the Iran war. Earlier, Vice President Vance gave the same reason.

headline: China's Xi says the Gulf should not become an arena for great-power rivalry as Beijing steps up its Iran war diplomacy
detail: According to Semafor, Chinese President Xi made the remarks as China increases its diplomatic efforts in the Gulf over the Iran war.

headline: Trump says the US will keep up its Iran campaign and that it was worth the midterm cost, as Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon
detail: In unscheduled remarks at the White House, President Trump said the action against Iran had been necessary and would continue. He said the war was worth it because Iran could not be allowed a nuclear weapon, and that he would probably get along with the Democrats unless they set out to be destructive.

headline: Trump says he would not have changed anything on Iran and the war will end when he decides, but any end has to be right
detail: Speaking on 4 November, the US President said he had not promised the Iran war would end straight after the midterm elections. He said he would have done nothing differently on Iran.

headline: Arab diplomatic sources report significant progress in US-Iran negotiations, with the direction expected to be clearer on Friday
detail: Lebanese broadcaster Al-Jadeed cited Arab diplomatic sources on 4 November. The report has not been officially confirmed.

headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent pledges sanctions on anyone who keeps supporting the Iranian regime by land, sea or air
detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent made the pledge in a post on X. It follows new US Treasury sanctions related to Iran announced earlier on 4 November.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says rates may rise gradually and need to go up if inflation risks spread
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said there could be a gradual increase in interest rates, and that rates would need to rise if inflation risks spread.

headline: US Treasury accepts $6B in debt buyback after receiving $39.636B of offers
detail: The US Treasury accepted 7 of 40 eligible issues in a buyback targeting coupon securities maturing from 2037 to 2046, against $39.636B of offers.

headline: ECB's Moulin says banks can cope with higher rates and the bank-sovereign loop risk has gone
detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said banks are able to handle rising rates, that a doom loop between banks and sovereigns is no longer a risk, and that France must solve its financial problems itself rather than rely on Frankfurt. He also said he is sceptical of the French government's plan to raise the cap on regulated savings.

headline: WTI crude futures settle 8.29% lower at $88.12 a barrel, down $7.97
detail: December NYMEX WTI crude futures settled at $88.12 a barrel, down $7.97 or 8.29% on the day. December gasoline futures settled at $2.7286 a gallon and diesel at $4.2055 a gallon.

headline: Brent crude futures settle 8.67% lower at $94.62 a barrel, down $8.98
detail: Brent crude futures closed the session at $94.62 a barrel after an $8.98 fall, or 8.67%. Earlier in the day, WTI settled 8.29% lower at $88.12.

headline: Brent crude futures settle at their lowest level since 31 August
detail: Brent futures settled at their lowest since 31 August, after the day's 8.67% fall to $94.62 a barrel.

headline: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is faltering as US fuel supplies hit a 20-year low, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Trump administration's diesel arrangement with Russia is stalling while US fuel supplies are at their lowest in 20 years.

headline: Trump rules out scaling back his tariffs after the midterms, citing 3,000 plants under construction
detail: In a CNBC interview, US President Trump said he would not pare back his tariffs, arguing that removing them would halt building at 3,000 plants now under construction. He also said he could work with Democrats on financial ideas, but declined to comment on a cap on credit card rates.

headline: US stocks and bonds rally after the midterm elections while oil prices fall
detail: A US market wrap reports US equities and bonds both gaining after the midterm election results as oil prices slid. No yield figures were given.

headline: BoJ September minutes show members agreed the bank should keep raising its policy rate and reducing monetary easing
detail: Minutes of the Bank of Japan's September meeting show one member favoured moving the policy rate closer to its target relatively soon, and another said hikes would need to speed up if prices showed signs of deviating upward. Many members said rising crude oil prices kept upside risks to prices high, and several noted underlying CPI inflation had been close to 2% lately.

headline: White House sets 14 December hearing on mortgage fraud allegations against Fed Governor Cook, NYT reports
detail: Citing an unnamed White House official, the New York Times reported that the hearing is a new step in President Trump's effort to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.

headline: SNB chairman Schlegel says the SNB will not hesitate to change policy if price stability is at risk
detail: Swiss National Bank chairman Schlegel said Swiss inflation rose, with the October figure above expectations. He said there have been no major second-round effects so far but they cannot be ruled out later, and the SNB will watch them closely.

headline: 20-year JGB yield falls 2bp to 3.64% as long-dated Japanese yields retreat after the drop in oil
detail: Long-dated Japanese government bond yields fell after the drop in oil prices, according to the WSJ. Asia-Pacific equities opened mostly higher after the US rally, while Treasury yields and oil moved lower.

headline: US Treasuries firm and the dollar weakens as lower oil prices ease inflation concerns; US 10-year yield at 4.88%
detail: A market wrap reports that falling oil prices after the US midterms supported Treasuries and weighed on the dollar, with the US 10-year yield at 4.88% in early Asian trading.

headline: Sterling edges higher above 1.3450 against the dollar ahead of today's Bank of England decision
detail: Sterling posted modest gains in Asian trading and was holding above 1.3450 against the dollar before the Bank of England's rate announcement due later today.

headline: Dollar index falls 0.26% to 101.21 in Asian trading, and the euro gains 0.25% to $1.1257
detail: The dollar extended its losses in Asian hours on Thursday as oil and chip stocks came under pressure following the US midterm results. The euro rose 0.25% to $1.1257 and the New Zealand dollar gained 0.60% to $0.5656.

headline: Bank of Thailand governor says 2% growth is below a sustainable pace and growth may slow in early 2027
detail: Thailand's central bank chief said economic growth of 2% is not enough to be sustainable. He added that growth may ease in early 2027.

headline: FT survey of economists puts UK inflation peak at 4.4% in 2027, with typical energy bills up nearly £470 in January
detail: An FT survey of economists shows UK inflation peaking at 4.4% in 2027. The FT also reports that typical household energy bills are expected to rise by nearly £470 in January, to about £2,200 a year.

headline: Russia steps up military support for Iran with a missile launcher deal, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that Moscow has increased its military aid to Tehran, including a deal on missile launchers, even though the Ukraine war is putting strain on its resources.

headline: Sterling slips against the yen ahead of today's Bank of England decision
detail: FXStreet reports that sterling is weaker against the yen in early trading before the Bank of England's policy announcement. No figures were given.

headline: German industrial orders rise 4.4% m/m, just short of the 4.5% forecast, after a 10.6% fall
detail: German industrial orders rose 4.4% month on month, against a forecast of 4.5%. The previous reading was a fall of 10.6%.

headline: Swedish CPIF inflation slows to 1.1% y/y in October, below the 1.4% forecast; CPI eases to 0.9%
detail: Statistics Sweden data show CPIF inflation down from 1.5%, against a 1.4% forecast, and flat on the month against an expected 0.3% rise. Headline CPI fell to 0.9% from 1.1% (forecast 1.2%), and CPIF excluding energy slowed to 0.1% y/y from 0.5%, with a 0.2% fall on the month.

headline: SNB chairman Schlegel says no significant second-round inflation effects have been seen so far
detail: Swiss National Bank chairman Martin Schlegel said significant second-round effects have not yet appeared. He also said the SNB would step in if price stability were threatened.

headline: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser says the board had very lively debates at its last meeting and members were not cornered
detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Hauser described the board as diverse, with very lively discussion at the last meeting. He rejected the view that board members are being driven into a corner at meetings.

headline: SNB chairman Schlegel says early signs point to the Swiss economy still growing
detail: Swiss National Bank chairman Schlegel said initial indications are that the Swiss economy continues to grow, according to remarks reported by HZ.

headline: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser says inflation is too high on every measure
detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said inflation is too high whichever measure is used. The remark follows his earlier comments on the board's last meeting.

headline: Oil holds on to its losses in early trading and is down almost a fifth this week
detail: The FT reported that oil prices held their losses on Thursday morning, leaving them down almost a fifth over the week, ahead of today's Bank of England decision.

headline: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser says consumption growth has been stronger than expected
detail: RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said consumer spending growth has held up better than the bank anticipated. He also said the bank had not tried to steer market expectations through open-mouth operations.

headline: French industrial production falls 0.5% m/m, missing the 0.3% rise forecast, after a 0.3% drop
detail: France's industrial production fell 0.5% month on month. The forecast was for a 0.3% rise, and the previous month showed a 0.3% fall.

headline: China says buying more US farm goods depends on both sides putting reciprocal tariff cuts into effect
detail: On Thursday China's Commerce Ministry said it is open to buying more US agricultural products, but only once both sides finalise and carry out reciprocal tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods each way.

headline: Swiss unemployment rate holds at 3.1% seasonally adjusted in October, in line with forecast
detail: The seasonally adjusted Swiss unemployment rate was 3.1%, matching both the forecast and the previous reading. The unadjusted rate was unchanged at 3.0%, also in line with forecast.

headline: ECB's Schnabel warns non-bank finance growth and higher public debt could threaten monetary dominance
detail: ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said the rise of non-bank finance and increased public debt could threaten monetary dominance. She also said returning public finances to a sustainable path has become harder.

headline: ECB's Schnabel says getting public finances back to a sustainable level has become harder; ECB will slowly build a long-term bond portfolio
detail: ECB Executive Board member Schnabel also said the ECB will build a long-term securities portfolio slowly once its legacy holdings have run down enough. She added that banks should again be able to use central bank loans without stigma.

headline: ECB's Moulin says French budget uncertainty is adding to the rise in bond yields and France must adopt a budget by year-end
detail: ECB official Moulin said higher yields are a new test for the financial sector and could weigh on the economy. He said it is essential for France to adopt a budget by the end of the year.

headline: German Chamber of Commerce raises 2026 German GDP growth forecast to 1% from 0.3%, and sees 1% growth in 2027
detail: The German Chamber of Commerce now forecasts German GDP growth of 1% in 2026, up from its previous 0.3%. It forecasts growth of 1% for 2027.

headline: Norges Bank holds its key policy rate at 4.5%, in line with forecasts
detail: Norway's central bank kept its key policy rate at 4.5%, matching the forecast and the previous setting. The decision came ahead of the Bank of England's announcement later today.

headline: Italian retail sales rise 0.1% m/m, slightly above the 0.05% forecast, after a 0.3% gain
detail: On a non-seasonally adjusted basis, Italian retail sales grew 1.6% year on year, up from 0.5% the month before.

headline: South Korea is reported to be considering purchases of long-dated US Treasuries
detail: A market news account reports that South Korea is weighing buying long-term US government debt. No size or timing was given.

headline: UK construction PMI drops to 43.6 in October, well below the 46.5 forecast, from 46.1
detail: The UK construction PMI came in at 43.6, against a forecast of 46.5 and a previous reading of 46.1. It was released ahead of today's Bank of England decision.

headline: Saudi Arabia issues civil defence alerts warning of potential danger in Yanbu
detail: Saudi authorities warned of potential danger in Yanbu, and the Saudi civil defence said it had issued alerts there. No further details were given and no market reaction was reported.

headline: Sterling heads for a seventh straight daily gain against a weaker dollar before the Bank of England decision
detail: Reuters says sterling is on course for its seventh consecutive daily rise against the dollar. Investors are holding back ahead of the Bank of England policy announcement later on Thursday.

headline: Bank of Korea and South Korean government to buy at least tens of billions of dollars of US Treasuries, Korean media report
detail: Korean media report that the purchases are meant to significantly increase South Korea's foreign exchange reserves, currently $443.1 billion. The total is expected to be at least tens of billions of dollars.

headline: RBA official warns public confidence in the bank's ability to control inflation is slipping
detail: A senior Reserve Bank of Australia official said on Thursday that public trust in the RBA's inflation fight is eroding, and that losing it could make bringing down inflation more costly, Reuters reports.

headline: Japan's PM Takaichi tells Macron that Japan has grave concern over the EU's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act
detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi raised Japan's concern about the EU's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act in a teleconference with French President Macron. She asked France to respond appropriately.

headline: Eurozone producer prices rise 2.5% m/m, matching forecast, after a 1.9% increase
detail: Eurozone PPI rose 2.5% month on month, in line with the 2.5% forecast and up from 1.9% previously.

headline: Eurozone producer prices rise 11.1% y/y in September, above the 10.6% forecast, up from 8.2%
detail: Eurozone PPI for September rose 11.1% year on year, against a forecast of 10.6% and 8.2% previously. The monthly rise was 2.5%, in line with forecasts.

headline: Kremlin says Russian diesel will find buyers as tankers change course, declining to discuss commercial matters
detail: The Kremlin said Russian diesel will find buyers when asked about tankers carrying it changing course, and said it could not discuss commercial issues. The remarks follow reports that the US diesel deal with Russia is faltering.

headline: Kremlin says military action in Ukraine will go on because peace efforts have stalled, though Russia still wants a peaceful outcome
detail: The Kremlin said Russia would protect its interests either militarily or through peace, if Kyiv shows political will. It added that safeguarding Russia's interests cannot depend on events in the United States after the US elections.

headline: Oman and Iran foreign ministers discuss securing sea routes and keeping trade and energy flowing
detail: Oman's state news agency ONA reported the foreign ministers said the focus should move from de-escalation to lasting agreements. They also discussed measures to keep trade and energy flowing.

headline: Oman and Iran foreign ministers call for moving beyond de-escalation towards lasting agreements
detail: Oman's state news agency ONA reports the two foreign ministers held a phone call. They discussed arrangements to secure sea routes and keep trade and energy flowing, and stressed a shift from de-escalation to durable deals.

headline: ECB's Zigman sees a fairly high likelihood of a rate rise in December but says the extent of further tightening is still unclear
detail: ECB Governing Council member Zigman said there is a sizeable chance that rates are raised in December. He added that it is too early to judge how much more tightening will be needed.

headline: Italy is set to approve reimbursements for gas-fired power plants to bring down electricity costs
detail: A newswire headline reports that the Italian government is preparing to approve the reimbursement measure for gas plants to reduce power costs. No figures were given.

headline: US Challenger job cuts come in at 43.994K, up from 43.281K
detail: The Challenger report puts announced US layoffs at 43.994K, compared with 43.281K in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

headline: European Commission pays €4.36bn to Ukraine from its €90bn support loan
detail: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the €4.36bn payment as Ukraine goes into its fifth winter of the war. She said EU support will continue alongside efforts to reach a peace settlement.

headline: Iraq's government is reported to be closing several of its border crossings with Iran
detail: Reports say the Iraqi government has announced that it is closing several border crossings with Iran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4.0% from 3.75%, in line with forecasts
detail: The consensus forecast was 4.0%.

headline: All nine MPC members vote to hike: eight back 25bp to 4.0%, Mann dissents in favour of a 50bp rise
detail: The Bank of England's vote was 8-1 for the move to 4.0%, with Mann preferring 50bp, against a Reuters poll forecast of 7-2. No member voted to hold or cut; the FT reports it is the first rise in borrowing costs since 2023.

headline: BoE changes its guidance and will now assess the evidence at each meeting, adjusting Bank Rate as necessary
detail: The Bank says most members judged policy to be still restrictive and that stronger than expected activity data added to the case for tightening. It says the risk of second-round effects has risen since September, though evidence of them from higher energy prices remains limited, and members still disagree on how much slack there is in the economy.

headline: BoE Monetary Policy Report sees CPI peaking around 5% in Q2 2027 and back at 2% by Q3 2028
detail: In its central projection the Bank raises its 2027 growth forecast to 1.3% from 1.1% and expects GDP growth to fall back in the coming quarters. It estimates the Budget will lower inflation by 0.25 percentage points by Q2 2027, with that effect reversing a year later, and will lift demand by 0.1% in 2026-27 before dragging on it by a little over 0.1% by 2029-30.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli, Pill and Greene point to further rate rises; Bailey calls current restrictiveness broadly appropriate
detail: Lombardelli and Pill see a case for another hike in the near term, with Pill reported as saying one 25bp rise is unlikely to be enough, and Greene says more hikes will likely be needed. Lombardelli says the price effects of the energy shock are larger and more persistent, Mann says second-order effects are now more robust, and Governor Bailey says part of the rise in the market curve reflects risk premia rather than expected rates.

headline: Traders add to BoE tightening bets after the decision, pricing a 35% chance of a December hike
detail: Money markets increased bets on further Bank of England rate rises after the decision and now price a 35% probability of another hike in December.

headline: BoE cuts its unemployment projections and raises its private-sector wage growth path from July
detail: The Monetary Policy Report sees unemployment at 4.8% in 2026, 4.9% in 2027 and 5.1% in 2028, against 5.0%, 5.3% and 5.2% in July. Private-sector regular pay growth is seen at 3.2% y/y in Q4 2026, 3.5% in Q4 2027 and 3.4% in Q4 2028 (July: 3.0%, 3.1%, 3.1%), and real post-tax labour income growth at -0.1% in 2026, -0.6% in 2027 and 1.0% in 2028 (July: 0.1%, 0.5%, 1.1%).

headline: BoE adverse scenario has CPI inflation peaking at 6.2% in Q3 2027
detail: The adverse scenario in the Bank of England's November Monetary Policy Report shows CPI peaking at 6.2% in Q3 2027.

headline: BoE forecasts are conditioned on market rates implying Bank Rate of 4.9% in Q4 2027
detail: According to the Monetary Policy Report, market rates imply Bank Rate at 3.9% in Q4 2026, 4.9% in Q4 2027, 4.9% in Q4 2028 and 4.7% in Q4 2029.

headline: BoE's Taylor and Dhingra describe the rate hike as insurance against worse inflation outcomes
detail: MPC members Alan Taylor and Swati Dhingra said the increase in Bank Rate serves as insurance against inflation turning out worse, according to remarks published with the decision.
