headline: Germany's Merz warns 'Made in Europe' rules could disrupt competition and says EU trade tools must not erode competitiveness
detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said EU 'Made in Europe' requirements could disrupt competition, and that EU trade instruments should not weaken Europe's competitive edge. No market reaction was reported.

headline: BoE's Bailey says the impact of the Iran conflict needs to be limited
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said the impact of the conflict in Iran must be contained. He spoke on the day the Bank raised Bank Rate to 4.0%.

headline: BoE's Bailey says domestic inflation pressures that were already present remain high
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said underlying domestic inflation pressures that predate the latest shock are still elevated. He made the remarks after the MPC raised Bank Rate to 4.0%.

headline: BoE's Bailey says economic activity has proved more resilient than expected and business investment has grown more than forecast
detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remarks after today's rate decision, alongside comments on limiting the impact of the Iran conflict and on high domestic inflation pressures.

headline: SNB's Schlegel says the policy rate is the main tool, with FX intervention used if necessary
detail: The Swiss National Bank chairman also said Switzerland is highly exposed to external shocks and the franc has relatively strong safe-haven properties.

headline: BoE's Bailey says a further rise in Bank Rate may be warranted unless there is progress towards resolving the conflict
detail: At his press conference after the hike, the Governor said market pricing for more tightening next year mostly reflects risk premia rather than expected rates, which he called a fair reflection of energy risks. He welcomed the latest fall in oil prices and said good news on the conflict would mean CPI peaking somewhat below 5%.

headline: Brent fell almost 7% on Wednesday after US Vice President Vance blamed the war for Republican midterm losses
detail: An economist reported that Brent dropped almost 7% after the Vice President's social media post, which linked the steep Republican losses at the midterms to the war.

headline: BoE's Bailey says the rate decision would have been the same even with knowledge of the past 48 hours' events
detail: The Bank of England Governor said news over the last 48 hours has an important bearing on the outlook, but the decision would not have changed. He added that a peace process would be welcome and would bring energy prices down.

headline: BoE's Bailey says he does not believe the Bank has moved too late
detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remark after the MPC raised Bank Rate to 4.0% from 3.75%.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli says eurozone inflation data show the UK is not alone in its exposure to energy prices
detail: The Bank of England Deputy Governor made the comment after the MPC's decision to raise Bank Rate to 4.0%.

headline: Oil heads for its biggest weekly fall since the pandemic, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters says the drop follows a Democratic sweep of Congress in the US midterm elections.

headline: BoE's Bailey rejects a 'two and done' rates outlook and sees a case for another 25bp hike if the war does not end
detail: Bank of England Governor Bailey said he would not commit to a two-hike path and that, without an end to the war, he can see the argument for a further 25bp rise. He added that conditions are too volatile to rely on two days of news that has not been backed by a clear move towards a peace process.

headline: BoE's Ramsden says the decline in UK services inflation appears to have slowed or stopped
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Ramsden said the downward trend in UK services price inflation looks to have slowed or halted.

headline: Banks take £142.8bn in the Bank of England's short-term repo operation
detail: Banks borrowed £142.8bn through the Bank of England's short-term repo operation on 5 November.

headline: SNB's Schlegel says the central bank does not believe in using forward guidance
detail: Swiss National Bank Chairman Schlegel said the SNB does not favour giving forward guidance.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli says public-sector pay is not a particular risk and the minimum wage rise is at or below expectations
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Lombardelli said the minimum wage increase was in line with or below expectations and that public-sector wages were not a particular risk. She added that consumer-facing firms report less pricing power than business-to-business firms. She spoke on the day of the Bank's rate decision.

headline: BoE's Bailey says he hopes the Bank will know more about the war's outcome by December
detail: Bank of England Governor Bailey said he hoped more information on how the war turns out would be available by the December meeting. He spoke on the day the Bank raised Bank Rate.

headline: BoE's Bailey backs greater trade and openness with the EU and links above-target inflation to very large supply shocks
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said he favours greater trade and openness when asked about closer ties with the EU. Asked about UK inflation staying above target, he said the economy has been dealing with very big supply shocks.

headline: US initial jobless claims fall to 189K in the week to 31 October, below the 196K forecast
detail: US initial claims fell by 6K to 189K, and the previous week was revised to 195K. Continuing claims for the week to 24 October rose by 23K to 1.718M, against a 1.71M forecast.

headline: SNB's Schlegel says Swiss inflation is mainly confined to fuel and energy, with no sign of broader price pressures
detail: SNB Chairman Schlegel said current Swiss inflation is mostly limited to fuel and energy, and the Bank does not see price pressures broadening at present. He also said the SNB has the right tools to fight inflation in future.

headline: Iran, Saudi and Qatari foreign ministers discuss progress in diplomatic efforts towards regional stability
detail: An Iranian statement said Iran's foreign minister spoke by phone with his Saudi and Qatari counterparts. According to the statement, they discussed the latest progress in diplomatic efforts to bring stability to the region.

headline: US Q3 productivity rises 3.6%, beating the 2.7% forecast, while unit labour costs fall 0.7% against a 0.4% rise expected
detail: Preliminary Q3 figures show US productivity at 3.6%, up from 1.4% previously, and unit labour costs at -0.7%, down from 1.2%. Treasury yields were reported as holding steady after the data, with the 10-year up 1.04bp at 4.902% and the 2-year up 3.31bp at 4.614%.

headline: Fed's Hammack says policy must move to a restrictive stance and favours gradual rate hikes to return inflation to 2%
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said inflation has been too high and moving in the wrong direction, and that she prefers frequent, smaller rate moves because they disrupt the economy and financial system less. She also said Fed independence is critical to bringing inflation back to 2%, and that the dollar's reserve status depends on US institutions, the rule of law and an independent Fed.

headline: Fed's Barkin calls inflation the Fed's biggest risk, puts policy near neutral and says a gradual pace makes sense
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said he expects inflation neither to speed up nor to fall for now, and that firms see broad cost pressures, starting with tariffs over the past 18 months, which they feel they must pass on. He described demand as solid and said businesses are cautious about hiring but are not yet laying staff off, that the budget deficit is sizeable, and that the policy path is clear and the question is pace.

headline: Iranian state media says two tankers hit sea mines and caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran's state broadcaster IRIB said two tankers struck mines and caught fire around midday on Thursday east of the Strait of Hormuz, and reported a rise in the number of tankers on fire in the area. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Resolution Foundation says the BoE's higher inflation forecast cuts average private-sector pay by £670 next year
detail: The Resolution Foundation said the Bank of England has raised its projected inflation peak to 4.9%. It estimates this takes £670 off the average private-sector salary next year.

headline: Fed's Barkin links productivity gains to adapting to post-pandemic labour shortages rather than to AI
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the main current driver of productivity is adaptation to the labour shortages that began during the pandemic, not AI. The remarks follow US Q3 productivity rising 3.6%.

headline: Fed's Barkin says the AI buildout has added to inflation in the near term
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the build-out of AI infrastructure has had an inflationary effect in the near term. He also said data centres lack natural local constituencies because they employ few workers.

headline: Resolution Foundation finds three in five of the richest fifth of households qualify for the £100 Household Energy Payment
detail: The Resolution Foundation says the £100 Household Energy Payment announced last week is poorly targeted. It adds that one in six of the poorest families report being unable to afford to heat their homes.

headline: Fed's Barkin says changing how often the Fed holds policy meetings would not be a big deal
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said a change in the number of policy-setting meetings would not matter much. He added that a different meeting pace would mean more data arriving before each meeting.

headline: Fed's Barkin says credit conditions in the banking sector look reassuring for now
detail: Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said on Thursday that credit dynamics in the banking sector are reassuring at present.

headline: Fed's Hammack says stablecoin use by AI agents would mark a major shift
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack commented on AI agents using stablecoins. Her remarks came on 5 November.

headline: Fed's Barkin says rate rises can weigh on demand and, over time, on oil prices
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin made the remark near the end of a Q&A session, which has since finished.

headline: Fed's Hammack says cutting FOMC meetings to six a year from eight would be a modest change
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said reducing the number of FOMC policy meetings from eight to six a year would be a modest shift. Earlier, Richmond Fed President Barkin also said changing how often meetings are held would not be a big deal.

headline: Fed's Hammack says she sees inflationary pressures spreading across the US economy
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said inflation pressures are spreading more widely through the economy. She made the comments in remarks on Thursday.

headline: Fed's Hammack sees the possibility that the US labour market is strengthening
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said she sees the labour market potentially getting stronger. She made the remark during the same appearance in which she earlier backed gradual rate rises.

headline: Iran reports three more tankers damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday
detail: Reuters reports that Iran said three more tankers had been damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. This follows earlier Iranian state media reports of two tankers hitting sea mines east of the strait.

headline: Gilt yields rise after the BoE's first rate hike in more than three years, Reuters reports
detail: Reuters reports that gilt yields rose after the Bank of England raised rates on Thursday, its first increase in over three years. The Bank said at least one more rise was likely if the US-Iran conflict continues.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says energy shock and AI pull in opposite directions and tools are still needed to stop inflation running away
detail: ECB President Lagarde said the current situation is complicated by the energy shock and AI pulling in opposite directions, and that separating supply-driven from demand-driven shocks is very difficult. She said it is still necessary to apply tools to prevent inflation from running away.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says many indicators will arrive before the December meeting
detail: ECB President Lagarde said a large amount of data will come in between now and the December policy meeting. She had also described the current situation as made difficult by the energy shock and AI pulling in opposite directions.

headline: BoE's Bailey says inflation risks lie to the upside and peace moves would bring only limited relief
detail: Bank of England Governor Bailey said the Bank is monitoring how far inflation passes through, that future decisions depend on how quickly inflation falls, and that the energy price cap currently locks in some inflation. He said the upside risks to inflation could change.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says US tariffs are unlikely to be revisited soon, though the midterm vote may affect them over time
detail: ECB President Lagarde said she does not expect US tariffs to be reconsidered right away. She said the US midterm result may have an effect on tariffs but that it would take time.

headline: ECB's Lagarde says the secondary effects of the energy price shock need watching, with demand shocks also under way
detail: ECB President Christine Lagarde said policymakers must monitor second-round effects of the energy price shock. She added that demand shocks are happening at the same time.

headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev praises the Oleshky ceasefire and says Putin values Trump's peace efforts
detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev held up the humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky as an example of what cooperation can achieve, and said Putin appreciates Trump's peacemaking efforts. Separately, there were reports that Melania Trump said she took part in planning the Oleshky humanitarian operation.

headline: BoC's Macklem hopes for lower US tariffs but says trade tensions could escalate before they improve
detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said he was optimistic that US tariffs could come down. He added that an escalation could not be ruled out before trade with the US improves.

headline: Iran's Rezaei says Tehran won't reopen the Strait of Hormuz until its seven conditions are met and won't negotiate on this
detail: Rezaei said the decision on the Strait of Hormuz is not open to negotiation. An Iranian source said that ending the war is the main focus of his talks with Russian President Putin. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran is reviewing concrete proposals on its nuclear programme, officials tell the NYT
detail: The New York Times reports, citing officials, that Iran is reviewing concrete proposals on its nuclear programme. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's Rezaei and Russia's Putin discuss ending the war, Al Mayadeen reports
detail: Al Mayadeen reports that ending the Iran war was the main focus of talks between Iranian official Rezaei and President Putin. Iran's position that the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until its seven conditions are met remains unchanged.

headline: Odds of a December Fed hike drop to 67% from above 80% as Democrats are reported to sweep Congress
detail: A market commentary account reported that, after the US midterm results, odds of a December Fed rate hike fell from above 80% to 67%. It said prediction markets now give a hold a 33% chance, the highest since mid-September.

headline: Yemen's Houthis claim an attack on King Fahd airport in Saudi Arabia's Dammam; no immediate Saudi confirmation
detail: Yemen's Houthi movement says it attacked King Fahd airport in Dammam, in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia has not immediately confirmed the claim.

headline: Iran's Rezaei says Putin pledged to do whatever it takes to end the war and condemned strikes on Iran's nuclear sites
detail: Iranian reports cite Major General Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, as saying that Russia's President Putin promised to do whatever is needed to end the war. Rezaei also said Putin condemned the bombing of Iran's nuclear sites and called the war against Iran cruel.

headline: Saudi Aramco cuts its December Arab Light official selling price for Asia to -$7/bbl
detail: Saudi Aramco has lowered the December official selling price for Arab Light crude to Asian buyers to -$7/bbl, according to a market news post.

headline: WTI crude December futures settle 2.72% higher at $90.52 a barrel
detail: NYMEX WTI December futures rose $2.40 to settle at $90.52 a barrel. NYMEX December diesel settled at $4.3519 a gallon and gasoline at $2.7634 a gallon.

headline: Trump blames the Republican midterm defeat on the Iran war but says he would make the same decision again
detail: Semafor reports that President Trump blamed the Republicans' midterm losses on the Iran war while saying he would do it again. Semafor also reports that traders saw the Democrats' wins as lowering the risk of escalation between Washington and Tehran.

headline: Brent crude futures settle 3.88% higher at $98.29 a barrel
detail: Brent futures settled up $3.67 at $98.29 a barrel on Thursday, a 3.88% gain on the day.

headline: Iran says it has sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatar, which the US is now reviewing
detail: A senior Iranian official said the proposal was passed on through Qatar and will be discussed only once the US meets Iran's seven demands. The official added that Washington is reviewing it.

headline: China urges the US and EU to reconsider tariffs on Chinese goods as its exports hit record highs
detail: Beijing said it would buy more US farm goods, but only if both sides agreed to make deep cuts to tariffs, Semafor reports.

headline: Canada projects a C$62.3bn federal deficit for 2026-27
detail: Canada's federal deficit is projected at C$62.3bn for the 2026-27 fiscal year, according to a market newswire report.

headline: Canada plans C$611bn of borrowing in 2027/28, including C$316bn in bonds, and lowers its GDP growth forecasts
detail: Canada's 2026 budget puts 2027/28 borrowing at C$611bn, up from C$587bn in 2026/27, with C$316bn in bond issuance, C$290bn in Treasury bills and 72% going to refinance maturing debt. It projects a 2027/28 deficit of C$62.5bn, has debt-to-GDP peaking at 40.4% in 2028/29, and cuts growth forecasts to 1.0% for 2026 and 1.7% for 2027.

headline: Trump says Iran is doing nothing without US approval and says he will take many actions over the next couple of weeks
detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Thursday evening while asked about Iran. He gave no details of what the actions would be.

headline: Trump says the US must choose between going further on Iran and certifying the current position
detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Thursday evening about Iran. The post did not say exactly what would be certified, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says he met Putin envoy Dmitriev and a Russia-Ukraine settlement is very close, in a deal involving all of Europe
detail: US President Trump said he met Russia's Dmitriev on Thursday and that the US is very close to settling the Russia-Ukraine war. He said the deal would be a big agreement involving all of Europe.

headline: US Treasury yields fall 6bp to 4.83% as a tech stock rout drives a flight to safety
detail: Treasury yields fell six basis points to 4.83% as selling spread to other markets after the Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.4% and the S&P 500 fell 4.4%. The selloff was linked to fears of AI regulation, slower data-centre investment and weak outlooks from Qualcomm and Arm.

headline: US envoy Kushner says the US will host the first US-Ukraine-Russia peace talks since February in Abu Dhabi next week
detail: US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington will convene the three-way talks with Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi next week. They would be the first such trilateral talks since February.

headline: Iran says its nuclear proposal to the US will be discussed only once Washington meets Tehran's seven demands
detail: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday that the proposal went to the United States via Qatar. The official said talks on it depend on the US first meeting Iran's seven demands.

headline: Japan's September total cash earnings rise 4.6% year on year, above the 3.8% forecast
detail: Japanese government data show September cash earnings up 4.6% year on year, against a 3.8% forecast and 3.8% previously. Real wages rose 2.2% and overtime pay rose 3.6%.

headline: 10-year JGB futures rise 0.9 point in early trade as Nikkei futures fall 7%
detail: Benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond futures gained 0.9 point in early Tokyo trade while Nikkei average futures fell 7%. South Korea's KOSPI dropped 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker that halted trading for 8 minutes.

headline: Japan's 2-year yield falls 6bp to 1.795% and China's 10-year yield hits a record low as the Asian tech sell-off deepens
detail: The 2-year JGB yield fell 6bp to 1.795% and China's 10-year yield fell to a record low. South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 8%, which set off a 20-minute trading halt, and the Nikkei was down 6.72%, 20% below its June peak.

headline: Japan's PM Takaichi wants proceeds from the BoJ's faster ETF sales to fund spending on economic security
detail: Takaichi said the proceeds could cover bond payments, allowing the government to fund public investment. In the same remarks she said she is watching the global market turbulence closely and that it is unclear whether the falls in AI and chip shares will be temporary.

headline: South Korea's finance minister pledges proactive steps to calm markets, including easing rules on borrowed investment
detail: South Korea's finance minister said the stock market is overreacting to external factors and that further stabilising measures will follow if volatility rises. The KOSPI fell below 5,000 during the Asian tech sell-off, Yonhap reported.

headline: US Democrats are drawing up a plan to reverse Trump's tariffs on Canada, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reported the plan after Democrats' midterm election gains.

headline: Brent crude futures climb more than $2 and break above $100 a barrel
detail: Brent futures rose by more than $2 in Asian trading to go above $100 a barrel. US crude futures earlier gained $1 to $91.52 a barrel.

headline: Qatar-led mediators step up efforts to broker an interim US-Iran deal to end the war, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that regional negotiators led by Qatar are pushing harder for an interim agreement between Washington and Tehran. It also reports that Iran is celebrating the Republicans' midterm defeat.

headline: EU-China trade truce comes under threat as both sides prepare for possible escalation, SCMP reports
detail: The South China Morning Post reports that the EU and China are each getting ready for the trade dispute to escalate, which puts their truce at risk.

headline: Shanghai crude front-month futures rise 2.00% intraday to 651.20 yuan a barrel
detail: China's Shanghai crude (SC) front-month contract rose 2.00% during the session to 651.20 yuan a barrel, according to a market commentary account.

headline: German September industrial production rises 0.7% m/m, beating the -0.1% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.4%
detail: German industrial production rose 0.7% month on month in September against a forecast of -0.1%, after 2.0% the month before. Year on year, output grew 0.4% against a 1.2% forecast, down from 2.3% previously.

headline: UK house prices fall 1.2% year on year in October, Lloyds says, with the average price at £296,285
detail: Lloyds puts the average UK house price in October at £296,285, the same as its September figure, and prices were down 1.2% on a year earlier. The lender says a difficult economic backdrop is testing housing demand.

headline: Qatar's Emir and Trump hold talks on efforts to de-escalate the Middle East conflict
detail: Qatar's Emir and US President Trump discussed efforts to de-escalate in the Middle East, according to reports on Friday morning. Qatar is leading mediation towards an interim US-Iran deal.

headline: Oil falls back below $100 a barrel as the global tech sell-off deepens
detail: City AM reports oil trading below $100 early on Friday, with the FTSE 100 expected to open sharply lower after South Korea's Kospi fell more than 5% and trading on the exchange was halted. Reuters also reports an oil slide on Friday.

headline: BoE's Bailey says he does not accept that UK inflation has become endemic
detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said he disagrees that the UK has endemic inflation. The remark follows the Bank's first rate hike in more than three years.

headline: BoE's Bailey says another rate hike is possible if energy prices stay high
detail: BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said a further rate rise could come if energy prices remain elevated, and that private-sector wage growth is at the upper end of the range consistent with the inflation target. In the same remarks he said the Bank is firmly on top of cyber risks and that recent hacks show the need to understand frontier AI models well.

headline: Swiss consumer confidence falls to -44.9, well below the -35.5 forecast
detail: The seasonally adjusted Swiss consumer confidence index came in at -44.9, against a forecast of -35.5 and a previous reading of -34.

headline: Fed's Williams calls the US economy remarkably resilient and says it is an appropriate time to gather more information
detail: New York Fed President Williams said growth has strengthened, the labour market is stable and solid, and the effects of tariffs are mostly behind them. He said energy is feeding through to inflation as expected, inflation expectations are well anchored and wage growth is consistent with the 2% goal.

headline: Kremlin says European security needs discussing in a Ukraine settlement but Europe cannot agree on its representatives
detail: The Kremlin also praised recent meetings at the White House and said there is willingness to continue humanitarian work after the evacuation from Oleshky.

headline: ECB's Lane says energy inflation will feed into wage talks and price setting; expects fiscal tightening next year
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said energy inflation would shape wage negotiations and price setting across the economy. He also said fiscal policy has been looser than expected, but the ECB expects it to tighten next year and beyond.

headline: Fed's Williams says US inflation has been too high for too long and must return to 2% promptly; sees tariff effects mostly past
detail: New York Fed President Williams said growth has improved, the labour market is strong, inflation expectations are stable and wage growth is consistent with the target. He also said monetary policy takes 1-2 years to have its effect and AI has had a limited impact on prices.

headline: ECB's Lane says inflation must return to target within one to two years and financial conditions have tightened
detail: ECB chief economist Lane said monetary policy's role is to contain spillover effects and that data should be gathered until December before any decision. He also said strong exports are giving the economy a boost.

headline: Eurozone retail sales fall 0.7% m/m, missing the -0.1% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.4%
detail: Eurozone retail sales fell 0.7% month on month against a forecast of -0.1% and a previous 0.1%. Year-on-year growth was 0.4%, below the 0.6% forecast and down from 0.8% previously.

headline: EU Council agrees position to delay EU methane rules by one year to 1 January 2028
detail: The Irish presidency says the Council of the EU has agreed to push the start of the EU methane regulation back to 1 January 2028. A document seen by Reuters shows the position allows further one-year postponements if implementation is not ready.

headline: Shriti Vadera becomes external adviser to UK finance minister Healey, focusing on delivery of the UK G20
detail: A market newswire reports that Shriti Vadera has been named an external adviser to UK finance minister Healey. Her role covers delivery of the UK G20.

headline: Iran says diplomacy with the US can only progress if Washington takes practical steps, state broadcaster reports
detail: Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported that Tehran wants practical steps from the US before diplomacy between the two moves forward. The report comes as mediators led by Qatar try to broker an interim US-Iran deal.

headline: Belgian King rejects PM De Wever's resignation and tells him to restart budget negotiations at once
detail: The Belgian royal palace says the King met Prime Minister Bart De Wever and the heads of the five majority parties, then declined to accept the prime minister's resignation. He asked him to resume budget negotiations immediately to resolve the crisis.

headline: Spain puts forward former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos as its candidate for ECB president
detail: Spain's deputy prime minister announced the nomination in a letter to the Eurogroup president.

headline: UK Budget keeps the Local Housing Allowance freeze in place into 2027-28, Resolution Foundation says
detail: The Resolution Foundation says keeping the LHA freeze into 2027-28 leaves more than a million families worse off, 91% of them in the bottom half of the income distribution. It also notes that the Budget's Your First Home scheme will help a small number of renters to buy.

headline: Senior Iranian official says written US commitments on a deal are not enough and Tehran wants action before talks begin
detail: According to reports, a senior Iranian official said Iran will not start negotiations until Washington takes practical steps, and that written American commitments on the agreement do not satisfy Tehran.

headline: US and Iran move closer to a possible deal to end the war, Bloomberg reports, with Tehran open to nuclear topics once ruled out
detail: Bloomberg reports that the US and Iran are nearing a possible agreement to end the war. It says Tehran is willing to discuss nuclear issues it had previously treated as off-limits.

headline: BoE's Pill calls the rate hike pre-emptive and says the Bank will not repeat the 2022 hiking cycle
detail: BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill said there is not yet evidence of second-round effects, but energy prices are creating pipeline pressure and activity and employment are adding to demand at the margin. He also said MPC members took different views and stressed different points around the decision.

headline: BoE's Pill says nothing is baked in for rates next year and Bank Rate could hold or even fall if growth stalls
detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said the outlook becomes more uncertain from the spring and that Bank Rate could stay on hold or fall if growth stalls next year. He named the squeeze on company margins, and how firms respond to it, as the key factor.

headline: BoE's Pill says a decision on a second hike will be made in the coming weeks and the rate path from spring will depend on data
detail: BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill said there is not yet enough evidence of second-round effects, energy prices are still building pressure in the pipeline, and evidence on second-round effects will come through from spring. He also said the MPC's camps differed in emphasis on the decision and called AI-driven growth somewhat encouraging.

headline: BoE's Pill says the Bank is giving weight to pay bargaining, costs and pricing
detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said the MPC is weighing pay settlements, cost pressures and firms' pricing behaviour. He made the remarks in the same appearance in which he said rates could be held or cut if growth stalls.

headline: BoE's Pill says margins and wage setting show no evidence of second-round effects
detail: Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill said there is no evidence of second-round effects in firms' margins or in wage setting.

headline: UK PM Burnham says he is ready to take difficult decisions on benefits
detail: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he is prepared to make tough choices on benefits spending, according to a report on Friday. No specific measures or figures were given.

headline: UK PM Burnham rules out crude spending cuts and says he will not chase numbers
detail: Prime Minister Burnham said the government would not pursue crude spending cuts or chase numbers. He spoke after earlier saying he was ready to take difficult decisions on benefits.

headline: FTSE 100 drops 2% and heads for its steepest fall in more than seven months as AI worries drive a global sell-off
detail: Reuters reports that the FTSE 100 fell 2% on Friday and was on course for a weekly decline. It links the global sell-off to jitters over AI that followed the change in the US political landscape.

headline: US payrolls rise 165K in October against a 70K forecast; unemployment rate falls to 4.1%
detail: US October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 against a 70,000 forecast, after 29,000 the previous month, and two-month revisions added 84,000. The unemployment rate was 4.1% against a 4.2% forecast, and average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m and 3.1% y/y, against forecasts of 0.3% and 2.9%.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises 6.3bp to 4.898% after jobs data as traders add to December Fed hike bets
detail: US Treasury yields extended gains after the October employment report, with the 10-year yield last up 6.3bp at 4.898%. Traders were reported to be adding to bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

headline: Canada loses 4.7K jobs in October against a forecast 15K gain; unemployment rate rises to 6.7%
detail: Canadian employment fell by 4,700 in October against a forecast rise of 15,000, after a 68,300 fall the previous month. The unemployment rate rose to 6.7% from 6.5%, and average hourly earnings growth slowed to 2% y/y from 2.30%, against a 2.05% forecast.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield rises 4bp after October payrolls beat forecasts
detail: An economist reported the US 2-year yield up 4bp after the payrolls release came in above forecasts. The rise came as the sell-off in AI and tech stocks continued.

headline: Bank of Canada December hike odds fall to about 32% from 40% after weak jobs report, swaps show
detail: Swaps pricing shows the market-implied chance of a December Bank of Canada rate hike fell to roughly 32% from 40% after Canada's October jobs data.

headline: ECB considers reviewing bank lending to data centres
detail: The ECB is weighing a review of bank loans to data centres, according to a market news post on Friday afternoon. No timing or scope was given.

headline: White House adviser Hassett points to three months of strong US job growth and says inflation should be slowing
detail: In a CNBC interview, White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said he was looking at the last three months of very strong job growth and, when asked about the Fed, said inflation should be slowing. He also said an AI bubble is a fair concern, but the US economy could still be very strong even if data centre building slows.

headline: Iranian source says Tehran is responding positively to the latest proposal from mediators
detail: An Iranian source told Al Arabiya that Tehran is responding positively to the newest proposal put forward by mediators in the US-Iran talks. Separately, a senior Iranian security official repeated that Tehran wants concrete US action before a new phase of diplomacy.

headline: Fed's Musalem says public concern about current inflation persists but expectations remain anchored
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said people are still worried about inflation at its present level. He also said inflation expectations remain anchored.

headline: Fed's Musalem blames excess US inflation on energy shocks and the AI build-out; says consumption and investment are growing fast
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said inflation must come back to 2% in a timely way. He said data-centre construction is adding to strong demand and that AI will bring much higher productivity.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says Trump will decide on Fed Governor Cook after reading the report
detail: Senior White House adviser Hassett also said headline inflation is being driven by energy and Iran, and that he sees no need to plan a policy change.

headline: White House adviser Hassett says inflation is falling and he sees no policy change that needs planning
detail: The National Economic Council's Hassett said the data show strong growth and slowing inflation, that the administration's policies are working, and that the job market is firing on all cylinders.

headline: Fed's Musalem says excess US inflation comes from both supply and demand; expects AI to lift productivity sharply
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said the data centre build-out is adding to strong demand and that AI will bring much higher productivity.

headline: Fed's Musalem says clear Fed communication helps policy pass through to the economy more smoothly
detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said that good communication from the Fed leads to smoother transmission of monetary policy. The remark was part of his comments on Friday.

headline: US UMich sentiment rises to 51 in preliminary reading against a 48 forecast; 1-year inflation expectations ease to 4.3%
detail: The University of Michigan preliminary sentiment index came in at 51 against a 48 forecast and 48.0 previously; current conditions were 51 (forecast 47, previous 46.7) and expectations 50.9 (forecast 49, previous 48.8). One-year inflation expectations fell to 4.3% from 4.7% (forecast 4.6%), and five-year expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.5% (forecast 3.5%).

headline: Canada's Ivey PMI edges up to 58.3 in October from 58.2
detail: Canada's Ivey purchasing managers' index came in at 58.3 for October, against 58.2 the previous month. No consensus forecast was given.

headline: CDS on US hyperscalers and chipmakers widen to levels implying heavy ratings downgrades as the AI debt sell-off spreads
detail: IFR reports that a sharp sell-off in debt has pushed credit default swaps on US hyperscalers and chipmakers to levels consistent with large ratings downgrades, with Oracle and SpaceX swaps trading well into junk territory. Reuters separately reports that traders' focus is shifting from inflation to growth as the tech rout deepens, raising questions over room for further central bank rate hikes.

headline: Polish foreign minister says a ceasefire must come before Ukraine peace talks can begin
detail: Poland's foreign minister set a ceasefire as a precondition for starting Ukraine peace talks. The US has said it will host US-Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says the EU must be part of any Ukraine peace deal
detail: The EU's foreign policy chief said the EU would need to be involved in any peace agreement on Ukraine. Separately, Poland's foreign minister said no settlement can be imposed on Ukraine unless it agrees and takes part.

headline: European officials fear a US security deal with Russia could undermine NATO, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that European officials are concerned Washington could reach a security agreement with Moscow that weakens NATO and restores a Russian sphere of influence.

headline: EU's Kallas says Putin has no veto over European security and Ukraine must become part of its security architecture
detail: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas also said Russian sabotage across Europe must stop. She made the remarks on Friday as talks continue over a possible Ukraine settlement.

headline: Polish foreign minister Sikorski says no deal to end the war can be reached without Ukraine and Europe
detail: Poland's foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski said on Friday that an agreement on the war in Ukraine cannot be made over the heads of Ukraine and Europe. No market reaction was reported.

headline: IMF's Georgieva says central banks must look through uncertainty and weigh any slowdown in AI-driven growth in the inflation fight
detail: The IMF Managing Director said the AI investment boom and high valuations are affecting markets worldwide. She added that if the growth boost from AI slowed, central banks would need to factor that in as they decide their next steps against inflation.

headline: IMF's Georgieva flags concern over large, rising global imbalances and expects AI-related market volatility to persist
detail: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said widening global imbalances have often come with fragile growth and have sometimes preceded financial crises. She also said market volatility linked to AI is likely to continue.

headline: France has sold 3.6 million barrels of diesel from its strategic reserves so far, energy ministry says
detail: The French energy ministry said 3.6 million barrels of diesel have been released from the country's strategic reserves to date.

headline: Iranian negotiators review proposals to limit Tehran's nuclear programme, Times of Israel reports
detail: The Times of Israel, citing a US official and a diplomat, reported that Iranian negotiators are reviewing proposals to curb the nuclear programme, an issue Tehran had long refused to discuss.

headline: Proposals to Iran cover its highly enriched uranium stockpile and offer major US sanctions relief, Times of Israel reports
detail: According to a diplomat familiar with the talks, the proposals do not go as far as fully dismantling Iran's nuclear programme. They do deal with Tehran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium and would give Iran significant sanctions relief from the US, the Times of Israel reports.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says Japan's current account has shifted sharply and is now driven by income flows
detail: In a speech, the Bank of Japan Governor described a marked shift in Japan's current account, which he said is now driven by income flows. He did not comment on the economic or policy outlook.

headline: French finance minister says the diesel sale is part of a plan to release 10 million barrels from stocks
detail: France's finance minister says the diesel sold so far from strategic reserves belongs to a wider 10 million barrel stock release plan. Earlier, the energy ministry put the amount of diesel sold at 3.6 million barrels.

headline: Eurogroup names Spain's de Cos and the Netherlands' Knot as the only two candidates for ECB president
detail: The Eurogroup says former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos and the Netherlands' Klaas Knot are the two candidates to become the next ECB president. No other candidates have been put forward.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says Japan's 1990s demographic decline cut expected returns on domestic capital at home
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said Japan's demographic decline in the 1990s held down the expected return on domestic capital. He added that a severe scarcity has only become a reality in recent years.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says Japanese firms spent years repaying debt after the bubble burst, and corporate saving stayed high afterwards
detail: In further remarks, the Bank of Japan Governor said Japan's experience shows why corporate adjustment matters. He said firms cut investment and repaired their balance sheets after the bubble collapsed, and that overseas investment grew in importance once that process was largely over.

headline: BoJ's Ueda expects domestic investment in Japan to rise but says the scale is highly uncertain
detail: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said he expects domestic investment in Japan to increase, though how far it will rise is very uncertain. The remarks came during the same appearance as his earlier comments on corporate saving and the current account.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says underlying inflation in Japan has hit 2% for the first time in decades and normalisation targets price stability
detail: The Bank of Japan governor said policy normalisation is aimed at price stability. He added that once it is achieved, nominal variables will do less to get in the way of resource allocation.

headline: IMF's Georgieva says the BoJ's policy normalisation has gone impressively smoothly
detail: The IMF Managing Director praised how smoothly the Bank of Japan has normalised its monetary policy.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says 2% inflation is not yet a social norm in Japan and the Bank has heard no major complaints about higher rates
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said wages are growing at a pace consistent with 2% inflation but it is not yet known whether that balance can last a long time. He added that real rates have not risen by as much, and that much work remains on inflation.

headline: BoJ's Ueda puts Japanese consumer inflation near 3%, sees upside risks and says unconventional tools could return after big shocks
detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said consumer prices are around 3% and expected to rise further into early next year as energy-related costs feed through, with underlying inflation likely to stay around 2% but facing upside risks. He said unconventional tools have had some positive effects but are not perfect substitutes for rate cuts from positive levels, and the Bank may have to use them again in a severe shock, in a way that limits the side effects.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the Bank watches other central banks closely, calls AI a positive demand shock and flags cyber risks to financial stability
detail: The Bank of Japan Governor said other central banks' actions affect asset prices including exchange rates and interest rates, and that AI has been a positive demand shock for Japan, which may benefit from AI replacing labour given significant labour shortages. On financial stability, he named cyber risks as a concern and said the Bank has been identifying vulnerable areas, including some small banks and small firms with weak protection.

headline: BoJ's Ueda says the aim is to hold underlying inflation at 2% and that the Bank has made no formal commitment on its communication
detail: The Bank of Japan Governor said that with underlying inflation now at 2%, the goal is to keep it at that level, and that the Bank is discussing how it communicates but has no formal commitment yet. He also reported a sharp rise in cyber attacks in Japan over the past one to two months.

headline: US tells China to meet the terms of the Busan trade truce immediately; officials say Beijing has met only two-thirds of rare earth pledges
detail: US officials say China has not raised rare earth supply and has delivered on only two-thirds of its rare earth commitments. The FT reports that Washington has warned Beijing it must comply with the Busan trade truce immediately.

headline: Qatar's prime minister says the US and Iran will not be able to reach a perfect deal
detail: Qatar's prime minister commented on the US-Iran negotiations as mediators' proposals are under review in Tehran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Putin and Russia's Security Council discuss the upcoming Ukraine talks
detail: Reports say President Putin discussed the forthcoming Ukraine negotiations with Russia's Security Council. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says he and USTR Greer held talks with China's Vice Premier He Lifeng on economic ties
detail: Bessent said that during the call with He Lifeng, he and Greer pressed China to honour its commitments under the Busan arrangement in full and without delay.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine keeps striking Russia's oil sector in response to Russian attacks on energy sites
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv is continuing to target Russian oil sector facilities, in retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Canada's PM Carney says Ottawa will keep working with the US towards a trade deal that suits Canada
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Friday that Canada would carry on talks with the United States aimed at a trade agreement that works for Canada. He gave no timetable or new terms.

headline: Fed's Daly calls the October jobs report good news for US workers and says wage growth is not booming
detail: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly commented on the October payrolls report in remarks reported via CNBC. She described the report as positive for American workers and said wage growth is not running hot.

headline: Fed's Daly says further policy tightening will be needed and the solid job market gives room to finish the inflation fight
detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said she wants to be more confident on inflation and that holding at the last meeting was right given uncertainty. She called the AI repricing orderly so far, said it could ease her view slightly if it signals slower demand growth, and said businesses are cautiously optimistic.

headline: White House CEA chair Phelan says he does not expect the Fed to treat the October jobs report as inflationary
detail: Council of Economic Advisers Chair Phelan commented on the October US payrolls report on Friday.

headline: Canadian dollar falls to a near three-week low against the US dollar after an unexpected drop in October jobs
detail: Reuters reports the Canadian dollar weakened on Friday after data showed the economy lost jobs for a third month in a row. The data cooled expectations of Bank of Canada rate hikes.

headline: Fed's Daly says the recent painful market volatility amounts to the kind of rebalancing policymakers would want
detail: San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said that, looking past the painful volatility, the adjustment is the sort of rebalancing the Fed would hope to see.

headline: Canada's PM Carney says Ottawa is in talks with China on next steps for trade
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada is talking to China about the next steps in developing trade between the two countries.

headline: Fed's Daly says policy may be anywhere from slightly restrictive to neutral and services inflation is not easing as expected
detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said on Friday that US rates could sit between slightly restrictive and neutral. She added that services inflation is not falling in the way policymakers would expect.

headline: White House CEA chair Phelan says the next US CPI print will show what the Fed does next
detail: The chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers said the next US consumer price data would need to be seen before judging the Fed's next move. He made the remarks after the October jobs report.

headline: White House CEA chair Phelan says he does not foresee a US recession
detail: The chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers said on 6 November that he does not expect a recession at all. He spoke after the October US jobs report.

headline: Italy has not yet backed either the Spanish or the Dutch candidate to succeed Lagarde as ECB president
detail: Officials in Italian Prime Minister Meloni's office said on Friday that Rome has not yet chosen between the two candidates to replace Christine Lagarde as ECB president, Reuters reports.

headline: USTR Greer says China must carry out its agricultural and rare earths commitments
detail: US Trade Representative Greer said China needs to implement its pledges on agriculture and rare earths. This follows earlier US calls for Beijing to meet the terms of the Busan trade truce.

headline: Zelenskiy says intelligence points to planned Russian strikes on energy sites, Dnipro bridges and infrastructure
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said intelligence shows Russian forces are preparing new strikes on energy targets, bridges over the Dnipro river and other infrastructure. No market reaction was reported.

headline: US Treasury announces new sanctions related to Iran
detail: The US Treasury Department announced a new round of Iran-related sanctions on Friday. No details or market reaction were given in the initial report.

headline: Oil traders reportedly in talks with US over using sanctioned tankers to bring down freight costs and oil prices
detail: A market news account reported that oil traders are discussing with the US the use of tankers under sanctions, with the aim of easing freight rates and oil prices. Separately, Brent crude futures settled 3 cents higher at $98.32 a barrel.

headline: Trump says the US is in talks with Iran and has been for some time
detail: President Trump told reporters that Washington is talking to Tehran. No details of the talks or any market reaction were reported.

headline: US consumer credit rises $27.84bn in September, well above the $13.8bn forecast
detail: US consumer credit grew by $27.84bn in September, against a forecast of $13.8bn and up from $8.28bn the month before.

headline: Early Tasnim reports say two missiles struck Iran's Qeshm Island; no official confirmation yet
detail: Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency says initial reports point to two missiles hitting Qeshm Island, but officials have not confirmed this. The reports do not say who fired the missiles, and no market reaction has been reported.

headline: Iranian state broadcaster reports two blasts heard near Suza on Qeshm Island, with no casualties reported
detail: Iran's state broadcaster cited an informed source on two explosions near the Suza area of Qeshm Island and said there were no casualty reports. Earlier, Tasnim had reported two missiles striking the island without official confirmation.

headline: Iraq says it has reached understandings with the US to let its oil exports pass through Hormuz via a lane near Oman
detail: Iraq's foreign minister, Fuad Hussein, told Al Jazeera that Iraqi oil exports would use a shipping lane near Oman under the arrangement with Washington.

headline: US Treasury asks Iraq to close all but two of its border crossings with Iran, Iraqi foreign minister says
detail: Iraq's foreign minister, Fuad Hussein, told Al Jazeera that the request forms part of Washington's policy of increasing economic pressure on Tehran.

headline: Drone attack halts production at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field in the Kurdistan region
detail: Two security sources said output stopped on Sunday at the field, one of the largest in the Kurdistan region. An engineer at the site reported a fire at a gas storage facility.

headline: US Secretary of State Rubio calls Iran talks unproductive and says Tehran's demands are unacceptable
detail: Rubio said the US would pursue a diplomatic solution with Iran where one is possible but that this is not always the case. He described some Iranian demands as outrageous.

headline: Trump says Task Force Iron Gate is fully in effect in Iran and, with the naval blockade, very little moves in or out
detail: The US president posted on Truth Social that the task force is fully in effect and, together with what he called history's greatest naval blockade, very little goods get into or out of Iran.

headline: Kurdistan region says nearly 2.8 GW of power lost from the grid after the attack on Iraq's Khor Mor gas field
detail: The Kurdistan region's electricity ministry gave the figure after production at Khor Mor was halted by a drone attack. Iraqi Kurdish ministries say they are working to limit the impact, and Iraq's armed forces command reports no casualties on initial assessment.

headline: RBA's Hunter says AI demand will lift inflation in the near term and flags risk of disorderly asset repricing
detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Hunter said AI could raise financial stability risks if returns disappoint, although its long-run effect on inflation is likely to be broadly neutral. She said there is limited evidence that AI has significantly boosted productivity or employment in advanced economies.

headline: Japan's largest daily intervention in July–September was 7.98 trillion yen on 30 July, Finance Ministry data show
detail: The Finance Ministry also reported foreign reserves of $1,179.119bn at the end of October, compared with $1,178.396bn at the end of September. Benchmark 10-year JGB futures fell 0.36 point in early trade.

headline: China's October PPI rises 5.7% y/y, above the 5.3% forecast, while CPI slows to 0.7% against 0.8% expected
detail: Chinese producer prices rose 5.7% on the year in October, up from 5.0%, and 0.7% on the month after 1.2%. Consumer prices rose 0.7% y/y after 0.9% and were flat on the month; core CPI was 0.8% against 0.9% forecast and 1.0% previously.

headline: JGB yields rise across the curve, with 5-year up 6.5bp to 2.110% and 30-year up 4bp to 3.865%
detail: Japanese government bond yields climbed in Asian trading on Monday: the 5-year rose 6.5bp to 2.110%, the 20-year rose 5bp to 3.595% and the 30-year rose 4bp to 3.865%.

headline: Trump says he expects the war in Ukraine to end soon and a Ukraine of a different shape afterwards
detail: The US president made the remarks in a pre-recorded CBS 60 Minutes interview released on Sunday.

headline: China keeps its 24% extra tariff on US imports suspended for two more months, holding the 10% rate
detail: China's finance ministry says the suspension of the additional 24% tariff on US imports is extended for two months, until 10 January, while the 10% tariff stays in place. China's transport ministry separately extends its suspension of special port fees on US vessels, and its shipping and shipbuilding probe, until 10 January 2027.

headline: Iranian state TV says navigation aids in southern Hormuz are destroyed, halting transit on an unauthorised route
detail: Iranian state television, citing an unnamed Revolutionary Guards navy official, says navigation aid systems in the southern Strait of Hormuz were destroyed. It says no vessels used the unauthorised route overnight.

headline: Japan's 40-year government bond yield rises to 3.990%
detail: The 40-year JGB yield climbs to 3.990% in Asian trading on Monday.

headline: Iranian official says an overnight US strike hit Qeshm Island but left key infrastructure and services intact
detail: An Iranian provincial official, quoted by Fars News, said the overnight US strike on Qeshm Island caused no disruption to essential services. Separately, Israel's Kan broadcaster reports that Israeli and US military officials support further military action against Iran.

headline: Iran says no unauthorised vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz overnight after southern navigation aids were destroyed
detail: An unnamed Revolutionary Guards Navy official told Iranian state media on Monday that no unauthorised vessels used the route overnight, Reuters reports.

headline: ECB presidency candidate Knot says he would act without hesitation in a debt crisis
detail: Klaas Knot, one of two candidates to succeed Lagarde, told the FT he would be prepared to create new crisis-fighting tools if needed.

headline: Chinese banks sharply raise dollar deposit rates, in some cases above 4%, as Beijing seeks to slow the yuan's rally
detail: Reuters, citing sources, reports that several Chinese banks have lifted dollar deposit rates in recent weeks, in some cases above US benchmarks. Exporters are reported to be hoarding cash.

headline: Russian Foreign Ministry says the Russia-US diesel deal could allow business ties between the two countries to recover gradually
detail: TASS reported the Russian Foreign Ministry's comments on the diesel deal between Russia and the US. The ministry described the deal as an opening for a gradual restoration of business ties.

headline: German trade surplus narrows to 15.6bn, below the 19.4bn forecast, as imports jump 4.2% m/m
detail: Germany's seasonally adjusted trade balance came in at 15.6bn against a 19.4bn forecast and 19.5bn previously. Imports rose 4.2% month on month, against a 0.5% forecast and 0.9% previously.

headline: UAE's Gargash says a full US-Iran settlement looks difficult and warns of prolonged regional uncertainty
detail: Senior Emirati official Anwar Gargash said on Monday that a comprehensive political settlement to end the more than eight-month US-Iran war appeared difficult, Reuters reported.

headline: Iran's Foreign Ministry calls Tehran's two-day proposal the most reasonable offer in talks with the US
detail: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei said Iran's two-day proposal is the most reasonable one under discussion. He also said pressure should not damage Iran's ties with Iraq.

headline: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman says the US Iron Gate task force is meant to divert attention from the US midterm results
detail: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei said the US Task Force Iron Gate operation is a way of deflecting attention from the outcome of the US midterm elections. No market reaction was reported.

headline: EU Economy Commissioner Dombrovskis says the economy faces uncertainty and downside risks
detail: EU Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said on Monday morning that the economy faces uncertainty and downside risks. The reports gave no figures.

headline: China extends its suspension of export controls aimed at US companies
detail: A market news feed reported that China will extend its suspension of export controls targeting US companies. The report gave no new expiry date. It follows China's decision to keep its extra tariff on US imports suspended for two more months.

headline: German exports grow 2% m/m in September, beating expectations
detail: Germany's federal statistics office said on Monday that exports rose 2% on the month in September, more than expected.

headline: Iran's foreign minister says mediators have stopped travelling since the US midterm results
detail: Iran's foreign minister said mediators in the US-Iran talks have made no trips since the US midterm election results came out. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Spain's economy minister says he is optimistic de Cos can win the ECB presidency
detail: Spain's economy minister said he is optimistic about Spanish candidate de Cos's chances of becoming ECB president. De Cos and the Netherlands' Knot are the two candidates the Eurogroup has named.

headline: Iraq prices December Basrah Medium to Asia at a $8.80/b discount and Basrah Heavy at a $11.80/b discount
detail: Iraq has set its December official selling prices for crude sold to Asia: Basrah Medium at a discount of $8.80 a barrel and Basrah Heavy at a discount of $11.80 a barrel.

headline: Dutch finance minister says the next ECB president should be chosen on merit, not through political bargaining
detail: The Dutch finance minister said the choice of Lagarde's successor should be based on merit and kept out of political discussions. Spain and the Netherlands both have candidates in the race.

headline: Oil prices fall as Trump says further US strikes on Iran are highly unlikely
detail: City AM's markets blog reports that oil prices are lower on Monday morning after President Trump said new strikes on Iran were highly unlikely. The FTSE 100 is reported higher at the open.

headline: Kremlin says this week's Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks are a three-way meeting between Russia and Ukraine, mediated by the US
detail: Asked whether European countries could join the talks in Abu Dhabi this week, the Kremlin said the format is Russia and Ukraine with the US as mediator. It added that the US and Ukraine each have their own channels to the Europeans.

headline: Eurozone Sentix investor confidence comes in at 2.4, above the 2.05 forecast but down from 2.7
detail: The Sentix investor confidence index for the eurozone was 2.4 in the latest reading. The forecast was 2.05 and the previous reading was 2.7.

headline: Gulf stock markets rise in early Monday trade after Trump signals new US strikes on Iran are unlikely
detail: Reuters reports Gulf stock markets gained early on Monday after President Trump indicated that new strikes on Iran were unlikely while talks continue to end the eight-month conflict.

headline: Saudi Arabia lifts Riyadh alert a day after a Houthi attack damaged an Aramco office building
detail: Saudi civil defence authorities said on Monday that the danger in Riyadh had passed, minutes after raising an alert, Reuters reported. The alert came a day after an attack by Yemen's Houthis damaged an office building belonging to Saudi Aramco in the capital.

headline: Turkey's Erdogan says he told Trump on a call that Ankara opposes any new wave of attacks on Iran
detail: Turkish President Erdogan said he raised Turkey's concerns about further strikes on Iran during a call with US President Trump. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Centre for Cities report looks at Mayor of London's view that new fiscal powers could back more than £10bn of infrastructure borrowing
detail: The Centre for Cities has published analysis of how London's borrowing plans of more than £10bn would fit within national fiscal rules, and compares them with Madrid. The Mayor of London has said new fiscal powers could support that level of infrastructure borrowing.

headline: Iran reportedly drops its demand to control the Strait of Hormuz and charge transit fees, Israel Hayom says
detail: Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom reports that Iran appears to have dropped its demand to control the Strait of Hormuz and collect fees from ships passing through. There is no official confirmation from Tehran in the inputs.

headline: Brent crude falls to an intraday low below $96/bbl
detail: Brent crude falls below $96 a barrel and hits a new intraday low on Monday. Earlier in the session, prices had already fallen after Trump said further US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely.

headline: France to lift its minimum wage by 1.6% to €1,502, with the increase brought forward to 1 December
detail: France's labour minister says the government will raise the minimum wage by 1.6% to €1,502. The minister says the increase will now take effect on 1 December.

headline: Lavrov says security issues are the main topic of the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks, which aim to agree principles for a settlement
detail: Russia's Foreign Minister Lavrov said the Abu Dhabi talks will centre on security issues for Russia, Ukraine and the wider region. He said they aim to agree principles that would be approved when talks on a comprehensive settlement in Ukraine conclude.

headline: European Commission says the EU must be present in any talks on a European security framework, responding to Kushner's proposal
detail: Responding to a proposal from Kushner, the European Commission said that deciding any European security framework is a matter for the EU, so the EU needs to take part in such discussions.

headline: France extends its €1,000 fuel bonus cap into 2027, finance minister Lescure says
detail: French finance minister Lescure says the cap of €1,000 on the fuel bonus will continue into 2027. No further details were given.

headline: Canada announces more sanctions on Russia aimed at reducing its missile capabilities
detail: The Canadian government announced the additional sanctions against Russia in a statement on Monday. The statement says they are meant to reduce Russia's missile capabilities.

headline: Iranian official Bagheri says moving enriched material out of Iran is not on the agenda, Iranian reports say
detail: Iranian media reports cite Bagheri as saying that taking enriched material out of Iran is not under discussion, amid the running US-Iran talks. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iraq's prime minister puts forward proposals to end the Iran war in a phone call with Trump, sources say
detail: Sources report that Iraq's prime minister set out proposals to end the Iran war during a phone call with US President Trump. No details of the proposals were given.

headline: Trump backs Iraqi PM's proposals to end the Iran war and asks him to pass them on to Tehran
detail: Reports of a phone call between Trump and Iraq's prime minister say Trump approved the Iraqi proposals for ending the war with Iran. He also asked the prime minister to convey them to Tehran.

headline: Qatari official says the US and Iran are working through deal details with mediators and calls reports on the proposal's terms false
detail: An unnamed Qatari official said the US and Iran are in contact with mediators over the details of a deal. The same official rejected circulating reports about the content of the US-Iran proposal as false.

headline: Eurogroup President says a decision on the next ECB president should ideally be made by the end of the year
detail: The Eurogroup President said the ideal outcome would be to choose a successor to Lagarde as ECB president by the end of the year.

headline: WTI crude drops to $86.60, its lowest level since early September
detail: US crude fell as low as $86.60 a barrel in Monday trade, its lowest since early September, according to market reports.

headline: USTR pauses action on China's shipbuilding sector until 10 January 2027 and extends 178 China tariff exclusions
detail: According to a Federal Register notice, the US Trade Representative has suspended any action on China's shipbuilding and maritime sector until 10 January 2027 to allow further talks. It also said it would further extend all 178 current exclusions linked to China's technology transfer, intellectual property and innovation.

headline: French 10-year yield falls to about 4.69%, its lowest since 25 September
detail: France's 10-year government bond yield fell to around 4.69% on Monday afternoon, its lowest level since 25 September, according to a market wire report.

headline: German foreign minister says the Abu Dhabi talks must show whether Russia is really willing to negotiate
detail: Germany's foreign minister commented on this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine, saying they need to show whether Moscow is serious about negotiating. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Dallas and New York Fed launch a pilot survey of the private credit market
detail: The Federal Reserve Banks of Dallas and New York said in a statement that they opened a pilot survey of the private credit market on 9 November.

headline: Germany's Merz threatens to block the EU's next budget unless the bloc unanimously agrees more financial support for Ukraine
detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Friedrich Merz is threatening to withhold Germany's agreement on the EU's next budget unless member states unanimously agree additional funding for Kyiv. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Brent crude losses deepen to 5% on the day
detail: A market news account reports that Brent crude's decline has reached 5%. Oil had already been falling after Trump said further US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely.

headline: Kremlin's Peskov says rare earth metals are not on the agenda at the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks
detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said rare earth metals will not be discussed at this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says Russia has been pretending to negotiate and hopes for more US sanctions after the midterms
detail: Kallas says she sees no good will from Moscow and that Russia has not kept to European security arrangements it agreed in the past. She says she hopes further US sanctions will add pressure on Russia after the US midterm elections, and that the EU should lead on European security in line with its treaties.

headline: US wholesale sales rise 2.8% m/m, above the 1.1% forecast; wholesale inventories revised up to 0.7%
detail: US wholesale sales grew 2.8% month on month, against a 1.1% forecast and a previous reading of 1.8%. Wholesale inventories were revised to 0.7% m/m, against a 0.6% forecast and a previous reading of 0.6%.

headline: EU's von der Leyen backs Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks and says Black Sea freedom of navigation must be preserved and restored
detail: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she supports the Ukraine peace talks due to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. She also said again that freedom of navigation in the Black Sea must be preserved and restored.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says growth and employment are stable but the main problem has been inflation
detail: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said employment and growth look fairly steady, that the main problem has been inflation, and that policymakers have to face up to a failure on inflation.

headline: Saudi and Omani foreign ministers call for diplomatic efforts to continue to contain the regional crisis
detail: Reports say the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Oman stressed that diplomatic efforts to contain the regional crisis need to continue.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says services inflation is starting to pick up and data centre activity resembles old-style overheating
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee also said the Fed has to accept it has failed on inflation, and that consumer spending has been the main driver of growth.

headline: Resolution Foundation says three in five of the richest fifth of households qualify for the £100 Household Energy Payment
detail: The think tank says the payment is poorly targeted, and notes that one in six of the poorest families report already being unable to afford to heat their homes.

headline: Senior Iranian official says Tehran will not hold talks with the US until Washington acts on its seven conditions
detail: A senior Iranian official told Press TV that Iran's position on negotiations with the US has not changed. The official said there will be no plan for talks unless the US takes practical action on Tehran's seven conditions.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says consumer spending has been the main driver of US growth
detail: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said in remarks on Monday that consumer spending has been the main source of US growth. He also repeated that employment and growth are fairly stable.

headline: US Secretary of State Rubio urges the EU to drop preference measures and overregulation aimed at US companies
detail: The US State Department reported that Secretary of State Rubio called for the EU to end preference measures and overregulation that target US companies. The statement followed his talks with French foreign minister Barrot.

headline: Fuel shortages hit Russian regions again after Ukrainian strikes on at least eight major refineries in two weeks
detail: Reuters reports that fuel shortages have returned to parts of Russia after Ukraine struck at least eight major oil refineries over the past two weeks. The report says drivers could again face long queues at filling stations.

headline: Rosneft rations petrol sales in Russia after a run of Ukrainian strikes on refineries
detail: According to the FT, the state-owned Rosneft is limiting petrol sales to 30 litres per car in cities and 50 litres on highways. The move comes after a wave of Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries.

headline: NY Fed survey: US one-year inflation expectations edge up to 3.91% in October, three-year steady at 3.3%
detail: The New York Fed's October Survey of Consumer Expectations put one-year-ahead inflation expectations at 3.91%, against a 3.79% forecast and 3.9% previously, with three-year expectations unchanged at 3.3%. Expectations of a rising unemployment rate were the highest since April 2020, and expected gas price rises moderated.

headline: France's foreign minister blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for a cyberattack on fridges and says EU sanctions on Iran will follow
detail: French Foreign Minister Barrot said Iran's ambassador had been summoned and that there will be consequences for Iran. Earlier, Paris prosecutors said the hacks used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices in Iran, and that they were carried out to serve a foreign power.

headline: Sterling rises against the dollar, recovering most of Friday's fall as oil prices drop
detail: Reuters reports that the pound gained on Monday as concerns over AI stocks, which had lifted the dollar late last week, eased and oil prices fell.

headline: Saudi energy ministry source says the East-West oil pipeline was targeted in the Medina region
detail: Saudi state media cited an energy ministry source as saying the East-West pipeline was targeted in the Medina region. The report gave no details on damage or on any effect on flows.

headline: Saudi energy ministry source says the East-West pipeline is still operating after the attack and there are no casualties
detail: A Saudi energy ministry source said the attack in the Medina region caused a limited fire, which has since been put out, and the pipeline's operations were not affected, according to reports.

headline: EU's Kallas says she has low expectations for the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks and wants clear concessions from Russia
detail: The EU foreign policy chief said she does not expect much from the Abu Dhabi talks and that Russia needs to make clear concessions.

headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve falls to 279.5mn barrels, its lowest level since 1982
detail: Crude oil held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 279.5mn barrels last week, the lowest since 1982. The report gave no price reaction.

headline: US Treasury sells $95bn of 3-month bills at 4.06% and $82bn of 6-month bills at 4.145%
detail: The 3-month bill auction had a bid-to-cover of 2.67, down from 2.880, with 79.03% awarded at the high, compared with 4.040% at the previous sale. The 6-month bill drew a bid-to-cover of 2.92, up from 2.890, with 70.91% awarded at the high; its yield compares with 4.150% previously.

headline: Brent crude falls to a 10-week low after Trump says US strikes on Iran are highly unlikely
detail: The Financial Times reports that Brent extended last week's losses, which came after the Republicans' midterm defeat, to reach its lowest level in 10 weeks.

headline: Fed's Barkin says inflation is where the risk lies and policy should move with care despite a clear direction
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the risk sits on the inflation side of the Fed's mandate. He described the US economy as remarkably stable and said the direction of policy is straightforward but changes should be made with care.

headline: Fed's Barkin reports broad-based cost pressures, with firms planning to pass higher costs on to customers
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said resilient demand and wide-ranging cost increases are pushing prices up, and that businesses are reporting strong earnings while bankers describe healthy loan pipelines. He said layoffs remain muted and consumers keep spending on the back of a resilient job market, even though consumer sentiment is weak.

headline: NY Fed survey shows Americans growing more worried about the US labour market outlook
detail: The New York Fed's consumer expectations survey for October, published on Monday, found US households more concerned about future unemployment. No figures for the labour market measures were given in the report.

headline: BoE's Bailey says UK activity is more resilient than expected, helped by AI investment, but warns an AI asset bubble threatens stability
detail: In a speech, Bank of England Governor Bailey said there are growing signs of an early positive supply shock from AI and investment, notably in business services. He also said an AI asset price bubble poses clear financial stability risks, as markets could overvalue AI returns, and that frontier AI has raised cyberattack risks.
