headline: US official says European partners will join the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks and both sides show some private flexibility on territory
detail: A US official said European partners will take part in the Abu Dhabi talks and that Washington will try to get Russia to accept a multilateral format, with daily contact with both Ukraine and Russia. The official also said Kyiv and Moscow have privately shown a little flexibility on territorial concessions, and that NATO will remain central to European collective defence.

headline: US official says Ukraine territorial issues will wait until post-war security architecture is settled; US to press Russia on wider format
detail: A US official briefing on the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks said the US will try to get Russia to accept a multilateral format with Europe at the table after the trilateral meeting, and that both parties are coming with good intentions. The official said territorial questions will not be resolved until the post-war security architecture is known.

headline: BoE's Bailey says policymakers can no longer afford to assume supply shocks will fade
detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remark in a speech on Monday evening. He said it can no longer be taken for granted that supply shocks will pass on their own.

headline: Fed's Barkin calls the US economy remarkably stable, with muted layoffs but bleak consumer sentiment
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said businesses are doing well, with strong earnings, few layoffs and healthy loan pipelines, and that loan demand goes well beyond AI. He said consumer sentiment is bleak but people are still spending because the job market is resilient.

headline: US official says Washington seeks NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine and a stronger NATO-Russia Council
detail: A US official speaking about the Ukraine talks said US security guarantees will be discussed and that Russia is showing positive signs on ending the war. The official also said the US wants to make a NATO-Russia Council more robust.

headline: Fed's Barkin says government debt, rather than consumer debt, is at a historically high level
detail: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said in remarks on Monday that government debt, not consumer debt, is at historic levels.

headline: US 3-year when-issued yield stands at 4.622% ahead of $58bn Treasury auction
detail: The when-issued 3-year US Treasury yield was 4.622% just before the US Treasury's $58 billion 3-year note auction on Monday.

headline: US $58bn 3-year note auction prices at 4.627% with a 0.5bp tail; bid-to-cover falls to 2.53
detail: The US Treasury sold $58bn of 3-year notes at a high yield of 4.627%, against 4.932% at the previous auction, with bid-to-cover of 2.53 compared with 2.62 last time. Indirect bidders took 55.48%, directs 35.04% and primary dealers 9.48%, and 73.41% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

headline: Fed's Barkin says he has no base case for December and sees policy rate around or slightly below neutral
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said he has no base case for the December meeting and called the last jobs report healthy, though firms remain in a low-hire, low-fire pattern. He also said it is hard to know how the elections will affect the economy.

headline: Italian cabinet approves a gas price cap to bring down energy bills
detail: Italy's cabinet has backed a cap on gas prices intended to lower household and business energy bills, according to a market news report.

headline: US officials say they do not expect the Abu Dhabi talks to end the Ukraine war, only to clarify each side's positions
detail: US officials told CBS the Abu Dhabi talks aim to get Russia and Ukraine to set out their positions so compromises can be explored later. They also said Washington wants Russia to agree to multilateral negotiations that include Europe.

headline: Zelenskyy tells European partners he expects sustained Russian attacks on Dnipro bridges aimed at splitting Ukraine
detail: The FT reports that Ukraine's president has warned European partners he expects Russia to launch sustained attacks on bridges across the Dnipro river in an attempt to cut the country in half. The warning comes during the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks.

headline: Fed's Barkin calls last jobs report healthy but says firms are still in a low-hire, low-fire mode
detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin also said ballot measures approved in recent US elections should not stop data centre expansion because firms will find other places to build. He added that it would help if each Fed policy meeting came with two full months of economic data.

headline: Bank of France says it faces great uncertainty in assessing growth
detail: The Bank of France said there is great uncertainty around its assessment of growth. No figures were reported with the comment.

headline: Bank of France expects moderate growth in the French economy in the fourth quarter
detail: The Bank of France says French economic growth will be moderate in the fourth quarter. It had earlier said it faces great uncertainty in assessing growth.

headline: OPEC oil output rises in October to 90% of its pre-war level, Reuters survey finds
detail: A Reuters survey shows OPEC production rose in October, led by gains in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq. Exports remain constrained by the Iran war and a US blockade on Iranian shipments.

headline: Iran says three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz after using unauthorised routes
detail: Iran said three tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and footage showed one tanker on fire on the shipping route. The posts report that attacks on commercial shipping are continuing; no market reaction was reported.

headline: WTI crude December futures settle at $86.85, down $3.98 or 4.38% on the day
detail: NYMEX WTI December crude futures settled at $86.85 a barrel, a fall of $3.98 or 4.38%. NYMEX natural gas December futures settled at $3.2180/MMBtu.

headline: US lets Iran enrich uranium at home to 3.67% and Tehran agrees, Al Arabiya sources say; preliminary enrichment deal seen as likely
detail: Al Arabiya, citing sources, reports that Washington has allowed Iran to enrich uranium domestically to 3.67%, that Tehran has accepted, and that a preliminary agreement on cutting Iran's enrichment is likely. The same sources say arrangements are being made to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran, without saying what their duties would cover.

headline: Brent crude futures settle at $92.57 a barrel, down $5.75 or 5.85% on the day
detail: Brent futures closed at $92.57 a barrel, $5.75 or 5.85% lower on the session.

headline: Proposed US-Iran framework would reopen Strait of Hormuz, lift naval blockade and free $6bn-$9bn of Iranian assets, Al Arabiya says
detail: Al Arabiya sources say the Strait of Hormuz would be opened and the naval blockade lifted immediately under the proposed framework, and the US would release $6 billion to $9 billion of Iranian assets if a deal is reached. The sources also say arrangements are being made to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran, without setting out the scope of their work.

headline: Trump's talks with Qatar's prime minister on Iran deal efforts were positive, a diplomat tells Axios
detail: Axios cites a diplomat who described the talks between President Trump and Qatar's prime minister as positive. Qatar is helping to mediate between the US and Iran on the details of a deal.

headline: Trump says US is prepared to strike Iran if needed, though Qatar and Saudi Arabia favour a peaceful settlement
detail: Speaking to Reuters after talks with Qatar's leader, US President Trump said Qatar would prefer a peaceful outcome with Iran but the US stands ready to carry out strikes if necessary. He added that Saudi Arabia would also prefer a peaceful solution to the conflict.

headline: Trump says this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine offer a chance of a possible breakthrough
detail: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the Abu Dhabi talks on the war in Ukraine, due this week, could bring a breakthrough. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine's gains on the battlefield give Kyiv a stronger hand in peace talks
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said recent battlefield successes have strengthened Kyiv's negotiating position. The remarks come ahead of this week's Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

headline: Arab and Muslim leaders press Trump not to restart war with Iran, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Arab and Muslim leaders are trying to ease tensions, amid fears that the US president will resume hostilities with Iran.

headline: Canada extends tariff relief on goods hit by US tariffs by one year, to 30 June 2028
detail: Canada's finance minister said the general remission for US tariffs is extended to 30 June 2028. Relief will also cover non-steel goods used in mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction, and certain imported goods that are in short supply in Canada.

headline: Trump says he had an excellent conversation with Qatar's prime minister
detail: The US president said this in a Truth Social post. Earlier reports said the talks covered efforts towards a deal with Iran.

headline: Trump says he sees positive momentum towards ending the Iran conflict and that an Iranian nuclear weapon is non-negotiable
detail: In a Truth Social post, US President Trump said all parties agree that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. He added that the US stands ready to act if the situation in the Middle East changes, but that this now looks quite unlikely.

headline: Iran's IRGC navy disables navigation systems of four large oil tankers using an unauthorised Strait of Hormuz route, Press TV says
detail: Iranian state broadcaster Press TV reports that the Revolutionary Guard navy disabled the navigation systems of four large oil tankers over the past 24 hours, leaving them unable to continue through the Strait of Hormuz. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says Iran is effectively finished as a military force and the US is keeping Iran at the status quo
detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Monday evening, and repeated that he sees momentum towards ending the conflict. The posts in this batch report no market reaction.

headline: Qatar's prime minister says he met Trump and Vance to discuss ways to move Iran negotiations forward
detail: Qatar's prime minister said the meeting with US President Trump and Vice President Vance covered ways to make progress in negotiations with Iran.

headline: Trump says the US has another aircraft carrier ready as Iran talks continue
detail: US President Trump said in remarks on Iran on Monday evening that the US has a further aircraft carrier loaded up. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran's top security official denies talks with the US are taking place and tells Washington to accept Tehran's seven conditions
detail: Iran's top security official told the US to stop putting out false reports of talks that he said do not exist. He also said it was time for Washington to give in to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out.

headline: Trump tells reporters US military action against Iran does not look necessary for now
detail: US President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that US military action against Iran did not currently appear necessary, Reuters reports.

headline: UK BRC retail sales rise 1.1% y/y, a little below the 1.2% forecast
detail: The British Retail Consortium's retail sales monitor shows annual growth of 1.1%, against a forecast of 1.2% and up from 1.0% previously.

headline: BoJ October summary of opinions shows several members favour further rate rises towards neutral
detail: In the Bank of Japan's October summary of opinions, one member said underlying inflation has reached 2% and the policy rate must reach neutral soon, and one said Japan's neutral rate is likely well above 1%. Other members urged caution, citing some economic weakness and the need to watch financial conditions for several months after each rate rise.

headline: Japan's September household spending falls 6.8% y/y, a much steeper drop than the 3.1% expected
detail: Japanese government data show household spending down 6.8% year on year and down 2.8% month on month in September, against a poll forecast of a 0.3% monthly rise.

headline: Barclays data show UK consumer spending up 2.3% y/y in October, the most since July 2025, while confidence hits its lowest since April
detail: Barclays said UK card spending rose 2.3% year on year in October, up from 2.0% in September and the largest increase since July 2025. It also said consumer confidence in October was the weakest since April.

headline: China's October dollar exports rise 35.2% y/y, above the 33.5% forecast; trade surplus of $105.28bn falls short of $125.8bn poll
detail: Chinese customs data show October dollar-denominated exports up 35.2% y/y against a poll of 33.5%, with the trade surplus at $105.28bn against a forecast of $125.8bn. The surplus with the United States was $32.71bn, and yuan-denominated exports rose 28.7% y/y.

headline: Japan offers 0.6 trillion yen of 30-year government bonds with a 4.200% coupon
detail: Japan's government is offering 0.6 trillion yen of 30-year JGBs carrying a 4.200% coupon. Separately, Finance Minister Katayama said no decision has been taken on tax incentives for retail JGBs and left the debate to the LDP.

headline: Japan's 30-year JGB auction tail widens to 0.35 from 0.16; 30-year yield rises 2.5bp to 3.865% afterwards
detail: The tail at Japan's 30-year government bond sale widened to 0.35, from 0.16 at the previous auction. The 30-year JGB yield rose 2.5bp to 3.865% after the result.

headline: China's trade surplus tops $1tn in the first 10 months of the year
detail: The FT and Reuters report China's January to October trade surplus passed $1tn, led by exports of high-tech goods linked to AI infrastructure. Customs data put October exports up 28.7% y/y in yuan terms and imports up 34.7%.

headline: Laden LNG tanker exits from the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest monthly level in October since the Iran war began
detail: Reuters cites vessel tracking data showing the monthly count of laden LNG tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since the US-Iran conflict disrupted shipping.

headline: China's October crude imports reach their highest since March but are down 13.3% y/y
detail: Official Chinese data show October crude oil imports fell 13.3% from a year earlier but were the highest since March, after the war on Iran disrupted Middle East supplies.

headline: US military moves aircraft out of a second UK base after an Iranian threat, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the US military evacuated aircraft from a UK airbase on Monday following a threat from Iran.

headline: Thames Water creditors ready a 'final' offer as PM Burnham weighs whether to nationalise the company, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Thames Water's creditors are preparing what they describe as a final offer. It says the prime minister has been reluctant to take the company into state ownership despite having supported the idea earlier.

headline: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli does not rule out a December rate hike but says she needs more information
detail: Lombardelli says she would not exclude a December rate rise but does not yet have enough information, according to The Guardian. She also says hiring in the UK labour market has fallen off sharply without much sign of redundancies, and that young people are being hurt by a low-gear economy.

headline: US crude futures fall 2% to $85.11 a barrel
detail: US oil futures were reported down 2% at $85.11 a barrel in early trading on 10 November.

headline: France says Europeans will attend Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks, rules out European security talks with Russia before a ceasefire
detail: France's foreign minister said European representatives will take part in the Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi. France also said there will be no discussions with Russia on European security until a ceasefire is in place and peace in Ukraine is secured.

headline: ECB's Moulin says there are positive signs on energy prices
detail: ECB official Moulin said on 10 November that the central bank sees positive signs on energy prices.

headline: ADNOC CFO says LNG exports through Hormuz are still below pre-conflict levels despite month-on-month improvement
detail: ADNOC's chief financial officer said LNG cargoes leaving the Strait of Hormuz are improving each month but have not yet returned to pre-conflict levels. He added that the company has made no decisions on alternative LNG export facilities.

headline: Norway's October CPI rises 3.6% y/y, below the 3.7% forecast and up from 3.4%
detail: Norwegian consumer prices rose 0.3% on the month, after 0.5% the previous month. The annual rate of 3.6% came in a little below the 3.7% forecast and above the previous 3.4%.

headline: ECB's Moulin expects ECB policy continuity if Knot or de Cos becomes president
detail: ECB official Moulin said he expects continuity at the central bank if either Knot or de Cos takes over.

headline: Norway's October underlying CPI slows to 2.7% y/y, matching forecasts and down from 3.0%
detail: Norway's underlying inflation rose 0.3% m/m in October, against a forecast of 0.4% and 0.2% the previous month. Headline CPI was 3.6% y/y, below the 3.7% estimate.

headline: Ukraine peace talks get under way in Abu Dhabi, with US, Ukrainian and European delegations meeting
detail: Market commentary accounts report that talks have begun in Abu Dhabi and that the US delegation is meeting Ukrainian and European delegations. No market reaction is reported.

headline: Brent crude futures drop 2% to $90.66 a barrel
detail: Brent crude futures were reported down 2% at $90.66 a barrel in early European trading on 10 November.

headline: Canada's foreign minister hopes for progress on US tariffs after the midterm elections
detail: Canada's foreign minister said she hopes for progress on US tariffs once the US midterm elections are over. No timetable or specific measures were reported.

headline: ECB's Lane says a December hike would be prudent if the data hold, and sees inflation slightly above 4% at year-end
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said inflation is likely to end the year a little above 4%, with more to come before the peak, and he expects core and food inflation to pick up. He also said oil prices could move a lot before the December meeting, that he would like markets to reprice in line with the wider macro picture, that Europe's resilience is reassuring, and that France's fiscal problems need to be fixed in Paris.

headline: Russia, Ukraine and US trilateral talks reportedly begin in Abu Dhabi
detail: Reports say three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US have started in Abu Dhabi. Ukraine's Umerov said the delegation's first meeting is with European, NATO and EU representatives and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli calls December MPC meeting live for a further rate hike and says the Iran war is pushing up unemployment
detail: In an interview with the Guardian, Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said the December MPC meeting is live for considering another rate rise. She said the Iran war has raised energy prices, clouded the outlook and driven up unemployment, and that young people are bearing the brunt of a sluggish economy.

headline: Ukraine's chief negotiator confirms trilateral talks with the US and Russia are under way; Russia's Medinsky hopes for progress
detail: Ukraine's chief negotiator Umerov said the talks with the US and Russia have moved to a trilateral format, with an agenda covering an end to hostilities and peace. Russia's lead negotiator Medinsky said he hopes the updated Russian delegation will help move things towards peace.

headline: Riksbank's Jansson says policy normalisation remains relatively cautious
detail: Riksbank Deputy Governor Jansson said Sweden's current policy normalisation is still relatively cautious.

headline: US gasoline price falls below $4 a gallon for the first time since July
detail: A market commentator reports that US gasoline has dropped under $4 per gallon, its first time below that level since July.

headline: Brent crude drops below $90 a barrel for the first time since August
detail: A market news account reported Brent futures falling below $90 a barrel on Tuesday morning, the lowest since August.

headline: BoE's Breeden says firms have become very good at adapting to cost shocks
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden, a member of the MPC, said businesses are now very good at adjusting to cost shocks. No remarks on the rate outlook were reported in the post.

headline: Fed's Waller backs a December hike and is open to 50bp if October core CPI is 0.3% or more; traders fully price 25bp
detail: Fed Governor Waller said he would back a quarter-point hike in December even if October CPI improves on September, and that a half-point move may be needed if October core CPI comes in around 0.3% or higher. He called US inflation too high, flagged concern about how widespread price rises are and the risk of a more persistent energy shock, and described the labour market as solid; traders were reported to have moved to fully price a 25bp December hike.

headline: Canada reimposes sanctions on 11 Iranian entities
detail: Canada's foreign minister, Anita Anand, announced that sanctions are being reimposed on 11 Iranian entities. She noted that Canada had delisted Iranian entities in 2016 after Iran's progress under the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

headline: Kremlin declines to predict chances of progress at Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks while negotiations continue
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi will decide how often and in what format to report to President Putin, depending on how the negotiations progress. He declined to give a view on the prospects for progress towards peace while talks are under way.

headline: EU says European partners, Ukraine and US agree any Ukraine deal must respect sovereignty and include credible security guarantees
detail: In an EU statement after a coordination meeting ahead of talks with Russia, European partners, Ukraine and the US said they share the goal of a practical and mutually reinforcing security framework, and that dealing with post-war security concerns and reducing the risk of conflict is essential. Participants said they will keep working closely together throughout the negotiations.

headline: Fed's Waller says real rates must rise to keep policy restrictive and higher rates are needed to bear down on inflation
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Waller said real interest rates need to rise to keep monetary policy as restrictive as it is now. He added that the Fed needs to raise rates to put downward pressure on inflation.

headline: UK 30-year gilt auction draws 3.75 times cover at an average yield of 5.54%
detail: The 30-year gilt sale was covered 3.75 times, down from 3.84 at the previous auction. The average yield was 5.54%, compared with 5.517% last time.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says policy must stop energy inflation spilling over and gradual action is still appropriate
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said policymakers must stay vigilant and cautious. He said it remains appropriate to act gradually and that policy must keep energy inflation from spreading further.

headline: Fed's Waller says reversing the three insurance cuts is the minimum needed but rules out hikes of 150bp to 200bp
detail: Fed Governor Waller said that at the very least the Fed needs to undo its three insurance rate cuts. He added that he is not super hawkish, does not want to slam the economy down and that the Fed will not raise rates by 150bp or 200bp.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says monetary policy still needs some hawkish edge but must avoid hurting the economy too much
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said policy should keep some hawkish edge. He also said inflation must be brought under control without doing too much damage to the economy.

headline: ECB's Kazaks says more tightening may be needed if the energy shock persists and sees no need to slow or end QT
detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks also said inflation is likely to go significantly above 4% in 2027. He described stress in French bonds as a repricing of fiscal risk.

headline: Fed's Waller says he doesn't think any Fed colleagues believe rates are at the right level
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he does not believe any of his Fed colleagues think policy rates are currently in the right place.

headline: Qatar says its US-Iran mediation continues and both sides have responded positively
detail: Qatar said its efforts to mediate between Iran and the US are continuing, and that both sides have reacted positively to the mediation.

headline: Iran's IRGC navy says two tankers caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iranian state media and Tasnim carried the IRGC navy's report of the two tankers catching fire in the strait. The inputs report no market reaction.

headline: Budget keeps the Local Housing Allowance freeze in place into 2027-28, Resolution Foundation says
detail: According to the Resolution Foundation, more than a million families lose out from extending the freeze, and 91% of them are in the bottom half of the income distribution. The think tank says the Budget's Your First Home scheme will help a small number of renters buy.

headline: Russia, US and Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi reportedly restart after being suspended
detail: Reports say the trilateral negotiations between Russia, the United States and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi have resumed after a suspension. No further details or market reaction were reported.

headline: US NFIB small business optimism index slips to 97.8, below the 98.2 forecast
detail: The NFIB small business optimism index was 97.8, against a forecast of 98.2 and a previous reading of 97.9.

headline: Lavrov says Russia rejects European calls for an immediate Ukraine ceasefire and accuses Brussels of stalling
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said Moscow will not accept European demands for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine. He added that Russia cannot and does not want to stop the US from talking to European partners on Ukraine, although it does not see that format as the best approach.

headline: Resolution Foundation publishes analysis of how the Budget's abolition of the gas standing charge affects households
detail: The Resolution Foundation has published an analysis of how scrapping the gas standing charge, announced in the October 2026 Budget, affects different households. It says the measure has drawn less attention than the £100 Household Energy Payment.

headline: EU says the US should respect pharmaceutical trade commitments made in their August joint statement
detail: An EU spokesperson said on Tuesday that the commitments on trade in the pharmaceutical sector set out in the EU-US joint statement in August should be respected.

headline: France and Ukraine welcome US efforts at the Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks
detail: Paris said France and Ukraine welcome the US role in the trilateral talks under way in Abu Dhabi. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Oil is more than 20% below its late-October peak as markets bet on the Iran conflict winding down, Reuters says
detail: Reuters reports that oil prices have fallen more than 20% from their late-October peak, with markets betting that the Iran conflict is winding down.

headline: BoE is reportedly considering changes to how it carries out its remaining APF gilt sales
detail: A market commentary account reported that the Bank of England is weighing an adjustment to how it conducts the remaining gilt sales from the Asset Purchase Facility. The post gave no further details or timing.

headline: Ukrainian strikes since late October have reportedly reduced Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30%
detail: Two industry sources say Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries since late October have reduced Russia's oil processing capacity by about 30%. According to the sources, actual processing volumes are down by about 200,000 tons per day.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli sees upside inflation risks as the energy shock proves more persistent, raising the chance of second-round effects
detail: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli said the energy shock has become more persistent, that high energy costs that last longer will push firms harder to restore margins, and that the balance of inflation risks lies to the upside. She also described the labour market as stuck in low gear.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli says conditions for persistent medium-term inflation are taking shape and risks remain to the upside
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said the balance of risks to inflation is still to the upside. She added that conditions for persistent inflationary dynamics over the medium term are starting to crystallise.

headline: Iran reportedly agrees to US demands to cut its highly enriched uranium levels, Al Hadath says
detail: Al Hadath cited sources as saying Iran has accepted US demands to reduce its stocks of highly enriched uranium. The report has not been officially confirmed, and no market reaction was reported.

headline: Germany's Merz says EU budget talks must not lead to reduced support for Ukraine
detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said, in the context of EU budget discussions, that support for Ukraine cannot be scaled back.

headline: Reuters poll: all 101 economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December to 4.00%-4.25%
detail: In the Reuters poll, 56 of the 101 economists expect the fed funds rate to peak at 4.00%-4.25% in this hiking cycle, and 29 of 37 said the risk to their medium-term US inflation view has not changed since the midterm elections. Prediction markets are reported to price an 87% chance of a 25bp hike, against 9% for a hold.

headline: First day of Russia-US-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ends after 4.5 hours, reports say
detail: Russian reports say the Russian, US and Ukrainian delegations finished their first day of negotiations in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. The session reportedly lasted 4.5 hours.

headline: Germany's Merz says the EU budget needs new priorities in defence and competitiveness
detail: German Chancellor Merz said the next EU budget must set new priorities in defence and competitiveness. He added that supporting Ukraine is a collective task for the European Union.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli says UK economy may have less slack than the Bank's central view, perhaps 0-1% rather than 1%
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said spare capacity in the UK economy may be smaller than the Bank's central estimate of 1%, putting it at perhaps 0-1%.

headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth says the US controls the Strait of Hormuz and over 80% of Iran's nuclear industrial base is gone
detail: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made the remarks at a press conference, where he also said Iran started the war.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli says wage growth is easing more slowly than hoped
detail: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli said pay is not slowing as quickly as hoped. She also said it is very hard to tell whether the UK economy has become more resilient to price shocks or is close to the limit of what households and firms can absorb.

headline: US ADP weekly employment change rises to 19.75K from 16.75K
detail: ADP's weekly employment change for the period to 24 October came in at 19.75K, up from 16.75K previously. No forecast was given.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli does not rule out back-to-back rate hikes and says every MPC meeting is live
detail: BoE Deputy Governor Lombardelli said she would not rule a hike in December or February in or out, and that the December vote will depend on the Middle East outlook, pricing and the labour market. She also said the UK's natural rate of unemployment may be somewhat higher than before.

headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth says the US is ready to act if Iran makes a wrong move and can strike its nuclear sites if needed
detail: US Defense Secretary Hegseth said US forces remain ready to respond to Iran and that the US can see Iran's nuclear sites and could take action if necessary.

headline: UK foreign minister calls for a full diplomatic push to end the Iran conflict
detail: The UK foreign minister called for a comprehensive diplomatic effort to bring the Iran conflict to an end.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli says long-term inflation expectations remain well anchored, with no sign of de-anchoring
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said long-term inflation expectations are very well anchored and the Bank does not see them de-anchoring. She made the remarks during her appearance on 10 November.

headline: US October CPI rises 0.4% m/m, above 0.3% forecast; core CPI up 0.3%, above 0.2% forecast
detail: US consumer prices rose 0.4% month on month in October, compared with a 0.3% forecast and 0.6% in the previous month. Core CPI rose 0.3%, against a 0.2% forecast and unchanged from the previous month's 0.3%.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli says monetary policy is less restrictive than the Bank had thought
detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said policy is less restrictive than previously judged. In the same remarks she said some European countries, including France, face very difficult debt trajectories.

headline: US 2- to 5-year Treasury yields rise at least 10bp on the day after October CPI beats forecasts
detail: Traders kept pricing for a December Fed hike at 100%.

headline: Rubio says economic pressure on Iran is working and major combat operations are no longer needed
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said he told G7 counterparts that the economic campaign against Iran is working well enough that President Trump has no need to carry out major combat operations.

headline: Rubio calls Abu Dhabi Russia-Ukraine talks very productive but says a deal will not come within 48 hours
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the Abu Dhabi talks on Russia and Ukraine were very productive, though much work remains. He said the US wants Europeans at the table soon.

headline: Traders increase bets on a 50bp Fed rate hike in December after the October US CPI release
detail: Market commentary reports traders adding to positions for a half-point Fed hike next month. This follows the October US CPI rise of 0.4% m/m, which was above forecast.

headline: US October supercore CPI rises 0.4% m/m, against 0.42% previously
detail: Supercore CPI rose 0.4% on the month, compared with 0.42% in the previous reading. Gold and copper were reported extending losses after the inflation report.

headline: Rubio says Iran's conditions for a deal are absurd and the sides are not close; US rejects reparations demands
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the US is ready to negotiate with Iran if a deal is possible but will not accept a bad one, and that Iran's demand for reparations will not be met. He also said economic pressure on Iran will get even worse.

headline: Rubio says US aims eventually to widen trilateral Ukraine talks to include European countries
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said the goal is at some point to bring Europeans into the US-Russia-Ukraine talks. He said US and European goals on Ukraine and Russia are the same and that Europe is at the table.

headline: Rubio says Trump has decided there is currently no need for US military operations against Iran and denies a stalemate
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio said President Trump had judged that military operations against Iran are not needed at present. He also said the situation with Iran is not a stalemate.

headline: Prediction markets price a 12% chance of a Fed hike above 25bp in December and 85% for a 25bp move
detail: Natixis says the stronger-than-expected October US CPI and hawkish Fed remarks have put a larger December hike in play. Prediction markets give a 12% chance of a move above 25bp and 85% for a standard 25bp increase.

headline: Rubio rejects negotiating over Lebanon with Iran as part of US-Iran talks
detail: US Secretary of State Rubio questioned why the US would negotiate with Iran over Lebanon. He made the remarks during comments on the US-Iran talks, which Qatar is mediating.

headline: ECB's Cipollone warns the digital euro could be delayed if legislative talks drag on
detail: ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone warned on Tuesday that the digital euro could be delayed if talks on it continue for too long. He made no reported comment on interest rates.

headline: Houthis say they have carried out several operations against Saudi Arabia
detail: The Houthis announced several operations against Saudi Arabia, according to a market news account. The report did not give details of targets or say whether markets moved.

headline: Houthis say they attacked Aramco's Abqaiq facility and pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline
detail: In a statement, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an Aramco facility at Abqaiq. They said the attacks also targeted King Khalid International Airport and a financial centre in Riyadh, as well as troops. None of the posts reports a market reaction.

headline: Houthis deny attacking East-West pipeline in Medina region and say their strike was only on the Riyadh section
detail: Yemen's Houthis denied attacking the Saudi East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region. They said they attacked the pipeline only in the Riyadh area.

headline: Zelenskiy says Abu Dhabi talks covered a prisoner exchange and security guarantees
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said he had received reports from his negotiators after the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. He said the talks covered a prisoner exchange and security guarantees.

headline: White House adviser Hassett calls US CPI report disappointing and says energy prices are feeding into the data
detail: White House senior adviser Hassett called the October US CPI report disappointing. In an interview with Fox Business, he said higher energy prices were feeding through into the data.

headline: SNB's Martin expects moderate Swiss growth over the coming quarters
detail: Swiss National Bank official Martin said the Swiss economy is expected to grow moderately over the next few quarters.

headline: IFS says Conservative welfare proposals imply large but uncertain reductions in benefit spending
detail: The Institute for Fiscal Studies published a response from its researcher Tom Waters assessing the opposition Conservatives' welfare plans. It says the plans imply substantial cuts to benefit spending, though the scale is uncertain.

headline: UK government security group investigates a possible leak of Budget measures that may have moved markets
detail: A letter published by the Treasury Select Committee confirms the investigation, which is being led by a government security group. It concerns a Bloomberg report on a bank tax published just before the Budget, and the committee's chair, Meg Hillier, was reported to have responded with exasperation.

headline: Two-year yield reported up 17.4bp on the day, with the 30-year yield up 6.3bp
detail: A market newswire reports the two-year yield up 17.4bp and the 30-year up 6.3bp on the day; the post does not name the market. It follows the October US CPI release.

headline: ECB's Nagel says a December rate rise is clearly needed and sees no risk of fiscal dominance
detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel said the ECB will do what is needed to bring inflation back to 2%, called the fall in energy prices since the US midterms good news, and said market expectations matter but are not the deciding factor. He also said France must address its fiscal challenges.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield heads for its biggest one-day rise since April 2025
detail: A market report says the US 2-year yield is on course for its largest single-session increase since April 2025, after the October CPI release.

headline: ECB's Nagel calls the fall in energy prices since the US midterms positive and says France must address its finances
detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel said action will be taken to return inflation to 2%, and that market expectations matter but are not the main influence on policy. He also said France needs to deal with its fiscal problems.

headline: Iran's foreign minister says diplomacy, not military action or sanctions, will end the war and denies reports of a Rezaei-Vance meeting
detail: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said the conflict will be resolved through diplomacy and acceptance of Iran's conditions, not by military action or sanctions. He also called reports of a meeting between security chief Rezaei and US Vice President Vance baseless media speculation.

headline: Zelenskiy calls Abu Dhabi talks constructive and substantive; trilateral talks set to continue tomorrow
detail: Ukraine's president says negotiators discussed the substance of security guarantees for Ukraine in detail. He says he has given his team instructions for tomorrow's trilateral round and for talks in the coming days with US and European representatives.

headline: Netanyahu tells Knesset Iran is reviving its nuclear programme and says overthrowing its regime is the only lasting solution
detail: In a speech to the Knesset, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said Iran is working to revive its nuclear programme after the immediate threat was removed. He said the only way to remove the threat permanently is to overthrow the regime.

headline: Netanyahu says Israel will soon face international pressure to accept a nuclear Iran and to pull back from security zones
detail: Israel's prime minister told the Knesset that Iran is working to renew its nuclear threat and has not dropped its aim of destroying Israel. He said Israel faces pressure to give up its gains in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza, and called for a national unity government.

headline: Fed's Logan says at least two more 25bp hikes are needed and that faster rate rises may be needed this winter
detail: Dallas Fed President Logan said in a speech that the Fed's policy rate is at least 50bp below a modestly restrictive level, that the real Fed funds rate is 78bp, and that it would make sense to pause and assess after two more hikes. She said inflation is trending meaningfully above the 2% goal, price pressures go beyond wartime energy disruptions and tariffs, and the labour market is balanced and even tightening a bit.

headline: Traders fully price two 25bp Bank of England rate hikes by March
detail: Market pricing now fully reflects two quarter-point increases in Bank Rate by March, a market commentary account reports.

headline: Fed's Logan puts policy rate at least 50bp below a mildly restrictive level and sees a pause after two more hikes
detail: Dallas Fed President Logan said accommodative policy is adding to inflation pressure, put the real fed funds rate at 78bp and said pausing to assess after two more increases would be logical. She said inflation is well above the 2% target, that price pressures go beyond energy and tariffs, and that the labour market is balanced to slightly tight.

headline: Iran's Rezaei says Iran has set seven conditions and the US has not yet given a clear response
detail: Iranian Major General Rezaei said Iran had laid down seven conditions and was still waiting for a clear US answer, and called the American response deceptive, Fars News reported. He also said US claims that talks with Iran are continuing are meant to bring oil prices down.

headline: Iranian officials say the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until Iran's seven conditions are met
detail: Major General Rezaei said Hormuz will not reopen until Iran's seven conditions are met, and the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the same. Rezaei separately repeated that the US has not yet given a clear response to the conditions.

headline: Iran's Rezaei says there are no US-Iran negotiations under way and calls US claims of continuing talks fabricated
detail: Iran's security chief Rezaei says no negotiations are currently taking place between Tehran and Washington, and that Iran has asked the US for a clear and explicit response to its conditions. He repeats that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until the US meets Iran's seven conditions.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs back to 5% for the first time in 12 days
detail: A market news feed reports the US 10-year Treasury yield back at 5%, the first time in 12 days. The move follows the October US CPI release, which came in above forecasts earlier in the session.

headline: Canada's Carney says some difficult areas remain in trade talks with the US
detail: Canadian Prime Minister Carney said Canada has settled its red lines with the US on cultural questions. He also said Canada does not need a contested tax on large web companies.

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield reported up 15bp on the day after October CPI beat
detail: The Financial Times reports the 10-year US Treasury yield has risen 15bp on the day, taking it back to 5%. The move follows a stronger-than-expected October CPI reading of 0.4% m/m.

headline: US EIA raises Brent forecasts to $97.44/bbl for 2026 and $85.78/bbl for 2027
detail: The US Energy Information Administration's Short-Term Energy Outlook raises its 2026 Brent average forecast from $96.32/bbl and its 2027 forecast from $83.74/bbl. It puts 2026 world oil output at 101.7m bpd, up from 101.1m bpd, and cuts its 2027 figure to 108.4m bpd from 109.6m bpd, with 2026 world demand unchanged at 102.4m bpd.

headline: Ukraine's foreign minister says Kyiv awaits Russia's reply on Black Sea ceasefire proposals and is not optimistic on progress
detail: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha also said the cost of the war will be higher in 2027 and called on allies to agree long-term funding commitments this year. He said he asked US Secretary of State Rubio to speed up deliveries of air-defence interceptors as Russia attacks energy infrastructure.

headline: UK PM Burnham rules out dynamic alignment of the UK with EU financial services rules
detail: Prime Minister Burnham rejected dynamically aligning the UK with EU rules on financial services, a market news account reported. No market reaction was reported.

headline: ECB's Lane sets a high bar for directional forward guidance and says a dot plot would sit poorly with the ECB's consensus approach
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said the Governing Council places great weight on consensus, which would make publishing rate projections in the style of a dot plot difficult. He added that he would set a high bar for directional forward guidance at present.

headline: ECB's Lane says the ECB needs a tool for dealing with multiple equilibria in bond markets
detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said it is important for the ECB to have an instrument for situations where bond markets could settle at more than one equilibrium. The remarks follow his earlier comments on forward guidance.

headline: ECB's Lane expects second-round effects and says headline inflation could fall as energy reverses while underlying inflation rises
detail: ECB chief economist Lane said underlying inflation has not yet moved, consistent with the usual delayed response, and that it guides inflation one year ahead. He added that energy prices are already reversing and it would be surprising if there were no second-round effects.

headline: EU's Costa says Ukraine financing will be taken up at the 26-27 November EU summit once the Commission sends its proposal
detail: European Council President Costa told German Chancellor Merz in a letter that Ukraine financing will be on the agenda of the EU summit on 26-27 November. He said this will follow receipt of a proposal from the European Commission.

headline: US 10-year when-issued yield stands at 5.010% ahead of $42bn Treasury auction
detail: Ahead of the US Treasury's $42 billion 10-year note auction, the 10-year when-issued yield was reported at 5.010%.

headline: US $42bn 10-year note auction tails by 1bp at 5.020% high yield; bid-to-cover falls to 2.46 from 2.770
detail: The US Treasury sold $42bn of 10-year notes at a high yield of 5.020%, against 5.300% at the previous sale, with a 1bp tail and 95.17% of bids awarded at the high. Primary dealers took 9.8%, direct bidders 29.0% and indirect bidders 61.2%.

headline: New US 10-year notes to carry a 5% coupon, the highest since 2006
detail: A market commentator reported the coupon after the $42bn US 10-year note auction, which had already been reported as tailing.

headline: Resolution Foundation puts real per-person public services spending growth at 1.7% a year from 2023-24 to 2028-29
detail: In its Budget analysis, the Resolution Foundation says day-to-day spending is growing moderately in this Parliament. It puts public services spending growth at 1.7% a year in real per-person terms between 2023-24 and 2028-29, which it says is similar to the two most recent periods under Conservative governments.

headline: US EIA holds 2026 world oil demand at 102.4m bpd, cuts 2027 to 104.4m bpd and trims its 2027 world output forecast
detail: The US Energy Information Administration's Short-Term Energy Outlook keeps 2026 world oil demand at 102.4m bpd and lowers 2027 to 104.4m bpd from 104.6m bpd. It raises 2026 world oil output to 101.7m bpd from 101.1m bpd and cuts 2027 to 108.4m bpd from 109.6m bpd.

headline: BoE's Lombardelli sees a case for another rate rise in the near term, citing high energy prices and resilient UK growth
detail: The Financial Times reports that Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said high energy prices and the resilience of UK growth support a further rate increase in the near term. She did not rule out back-to-back rate rises.

headline: Bank of Canada minutes keep further rate hikes on the table and say policy can stop energy prices becoming generalised inflation
detail: Minutes of the deliberations before the Bank of Canada's 28 October rate announcement show the Governing Council saying uncertainty over rates did not mean inaction, and that rising cost pressures would eventually show up in core inflation. Members also said inflation expectations may have become more sensitive to recent price changes, and that businesses face higher costs for non-energy imports such as semiconductors.

headline: Qatar's PM tells G7 foreign ministers Doha has won at least two weeks for diplomacy towards a US-Iran understanding
detail: According to the Jerusalem Post, Qatari Prime Minister Al Thani told G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris that Doha had secured a window of at least two weeks to pursue diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran.

headline: Fed's Schmid sees some concerning price trends beneath the energy-driven inflation story
detail: Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said there are some worrying trends in prices underlying the effect of energy. The remarks come on the day US October CPI came in above forecasts.

headline: Fed's Schmid calls policy rate fairly accommodative and finds no restriction outside housing
detail: Kansas City Fed President Schmid said US hiring had been quite robust lately and demand was strong. He said rates gave no cause for hesitation, and that apart from the housing market he could find no sign that policy was restrictive.

headline: US envoy Kushner calls the day's Ukraine talks constructive and says the US is working to end the war
detail: Kushner said the US was acting at President Trump's direction to end the war and to agree security arrangements for a sovereign Ukraine and lasting peace in Europe.

headline: Fed's Schmid says inflation is his main concern
detail: Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said inflation is foremost in his thinking, in further remarks on 10 November.

headline: Fed's Schmid expects instant payments to overtake digital asset structures
detail: Kansas City Fed President Schmid said instant payment systems are likely to leapfrog digital asset structures. The remarks were about payments, not monetary policy.

headline: Fed's Schmid says US hiring has been fairly robust and demand is strong
detail: Fed's Schmid said recent US hiring has been fairly robust, demand is strong and interest rates are not holding activity back. He added that a lot of data is due before the Fed's December meeting.

headline: Fire on a platform at Iran's South Pars gas field is under control, Iranian media report; cause under investigation
detail: Iran's Fars news agency reports the fire is under control. Iranian reports say the platform produces 14.5m cubic metres of gas out of the field's total 700m, and that a gas leak or an operational incident are the two possible causes.

headline: Iran's Fars says the South Pars platform hit by fire produces 14.5m cubic metres of the field's 700m cubic metres of gas
detail: Iran's Fars news agency gave the output of the platform at the South Pars gas field where a fire was earlier reported to be under control. It put the platform's production at 14.5m cubic metres of gas, out of a field total of 700m cubic metres.

headline: Zelenskiy says Europe must settle this month who will represent it in Ukraine peace negotiations
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said in Copenhagen that a decision on Europe's representative in the negotiations is needed this month. He also said he hopes the US Congress will act more decisively.

headline: Fed's Bowman says persistent inflation and a firming labour market mean there is still work to do
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Bowman cited persistent inflation and firmer labour market conditions in her remarks.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine is ready to discuss territory and to meet Putin, but doubts Russia is ready for a leaders' meeting
detail: Ukraine's president said Kyiv will request a meeting of leaders and is prepared to talk about territory. He added that Ukraine and Russia discussed a possible prisoner exchange of 1000 for 1000 or 1500 for 1500.

headline: Fed's Bowman estimates October core PCE at 3.3% and says the Fed must weigh the costs of further tightening as financial conditions tighten
detail: In a speech to the Council on Foreign Relations, Federal Reserve Governor Bowman said core PCE probably rose 3.3% in October because of energy prices and AI-related demand, and that she expects it to move closer to 2% next year as those shocks unwind. She also said financial conditions have tightened, and that the labour market has improved but is not tight and is not adding to inflation.

headline: Zelenskiy says a new European security architecture is on the agenda at the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy, speaking in Copenhagen, said a new European security architecture is among the topics in the Abu Dhabi talks on ending the war.

headline: Zelenskiy welcomes recent US messages and sees a change in approach from envoys Witkoff and Kushner
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy, speaking in Copenhagen, said he was very pleased with recent messages from the US side and saw changes in the approach of US envoys Witkoff and Kushner. The remarks follow the Abu Dhabi talks on ending the war.

headline: Fed's Bowman says she would need AI and Middle East risks to ease before being confident inflation falls next year
detail: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said she is shifting her focus to inflation and that longer-term inflation expectations remain very well anchored. She added that expectations are an important input but do not necessarily drive her thinking.

headline: Fed's Bowman says the Fed is collecting data on AI debt counterparties and stresses open communication with the Treasury
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Bowman said the Fed is seeking data on counterparties to AI-related debt, and that keeping lines of communication open with the US Treasury is critically important.

headline: Fed's Bowman says AI will raise worker productivity, create new jobs and remove less essential ones
detail: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman commented on the labour market effects of artificial intelligence in remarks on Tuesday.

headline: Fed's Waller warns a half-point rate rise in December may be necessary
detail: Waller's warning came on the same day Fed's Logan backed at least two more quarter-point rises, after a stronger-than-expected US CPI print. Market wraps report that US stocks and Treasuries fell, with short-dated Treasuries hit hardest, while the dollar rose and money markets priced in a December move larger than 25bp.

headline: Fed's Bowman likens possible action on inflation in coming months to last year's gradual cuts followed by a pause
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Bowman said the Fed cut rates gradually last year, paused and then resumed, and that it may take a similar approach to addressing inflation in the coming months.

headline: Fed's Bowman says inflation is not trending lower and the Fed must consider the pace and timeline of its response
detail: Fed Governor Bowman said that inflation not moving down should give policymakers pause. She added that the Fed needs to weigh how fast to act on it and over what timeline.

headline: US Senate advances permitting reform bill meant to speed up building of energy infrastructure
detail: Semafor reports that the US Senate has moved forward major permitting reforms designed to speed up construction of energy infrastructure. The outlet says the Democrats' win in last week's midterms has added momentum to the reform.

headline: UK ministers reject Botley West, which would have been Britain's largest solar farm
detail: The UK government turned down the Oxfordshire project, saying it would do substantial harm to the green belt and to Blenheim Palace, the FT reports.

headline: Poland's Orlen ends a long-term LNG supply contract with QatarEnergy, citing ongoing force majeure
detail: Orlen, Poland's largest energy group, said on Tuesday it had terminated one of its two long-term LNG supply contracts with QatarEnergy. It said an ongoing force majeure had left the supplier unable to meet its delivery obligations.

headline: NIESR calls on the Bank of England to raise rates from 4% to 5% and says inflation may not reach 2% target until 2030
detail: In its autumn report, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research says the Bank should raise Bank Rate sharply to 5% from 4%. It also says inflation may not return to the 2% target until 2030.

headline: Oil falls to $90 a barrel on hopes that talks will end the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine
detail: Semafor reports that oil fell to $90 a barrel after US President Trump played down the risk of renewed conflict with Iran and talks between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington began.

headline: Fed's Paulson backs further gradual rate rises and says CPI data show inflation is still a problem
detail: Fed official Paulson says policy must stay somewhat tight, the Fed has more work to do, and underlying inflation remains between 2.5% and 3%. He calls the economy more resilient than expected, with a firm and steady job market, and says he backed recent rate moves.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee says the US faces a genuine inflation challenge and all policy options remain open
detail: Speaking on PBS NewsHour, Fed official Goolsbee calls the CPI report borderline troubling and says his biggest concerns are high services inflation and emerging widespread overheating in prices. He says the Fed must bring inflation back to target and that the job market remains steady.

headline: UK investigation into the Budget leak covers details of bank tax measures
detail: British authorities are reported to be investigating a leak of Budget details on bank taxes. This adds to the earlier report that a government security group was looking into a possible leak of Budget measures.

headline: Japan's 10-year JGB yield rises 6.5bp to 2.755% and 2-year climbs 7bp to 1.845%
detail: Japanese government bond yields rose in early Tokyo trade, with the 10-year up 6.5bp at 2.755% and the 2-year up 7bp at 1.845%. Earlier in the session, 10-year JGB futures fell 0.56 point.

headline: Fed's Paulson puts underlying US inflation at 2.5% to 3% and says policy must stay somewhat tight
detail: Fed official Paulson said the US economy has been more resilient than expected, with a firm and steady job market, and that the Fed has more work to do on inflation. She said the effect of AI and energy on inflation is difficult to measure and that the path of rates will depend on economic developments.

headline: Japan's 10-year JGB yield rises 9bp to 2.780% and 5-year climbs 8.5bp to 2.185%
detail: The 10-year JGB yield extended its rise to 2.780%, up 9bp, after the 5-year yield earlier gained 8.5bp to 2.185%. Asian bond yields rose as bets on a Federal Reserve rate increase grew.

headline: Global bonds fall and dollar holds firm as hot US inflation raises risk of a half-point Fed hike
detail: Reuters reports that global bonds fell sharply after a hot US inflation print and hawkish central bank comments raised the chance of a half-point Federal Reserve rate rise next month. Equities held up and the dollar stayed firm.

headline: Japan PM Takaichi rules out fiscal measures that risk high inflation and expects BoJ to secure 2% goal
detail: Japan's Prime Minister said the government has no intention of adopting fiscal policies that could push inflation excessively higher. She said she expects the Bank of Japan to set suitable policy to reach its 2% inflation target sustainably.

headline: Rubio tells G7 counterparts Trump has opted to pressure Iran's regime rather than go to war or strike a deal
detail: Axios reports that the US Secretary of State told G7 peers the president has chosen a policy of pressure on Iran's government instead of either military action or an agreement.

headline: Japan's 10-year JGB yield extends rise to 2.795%, up 10.5bp, as longer maturities also climb
detail: Market reports put the 10-year JGB yield at 2.795%, up 10.5bp on the day. The 30-year yield rose 6.5bp to 3.935% and the 40-year rose 4bp to 4.100%.

headline: Oil rebounds from a two-month low as attacks on Hormuz shipping offset hopes of an Iran truce
detail: Reuters reports oil prices rose on Wednesday after falling to two-month lows in the previous session. It says traders were weighing hopes of de-escalation in the Iran war against continuing attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: UK government backs approval of two major offshore wind projects with £1bn from the National Wealth Fund
detail: The UK government welcomed the approval of two large offshore wind projects. It confirmed a £12bn investment announcement by RWE and KKR, with £1bn of the financing package coming from the National Wealth Fund. It said more than 2,400 jobs would be supported during construction and operation.

headline: German final HICP confirms annual inflation at 2.8%, in line with forecasts
detail: Final German HICP shows 2.8% year on year and -0.1% month on month, both matching forecasts and the previous readings. Final German CPI shows -0.2% month on month, also as expected.

headline: ECB's Nagel says Germany's recovery is beating forecasts and expects growth to pick up in Q4
detail: Bundesbank President and ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said the German economic recovery has been stronger than forecast. He said growth is likely to accelerate in the fourth quarter.

headline: Banks use credit insurance to free up lending capacity as they hit limits on exposure to the AI boom, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Barclays, HSBC and JPMorgan Chase are among the lenders exploring or using credit insurance to free up capacity after reaching limits on lending to AI.

headline: Italian industrial production rises 1.2% on the month, above the 0.7% forecast
detail: Italy's monthly industrial production rose 1.2%, against a forecast of 0.7%, after falling 1.3% in the previous month.

headline: Japan PM Takaichi says the government is coordinating with the BoJ under their existing joint statement
detail: Japan's prime minister said the government will work with the Bank of Japan towards price stability and economic growth, as set out in the existing joint statement.

headline: Belgium joins France as investors target weaker eurozone credits over debt and deficits, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that investors are paying renewed attention to fiscal and political risks and are increasingly targeting the eurozone's weaker credits, now including Belgium alongside France, over debt and deficit concerns.

headline: Iran's security chief says Tehran will not let any enriched nuclear material leave the country
detail: Iran's security chief Rezaei made the remarks in an exchange with a Lebanese official, according to a newswire headline, and Al Mayadeen separately reported that Iran will not remove enriched material from the country. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran warns any US attack would trigger strikes on distant US bases
detail: A wire-style headline reports an Iranian warning that it would answer a US attack by striking US bases far from Iran. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Goldman Sachs adds a 25bp Fed rate rise in March to its outlook after hotter-than-expected US October inflation
detail: Reuters reports that Goldman Sachs now expects a 25bp Federal Reserve rate rise in March. It made the change on Tuesday after US October inflation came in above expectations, dropping its earlier call that the hiking cycle would end in December.

headline: Kremlin says Russia has no plans for contacts with the EU delegation at the Abu Dhabi talks and has held no such meetings
detail: The Kremlin also said Russia and the EU effectively have no relations at present, and that the Russian delegation has kept President Putin briefed throughout the Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine.

headline: PBOC's third-quarter policy report pledges more support for domestic demand and action against an exchange rate overshoot
detail: China's central bank published its monetary policy implementation report for the third quarter. It describes the external environment as more complex and volatile and global growth as lacking resilience, and says it will use and adjust its policy tools at the appropriate time.

headline: PBOC says Chinese loan rates are already relatively low and expects prices to grow at a reasonable pace
detail: China's central bank says lending rates in China are already fairly low and that it expects reasonable growth in prices.

headline: Dollar rises 0.2% to 159.04 yen, its highest since 24 September
detail: USD/JPY gains 0.2% to 159.04, reaching its highest level since 24 September.

headline: Iran's IRGC says two tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz overnight
detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz overnight, Iran's Fars news agency reports.

headline: Zelenskiy welcomes the US decision to include Europe in the Abu Dhabi peace talks
detail: Ukraine's president says he welcomes the US move to bring Europe into the Abu Dhabi talks on ending the war.

headline: Three-way Russia-US-Ukraine talks on a Ukraine settlement conclude in Abu Dhabi
detail: Reports citing a source and Russian media say the round of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi has ended. The second day of talks lasted almost two hours.

headline: German 30-year Bund auction draws 1.297 bid-to-cover, down from 1.4, with yield at 3.66%
detail: Germany's 30-year Bund auction had a bid-to-cover ratio of 1.297, down from 1.4 at the previous sale. The yield was 3.66%, against 3.8% last time.

headline: Bank of Mauritius sets its repo rate at 5%
detail: The Bank of Mauritius has announced its policy decision, setting the repo rate at 5%. The post did not say whether the rate had changed.

headline: Ireland's final October CPI shows 4.3% annual inflation, with the harmonised measure at 4.2%
detail: Final October figures put Ireland's consumer price inflation at 4.3% year on year and the harmonised index at 4.2% year on year.

headline: Portugal's final October CPI confirms 3.8% annual inflation, with the harmonised measure at 3.9%
detail: Portugal's statistics office INE confirmed the flash reading of 3.8% annual inflation for October and 0.2% on the month. The harmonised index rose 3.9% on the year and was unchanged on the month.

headline: Russia's chief negotiator says Abu Dhabi talks will continue, with a large prisoner exchange agreed with Ukraine
detail: After the three-way talks in Abu Dhabi ended, Russia's chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky said the sides agreed on some issues but not others, and that European security was the main topic. He said Russia and Ukraine had agreed a new large-scale exchange of prisoners of war and that Russia had received no peace proposal from the EU.

headline: Germany's Council of Economic Experts chair says the panel's growth forecasts will rise significantly
detail: Monika Schnitzer, chair of Germany's Council of Economic Experts, said the panel's economic forecasts would be raised significantly. She said the recovery from the oil price surge caused by the Iran war had come sooner than expected.

headline: Russia's chief negotiator praises US envoys and says Europe can join the Ukraine peace process only once it changes its stance
detail: Russia's chief negotiator Medinsky said European security architecture was the central topic at the Abu Dhabi talks, described the US envoys as constructive, and said Europe had made no proposals. He said details would not be made public until agreements are reached.

headline: German Chancellor Merz says Germany must do everything it can to keep its AAA credit rating
detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Germany must do all it can to preserve its AAA credit rating.

headline: US envoy Kushner reports good progress on Ukraine security guarantees but says territory will be the hardest issue to settle
detail: Speaking at a joint US-Ukrainian press conference after the Abu Dhabi talks, Kushner said no post-war security agreement will happen without a deal on territory, and that the US is trying to bring the Europeans into the talks. He also said the numbers for the agreed prisoner swap will be finalised tomorrow, and that he and Witkoff will meet Putin in Moscow tomorrow.

headline: Ukrainian negotiators see momentum towards a settlement before year-end and call for multilateral talks that include Europe
detail: After the Abu Dhabi talks, Ukrainian negotiators said a solution before the end of the year was possible and reported major progress on European security. They also said the talks should be multilateral rather than three-way and that Russia's delegation had arrived with strict instructions, which made discussions difficult.

headline: Russia's deputy foreign minister Ryabkov says Abu Dhabi meetings have laid groundwork for further work
detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said the Abu Dhabi talks on a Ukraine settlement had laid a foundation for further work.

headline: US envoy Kushner says Europe should name one negotiator and that Russia wants more progress before a Putin-Zelenskiy meeting
detail: US envoy Kushner said talks with the EU and NATO went very well, that Europeans are needed at the table for post-war security talks, and that the two sides do not trust each other but should be guided by their interests. He said he and Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday to discuss a prisoner exchange.

headline: US envoy Kushner backs a Putin-Zelenskiy meeting and says he and Witkoff go to Moscow tomorrow
detail: After the Abu Dhabi talks on a Ukraine settlement, US envoy Kushner said a meeting between Zelenskiy and Putin would be welcome. He also said he and fellow envoy Witkoff will travel to Moscow tomorrow. Separate reports say the Russian delegation leaves the UAE for Moscow today.

headline: Ukrainian negotiator says Kyiv heard no ultimatums from either side at the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: Ukrainian negotiator Serhii Kyslytsya said no side issued ultimatums during the three-way talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Russia's chief negotiator Medinsky says all Russian land will be returned by one means or another
detail: Russian presidential aide and chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky made the remark on territory after the three-way Russia-US-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi ended. The post reported no market reaction.

headline: Kremlin says Putin is open to contacts with European leaders including Merz and that dialogue with the US will continue
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said Putin has not yet received a full report on the Abu Dhabi talks and will meet Russian negotiators if he deems it necessary. He said no decision has been made on Putin attending the G20 summit in Miami.

headline: ECB's Makhlouf says price pressures sit mainly in energy but upside inflation risks persist
detail: ECB Governing Council member Gabriel Makhlouf said price pressures were largely limited to energy and that upside risks to inflation remain. He added that financing conditions have tightened following the rise in yields.

headline: UK PM Burnham says he will set out a plan for the UK before the Christmas recess
detail: The Prime Minister made the pledge while taking questions in parliament on 11 November. He gave no further details of the plan's content.

headline: Russia-Ukraine prisoner swap to be the largest yet, with more than 1,000 people on each side
detail: A Russian official, General Zorin, gave the figure for the exchange agreed at the Abu Dhabi talks.

headline: UK PM Burnham says an EU deal could lift UK GDP by 0.4%
detail: Prime Minister Burnham gave the estimate of an EU deal's potential effect on UK GDP in remarks reported on Wednesday. No market reaction was reported.

headline: German finance minister says Germany's AAA credit rating is not under threat
detail: Germany's finance minister said the country's top AAA sovereign rating is not in danger, after Chancellor Merz said Germany must do everything it can to keep the rating.

headline: G7 foreign ministers condemn North Korean, Iranian and Chinese support for Russia's military, UK reports
detail: According to the UK, the G7 foreign ministers' statement condemns North Korea and Iran for giving military assistance to Russia, and China for supplying weapons, military training and dual-use components. The ministers also express grave concern over Iranian involvement in violent plots, including one against the UK's RAF Fairford base.

headline: OPEC keeps its 2026 and 2027 global oil demand growth forecasts unchanged in its monthly report
detail: OPEC's monthly oil market report leaves its world oil demand growth projections for 2026 and 2027 unchanged.

headline: OPEC+ crude output rises 2.04m bpd to 41.23m bpd in October as Saudi output jumps to 10.563m bpd
detail: OPEC's monthly report puts OPEC+ crude production, including former member UAE, at an average 41.23 million bpd in October, up 2.04 million bpd from September. Saudi Arabia told OPEC it produced 10.563 million bpd in October, up 26% from 8.372 million bpd in September, and the rise was reported as a new wartime high.

headline: German government says a proposal exists for Europeans to take part in future Ukraine talks
detail: A German government spokesperson said Europe's involvement in several formats at the Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine had paid off. The spokesperson added that agreements could not be put into effect without consensus among NATO members.

headline: Zelenskiy calls for Europe to join Ukraine negotiations and for a firm US position in the peace talks
detail: Ukraine's president said Europe should take part in the negotiations and that Kyiv needs the US to take a strong stance in the peace talks. The remarks follow the three-way talks in Abu Dhabi.

headline: German government says it is waiting for Russia to respond to proposals for future Ukraine talks
detail: A German government spokesperson said Berlin is awaiting Russia's reaction to the proposals for future Ukraine talks. The spokesperson added that the US has as much interest as Europe in a peaceful settlement for Ukraine.

headline: German government says any Putin-Merz talks could build on principles agreed in Abu Dhabi
detail: The German government said possible talks between Russian President Putin and Chancellor Merz could go ahead based on the principles agreed at the Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks.

headline: German Council of Economic Experts forecasts inflation at 2.8% in 2026 and 3.3% in 2027
detail: Germany's Council of Economic Experts projects inflation of 2.8% for 2026, rising to 3.3% in 2027.

headline: German Council of Economic Experts forecasts growth of 1.3% in 2026 and 1% in 2027, flags defence borrowing strain
detail: Germany's Council of Economic Experts projects GDP growth of 1.3% in 2026 and 1% in 2027. The panel also warns that defence-related borrowing is putting pressure on the public finances.

headline: Lavrov says Putin will decide next steps on Ukraine after US envoys Witkoff and Kushner brief him in Moscow
detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said US envoys Witkoff and Kushner will brief President Putin in Moscow, after which Putin will determine the further course of action, according to reports.

headline: Dollar extends gains against the yen, up 0.5% at 159.55
detail: A market newswire reports the dollar up 0.5% at 159.55 yen. Earlier in the session it was up 0.2% at 159.04.

headline: Russia's chief negotiator Medinsky says the sides have moved closer to peace after the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: Russia's top Ukraine negotiator Medinsky said the parties appear closer to peace following the three-way negotiations in Abu Dhabi, according to Interfax reports.

headline: Saudi oil output recovers to above its average before the Iran conflict, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Saudi Arabia's crude production has rebounded to near prewar levels and is above its average before the Iran conflict. The kingdom has kept exports moving despite attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure.

headline: German economic advisers urge Merz to fund defence from the regular budget to keep debt from reaching 98% of GDP by 2040
detail: The Financial Times reports that Germany's Council of Economic Experts wants military spending moved gradually onto the regular budget. The panel warns that otherwise debt could reach 98% of GDP by 2040.

headline: Euro falls to its lowest against the dollar since May 2025, down 0.61% at $1.1097
detail: A market news account reported the euro last down 0.61% at $1.1097 against the US dollar, its weakest level since May 2025.

headline: Iran's Rezaei says Tehran will target US bases in European countries if US aircraft use them to strike Iran
detail: Iranian senior official Mohsen Rezaei made the warning and separately said Putin told him he had stressed to the US that Iran cannot be overthrown. No market reaction was reported.
