headline: Chancellor Healey says the UK economy is proving resilient and she aims to beat growth forecasts next year
detail: UK Chancellor Rachel Healey said the UK economy is showing real resilience. She also said she aims to beat next year's growth forecasts.

headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov calls Abu Dhabi talks substantial and says a Putin-Trump meeting at APEC is being prepared
detail: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov called the Abu Dhabi talks substantial and very useful, and said European-format talks will assess their outcome, Russian agencies report. The Kremlin also said a Putin-Trump meeting at APEC is being prepared.

headline: Russian foreign ministry says Russia has no plans to attack Europe
detail: Russia's foreign ministry made the statement on 11 November, as US-brokered talks on a Ukraine settlement continue. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Kremlin says no Putin-Trump conversation is currently planned after the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said no conversation between Putin and Trump is planned at present following the three-way talks between delegations in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Large-scale attack on Russia's Omsk refinery, the country's largest, sets off a fire, reports say
detail: Unconfirmed reports say explosions have been heard at the Omsk Oil Refinery for more than two hours and the strikes have caused a fire at the site. The reports do not mention any market reaction.

headline: Chancellor Healey says an end to the Middle East war would be the biggest single economic gain for the UK
detail: UK Chancellor Rachel Healey made the remarks on Wednesday, according to a market news account. No market reaction was reported.

headline: China's Wang Yi and US Secretary of State Rubio hold phone call that Xinhua calls positive and constructive
detail: According to Xinhua, China's Foreign Minister said Beijing is willing to step up communication and cooperation with the US and to handle differences and sensitive issues properly. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Russia's chief negotiator Medinsky rules out territorial swaps with Ukraine and says the border security zone will keep growing
detail: TASS and Vesti report that Medinsky said Russia sees no possibility of territorial exchanges with Ukraine. He also said the security zone along the border is substantial and will expand further, and that a fair security system could secure peace in Europe for decades.

headline: Chancellor Healey says fiscal headroom should be used when needed and rebuilt when possible
detail: UK Chancellor Healey set out her approach to fiscal headroom: draw on it when it is needed and restore it when conditions allow. The post gave no figures.

headline: Russia's chief negotiator Medinsky says a fair security system from the talks would secure peace in Europe for decades
detail: Medinsky made the remarks after the Abu Dhabi talks on a Ukraine settlement, according to reports from Russia. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Brent crude extends gains, up $2 a barrel amid uncertainty over talks to end the Iran and Ukraine wars
detail: Oil futures extended their rise, with Brent reported up $2 a barrel, citing uncertainty over negotiations to end the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

headline: US envoy Kushner says Russia and Ukraine have reached an important breakthrough in the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: US envoy Kushner described the Abu Dhabi talks as serious and frank and said Russia and Ukraine had achieved an important breakthrough, according to reports.

headline: Fed officials reportedly split over whether New York Fed President Williams should leave in 2027 or 2028
detail: Sources say there is an internal Federal Reserve debate over the timing of New York Fed President John Williams' departure, with 2027 and 2028 both under consideration. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Brent crude adds to gains and is up $3 a barrel amid uncertainty over the Iran and Ukraine talks
detail: Oil futures extended their rise, with Brent up $3 a barrel, from the earlier $2 gain. Reports linked the move to uncertainty over talks on Iran and Ukraine.

headline: Saudi Arabia reportedly says it intercepted three Houthi cruise missiles over Riyadh
detail: Reports say Saudi Arabia intercepted three cruise missiles launched by the Houthis over its capital, Riyadh. No market reaction was reported in the inputs.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf says US must meet all seven of Iran's conditions before Hormuz reopens and talks resume
detail: Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Washington has not yet formally answered Iran's message and plan, and that the decision now rests with the US, Al Jazeera reported. He said the Strait of Hormuz will reopen and talks will resume only once the US fully implements Iran's seven conditions.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf says US envoys asked Putin to help set up direct Iran-US talks
detail: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said US officials who travelled to Russia asked Putin to speak to Iran about holding direct talks between Tehran and Washington, according to Fars News. Iranian reports also quoted him as saying Trump would be defeated again if he returned to war.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf says Iran and Oman have agreed a Hormuz shipping lane and traffic separation arrangement
detail: In an interview with Al Jazeera, Ghalibaf said Iran had reached an understanding with Oman on the shipping route and traffic separation system in the Strait of Hormuz, but that the strait will not go back to how it was before the war because this is one of Iran's seven conditions. He also said Iran does not want the war to go on but its demands must be met, and offered to help Saudi Arabia and the Houthis settle their differences if asked.

headline: Sterling falls against a stronger dollar as markets bet on a Fed rate hike next month
detail: Reuters reports the pound fell against the dollar on Wednesday. The dollar strengthened across the board after US inflation data and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials the day before raised bets on a Fed hike next month.

headline: Ukraine's military says it struck Russia's Baltic oil port of Ust-Luga, damaging storage tanks
detail: Ukraine's military said it carried out a strike on the Russian Baltic port of Ust-Luga and that tanks at the port were damaged. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump says Iran will never be allowed to have a nuclear weapon
detail: US President Trump repeated that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, as talks continue on reopening Hormuz and on direct Iran-US talks. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Trump declares US victory in Iran and says it will take Iran 25 years to rebuild its losses
detail: US President Trump said the US had won in Iran and that rebuilding what Iran had lost would take 25 years. He also said the US was more respected than ever.

headline: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf warns Trump he would be defeated if he returns to war, and says the US must decide
detail: Iranian reports quote parliament speaker Ghalibaf as saying it is now up to the US to decide whether talks continue, which requires it to meet Iran's seven conditions. He also said Trump would face defeat if he chose to go to war again.

headline: US seeks to close Iran's land borders to tighten blockade, but neighbouring states push back, NYT reports
detail: The New York Times reports that Washington wants to step up economic pressure on Iran by sealing its land borders. Neighbouring countries are resisting because they fear the economic fallout.

headline: Iran attacks ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in the Strait of Hormuz, sources say
detail: Reuters cites three sources with knowledge of the matter as confirming that Iran attacked shipping navigation systems on the Omani island, which is infrastructure used to restore Gulf oil flows. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

headline: Brazil central bank chief Galipolo calls the external environment adverse and urges emerging markets to take extra care
detail: Galipolo said growing global demand for capital is putting pressure on interest rates, and that the short end of the yield curve is more sensitive to currency volatility. He also said there had been no debate at the central bank about changing the inflation-targeting regime, and that calls for lower rates are normal when growth slows while inflation picks up.

headline: Fed official warns an Anthropic IPO could set off a large market correction, Semafor reports
detail: Semafor reported the warning from a Federal Reserve official. The post did not name the official or give further detail.

headline: US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi end with a prisoner swap but without a breakthrough, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the Abu Dhabi talks, the first in about nine months after a pause caused by the war in Iran, ended with an agreed prisoner exchange but no breakthrough.

headline: BoE's Green backs tightening policy proactively to guard against wage growth staying high, FT reports
detail: Bank of England MPC member Megan Green said it is right to tighten the monetary policy stance proactively to lean against the risk that wage growth stays at higher levels, according to the Financial Times.

headline: Houthis claim cruise missile attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport and a drone strike on a pumping station in Saudi Arabia's Yanbu region
detail: Yemen's Houthis said they fired three cruise missiles at King Khalid airport in Riyadh and attacked a pumping station in the Yanbu region with a drone. Saudi Arabia had earlier reportedly said it intercepted three Houthi cruise missiles over Riyadh; no market reaction was reported.

headline: BoE's Greene says UK labour market has less slack than thought and data show wage growth is too high
detail: MPC member Megan Greene made the remarks in comments reported by the FT, in which she also repeated her support for tightening monetary policy proactively.

headline: Chancellor Healey says the Treasury is discussing worst-case energy support for UK households, FT reports
detail: The FT reports that Chancellor Rachel Healey is preparing for a deepening energy crisis, with the Treasury discussing worst-case support for households. No cost or details of the support were given.

headline: Zelenskiy says Russian envoys have rejected ceasefire proposals
detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Russia's negotiators turned down proposals for a ceasefire. The statement follows the US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Dollar hits a session high against the Swiss franc, up 0.98% at 0.83325
detail: A market commentator reported that the dollar reached a session high against the Swiss franc and was last up 0.98% at 0.83325 francs.

headline: US asks Russia to put forward a new European security proposal, Axios reports
detail: Axios reports that the US has asked Russia to submit a new proposal on European security, following the US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine aims to get results from the peace talks by the end of the year
detail: Speaking in Dublin, Ukrainian President Zelenskiy said Kyiv wants the peace talks to produce results by year end and will do everything it can to achieve that.

headline: Trade-weighted dollar rises sharply on hawkish Fed bets after hot US CPI and Waller's mention of a 50bp hike
detail: An economist reports a big rise in the trade-weighted dollar on Wednesday, driven by rate differentials, as markets digest Tuesday's hot US CPI data and Fed Governor Waller's talk of a 50bp rate hike next month.

headline: Iranian general Heydari says Strait of Hormuz is closed and will reopen only on the Supreme Leader's order
detail: Brigadier General Heydari said Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz and will not reopen it unless the leader of the revolution orders it, the ISNA news agency reported. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Markets price 76bp of Fed hikes through June 2027, up from 72bp at Tuesday's close
detail: Fed pricing moved further in the hawkish direction after the hot US CPI print. Gold is reported to be falling and all G10 currencies are down against the dollar.

headline: German coalition agrees 2027 budget and drops planned electricity tax cut, Spiegel reports
detail: Spiegel reports that Germany's governing coalition has agreed its 2027 budget and that a planned cut to electricity tax is not in it.

headline: UK RICS house price balance falls to -36 in October, weaker than the -33.5 forecast
detail: The RICS housing survey balance came in at -36, compared with a forecast of -33.5 and -32 the previous month.

headline: Japan's producer prices rise 7.1% year on year in October, above the 6.5% forecast
detail: BoJ data show the corporate goods price index rose 7.1% year on year, against a 6.5% forecast and 6.8% previously, and 0.7% month on month against a 0.3% forecast. In early trade, benchmark 10-year JGB futures were reported up 0.03 point.

headline: Fed's Goolsbee calls the latest US inflation report borderline disturbing
detail: The Chicago Fed president's remarks came as hot US inflation data and hawkish Fed comments raised expectations of a rate hike in December. Gold fell 0.8% to $4,002.54 an ounce and the dollar index was reported up 0.4%.

headline: Japan's top currency official Mimura says currency moves are too rapid
detail: Japan's vice finance minister for international affairs commented on the speed of moves in the currency market. The dollar was trading near 159.55 yen after recent gains.

headline: US and China agree leader-level talks matter, including a possible trilateral summit with Russia
detail: The US State Department said Secretary of State Rubio and China's Wang Yi agreed on the importance of leader-level talks to advance peace and denuclearisation, including a potential trilateral summit with Russia.

headline: BoJ's Asada urges caution on further rate rises, saying hikes from a neutral policy rate could hit the economy harder
detail: Bank of Japan board member Asada said financial conditions remain accommodative and underlying inflation is around levels consistent with the 2% target. She said the BoJ must be cautious about the pace of any future increases and can use consumer price data to judge the risk of inflation overshooting.

headline: US 2-year Treasury yield rises nearly 5bp to a two-week high of 4.7756%
detail: The US 2-year Treasury yield reached a two-week high in Asian trading, while the 10-year yield was reported steady at 4.99%. Gold prices were reported under pressure from rising expectations of Fed rate hikes.

headline: Brent and WTI crude fall $1 a barrel on Middle East peace optimism
detail: Brent and WTI crude oil were both reported $1 a barrel lower in Asian trading, with the fall attributed to optimism over peace in the Middle East.

headline: Dollar reaches a 19-month high as markets price further Fed tightening and the yen weakens
detail: The dollar rose to its strongest level in 19 months in Asian trade on bets on further Federal Reserve tightening. Asian currencies came under renewed pressure, and the New Zealand dollar fell as traders weighed a bigger Fed rate rise.

headline: BoJ's Asada says Japan's inflation is not necessarily demand-led and that consumption data may be weaker than they look
detail: BoJ board member Asada said any further rate rises must come at a cautious pace and that policy takes at least a year to feed through to borrowing. He expects Japan's growth to pick up moderately.

headline: Japan's 5-year government bond yield falls 2bp to 2.170%
detail: The 5-year JGB yield fell 2bp to 2.170% in Asian trade, after BoJ board member Asada's remarks urging caution on rate rises.

headline: EU and UK set to postpone a planned 10% tariff on electric vehicles, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that the EU and the UK plan to delay a 10% tariff on electric cars. European carmakers had warned that the levy would leave them more exposed to Chinese competition.

headline: China's central bank signals more room for monetary easing as growth holds up, WSJ reports
detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that the People's Bank of China has signalled greater scope to ease monetary policy while growth remains firm.

headline: France backs Spain's Hernandez de Cos as candidate for ECB president, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that France has signalled its support for Spain's candidate, Pablo Hernandez de Cos, for the presidency of the European Central Bank.

headline: Russia's diesel exports double after US sanctions relief, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that Russian diesel exports have doubled following US sanctions relief, with none of the supply going to the US.

headline: BoJ's Asada puts Japan's neutral rate near the low end of the staff range and says any further hikes should come slowly
detail: BoJ board member Asada said no terminal rate target has been set, that rate rises could weaken underlying inflation as consumption slows, and that a rate cut is not under consideration. He said he is not wholly opposed to hikes and that rates may need to rise gradually at some point. He also said the neutral rate may be somewhat above the current policy rate.

headline: EU leaders aim to agree Hernández de Cos as next ECB president as soon as this month, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports growing support for the Spanish economist Pablo Hernández de Cos's bid to become president of the European Central Bank. It says EU leaders want to seal a deal as early as November.

headline: Chinese and UK trade ministers discuss electric vehicles, China's commerce ministry says
detail: China's Commerce Ministry said its trade minister and the UK trade minister exchanged views on electric vehicles. It gave no details of any outcome.

headline: Iran's IRGC Navy claims two supertankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz overnight
detail: Sepah News, the IRGC's news outlet, reports the IRGC Navy's claim that two supertankers exploded in the Strait of Hormuz overnight. The claim has not been independently confirmed, and no market reaction has been reported.

headline: UK GDP grows 0.7% in the third quarter, in line with forecasts, while monthly GDP rises 0.2% against an expected 0%
detail: The preliminary estimate shows annual growth of 1.9%, matching forecasts, up from 0.5% quarterly and 1.4% annual growth previously; services rose 0.2% on the month against a forecast of 0%. Construction output rose 0.8% month on month (forecast -0.1%), industrial production grew 3.1% year on year (forecast 2.8%) and business investment rose 0.43% quarter on quarter (forecast 0.6%, previous 1.8%).

headline: UK manufacturing output rises 0.7% in September against a forecast 0.5% fall; industrial production up 0.3%
detail: ONS data show September industrial production rose 0.3% on the month against a forecast -0.4%, and manufacturing rose 4.4% year on year against a 3.8% forecast. Construction output rose 0.8% on the month against a forecast 0.0%.

headline: UK goods trade deficit widens to 22.29bn in September, wider than the 19.2bn forecast
detail: The September goods trade deficit was 22.29bn against 18.01bn the previous month, with the non-EU deficit at 8.99bn. Third-quarter business investment rose 0.4% on the quarter, in line with forecasts, and Q3 GDP grew 1.9% year on year, also as expected.

headline: France's European affairs minister says the EU will approve further sanctions on Russia on Monday
detail: France's European affairs minister, Haddad, said EU approval of a further package of sanctions on Russia is due on Monday.

headline: China's commerce ministry says Beijing and Washington are in close contact on tariff cuts, trade and investment
detail: China's commerce ministry said it is in close communication with the US over tariff reduction, trade and investment, and on interaction between Xi and Trump. It added that China is willing to keep strengthening cooperation and to manage differences properly.

headline: France's European affairs minister says sanctions on Iran will be tightened after a cyber attack involving fridges
detail: France's European affairs minister Haddad said sanctions against Iran would be strengthened in response to a cyber attack that targeted fridges. No further details or market reaction were reported.

headline: Turkey lifts its end-2027 inflation estimate to 21% from 15%
detail: Turkey has revised its inflation estimate for the end of 2027 up to 21%, from 15% previously, according to a market news feed.

headline: Russia's Ryabkov denies that the Abu Dhabi negotiations have restored trust between the parties
detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Ryabkov said it was wrong to describe trust between the sides as restored after the Abu Dhabi talks. Earlier, US envoy Kushner had described the talks as an important breakthrough.

headline: Russia's Ryabkov says uncontrolled escalation should be avoided after the negotiations
detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said escalation should not be allowed to get out of control following the negotiations. He spoke after the US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Gassco extends reduced capacity at Norway's Troll gas field by one day to Saturday
detail: Norwegian gas system operator Gassco says the capacity reduction at the Troll field will now last one extra day, until Saturday. No figure for the size of the reduction was given.

headline: Russia's Ryabkov says Putin will set out Russia's position to US negotiators, leaving Washington to persuade European allies
detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Ryabkov says Putin will give Russia's position to the American negotiators, after which it falls to the United States to bring its European allies round. The remarks follow US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Russia's Ryabkov says US and European approaches differ sharply and bringing Europe into Ukraine talks could derail progress
detail: Russian media report that Deputy Foreign Minister Ryabkov said the United States and Europe take very different approaches to the Ukraine negotiations. He said that involving European countries could undermine constructive efforts.

headline: US envoy Witkoff hopes the Abu Dhabi trilateral talks bring Ukraine peace a step closer
detail: Reports say US envoy Witkoff expressed hope after the US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, and Kremlin aide Ushakov set out what Putin, Witkoff and Kushner will discuss. The same reports say military and energy facilities in Ukraine have been hit.

headline: Iran's IRGC Navy says a third tanker has exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine
detail: The IRGC Navy's public relations office said the tanker had breached its rules for the Strait of Hormuz, according to reports. The statement follows its earlier claim that two supertankers exploded in the strait overnight.

headline: Russia's Ryabkov says the US is committed to resolving the Ukraine conflict
detail: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Ryabkov said Washington is committed to finding a solution to the war in Ukraine, according to reports. He also said that NATO's Supreme Commander Grinkevich being at the Abu Dhabi talks made the discussion of European security more professional.

headline: Resolution Foundation says UK GDP has grown 1.9% over the first nine months of the year
detail: Following the third-quarter GDP release, the Resolution Foundation said UK output rose 1.9% over the first nine months of the year. It said this puts the UK on track to be the second-fastest growing economy in the G7.

headline: Chancellor Healey says any UK deal with the EU must bring benefits greater than its trade-offs
detail: The UK Chancellor made the comment when asked about a deal with the EU. No further detail or market reaction was reported.

headline: India's consumer price inflation reaches 6.09% in October, above the 5.93% forecast
detail: India's government says consumer prices rose 6.09% year on year in October. A Reuters poll had forecast 5.93%.

headline: NIESR raises its UK fourth-quarter GDP growth projection to 0.4% from 0.2%
detail: NIESR's GDP tracker confirms that UK GDP grew 0.7% in Q3, up from 0.5% in Q2, and now projects 0.4% growth in Q4 2026, revised up from last month's 0.2%. The institute says the Bank of England should stay focused on second-round effects.

headline: EU's Kallas says Russia is showing no goodwill and that the focus in Ukraine should be on a ceasefire
detail: EU foreign policy chief Kallas said the EU sees no goodwill from Russia and that attention in Ukraine should be on a ceasefire. She also said European Council President Costa and the High Representative should represent the EU.

headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says she would very much like Britain to return to Europe
detail: Kaja Kallas, the EU's foreign policy chief, said she would strongly welcome Britain rejoining Europe. Earlier on the blotter, Chancellor Healey said any UK deal with the EU must bring benefits greater than its trade-offs.

headline: EU's von der Leyen says the next Russia sanctions package and a Ukraine financing proposal will come before the new year
detail: European Commission President von der Leyen said the Commission will present its next sanctions package and a proposal on financial rules for Ukraine before next year. She also said she strongly welcomes the peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Germany's Merz says Europeans must be involved in Ukraine talks and expects Putin to agree to give them a seat
detail: German Chancellor Merz said it was important that Russia is willing to engage in talks, and that he expects Putin to agree that Europeans should have a seat at the table. He also said he sees a good chance of concluding EU budget talks before the end of the year.

headline: All 71 economists in a poll expect the ECB to raise its deposit rate to 2.75% in December
detail: In a poll of economists, all 71 respondents expect the ECB to raise its deposit rate to 2.75% in December, up from 64 of 73 in the October poll. 46 of the 71 see the deposit rate peaking at 2.75%, while 25 see a peak of 3.00%.

headline: Iran says it is reviewing withdrawal from the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, calling the move an unavoidable necessity
detail: Iran's Fars news agency reported the statement. No market reaction was reported.

headline: Iran says reviewing an exit from the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty is now a national demand
detail: Iran described its review of withdrawing from the NPT as having become a national demand, Fars news agency reported. No market reaction was reported.

headline: France's Macron says Europe needs a clear, united vision of what it wants for Ukraine
detail: French President Macron said on Thursday that Europe must have a clear and shared position on its goals for Ukraine. No market reaction was reported.

headline: NATO's Rutte calls Abu Dhabi talks news positive but says whether Russia will cooperate will be judged later
detail: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte described the outcome of the Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine as positive and said Russia's willingness to cooperate would be assessed later. He also said Ukraine needs to be as strong as possible, both in the fighting and in negotiations with Russia.

headline: NATO's Rutte says US, European and Ukrainian positions were closely aligned at the Abu Dhabi talks
detail: NATO Secretary General Rutte also said Europe and the US reached agreement in January on the outline of security guarantees, and that this work is complete.

headline: Zelenskiy calls US approach of discussing a new security order with Russia strange and wants Europe at the table
detail: Speaking in Dublin, Ukraine's president said Europe should be a regular part of negotiations with Russia and that he will hold talks with US representatives later on Thursday. He also said Russia treats energy as a battlefield each winter and that Ukraine needs air defence interceptors.

headline: Zelenskiy asks for energy support for Ukraine now and through the winter, citing equipment destroyed by Russia
detail: Speaking in Dublin, Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Ukraine needs energy support now and through the winter. He said his team has a list of the equipment it needs to replace after Russian attacks destroyed it.

headline: Putin thanks Trump through US envoys for helping Russia-Ukraine contacts as Kremlin talks with Witkoff and Kushner begin
detail: According to Interfax and other reports, Putin met US envoys Witkoff and Kushner at the Kremlin. He asked them to pass his thanks to Trump for facilitating contacts between Russia and Ukraine and pointed to progress on the humanitarian track.

headline: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico immediately unless it stops migrant caravans
detail: US President Trump said tariffs on Mexico would be doubled straight away if Mexico does not stop migrant caravans.

headline: European Council President Costa says next week will be a decisive test of whether Russia is willing to end the war
detail: European Council President António Costa made the remarks in a speech in Dublin on Thursday. He did not give further detail on the timing.

headline: US envoy Witkoff tells Putin meeting the Abu Dhabi contacts were held in a positive atmosphere
detail: Witkoff and Kushner are meeting Putin, with Russian officials Medinsky, Dmitriev and Ushakov also present. Reports say Putin told the envoys it was important for him to hear their assessment of the Abu Dhabi talks, and that he noted the success of humanitarian efforts in Ukraine.

headline: US envoy Witkoff says planned Russia-Ukraine prisoner swap shows progress towards a settlement
detail: Speaking around his Kremlin talks with Putin, US envoy Witkoff said the Russian and Ukrainian delegations worked effectively in Abu Dhabi and that Europeans were kept informed but did not sit at the negotiating table. He said he will brief Zelenskiy on the talks.

headline: Riksbank's Bunge says the policy rate will likely need to rise over the coming year, with gradual changes important
detail: Riksbank policymaker Bunge said a rate rise is likely to be needed over the coming year. She added that it is important for monetary policy to change gradually.

headline: US envoy Kushner says Washington has begun talks with European partners on the continent's security architecture
detail: US envoy Kushner said the US has started discussing Europe's security architecture with European partners. He also said the US sees a strong European wish to take part in negotiations and end the war in Ukraine, Interfax reported.

headline: Putin says Russia recognises only one demarcation line with Ukraine, the state border
detail: Russian President Putin said that for Russia the only demarcation line with Ukraine is the state border. He spoke as the Kremlin's talks with US envoys continued.

headline: Putin proposes a humanitarian mission from Kostiantynivka modelled on earlier cooperation with Ukraine over Oleshky
detail: At his Kremlin meeting with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner, President Putin described humanitarian cooperation with Ukraine over Oleshky as positive. He proposed organising a similar mission from Kostiantynivka, according to reports.

headline: Putin says any foreign troops in Ukraine would be a legitimate target for Russia and calls their presence unacceptable
detail: Interfax reports that President Putin also said Russia has never opposed dialogue with Europe and wants peace in Ukraine to be permanent. He said Russia controls Kostiantynivka and needs five days to clear mines there, and proposed that Russian and Ukrainian ombudsmen organise the humanitarian mission.

headline: Putin says Russia wants the US to work out with Europe whether they want peace or war
detail: Russian President Putin said Russia would like Washington to work with European allies to decide whether they are seeking peace or war over Ukraine, according to reports. The remarks follow his comments earlier in the day on foreign troops in Ukraine.

headline: US envoy Witkoff hopes Putin talks lead to a new round of trilateral Ukraine talks with Europeans taking part
detail: US envoy Witkoff said he hoped a new round of trilateral talks, with European participation, could be announced after the negotiations with Putin in Moscow.

headline: Putin says leaving 'grey zones' in place would make any agreement unstable and rule out lasting peace
detail: Russian President Putin said during talks with US envoys that keeping grey zones would undermine any agreements on Ukraine and prevent a lasting peace.

headline: US envoy Witkoff expects to announce today the date of a three-way meeting on Ukraine
detail: Interfax reports that US envoy Witkoff expects to give the date of a tripartite meeting on Ukraine later today. Separate reports say he hopes the new round of talks will include European representatives.

headline: Putin says he will raise territorial questions with US envoys today and that Russia and Ukraine read them differently
detail: Russian President Putin said territory would be among the topics in his talks with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner on Thursday, according to TASS. He said Russia and Ukraine interpret territorial issues differently, and that Russia's priority is people being able to live by their own values.

headline: Trump says the US does not need a deal with Iran
detail: US President Trump said in remarks on Thursday that Washington has no need for an agreement with Iran. Iran had earlier said it was reviewing withdrawal from the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

headline: European gas climbs as much as 5.2% and Brent adds to gains after Trump's Iran comments
detail: Market reports say European gas prices rose by up to 5.2% after President Trump's remarks on Iran. Brent crude added to its earlier gain and was up 1%.

headline: US initial jobless claims rise to 200K, above the 194K forecast; continuing claims fall to 1.697M
detail: US weekly initial jobless claims came in at 200K, up from 189K the week before and above the 194K forecast. Continuing claims dropped to 1.697M from 1.718M, below the 1.71M forecast.

headline: UK sanctions Russia's ten largest oil producers, plus shadow fleet vessels, coal firms and Rosneft's Vostok Oil project
detail: The UK government announced sanctions on Russia's top ten oil producers. The package also covers shadow fleet vessels, coal companies and Rosneft's Vostok Oil project.

headline: UK adds Slavneft to Russia sanctions, with 11 new designations and 9 new specifications under the regime
detail: The UK government also named Russian oil producer Slavneft in its latest sanctions action, adding 11 new designations and 9 new specifications under the Russia sanctions regime. The move extends earlier measures on Russia's largest oil producers.

headline: USTR Greer says China is only partly complying on trade and Trump is ready to act on Mexico tariffs
detail: In a CNBC interview, US Trade Representative Greer said China's compliance was partial, with the US getting some of the rare earths it needs but wanting more progress. He said the president was prepared to take tariff action on Mexico, that talks with Canada were continuing without a timeline, and that tariff options would stay open.

headline: Fed's Hammack says policy needs to move to a restrictive stance as inflation moves the wrong way
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said the Fed has missed its inflation mandate for years while doing well on jobs. She pointed to real demand pressures, including from the AI build-out, and said she is worried an inflationary mindset could take hold.

headline: USTR Greer says the US will set its own export controls and act on enforcement, with tech exports in focus
detail: US Trade Representative Greer told CNBC that export controls matter to the US and should be enforced appropriately. He said the administration will investigate any problems and take action if needed.

headline: USTR Greer says trade issues will be taken up with China next week and declines to give a timeline for a Canada trade deal
detail: US Trade Representative Greer also said national security is paramount in trade and that he expects to work with the new Congress on tariffs. He gave no timeline for a trade deal with Canada.

headline: Fed's Hammack says she favours smaller, steadier rate moves and enters every FOMC meeting with an open mind
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack made the remarks in further comments on Thursday. They follow her earlier call for policy to move to a restrictive stance.

headline: Fed's Hammack sees broadening price pressures and secondary effects from energy, but says the Fed is not behind the curve
detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said recent inflation data show price pressures broadening, including secondary effects from energy. She said she does not think the Fed is behind the curve, but would consider larger or more aggressive moves if it fell behind.

headline: Fed's Hammack calls the US job market static and says it lacks the dynamism to be described as healthy
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack made the remarks on the labour market on Thursday, during the same appearance in which she discussed inflation and the policy stance.

headline: Fed's Hammack says financial conditions are supportive of growth
detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said current financial conditions are supporting growth. She made the remark in further comments on 12 November.

headline: About 40 countries are set to sign a draft European security declaration backing Ukraine's sovereignty and security guarantees
detail: Reuters reports that it has seen a draft declaration on the key principles of European security. The draft supports Ukraine's territorial integrity, calls for robust security guarantees for Ukraine and says any matter affecting European security should be decided with the Europeans.

headline: Mexico's Sheinbaum says no migrant caravan has reached the US border since Trump took office
detail: Mexico's president made the remarks after Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico immediately unless it stops migrant caravans.

headline: Putin's Kremlin meeting with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner on Ukraine ends
detail: Market news accounts report that the talks between Russian President Putin and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner have finished. No outcome was reported.

headline: Draft European security declaration reportedly links future strategic stability to the end of the war in Ukraine
detail: Reports on the draft declaration that about 40 countries are set to sign say future progress on European strategic stability will depend on the war in Ukraine ending.

headline: Iranian army says two tankers have hit naval mines while passing through the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iranian state TV carried the army statement. It follows an earlier IRGC Navy report that a third tanker had exploded in the strait after hitting a mine.

headline: Iran's Assembly of Experts says a revision of the country's defence doctrine is unavoidable
detail: The statement was reported on Thursday, after Iran said it is reviewing withdrawal from the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

headline: US House Speaker Johnson says a consensus is forming in Congress on limiting chip exports to China
detail: Reuters reported the remarks on Thursday, after a scandal forced Nvidia's chief executive to step down. Separately, a White House official told CNN that Trump is standing by Commerce Secretary Lutnick despite growing scrutiny of export controls.

headline: Fed's Barr warns AI could cause serious short-term disruption in the US job market
detail: Fed Governor Barr said there are signs AI is replacing labour in some sectors and that the dislocation could be large if change comes quickly, though so far few workers have been displaced. He also noted that labour's share of income is falling, and said it is an open question whether AI will further raise returns to capital.

headline: US existing home sales fall 5.5% to 3.75M, below the 3.85M forecast
detail: US existing home sales came in at an annualised 3.75M, against a forecast of 3.85M and a previous 3.99M. The monthly change was -5.5%, compared with a forecast of -3.5% and a previous 1.5%.

headline: US 2- to 5-year Treasury yields are up at least 10bp on the day
detail: A market newswire reports that US Treasury yields from 2 to 5 years are at least 10bp higher on the day. The rise follows remarks today by the Fed's Hammack and US jobless claims data.

headline: Draft declaration by about 40 countries says matters affecting European security should be decided with Europeans
detail: Reuters says it has seen a draft declaration on key principles of European security. About 40 countries are expected to issue it on Thursday, and it says any matter affecting European security should be decided with the Europeans.

headline: Fed's Barr says the Fed is watching AI-related liabilities and the potential for shocks
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr said the central bank is monitoring liabilities linked to AI and possible shocks from it. He made the remarks after earlier warning about AI disruption to the US job market.

headline: Fed's Barr says AI's impact so far falls mostly on prices, with input cost pressure feeding into consumer electronics
detail: Fed Governor Barr said AI is currently boosting investment and GDP, and that pressure on AI input prices is spreading to goods such as phones, computers and gaming consoles. He said he does not yet see a big labour market impact, though AI may be contributing to low hiring of younger workers, and that rapid adoption could make the labour adjustment harder.

headline: Fed's Barr says banks are concentrating on AI risk controls and flags agentic AI as a major issue for them
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr said banks are paying close attention to risk controls and usage standards for AI. He added that agentic AI will be a significant challenge for banks in ensuring the tools follow customer instructions.

headline: Kremlin's Peskov accuses Europeans of saying they want peace while moving to continue and widen the Ukraine war
detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said European actions must stop being contradictory, echoing Putin's remarks earlier in the day. He said this gap between Europe's words and actions has created a vicious circle.

headline: US envoy Witkoff says a new round of Ukraine talks was agreed after his meeting with Putin
detail: RIA reported Witkoff's remarks after the Kremlin meeting. Fellow US envoy Kushner called the talks with Putin substantive and detailed.

headline: Iran's military says four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Iran's military said on Thursday that the four vessels had ignored warnings and entered waters of the strait that it treats as restricted. Earlier, the Iranian army had said two tankers hit naval mines in the strait.

headline: US envoy Witkoff says Europeans will take part in the next round of Ukraine negotiations
detail: After the Kremlin meeting with Putin, US envoy Witkoff said progress had been made and the next round of trilateral talks would include Europeans. US envoy Kushner called the meeting fruitful.

headline: European leaders reject Russia's push to overhaul Europe's security architecture, FT reports
detail: The Financial Times reports that European leaders have rejected the Russian proposals. It also reports Ukraine's President Zelenskiy warning after the Abu Dhabi talks that Europe needs to pay attention.

headline: ECB's Vujcic says the direction of travel on rates is unchanged and further price pressures may arrive with a lag
detail: ECB Governing Council member Vujcic gave both comments on Thursday afternoon.

headline: Fed's Barr says he is worried that deregulation is taking place in a risk-on environment
detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr made the comment in remarks on Thursday that also covered AI risks to banks and the labour market.

headline: US envoy Kushner calls Kremlin talks with Putin thorough and a basis for further consultations
detail: Reports say US envoy Kushner described the latest Ukraine talks with Putin as thorough and detailed. He said they would serve as a foundation for future consultations.

headline: US Treasury sets $16bn 20-year bond sale for 18 November and $19bn 10-year TIPS reopening for 19 November
detail: The US Treasury will also sell $95bn of 3-month bills and $82bn of 6-month bills on 16 November, settling 19 November. The 20-year bond and 10-year TIPS sales both settle on 30 November.

headline: US push to close land routes and tighten Iran blockade is reportedly failing as neighbouring states refuse to comply
detail: Unattributed market reports say countries bordering Iran are declining to follow Washington's orders to shut land routes as part of the blockade. No market reaction was reported.
